{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:19:00.865894+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6817c8724c1821a448a09581f15c3ef4603768f37a8436a3d39be65abfe8ad46","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 17 (Doob's maximal identity / Ville tightness) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $(M_t)$ be a nonnegative martingale with $M_0=1$ and $M_t\to0$ a.s., let $\tau^\star$ be its ultimate-maximum time of~\eqref{eq:tau-star}, and fix a level $x > 1$.  Then
\[
  \PP(M_{\tau^\star} \geq x)
  = \PP\!\left(\sup_{t\geq 0} M_t \geq x\right)
  \leq \frac{1}{x},
\]
with equality at that level exactly when $x$ is crossed without overshoot: writing $\sigma_x := \inf\{t : M_t \geq x\}$ for the first passage to $x$, $M_{\sigma_x} = x$ a.s.\ on $\{\sigma_x < \infty\}$; the deficit is the mean overshoot of Theorem~\ref{thm:firstpassage-exact}, divided by the level.
A continuous-time vanishing martingale with continuous paths crosses every level without overshoot, and its running maximum is then exactly Pareto$(1)$~\cite{nikeghbali2006doobs}.
No discrete-time vanishing martingale attains equality at every level at once: absence of overshoot at every $x \geq 1$ forces $\sup_{t} M_t \leq 1$ a.s., and a nonnegative martingale with $M_0 = 1$ bounded by $1$ is constant.
The Pareto$(1)$ law is the continuous-time idealization that the discrete-time tail approaches from below, level by level, as the overshoot vanishes. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.642083+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_682272fa91a23b289b7e5e88ab8e4bb955ba3f2d9df89f79fd487d00e64550d1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.00702, 'On the Set-Valued Katugampola Fractional Integral: Properties and Regular Selections'] Let $F$ be a compact set-valued function such that $F:I\rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}$ and for each $u\in [a,b]$, $F(u)$ is compact. For any partition $\mathcal{T}=\{t_0,t_1,t_2,\ldots t_n\}\subset I= [a,b]$ and $n\in \mathbb{N},$ the total Jordan variation of $ F$ is
    \[ V_a^b(F)=\sup_{\mathcal{T}} \sum_{i=1}^nH_d(F(t_i),F(t_{i-1})), \]
    with the supremum over all partitions $\mathcal{T}$ of $I.$ If $V_a^b(F)< \infty,$ then we say that $F$ is of bounded variation on $I.$ 

 \begin{definition}
     A set valued map $F:I\to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be Lipschitz on $I$ with respect to $H_d$ if there exists a constant $C_F>0$ such that 
     \[ H_d(F(t_1),F(t_2)) \le C_F|t_1-t_2| \text{ for all } t_1,t_2 \in I \] 
     and such a constant $C_F$ is called the Lipschitz constant of $F.$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:55:37.369054+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6823162ea13653b36b31490bbcb3749a3b9e007b626bcd33709ee80a5f10393f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 10 (Positive definiteness of the Mellin quotient) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] For $p,q>0$, the function

where the star denotes ordinary size-biasing of the positive random variable $S_{p/q}^{-1/q}$. If $p=q$, then $\Phi_{p,p}\equiv1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.389943+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6826341996111181ac8f7eb849e797b7b0a0b52ec8b838320e06c62e725a2b7d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 123 (Covariance cross-responses and the orthogonal-martingale boundary) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix $P\in\cP$ and let $M$ be a continuous square-integrable scalar
$P$-martingale.  Its Galtchouk--Kunita--Watanabe decomposition relative to the
closed stable subspace generated by $X$ is
\begin{equation}
 M_t-M_0=\int_0^t\langle z_r^P,\dd X_r\rangle_H+N_t^P,

\[
 [N^P,\langle X,h\rangle]=0,

 =\langle a_t^Pz_t^P,h\rangle_H
\]
whenever the displayed density is defined.  Hence covariance cross-responses
determine only the energy class of $z^P$ and are blind to $N^P$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.495476+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_683cc9a15b3f17360622ecb0d0fd601721ecf791773e2f3f7aa2085c62c4e651","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 35 (Double-hive KL bound using a shared large-gap side) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:doubleKLhive}
Let \(w,w'>0\) and \(u,u'\geq 0\). Let \(G_n,\widetilde G_n,G'_n,\widetilde G'_n\) be independent GUE
matrices, and set
\[
D_n=\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G_n)),
\qquad
D'_n=\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G'_n)).
\]
Let
\[
X_n=\sqrt n\,(wG_n+uD_n),
\qquad
Y_n=\sqrt n\,(w'G'_n+u'D'_n),
\]
and put
\[
a^2=w^2+u^2,\qquad b^2=(w')^2+(u')^2.
\]
Assume
\[
\frac{u}{w^2}=\frac{u'}{(w')^2}.
\]
Let
\[
\lambda_n=\operatorname{spec}(X_n),
\qquad
\mu_n=\operatorname{spec}(Y_n).
\]
Let \(L_n\) be the corrected regularized large-gap side from
\eqref{eq:corrected-large-gap}, and set
\[
N_n=L_n+\operatorname{diag}(X_n),
\qquad
P_n=L_n - \operatorname{diag}(Y_n).
\]
Let
\[
h_n^{(1)}\in H_n(\lambda_n,L_n;N_n),
\qquad
h_n^{(2)}\in H_n(\mu_n,L_n;P_n)
\]
be the two hives obtained, via Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv), from the
large-gap construction applied to the two deformed minor processes arising from
$X_n$ and $Y_n$ respectively.  Paste them along the common side \(L_n\), with
the exterior sides in clockwise cyclic order
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad \mu_n,\qquad P_n,\qquad N_n.
\]
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\small}]
  \coordinate (L) at (0,0);
  \coordinate (T) at (2,2);
  \coordinate (R) at (4,0);
  \coordinate (B) at (2,-2);
  \draw[thick] (L) -- (T) -- (R) -- (B) -- cycle;
  \draw[thick] (L) -- (R);
  \node[below left] at (1,-1) {\(\lambda_n\)};
  \node[above left] at (1,1) {\(\mu_n\)};
  \node[above right] at (3,1) {\(P_n\)};
  \node[below right] at (3,-1) {\(N_n\)};
  \node[above] at (2,0) {\(L_n\)};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
Decorate these four exterior sides, with
independent uniform Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.  Let \(q_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\)
be the resulting density on the four-boundary double-hive cone \(\mathbb D^4\).

Let \(p_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\) be the maximum-entropy density on \(\mathbb D^4\)
whose four exterior sides, in clockwise cyclic order, have the same expected
quadratic moments as
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad \mu_n,\qquad P_n,\qquad N_n .
\]
Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(q_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\Vert p_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\right)
=O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.767500+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_683eb2708acf74fea6502b4c2698534b160300eacdd11ef2bbe48879632e830a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 4 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Let $T>0$, let $D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\} \subset [0,T]$ be a finite subset,
and call \[[0,d_1),[d_1,d_2),\ldots,[d_{m-1},d_m),[d_m,T]\] 
the maximal intervals of $[0,T] \setminus D$. 

Fixing $T$-dependent
constants $K_0,K_1,K_2,K_3>0$ where $K_0,K_1$ define the above envelopes,
let $\mathcal{S}_\theta^+(T,D)$ be the space of all
pairs $(C_\theta,R_\theta)$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item $C_\theta:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a positive-semidefinite
covariance kernel satisfying
\[C_\theta(t,t) \leq \Phi_{C_\theta}(t) \text{ for all } 0\leq t\leq T,\]
and for any maximal interval $I$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
        \begin{equation}
            |C_\theta(t,t)+C_\theta(s,s)-2C_\theta(t,s)| \leq  K_2|t-s|
\text{ for all } t,s \in I.
        \end{equation}
        \item $R_\theta:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a function satisfying
\[|R_\theta(t,s)| \leq \Phi_{R_\theta}(t-s) \text{ for all } 0 \leq s \leq t
\leq T, \qquad R_\theta(t,s)=0 \text{ for all } s>t,\]
and for any two maximal intervals $I,I'$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
\begin{equation}
|R_\theta(t,s)-R_\theta(t',s')| \leq K_2(|t-t'|+|s-s'|) \text{ for all } t,t'\in
I,~s,s'\in I' \text{ with } s\le t \text{ and } s'\le t'.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{S}_g(T,D)$ be the space of all pairs
$(C_g,R_g)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $C_g:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a symmetric function (not necessarily
positive-semidefinite) satisfying
\[C_g(t,t) \leq \Phi_{C_g}(t) \text{ for all } 0\leq t\leq T,\]
and for any two maximal intervals $I,I'$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
        \begin{equation}
|C_g(t,t)+C_g(s,s)-2C_g(t,s)| \leq K_2K_3|t-s|
\text{ for all } t,s \in I,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
            |C_g(t,s)-C_g(t',s')| \leq K_2K_3(\sqrt{|t-t'|}+\sqrt{|s-s'|})
\text{ for all } t,t' \in I,~s,s' \in I'.
        \end{equation}
      \item $R_g:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a function satisfying
\[|R_g(t,s)| \leq \Phi_{R_g}(t-s) \text{ for all } 0 \leq s \leq t \leq T,
\qquad R_g(t,s)=0 \text{ for all } s>t,\]
and for any two maximal intervals $I,I'$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
\begin{equation}
|R_g(t,s)-R_g(t',s')| \leq K_2K_3(|t-t'|+|s-s'|) \text{ for all } t,t'\in
I,~s,s'\in I' \text{ with } s\le t \text{ and } s'\le t'.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
We denote by $\cS_g^+(T,D) \subset \cS_g(T,D)$
the subset of pairs $(C_g,R_g)$ where $C_g$ is positive-semidefinite.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Both semigroups strongly continuous with the SAME generator including the same domain - two operators that agree on a common core but have different domains can generate different semigroups, which is precisely the non-uniqueness phenomenon for symmetric operators with several self-adjoint extensions."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:06:45.871339+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, semigroup theory","id":"claim_684380ee4334e17df539211dc9360d736e96ca633045262ed3ef27d741f7e789","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let A be the infinitesimal generator of a strongly continuous (C_0) semigroup on a Banach space. Then the semigroup is UNIQUELY determined by A: if (S(t)) and (T(t)) are C_0-semigroups with the same generator then S(t) = T(t) for every t >= 0. Equivalently, the Laplace transform of the semigroup is the resolvent of A, and the resolvent determines the semigroup. The Hille-Yosida theorem says which operators are generators: A is the generator of a contraction semigroup exactly when A is densely defined and closed and every lambda > 0 lies in the resolvent set with ||(lambda I - A)^{-1}|| <= 1/lambda.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Counterexample: sawtooth functions u_k = dist(·, (1/k)Z) for the eikonal equation |u'| = 1 on R","Viscosity stability requires locally uniform convergence of the solutions (convergence of the equations must also be locally uniform)","Half-relaxed limit techniques replace uniform convergence only when combined with semicontinuous envelopes, not with a.e. solutions"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.418309+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: viscosity solution theory","id":"claim_686c4951f47d3257d9394437cec0033cb5f7dec3b6ad9bdad4ce29fab5a2d321","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis in the stability theorem: the approximating functions must be VISCOSITY sub/supersolutions and the convergence must be LOCALLY UNIFORM. Then |u_k'| = 1 at every point of differentiability, 0 ≤ u_k ≤ 1/(2k), so u_k → 0 uniformly, yet the limit u ≡ 0 satisfies |u'| = 0 and solves the eikonal equation nowhere. The u_k are not viscosity solutions of |u'| - 1 = 0 (at each of their convex kinks, on (1/k)Z, the supersolution test with the touching slope p = 0 fails), which is exactly why the stability theorem does not apply. (2) The convergence hypothesis cannot be weakened to pointwise or weak-* convergence. What goes wrong in the a.e. setting is already visible in (1): Du_k = ±1 a.e. while Du_k ⇀ 0 weakly-*, and the nonlinear expression H(Du_k) does not pass to weak limits. For genuine viscosity sub/supersolutions the proof of the stability theorem uses LOCALLY UNIFORM convergence to move maximum points of u_k - φ to a maximum point of u - φ; for a family that is merely locally uniformly bounded the correct substitutes are the half-relaxed limits limsup* u_k and liminf* u_k (Barles-Perthame), which are respectively a subsolution and a supersolution but in general differ from a pointwise limit. (If the u_k are locally equi-Lipschitz, pointwise convergence already forces locally uniform convergence, so the gap between the two modes of convergence bites only in the absence of equicontinuity.) Auditor's check: any passage to the limit in a nonlinear first-order PDE that is justified only by 'u_k → u and each u_k solves the equation a.e.' is invalid.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T14:24:13.477138+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_68724c8134dfcc0ae4992f700876980e044d69d7ce8ec6254ca4f97fecc65d60","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (S, A) be a measurable space and mu a sigma-finite measure on it, the intensity measure. A Poisson point process with intensity mu is a random counting measure N on S (N(A) is a random element of {0, 1, 2, ...} union {infinity} for each A in A, and N is a measure for each outcome) such that (i) for every A with mu(A) < infinity, N(A) has the Poisson distribution with mean mu(A), and (ii) for pairwise disjoint A_1, ..., A_k the counts N(A_1), ..., N(A_k) are independent. Such a process exists for every sigma-finite mu (construct it on each piece of finite measure by throwing a Poisson(mu(A)) number of independent points with law mu restricted to A and normalised, then superpose the pieces). When mu has no atoms the points are almost surely distinct; when mu is a multiple of Lebesgue measure on R^d the process is homogeneous with rate equal to that multiple. Basic calculus: the mapping theorem (the image of a Poisson process under a measurable map is Poisson with the image intensity), superposition (independent Poisson processes add to a Poisson process with the summed intensity), thinning (keeping each point independently with probability p(x) gives a Poisson process with intensity p mu), and Campbell's formula E sum_{x in N} f(x) = integral f d mu.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:48:17.119601+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_68ac634325dda74dbba1388167978eafab5735e68721274d18b971ece0ede23e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 24 (Heisenberg representation facts) of arXiv:2605.27212, '2605.27212'] Let \(\Heis=W\times\Fp\) be the group in \eqref{eq:heis-law}, with
\(\dim W=2m\).  For \(\xi\in W^*\), define
\[
    \chi_\xi(v,z)=\psi(\xi(v)).
\]
The following facts hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=*]
    \item The functions \(\chi_\xi\), \(\xi\in W^*\), are exactly the
    irreducible complex representations of \(\Heis\) on which the center
    \(\{0\}\times\Fp\) acts trivially.
    \item For each \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\), there is an irreducible unitary
    representation \(\rho_\lambda\) of \(\Heis\), of dimension \(p^m\), such
    that
    \[
        \rho_\lambda(0,z)=\psi(\lambda z)I,\qquad z\in\Fp.
    \]
    \item If \(\sigma\) is any irreducible complex representation of \(\Heis\)
    on which the center does not act trivially, then there is a unique
    \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\) such that
    \[
        \sigma(0,z)=\psi(\lambda z)I,\qquad z\in\Fp.
    \]
    For this \(\lambda\), there is a unitary map \(U\) from the representation
    space of \(\sigma\) to that of \(\rho_\lambda\) such that
    \[
        U\sigma(g)U^{-1}=\rho_\lambda(g),\qquad g\in\Heis.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if \(g=(v,z)\), \(g'=(w,t)\), and \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\), then
\begin{equation}
    \rho_\lambda(g)\rho_\lambda(g')
    =
    \psi(\lambda\omega(v,w))\rho_\lambda(g')\rho_\lambda(g).
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.499359+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_68b8e8caeed23137397373bc1467fc091520c09bb87396b9d98dc79655f8f009","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Both hypotheses are used, and each failure has a clean counterexample on the unit disk D. The sequence f_n = (-1)^n B is uniformly bounded by 1 and converges (to 0) at every point of E = {a_k}, a set whose only accumulation point is the boundary point 1, yet f_n diverges at every point where B ≠ 0, for instance at 0. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:40:22.423546+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_68cd1a58bafcaad2601ba840550fd58223bea6538d768d3afc58a6e819bfa975","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def-supercritical-map of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Fix ${\mathbf{c}} \in (1,25)$, let $Q = \sqrt{\frac{{\mathbf{c}}-1}{6}} \in (0,2)$, and let $\bf q$ be a non-generic critical weight sequence of type 2 (Definition~(def-critical of the paper)). 
Also let $k\in\mathbbm N$. 
We inductively define random planar maps $\{\mathfrak M_j\}_{j\in\mathbbm N}$, each of which is equipped with a set of \textbf{holes} $\mathcal H_j \subset \mathcal F \mathfrak M_j$, as follows. 
\begin{itemize}
\item
Let $\mathfrak M_0$ be a Boltzmann map with perimeter $2k$ and weights $\bf q$ (Definition~(def-critical of the paper)) and let $\mathcal H_0$ be the set of faces of $\mathfrak M_0$ other than the external face. 
\item 
Inductively, assume that $j \geq 1$ and $(\mathfrak M_{j-1}, \mathcal H_{j-1})$ has been defined. 
Conditional on $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1})$, let $\{Y_h\}_{h \in \mathcal H_{j-1}}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables with the uniform distribution on $\{-1,1\}$, indexed by the holes $ h\in \mathcal H_{j-1}$. Conditional on $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1}, \{Y_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}})$, for each $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$, sample a ring $R_h$ from the uniform distribution on rings of outer perimeter $\deg(h)$ and inner perimeter\footnote{
The reason for the strange looking quantity $\exp\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( \pm \frac{\pi\sqrt{4-Q^2}}{Q}  \aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$ in~(equation eqn-perimeter-ratio of the paper) is that this quantity coincides with the ratio of the LQG lengths of a CLE$_4$ loop as measured from inside and outside the loop in the coupling of~[ag-supercritical-cle4], see~[ag-supercritical-cle4]. 
}
\begin{equation}  
2 \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor \exp\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( Y_h  \frac{\pi\sqrt{4-Q^2}}{Q}  \aftergroup\egroup\originalright) \frac{\deg(h)}{2} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor  .
\end{equation}  
We take the rings $R_h$ to be conditionally independent given $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1}, \{Y_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}})$. 
For each $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$, we identify the edges of the outer boundary of $R_h$ to the edges of the boundary of $h$ in cyclic order. There are $\deg(h)$ ways to do this identification. We choose one way uniformly at random. 
\item 
Conditional on $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1}, \{R_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}})$, for each $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$ such that $R_h$ has non-zero inner perimeter, we sample a Boltzmann map $M_h$ of perimeter equal to the inner perimeter~(equation eqn-perimeter-ratio of the paper) of $R_h$ (we take the maps $M_h$ to be conditionally independent). We then identify the edges of the boundary of $M_h$ to the edges of the inner boundary of $R_h$ in cyclic order (as above, we choose one of the possible ways to do the identification uniformly at random). 
\item 
We define $\mathfrak M_j$ to be the map which is the union of $\mathfrak M_{j-1}$, $\{R_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}}$, and $\{M_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}}$, subject to the above identifications. We define $\mathcal H_j$ to be the set of faces of $\mathfrak M_j$ which are also faces of $M_h$ for some $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$. 
\item We define $\mathcal M = \mathcal M_k$ to be the planar map which is the increasing union of the maps $\mathfrak M_j$, and call it the \textbf{supercritical random planar map of central charge ${\mathbf{c}}$ and perimeter $2k$}. We define $\mathcal L_k$ to be the collection of simple loops on the dual of $\mathcal M_k$ such that each loop traverses the faces of one of the rings in the above construction (these loops are shown in red in Figure~(fig-model of the paper)). 
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.488292+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_68d7aba1f90aef7637c434f3a188d05f04ac5406fcde6b993830a1f1d44f552f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn rational SLE of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $e^{i\theta} \in \partial\mathbb{D}$ be the growth point, and let $u_1 = e^{i\theta_1}, u_2 = e^{i\theta_2}, \dots, u_k = e^{i\theta_k} \in \overline{\mathbb{D}}$ be marked points. A symmetric double divisor $(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+, \boldsymbol{\sigma}^-)$ assigns a charge distribution on $e^{i\theta}$ and $\{u_1, \dots, u_k\}$, where
\[
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+ = a \cdot e^{i\theta} + \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sigma_j \cdot u_j,
\quad \text{and} \quad
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^- = \overline{\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+}|_{\mathbb{D}},
\]
and the total charge satisfies the neutrality condition $(\mathrm{NC}_b)$.

We define the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ as a random normalized conformal map $g_t(z)$, with initial condition $g_0(z) = z$ and normalization $g_t'(0) = e^{-t}$. It evolves according to the radial Loewner equation:
\[
\partial_t g_t(z) = g_t(z) \frac{e^{i\theta(t)} + g_t(z)}{e^{i\theta(t)} - g_t(z)}, \quad g_0(z) = z.
\]

Let $h_t(z)$ be the covering map of $g_t(z)$, defined via
\[
e^{i h_t(z)} = g_t(e^{i z}),
\]
so that $h_0(z) = z$, and
\[
\partial_t h_t(z) = \cot\left( \frac{h_t(z) - \theta(t)}{2} \right).
\]

The driving function $\theta(t)$ evolves as
\[
d\theta(t) = \frac{\partial \log \mathcal{Z}(\theta)}{\partial \theta} \, dt + \sqrt{\kappa} \, dB_t,
\]
where the Coulomb gas partition function is
\begin{equation} 
\mathcal{Z}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_{j < k} \sin\left( \frac{\theta_j - \theta_k}{2} \right)^{\sigma_j \sigma_k} 
\cdot \prod_j e^{\frac{i}{2} \sigma_j (\sigma_0 - \sigma_\infty)\theta_j}.
\end{equation}

The flow map $g_t$ is well-defined up to the first time $\tau$ when $\zeta(t) = g_t(w)$ for some $w$ in the support of $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$. For any $z \in \mathbb{D}$, the process $t \mapsto g_t(z)$ is defined up to time $\tau_z \wedge \tau$, where $\tau_z$ is the first time such that $g_t(z) = e^{i\theta(t)}$. Define the associated hull by
\[
K_t = \left\{ z \in \overline{\mathbb{D}} : \tau_z \le t \right\}.
\]

Furthermore, the law of the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ Loewner chain is invariant under Möbius transformations $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$, up to a time change, due to the conformal covariance of the Coulomb gas correlation functions. Thus, we define rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ in a general simply connected domain $\Omega$ via a conformal map $\phi: \Omega \to \mathbb{D}$ by pulling back the flow.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:33:17.714907+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_68e56b396d2d832e0a7ad56a0e25e3f3f6a57c6a56f713769de37dca1538f865","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 53 (Finite-state stabilization for fixed-profile dyadic cutoffs) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $m_\Lambda(\xi)=m(\xi/\Lambda)$ be a fixed-profile cutoff from
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-cutoff}, with $\Lambda\in\Dyd$.  Let
$\rho_N$ be supported in an annulus
$\{\kappa_-N\le|\xi|\le\kappa_+N\}$ for $N\ge2$.  There exist integers
$k_-<k_+$, depending only on $(\kappa_-,\kappa_+,c_0,C_0)$, such that
\begin{align*}
 m_\Lambda\rho_N&=0 &&\text{if }\log_2(\Lambda/N)\le k_-,\\
 m_\Lambda\rho_N&=\rho_N &&\text{if }\log_2(\Lambda/N)\ge k_+.
\end{align*}
Consequently the restriction of $m_\Lambda$ to a fixed dyadic shell has only
$k_+-k_-+2$ possible states as $\Lambda$ ranges over the dyadic cutoffs.  The
inhomogeneous unit shell is handled separately and also has only finitely many
states.  More generally, for any fixed number of cutoff factors carried by
arbitrary dyadic shells (not necessarily comparable), their joint restriction
has a scale-independent finite number of states.  This number depends only on
the cutoff profile, the shell support constants, and the number of factors,
not on the ratios of the shell scales.

In particular, if a dyadic random block $X_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}$ depends on
$\Lambda$ only through these cutoff factors and every one of its possible
states satisfies $\|\|X\|\|_{L^p}\le A_{N,Q,M}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd}\|X_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}\|\right\|_{L^p}
 \lesssim_m A_{N,Q,M}.
\end{equation}
For every fixed block, $X_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}$ agrees with its uncut value for
all sufficiently large $\Lambda$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f, g in L^1(R^n) for the basic identity; the dual identity needs f, g in L^2 (or transforms in L^1)","normalisation exp(-2 pi i x . xi); with exp(-i x . xi) the identity acquires the factor (2 pi)^{n/2} or (2 pi)^n depending on the convention"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.479276+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis","id":"claim_68ec73ffb62be77db080fa917d7d7adccc085f8817f70ee4d86c012bfa989123","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For f, g in L^1(R^n) the convolution (f * g)(x) = integral over R^n of f(x - y) g(y) dy is defined for almost every x, belongs to L^1(R^n) with ||f * g||_1 <= ||f||_1 ||g||_1, and its Fourier transform is the product of the transforms: (f * g)^(xi) = f^(xi) g^(xi) for every xi, with f^(xi) = integral f(x) exp(-2 pi i x . xi) dx (with another normalisation of the transform a constant factor appears). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:50:36.760435+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_68f39b1f3f769a3c139b0af96fe8563c1e0d0a73de76220a1f74956d9950ef4d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 56 (Keller--Liverani, \cite{Keller_Liverani}) of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $(X,\|\cdot \|_{X})$ be a Banach space, embedding compactly into the Banach space $(Y,\|\cdot \|_{Y})$, so that furthermore $\|\cdot \|_{Y} \leq \|\cdot \|_{X}$.

A family of bounded linear operators $\{R_{t,s}\}_{(t,s) \in \Delta}$ on $\mathcal{B}_{m}(H)$ is called a $\pi$-continuous evolution family if:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\textit{\roman*})}, leftmargin=*]
    \item \emph{Evolution property.} For all $t \in [0,T]$, $R_{t,t} = I$, and for all $0 \le t \le r \le s \le T$, $R_{t,s} = R_{t,r} \circ R_{r,s}$.
    
    \item \emph{Exponential bound.} There exist $M \ge 1$ and $\omega \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\|R_{t,s}\|_{\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B}_{m}(H))} \le M e^{\omega (s-t)}$, for all $(t,s) \in \Delta.$
    
    \item \emph{$\pi$-continuity.} For any sequence $(f_n) \subset \mathcal{B}_{m}(H)$ and $f \in \mathcal{B}_{m}(H)$ such that $f_n \xrightarrow{\pi} f$, we have $R_{t,s}f_n \xrightarrow[n \to +\infty]{\pi} R_{t,s}f$ for all $(t,s) \in \Delta$.
    
    \item \emph{Temporal continuity.} For any $x \in H$ and $f \in \mathcal{B}_{m}(H)$, the map $(t,s) \mapsto (R_{t,s}f)(x)$ is continuous from $\Delta$ into $\mathbb{R}$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:32:28.996091+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6948d744794c4b75dd9bcd5a67c149ca690264b53e413cd7e3006cd98ba24491","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn smooth of arXiv:2608.25471, 'Exact Hausdorff measures and fine geometry of collisions of independent Markov processes'] [{Smooth measures}] 
  A Borel measure $\nu$ on $M$ is said to be a \textit{smooth measure} if it satisfies the following conditions:
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      $\nu$ charges no semipolar sets, i.e., 
      $\nu(E) = 0$ for any semipolar $E \in \mathcal{B}(M)$;
    \item 
      there exists an increasing sequence $(E_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ of Borel subsets 
      such that $M = \bigcup_{n \geq 1} E_n$, $\nu(E_{n}) < \infty$ for each $n$, 
      $\int_{E_n} r_1(x,y)\, \nu(dy)$ is bounded in $x$ for each $n$,
      and $P_x( \lim_{n \to \infty} \tau_{E_n} \geq \zeta) = 1$ for all $x \in M$,
      where $\tau_{E_n} \coloneqq \inf\{t > 0 \mid X_t \notin E_n\}$.
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:53:31.977852+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6953bdb3511151788c7d105b044fc217b7822a50326dda0fc6f3a84741b1f3f7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 4 (Kernel representation of the limit) of arXiv:2606.11369, 'Mean-field limits for stochastic particle systems on dense graphs'] Assume the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{mainthm}. Then, for every \(t\ge 0\), the first marginal of \(\pi_t\) is a Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]\). Hence there exists a measurable probability kernel
\[
u\mapsto p_t(u,\cdot)\in \mathcal P(\mathbb N_0)
\]
such that
\[
\pi_t(du,\{k\})=p_t(u,k)\,du,
\qquad k\in\mathbb N_0.
\]
In particular,
\[
p_t(u,k)\ge 0,
\qquad
\sum_{k\ge 0}p_t(u,k)=1
\quad\text{for a.e. }u\in[0,1].
\]
Moreover, for all  $u\in [0,1]$, and $ k\in \N_0$, in distributional form,  the family \(p_t\) satisfies the nonlinear master equation: 
\begin{align}

\partial_t p_t(u,k)
&=
p_t(u,k+1)\,\mu_t(u,k+1)
+\mathbf 1_{\{k\ge 1\}}\,p_t(u,k-1)\,\lambda_t(u,k-1)
\nonumber\\
&\quad
- p_t(u,k)\big(\mu_t(u,k)+\lambda_t(u,k)\big),
\end{align}
where the nonlinear loss and gain rates are given by
\begin{align}

\mu_t(u,k)
&:=
\int_0^1 \sum_{\ell\ge0}
W(u,v)c(k,\ell)p_t(v,\ell)\,dv,
\\
\lambda_t(u,k)
&:=
\int_0^1 \sum_{\ell\ge0}
W(v,u)c(\ell,k)p_t(v,\ell)\,dv.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:36:49.819483+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_69581bc07dcd3807aee9a6e3b21a27a717a81f11a0d3509c2c4f64f7c22eb21e","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:weighted-exp-conc of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N$ be independent real-valued random variables, and let $F=F(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N)$ be real-valued and measurable. Let $\xi_i'$ be an independent copy of $\xi_i$, independent of all coordinates, and let $\xi^{(i)}$ be obtained from $\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N)$ by replacing only $\xi_i$ with $\xi_i'$. Assume that, for deterministic numbers $\ell_i\geq0$, not all zero, for every $1\leq i\leq N$,
		\[
			|F(\xi)-F(\xi^{(i)})|\leq \ell_i|\xi_i-\xi_i'|\, .
		\]
		Write
		\[
			\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}\coloneqq\left(\sum_{i=1}^N\ell_i^2\right)^{1/2}\, ,
			\qquad
			\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}\coloneqq\max_{1\leq i\leq N}\ell_i\, .
		\]
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
			\item If $p\geq2$ and $\mathbb{E}|\xi_i|^p<\infty$ for every $i$, then there is
			$C=C(p)$ such that
			\[
				\bigl(\mathbb{E}|F-\mathbb{E} F|^p\bigr)^{1/p}
				\leq
				C
				\left[
				\left(\sum_{i=1}^N \ell_i^2\bigl(\mathbb{E}|\xi_i-\xi_i'|^p\bigr)^{2/p}\right)^{1/2}
				+
				\left(\sum_{i=1}^N \ell_i^p \mathbb{E}|\xi_i-\xi_i'|^p\right)^{1/p}
				\right]\, .
			\]

			\item If the $\xi_i$ are i.i.d.\ and
			$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\xi_1|}\leq K_0$, then there are $c>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending
			only on $\theta_0$ and $K_0$, such that, for all $r\geq0$,
			\[
				\mathbb{P}(|F-\mathbb{E} F|\geq r)
				\leq
				C\exp\left\{
				-c\min\left(
				\frac{r^2}{\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}^2}\, , 
					\frac{r}{\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}}
				\right)
				\right\}\, .
			\]

				\item If the $\xi_i$ are i.i.d.\ with $\mathbb{E}\xi_1=0$ and
				$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\xi_1|}\leq K_0$, then there are $c>0$ and
				$C<\infty$, depending only on $\theta_0$ and $K_0$, such that,
				for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ with
				$|\lambda|\,\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}\leq c$,
				\[
					\log\mathbb{E}\exp\Bigl\{\lambda\sum_{i=1}^N\ell_i\xi_i\Bigr\}
					\leq
					C\lambda^2\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}^2\, .
				\]

			\item Under the assumptions of part~\textup{(b)}, if
				$|\lambda|\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}<\theta_0$, then
				\[
					\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda(F-\mathbb{E} F)}
					\leq
					\exp\{C\lambda^2\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}^2\}\, ,
				\]
				where $C$ depends only on $\theta_0$, $K_0$, and
				$\theta_0-|\lambda|\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.640129+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_695c12159cb1e2d9b1a7fa0c02b83a78756f59fd3de956c4e62f43fefd2d6869","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.00690, 'Boundary behavior and optimal pointwise H\"older exponent of the total local time of $(1+\'] Let $\{K_t : t \in [0,T]\}$ be a c\`adl\`ag stochastic process. Suppose there are constants $a > 1$, $b > 0$, and $C > 0$ such that for all $s,t \in [0,T]$,
	\[
	\mathbb{E}|K_t - K_s|^a \le C |t-s|^{1+b}.
	\]
	Fix $\gamma \in (0, b/a)$. Define
	\[
	\bar\rho_\gamma := \sup\{ r\in[0,T] : \forall s,t \in [0,T],\ |t-s| \leq r \Rightarrow |K_t - K_s| \leq |t-s|^\gamma \},
	\qquad \rho_\gamma:=\frac12\bar\rho_\gamma.
	\]
	Then 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[{\rm(1)}] $|K_t - K_s| \leq |t-s|^\gamma$ whenever $|t-s| \leq\rho_\gamma$,\ $s,t \in [0,T]$;

		\item[{\rm(3)}] for all $0 < h < h_{\gamma}/2$,

		\]
		where $\gamma_0 =(\gamma+b/a)/2$, $h_\gamma= [2^{-\gamma_0}(1 - 2^{-\gamma_0})/3]^{1/(\gamma_0 - \gamma)}$ and 
		\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:49.209792+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_695fcc868d7a5076be43b1232e5cb6b799d6633e78efe5b25e7c91d2ee9bf4e5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2604.27242, 'Statistical Inference for Homogenization Limits Driven by Wiener or Hermite Processes'] For \(m>1\) and \(H^*(m)<1/2\), and any \(1\leq r\leq m-1\), with \(r_I, r_S\) as in \eqref{eq: rI rS def}, the diagonal and off-diagonal contributions in \eqref{eq: second moment of chaos term} satisfy

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:37:25.946469+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_69768534155f77baf6ae5e8e2d46921fb65f121e890884ff0057fee412aa9ca7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 64 (Rank-uniform Newton element) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every zero-framed knot $K$, the series
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr H_K(X,A,q)=
 \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
 B_k(X;A,q)\mathsf H_k(K;A,q)
\end{equation}
converges in $\widehat{\mathscr C}_{A,q}$ and has the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

\begin{equation}
 \mathscr H_K(X_r(A,q),A,q)=\HH_r(K;A,q).
\end{equation}

\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ev}_{n,r,\zeta}(\mathscr H_K)
 =J_r^{SU(n)}(K;\zeta),
\end{equation}

then $X=X_r(q^n,q)$, and finally $q=\zeta$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:44:12.655523+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_697e7a64ccfa0ed18bc39ccd14c972abd69a3f484c97b04cf84cd059acfc9833","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary $n/\log n$ threshold of arXiv:2512.05896, 'T\'oth's buses and the ``detachment process'''] Asymptotic regimes ($n\to\infty$) in terms of \(k(n)\):

 1. super-linear growth (\(k(n)\gg n\), i.e. \(\lambda_n\to 0\))
$R_{n,k}\sim \frac{2}{k}\ \longrightarrow\ 0.$

 2. Linear growth (\(k(n)\sim c\,n\) for some \(c>0\))
\[
R_{n,k}= \frac{e^{1/c}-1+1/c-1/c^2}{n}+\mathcal{O}\!\Big(\frac{1}{n}\Big)
 \longrightarrow\ 0.
\]

 3. Sublinear, but still above threshold (\(\tfrac{n}{\log n}\ll k(n)\ll n\))
Here \(\lambda_n=o(\log n)\) (possibly large but \(o(\log n)\)). Then
$
R_{n,k}\sim \dfrac{1}{k}\ \longrightarrow\ 0.
$

 4. Critical regime (\(k(n)\sim \tfrac{n}{\alpha\log n}\) with fixed \(\alpha>0\))
\[
R_{n,k}\sim n^{\alpha-1},
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\begin{cases}
\alpha<1:& R_{n,k}\to 0,\\[4pt]
\alpha=1:& R_{n,k}\to 1,\\[4pt]
\alpha>1:& R_{n,k}\to\infty.
\end{cases}
\]

 5. Subcritical regime (\(k(n)\ll \tfrac{n}{\log n}\), i.e. \(\lambda_n\gg \log n\)). Then
$
R_{n,k}\sim \dfrac{e^{n/k}}{n}\ \longrightarrow\ \infty.
$

---

In summary,
\[
R_{n,k}\asymp \max\!\left\{\frac{e^{n/k}}{n},\,\frac{1}{k}\right\},
\]
with the phase transition occurring at \(k(n)\sim n/\log n\),
where \(R_{n,k}\) crosses from vanishing  to diverging.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \underline{super-linearly many buses:}  $k(n)\gg n$ (so $\lambda_n\to 0$). Then $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\sim n\to\infty$;
  $\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm{Var}^{(n)}(L^n_k)}{E^{(n)}[L^n_k]^2}\sim \frac{\lambda_n}{n}=\frac{1}{k(n)}\to 0$.

\item \underline{Linearly many buses:} $k(n)\sim c\,n$ with $c\in(0,\infty)$. Then $\lambda_n\to 1/c$, so
  $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\sim n e^{-1/c}\to\infty$ and the ratio $\sim \frac{e^{1/c}-1}{n}\to 0$.
  
\item \underline{Slightly above the threshold:}  $k(n)=\dfrac{n}{(1-\varepsilon)\log n}$ with $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$.
Then $\lambda_n=(1-\varepsilon)\log n$, so $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\asymp n^{\varepsilon}\to\infty$ and the ratio $\to 0$.

\item \underline{Slightly below the threshold:}  $k(n)=\dfrac{n}{(\log n + c)}$ with  $c\in\mathbb R$.
Then $\lambda_n=\log n + c$, so $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\to e^{-c}\in(0,\infty)$ while
$\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm{Var}^{(n)}(L^n_k)}{E^{(n)}[L^n_k]^2}\to e^{c}\ (\neq 0)$; the criterion in Theorem (thm: conc of the paper) fails.
  
\item \underline{Too few buses:}  $k(n)\ll \dfrac{n}{\log n}$ (so $\lambda_n\gg \log n$). Then 
$E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\to 0$ and $\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm{Var}^{(n)}(L^n_k)}{E^{(n)}[L^n_k]^2}\to\infty$; the criterion in Theorem (thm: conc of the paper) fails.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.914114+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_699de2d720ce703b5a31f147c03b08d7c8a592519e8e2bfb7341edc02aad6927","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:geometry of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $\Theta$ be an atomless Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R_+$ such

{"assumptions":["U ⊂ C is open","each f_n is holomorphic on U","f_n → f uniformly on each compact subset of U"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.482149+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_69c713d822544e9382053e6fc38bc15f67607735457acfbc92e7f6a34cad9c3b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let U ⊂ C be open and let f_n be holomorphic on U with f_n → f uniformly on every compact subset of U. Then f is holomorphic on U, and for every k ≥ 1 the derivatives f_n^(k) converge to f^(k) uniformly on every compact subset of U. Quantitatively, if the closed disk of radius 2r about a lies in U and g is holomorphic on U, then sup over |z - a| ≤ r of |g^(k)(z)| ≤ k! r^{-k} sup over |z - a| ≤ 2r of |g(z)|. The same holds for series: a series of holomorphic functions converging locally uniformly may be differentiated term by term any number of times. The convergence of derivatives is locally uniform, not uniform on all of U.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:57:51.747753+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_69d9fc3e08309abe3aa101187617150dbe9f74efd797339ff4780d0660d3c2e3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 11 (Compatibility conditions) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Fix $k\geq1$. Assume $ u_0\in H^{k+1}(\Omega)$, $v_0\in H^k(\Omega)$, 
and
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^\ell u_-
\in
C_{\mathrm b}\bigl((-\infty,0];
H^{k+1-\ell}(\Omega)\bigr),
\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
\end{equation}
Assume also that
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^\ell f
\in
C\bigl([0,T];H^{k-\ell}(\Omega)\bigr),
\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\partial_t^k f\in C([0,T];L^2(\Omega))$. 

We say that $(u_0,v_0,u_-,f)$ satisfies the compatibility conditions of
order $k$ if the following two conditions hold.

(i) The forward jets agree with the corresponding prehistory jets:
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^j u_-(0-,\cdot)=U_j
\quad\text{in }H^{k+1-j}(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\end{equation}

(ii) The forward jets satisfy the Dirichlet boundary condition:
\begin{equation}
U_j\in H^{k+1-j}(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\end{equation}
 
For $0\leq j\leq k$, define the concrete differentiated initial history
by
\begin{equation}
\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}(s,\cdot)
:=
U_j-\partial_t^j u_-(-s,\cdot),
\qquad s\geq0.
\end{equation}
Then \eqref{eq:corner-compatibility} is equivalently
\[
\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}(0,\cdot)=0
\quad\text{in }H^{k+1-j}(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\]
Here $\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}$ denotes the concrete history function. If
$\eta_j^0\in\mathcal M$ denotes the corresponding abstract history
element, no pointwise value $\eta_j^0(0)$ is being asserted.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.453202+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_69e554db51ef16782d5703616d441a55f6f80f897e360de5beb98a41b93822e1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 34 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Suppose $\cX$ is a Banach space, $\cU \subseteq \cX$ is an open set, and $-\infty < a < T < \infty$.
If $f \colon [a,\infty) \times \cU \to \cX$ is locally Lipschitz in space, locally uniformly in time; $c_1,c_2 \in C([a,T];\cX)$; and $y_1,y_2 \in C([a,T];\cU)$ satisfy
\[
y_i(t) = c_i(t) + \int_a^t f(s,y_i(s))\,\d s \qquad (a \leq t \leq T, \; i=1,2),
\]
then
\[
\norm{y_1(t) - y_2(t)}_{\cX} \leq  e^{C(t-a)}\sup_{a \leq s \leq t}\norm{c_1(s) - c_2(s)}_{\cX} \qquad (a \leq t \leq T),
\]
where $C = c_{J,K}$ is as in \eqref{eq.locLip} with $J \coloneqq [a,T]$ and $K \coloneqq y_1([a,T]) \cup y_2([a,T])$.
In particular, if $c_1 \equiv c_2$, then $y_1 \equiv y_2$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["S is a smooth surface immersed in Euclidean R^3","f is a diffeomorphism between surfaces preserving the induced first fundamental form"],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:47:41.428609+00:00","domain":"differential geometry","id":"claim_69e64304021ea782fd02517f107d971b629df1ef9215703937dce80898906eb8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let S be a smooth surface in R^3 with its induced Riemannian metric (first fundamental form), and let K denote its Gaussian curvature (the product of the two principal curvatures). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:55:18.952496+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_69e86a199216bbab14fd2f83acbfc69759619bea38fbd85a8fc3e95cea7b1295","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] There exists a sequence of random $\mathfrak{g}$-valued $1$-forms $(A_N)_{N\geqslant 0}$ on $\mathcal{S}$ such that the following properties hold, where $(\Lambda_N)_{N\geqslant 0}$ is the sequence of Morse lattices from Section~(s:Morselattice of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each $N$, let $(g_e)_{e \in \mathbb{E}_N}$ be a discrete connection on $\Lambda_N$ with law $\mathrm{DS}(\rho,\Lambda_N)$. 
Then the family of loop holonomies of $A_N$ has the same law as the family of loop holonomies of $(g_e)_{e \in \mathbb{E}_N}$, in the sense that
\[
\big(\mathrm{Hol}(A_N,c)\big)_{c \in \mathrm{Loop}_o(\Lambda_N)}
\;\stackrel{\mathrm{law}}{=}\;
\big(\mathrm{Hol}\big((g_e)_{e\in\mathbb{E}_N},c\big)\big)_{c \in \mathrm{Loop}_o(\Lambda_N)}.
\]
\item There exists a random distributional $1$-form $A$ on $\mathcal{S}$ such that
\[
A_N \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{\;\mathrm{law}\;} A
\]
in $\mathcal{D}^{'^2}(\mathcal{S},\mathfrak{g})$, where the test $1$-forms are taken to vanish to all orders on the boundary of $\mathcal{S}$. 
Moreover, the limit $A$ coincides with the random $1$-form constructed in the first part of the article.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Theorem 3.13: if moreover Var(X) = σ², X^s is defined on the same space as X, W = (X − μ)/σ and Z ~ N(0,1), then d_W(W, Z) ≤ (μ/σ²) √(2/π) √(Var(E[X^s − X | X])) + (μ/σ³) E[(X^s − X)²]. Theorem 4.10: if W ≥ 0 is integer valued with E[W] = λ > 0, W^s is a size-bias coupling of W and Z ~ Po(λ), then d_TV(W, Z) ≤ min{1, λ} E|W + 1 − W^s|. Theorem 7.6: if X ≥ 0 with E[X] = μ and 0 < Var(X) = σ² < ∞, and X^s is a size-biased coupling of X with |X − X^s| ≤ C < ∞, then (1) if X^s ≥ X, P((X − μ)/σ ≤ −t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2Cμ/σ²)); (2) if E[e^{θX}] < ∞ for θ = 2/C, then P((X − μ)/σ ≥ t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2(Cμ/σ² + Ct/(2σ)))).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:38:25.214530+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6a257a9d22943842290a3846155fa791afed1689a64d30d1315bca773555e59a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold and let $\delta$ be a simple closed geodesic in $M$. Then $\delta$ lifts to a set of hyperbolic lines $\{\delta_i\}$ in $\mathbb H^3$. For each $i \ne j$, define the \textit{orthocurve} $s_{ij}$ to be the shortest hyperbolic line segment in $\mathbb H^3$ between $\delta_i$ and $\delta_j$. Define the \textit{midplane} $D_{ij}$ to be the hyperbolic plane in $\mathbb H^3$ which meets $s_{ij}$ orthogonally at its midpoint.

By considering the completion $\overline{\mathbb H^3}$ and corresponding boundary $\partial \mathbb H^3$ ($\cong S^2$), we have a curve $\lambda_{ij} = \partial D_{ij}$ which separates the pair of points $\partial \delta_i$ from the pair of points $\partial \delta_j$.
The set of simple closed curves $\{ \lambda_{ij} \mid i \ne j\}$ in $\partial \mathbb H^3$ is known as the \textit{Dirichlet insulator family} associated to the geodesic $\delta$.

We say that a Dirichlet insulator family $\{\lambda_{ij} \mid i \ne j\}$ is \textit{non-coalescable} if there does not exist $i, j_1,j_2,j_3$ such that $\lambda_{ij_1} \cup \lambda_{ij_2} \cup \lambda_{ij_3}$ separates the two points $\partial \delta_i$. See (fig:DIT of the paper) for an example where this condition fails.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["A is self-adjoint","the perturbation is claimed to be small relative to A"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.772201+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, perturbation theory, Schrodinger operators","id":"claim_6a489f3aa69fc8c053255532a89d8dafa488b42e2454afe14d89e8625076239b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypotheses: (i) B is symmetric; (ii) D(A) ⊂ D(B); (iii) ‖Bx‖ ≤ a‖Ax‖ + b‖x‖ on D(A) with a strictly less than 1. What fails. Dropping symmetry: take A self-adjoint unbounded and B = icA with 0 < c < 1. Then D(A) = D(B) and ‖Bx‖ = c‖Ax‖, so the relative bound is c < 1, yet A + B = (1 + ic)A has spectrum (1 + ic)σ(A), which is not contained in ℝ, so A + B is not self-adjoint; it is not even symmetric. Losing the strict inequality: take B = −A (symmetric, relative bound exactly a = 1, b = 0). Then A + B = 0 on D(A), which is symmetric and essentially self-adjoint but not self-adjoint on D(A), since D(A) ≠ H when A is unbounded; the conclusion 'self-adjoint on D(A)' is false at a = 1, and only Wüst's weaker conclusion (essential self-adjointness) survives. Dropping relative boundedness entirely: A = −d²/dx² on H²(ℝ) and B = multiplication by −x⁴ (maximal domain) are both self-adjoint and C_c^∞(ℝ) is a common dense invariant-looking core, but −d²/dx² − x⁴ is not essentially self-adjoint on C_c^∞(ℝ) (it is in the limit circle case at both ±∞, with deficiency indices (2,2)); the sum of two self-adjoint operators is in general neither self-adjoint nor essentially self-adjoint on the intersection of their domains, and that intersection can even be {0}. Also note that the relative bound of the perturbation must be measured against A itself, not against A + B, and that the infimum defining the relative bound need not be attained, so 'a ≤ 1' in a cited inequality is not the same as 'relative bound a < 1'. Audit rule: check symmetry of B, the domain inclusion, and the strict inequality with the constants actually produced by the estimate.","status":"unverified"}

  -\left(\frac{\mathbf{1} \{\ell x+i \geq \ell x'+i'+1\}}{2\pi\i}\int_\Gamma \prod_{m=2\ell x'+2i'+2}^{2\ell x+2i} \phi_m(z)z^{y'-y}\frac{\d z}{z}\right)_{j'+1,j+1}\\

Then
\[
  Z_t(\alpha)
  = \sum_{x_0,\dots,x_t}
     \mu_\alpha(x_0)\prod_{s=0}^{t-1} T_\alpha(x_s,x_{s+1})
  = \langle \mu_\alpha, T_\alpha^t \mathbf{1}\rangle.
\]
If $T_\alpha$ is irreducible and aperiodic (e.g., Perron--Frobenius applies) and $\mu_\alpha \not\equiv 0$ (the weighted initial supports overlap, i.e.\ $Z_0(\alpha) > 0$), then $\lim_{t \to \infty}\frac{1}{t}\log Z_t(\alpha) = \log r(T_\alpha)$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:05:37.777397+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6a7e5e0626f734eea49b6bf89a01baa06d54732174bf37a83e5fc777001559ea","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm: percolation_reference of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $d\ge2$. For $m\ge1$ and $p\in(0,1)$, consider Bernoulli site percolation with parameter $p$ on $\mathbb{T}_m^d$, and let $\mathrm{GC}=\mathrm{GC}(m,p)$ denote its largest open cluster, with ties broken arbitrarily. 
    \begin{itemize} 
    \item[(i)] For every $p > p^{\mathrm{site}}_c(d)$, there exist constants $C=C(d,p)>0$ and $c=c(p)>0$ such that the following holds for all large $m$. Set
    \[
    n(m):=\left\lceil C(\log m)^{1/(d-1)}\right\rceil .
    \]
    Then, with probability at least $1-m^{-1}$, every box of side length $n(m)$ contains at least $c \, n(m)^d$ vertices of $\mathrm{GC}$. Moreover, we can choose $c(p)$ such that $c(p) \rightarrow 1$ as $p \rightarrow 1$.
    \item[(ii)] There exists $p_o(d) \in (0,1)$ such that, for every $p\in(p_o(d),1)$, there exists $\beta=\beta(d)>0$ such that, for every $m\ge1$ and every $U\subseteq\mathbb{T}_m^d$ 
    \[
    \mathbb P_p\bigl(U\cap\mathrm{GC}=\varnothing\bigr)
    \le
    \exp\left(-\beta |U|^{(d-1)/d}\right) + e^{-\beta m} \, .
    \]
    \item[(iii)] For every $p>p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(d)$ and every $\gamma>1$, there exists $C'=C'(d,p)>0$ such that, upon setting
    \[
    r(m):=\left\lceil(\log m)^\gamma\right\rceil ,
    \]
    we have
    \[
    \mathbb P_p\left(
    \mathrm{diam}(\mathrm{GC}\cap B)
    \le C'r(m)
    \ \text{for every box $B$ of side length $r(m)$}
    \right)
    \longrightarrow 1
    \]
    as $m\to\infty$. Here $\mathrm{diam}$ is measured in the intrinsic graph metric of $\mathrm{GC}$ on the full torus $\mathbb{T}_m^d$; thus, connecting paths may leave $B$.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

${\mathcal A}(H)$ be the set of all

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:38:25.215003+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6ad01b1f34e805dc6860e6d8483ed7c05faa65fd65eba0ea2ff8be713d9bb465","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def-standard fibred torus of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let \(a\) and \(b\) coprime integers with $0 \leq b < a$. Define an automorphism \[f_{a,b} \colon D^2 \rightarrow D^2 ; \ z \mapsto e^{2\pi i b/a}z\] which is a rotation of the disc by an angle of \(2\pi b/a\).
Consider the mapping torus $f_{a,b}$.  For each $p\in D^2$ we take $\{p\}\times I$ and identify $\{p\}\times \{0\}$ with $\{f_{a,b}(p)\}\times \{1\}$.
Under this identification the union of intervals
\[
\cup_{k=0}^{a-1}\{(f_{a,b})^k(p)\}\times I
\]
is a simple closed curve in the mapping torus.
This collection of simple closed curves endows the mapping torus of $f_{a,b}$, which is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times D^2$, with a decomposition into disjoint copies of $S^1$.
A \emph{standard fibred torus} is the mapping torus of $f_{a,b}$, together with the induced decomposition into copies of $S^1$, for some \(a\) and \(b\).","status":"unverified"}

## 1. Deterministic finite-horizon lemma
Use a coupling (Z,X) of two population laws, paired training samples z_i,x_i,
and the same n label noises. Write K_ij=H(z_i,z_j)/n and Ktilde_ij=H(x_i,x_j)/n.
Let b(Z)_i=H(Z,z_i)/sqrt(n), btilde(X)_i=H(X,x_i)/sqrt(n).
Assume K,Ktilde are symmetric positive semidefinite and their spectra lie in
[0,2/gamma]. Thus A=I-gamma K and Atilde=I-gamma Ktilde are contractions.
Assume ||Ktilde-K|| <= eps, ||b||_{L2(row Euclidean)} <= B,
||btilde-b||_{L2} <= eps_cross. Set v_0=-y/sqrt(n),
vtilde_0=-ytilde/sqrt(n), with both initial norms <= Y and

Then, for every integer k <= T,

 ||ftilde_k-f_k||_L2 <= gamma k eps_cross Y + gamma B k delta
                         + gamma^2 B eps Y k(k-1)/2.                 (1)

Proof. The noncommuting telescoping identity is
 Atilde^j-A^j=sum_{l=0}^{j-1} Atilde^(j-1-l)(Atilde-A)A^l.
Consequently ||vtilde_j-v_j|| <= delta+gamma j eps Y.
Split btilde vtilde_j-b v_j=(btilde-b)vtilde_j+b(vtilde_j-v_j).
Cauchy-Schwarz on the coupled population and contraction give each summand
at most eps_cross Y+B(delta+gamma j eps Y). Sum j=0,...,k-1.
No commutation, eigengap, or training-only population inference is used.
If ||gtilde-g||_L2 <= delta_g and ||f_k-g||_L2 <= R, the clean risks differ by
at most 2 R E+E^2, where E is the right side of (1) plus delta_g.

{"assumptions":["T is trace class (or positive) for the diagonal sum to be basis-independent","cyclicity tr(AB) = tr(BA) needs one factor trace class and the other bounded, or both Hilbert-Schmidt","Hilbert-Schmidt does not imply trace class"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:46.573399+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator ideals","id":"claim_6b062606a8899853447fad7c25599be3992c8f16f17ceb5224a67851c9805cf3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"The expression sum_i <T e_i, e_i> is basis-independent and deserves the name 'trace' only when T is trace class (or T >= 0, where the sum is basis-independent in [0, infinity]). Two concrete failures. (1) Conditional convergence, basis-dependent value: on l^2 let T = diag((-1)^{n+1}/n) with respect to the standard basis. T is self-adjoint, compact and Hilbert-Schmidt, but not trace class since sum_n 1/n = infinity. In the standard basis sum_n <T e_n, e_n> converges conditionally to log 2, and permuting the orthonormal basis rearranges the series, so by the Riemann rearrangement theorem the 'trace' can be made any real number or made to diverge. (2) An absolutely convergent, even identically zero, diagonal without trace class: let T be the block-diagonal operator on l^2 whose n-th two-by-two block is [[0, 1/n], [1/n, 0]]. Every diagonal entry in the standard basis is 0, so the diagonal sum is 0, yet the singular values are 1/n twice each, so sum s_n = infinity and T is not trace class; the eigenvalues are plus and minus 1/n and no trace can be assigned consistently. Related traps: tr(AB) = tr(BA) requires a hypothesis such as A trace class and B bounded, or A and B both Hilbert-Schmidt. For merely bounded A, B the commutator identity fails: on l^2 with the unilateral shift S, the commutator [S*, S] = I - S S* is the rank-one projection onto the first coordinate, so it is trace class with trace 1, not 0, even though it is a commutator. Finally, 'T is Hilbert-Schmidt' does not imply 'T is trace class': sum s_n^2 < infinity is strictly weaker than sum s_n < infinity, as diag(1, 1/2, 1/3, ...) on l^2 shows.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.815054+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6b0bff57f96de65d028bb9df7fb7ae1c171112ea22f8c1ba31d86264d91448b8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:maximal-rank-saturation of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $k\geq4$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \emph{Structured label saturation.}
There are constants \(0<\alpha_k<\beta_k\) such that, for every sufficiently
large $h$, there is a set
\[
 \mathcal L^{\mathrm{end}}_{h,k}\subseteq
 \Lambda^{\max}_{h,k}\cap[\alpha_kh^{k-1},\beta_kh^{k-1}]
\]
with
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal L^{\mathrm{end}}_{h,k}|
 \geq h^{k-1}
 \exp\!\left(-O_k\!\left(\frac{\log h}{\log\log h}\right)\right).
\end{equation}
Each $n\in\mathcal L^{\mathrm{end}}_{h,k}$ has a primitive representative
$A$ satisfying
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  r_h(A)=k-2,\qquad
  p_i(A)\asymp_k h\quad(1\leq i\leq k-2),\\
  \operatorname{ndiam}(A)\asymp_k\prod_{i=1}^{k-2}p_i(A)\asymp_k h^{k-2}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Its defining ideal is a prime toric almost complete intersection, while its
coordinate ring is arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay of type two, with total
Betti polynomial $(1+2\xi)(1+\xi)^{k-3}$ and graded Betti tower
(equation eq:endpoint-betti-tower of the paper).

\item \emph{One intrinsic rank layer.}
For every sufficiently large $h$ there are
\[
 r^\ast_{h,k}\in\{2,\ldots,k-2\}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \mathcal E_{h,k}\subseteq
 \mathcal L^{\mathrm{end}}_{h,k}\cap\mathcal R^{[r^\ast_{h,k}]}(h,k)
\]
such that every label in $\mathcal E_{h,k}$ retains a representative from
part~\textup{(i)} and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal E_{h,k}|\geq h^{k-1}
 \exp\!\left(-O_k\!\left(\frac{\log h}{\log\log h}\right)\right).
\end{equation}
For fixed $h$, the aggregate realization count
\[
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathcal E}(q)
 =\#\{A\in\tbinom{[q]}k:|hA|\in\mathcal E_{h,k}\}
\]
is an exact quasipolynomial in $q-1$ of degree $k-r^\ast_{h,k}$.  If $A_q$
is uniform in $\binom{[q]}k$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\bigl(|hA_q|\in\mathcal E_{h,k}\bigr)
 =\Theta_{h,k}(q^{-r^\ast_{h,k}})
 \qquad(q\to\infty),
\end{equation}
and, for every $n\in\mathcal E_{h,k}$, the normalized shape locus of $n$
has dimension $k-2-r^\ast_{h,k}$.
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{h\to\infty}
 \frac{\log\max_{2\leq r\leq k-2}|\mathcal R^{[r]}(h,k)|}{\log h}=k-1.
\end{equation}
When $k=4$, necessarily $r^\ast_{h,4}=2$ and
$|\mathcal R^{[2]}(h,4)|=\Theta(h^3)$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:29:28.004217+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6b11b6a70a31e3952df211c69a320ccb096fa9ddc15b31e146ba62a6a04c8489","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 2 (Power-distance specialization) of arXiv:2608.24964, 'Common-Center Geometry and Certified Radial Reconstruction for Energy-Form Full Conformal '] For $\beta\ge1$, the abstract assumptions required for the deterministic geometry are satisfied with $q=0$.  The Fr\'echet objective
\[
F_\beta(t)=\sum_{i=1}^m\|t-y_i\|^\beta
\]
is coercive and therefore attains a global minimum, and each
\[
G_j(t)=\sum_{i\ne j}\|t-y_i\|^\beta
\]
is convex.  Thus
\[
I_j=\{t:G_j(t)\le d_j\},
\qquad
d_j=\sum_{i\ne j}\|y_j-y_i\|^\beta,
\]
all $I_j$ contain any chosen minimizer $c$ of $F_\beta$, and the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:common-center} apply.

For $m=1$,
\[
I_1=\mathbb R^d,
\]
so finite-radius reconstruction is degenerate.  For $m\ge2$, each power-distance comparison set is bounded and has finite radial exits.

Under the conventional distributional energy-score interpretation, define
\[
\mathcal P_\beta
=
\left\{
P:\int\|x\|^\beta\,dP(x)<\infty
\right\}.
\]
On the appropriate finite-moment class, the conventional power-distance energy score is strictly proper for
\[
0<\beta<2.
\]
Hence the overlap between strict propriety and the deterministic star-shaped geometry is
\[
1\le\beta<2.
\]
At $\beta=2$, the score is proper but not strictly proper and its expected score depends only on the forecast mean.  For $\beta>2$, the Euclidean distance-power energy-form score is not proper.

For $d=1$ and $\beta=1$, the score is exactly the fixed-bin empirical-CRPS score used by \citet[Section~8.1]{toccaceli_2026_crps}.  Write the ordered observations as
\[
y_{(1)}\le\cdots\le y_{(m)}
\]
and define the full empirical median set
\[
\mathcal M
=
\arg\min_t F_1(t)
=
\left[
y_{(\lceil m/2\rceil)},
y_{(\lfloor m/2\rfloor+1)}
\right].
\]
Every point of $\mathcal M$ belongs to every comparison region.  In the nontrivial threshold regime $1\le k\le m$, every corresponding FullCP region is therefore a nonempty closed interval containing $\mathcal M$.  For $m\ge2$ this interval is compact, while for $m=1$ it is $\mathbb R$.  In particular, this proves the single-interval property reported for Toccaceli's fixed-bin empirical-CRPS construction and settles the motivating CRPS case of the connectedness question.  The scoring-rule facts and the CRPS/energy representation are classical \citep{gneiting_raftery_2007_scoring}; the interval conclusion follows from the deterministic comparison geometry above and does not by itself extend to proper distributional scoring rules in general.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(S, d) is a metric space with its Borel sigma-algebra","the members of the family are Borel probability measures"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T02:01:13.770398+00:00","domain":"probability, weak convergence of measures, tightness","id":"claim_6b379f9f39b8f899e353d04b96592d438754cd075fffcd3c5f233e7113013891","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $(S, d)$ be a metric space. A family $\\Gamma$ of Borel probability measures on $S$ is tight (uniformly tight) if for every $\\varepsilon > 0$ there is a compact set $K_\\varepsilon \\subset S$ such that $\\mu(S \\setminus K_\\varepsilon) \\le \\varepsilon$ for EVERY $\\mu \\in \\Gamma$ - the same compact set works for all members of the family. A single measure $\\mu$ is tight if $\\{\\mu\\}$ is.\n\nFacts to keep straight. (1) On a Polish space (separable and complete metric space) every single Borel probability measure is tight (Ulam), and a finite family is then tight as well. (2) On a separable metric space that is not complete a single Borel probability measure can fail to be tight: for a set $S \\subset [0,1]$ with Lebesgue outer measure 1 and inner measure 0 (a Bernstein-type set) the trace of Lebesgue measure is a Borel probability measure on $S$ whose compact subsets are all null. (3) In a compact metric space every family is tight (take $K = S$). (4) On $\\mathbb{R}^k$ tightness of $\\Gamma$ means $\\sup_{\\mu \\in \\Gamma} \\mu(\\{|x| > R\\}) \\to 0$ as $R \\to \\infty$, i.e. no mass escapes to infinity uniformly in the family; in $C[0,1]$ tightness is characterised by the Arzelà-Ascoli type conditions (bounded initial values plus a uniform modulus-of-continuity control). (5) Tightness is the hypothesis of Prokhorov's theorem, which turns it into relative compactness in the weak topology.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. summands with zero mean, finite positive variance and finite third absolute moment","C absolute; no numerical value is asserted by this node"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T17:07:35.390398+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6b44f8f2cf7849479e4ac1266f5d003a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1,X_2,... be independent identically distributed real random variables with E[X_1]=0, E[X_1^2]=sigma^2 in (0,infinity), and rho=E|X_1|^3<infinity. For S_n=sum_{i=1}^n X_i and the standard normal distribution function Phi, the Berry-Esseen inequality is sup_{x in R}|P(S_n/(sigma sqrt(n))<=x)-Phi(x)| <= C rho/(sigma^3 sqrt(n)), where C is an absolute constant independent of n and the distribution. The explicit choice C=0.4748 is valid for every n>=1 (Shevtsova, 2011, Theorem 2 and Corollary 1, https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.6554); it is a proven historical upper bound, not an assertion of the exact or currently best constant. If C_opt denotes the infimum of all universally admissible iid constants, Esseen's lower bound gives C_opt >= (3+sqrt(10))/(6 sqrt(2 pi)) > 0.4097, while C_opt <= 0.4748. The order n^{-1/2} is optimal in general: symmetric two-point summands give lattice jumps of this order along a subsequence. For independent, not necessarily identically distributed, centered real summands with finite third absolute moments and V=sum_i E[X_i^2]>0, an absolute constant C_ind gives sup_x|P(sum_i X_i/sqrt(V)<=x)-Phi(x)| <= C_ind sum_i E|X_i|^3/V^{3/2}; no claim that the iid constant 0.4748 applies to this general version is made. The third absolute moment is an essential hypothesis for a bound of this form; finite variance alone gives the iid CLT but not this universal moment-based rate. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:31:47.860408+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_6b7236fbd383918903b04973e544cb8076d237ab81d7c669c598be85ba4f6727","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"The Collatz conjecture is one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics. The conjecture asks whether repeating two simple arithmetic operations will eventually transform every positive integer into 1. It concerns sequences of integers in which each term is obtained from the previous term as follows: if a term is even, the next term is one half of it. If a term is odd, the next term is 3 times the previous term plus 1. The conjecture is that these sequences always reach 1, no matter which positive integer is chosen to start the sequence. The conjecture has been shown to hold for all positive integers up to 2.36×1021, but no general proof has been found.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Finite one-hot task identifiers with positive power-law task weights; independent uniform skill bits.","Fixed task parity functions; first N supplied as basis functions; noiseless target amplitude S>0."],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:24:35.629108+00:00","domain":"Multitask sparse parity and skill emergence","id":"claim_6b8bb2f11abe9145368bad240c2dab04e24a2526e3b98efbfeac8938553e0ab6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Nam-Fonseca-Lee-Mingard-Louis fixed-basis multitask parity model. Fix integers n_s,n_b,m with 1<=m<=n_b, alpha>0 and S>0. The task I in {1,...,n_s} has probabilities p_k=A*k^(-alpha-1), A=(sum_{j=1}^{n_s} j^(-alpha-1))^(-1), and is represented by a one-hot n_s-bit control vector. Independently, X is uniform on {0,1}^{n_b}. For each task choose an m-element subset A_k of skill-bit coordinates and set g_k(i,x)=1_{i=k}*(-1)^(sum_{j in A_k} x_j). Distinct tasks have disjoint task support, so E[g_j(I,X)*g_k(I,X)]=p_k*1_{j=k}; these basis functions are not unit-normalized in the population measure. The noiseless target is f_star(i,x)=S*sum_{k=1}^{n_s} g_k(i,x). For 1<=N<=n_s the source multilinear model fixes the N most frequent skill functions in advance and trains only the 2N real scalars in f(i,x)=sum_{k=1}^N a_k*b_k*g_k(i,x). Its represented skill strengths are R_k=a_k*b_k. Define R_k=E_X[g_k(k,X)*f(k,X)] and conditional MSE L_k=(1/2)*E_X[(S*g_k(k,X)-f(k,X))^2]. For this model L_k=(1/2)*(S-R_k)^2 when k<=N, and L_k=S^2/2 when k>N. In contrast, for an arbitrary predictor f the definition gives L_k=(1/2)*(S^2+E_X[f(k,X)^2]-2*S*R_k), so skill strength alone need not determine skill loss. Population MSE is sum_k p_k*L_k. The skill functions in this exactly solvable model are supplied, rather than learned from examples.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.376193+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6b9d43713bc4bdf1eebb0779f4b9b5aed1f07112b43dafad1d1a9b10dfff6a6f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $S_3\sim 2\Phi(1)-1\approx0.68$, where $\Phi$ is the cumulative distribution function of an $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ random variable.
    \begin{proof}
        Using symmetry and re-indexing, we may rewrite
            \[S_3=2\sum_{i=\frac{n}{2}-m}^{\frac{n}{2}}\frac{\binom{n-1}{i-1}}{2^{n-1}}=2\sum_{k=\frac{n}{2}-m-1}^{\frac{n}{2}-1}\frac{\binom{n-1}{k}}{2^{n-1}}\]
        We check that
        \[\frac{n}{2}-m-1=\frac{n-1}{2}-\left\lceil\frac{\sqrt{n-1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right\rceil-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{n-1}{2}+O(\sqrt{n})\]
        and this is clearly the farthest term from the central binomial coefficient. Lemma $(de Moivre-Laplace of the paper)$ implies that the central limit theorem holds. By a simple algebraic manipulation of the endpoints of the sum, we obtain
        \[S_3\sim 2\,\Phi\left(\frac{2m+1}{\sqrt{n-1}}\right)-2\,\Phi\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n-1}}\right)\]
        \[=2\,\Phi\left(\frac{\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil}{\sqrt{n-1}}\right)-2\,\Phi\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n-1}}\right)\]
        \[\to 2\,\Phi(1)-1\]
        by the continuity of $\Phi$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:48:47.287113+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6bb2c0776e83bb34d3ae44b86b3bbdbcfdc30a6e46dc3ef2a704afc21123ffba","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma law Xt s of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Let $\zeta\in\mathcal P([0,1])$ and let $(X_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ solve the Auffinger--Chen SDE
		\[
		\mathrm{d} X_t=\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,\partial_x \Phi_\zeta(t,X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t+\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\,\mathrm{d} B_t,
		\qquad X_0=0.
		\]
		Fix $0\le s<t\le 1$ and assume that
		\[
		\zeta((s,t))=0,
		\]
		so that $\zeta([0,u])=\zeta([0,s])$ for every $u\in[s,t)$. Set $\alpha:=\zeta([0,s])$.
		Then, conditionally on $X_s=x$, the law of $X_t$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and satisfies
		\[
		\mathrm{Law}(X_t\mid X_s=x)(\mathrm{d} y)\ \propto\
		\exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-x)^2}{2(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}+\alpha\,\Phi_\zeta(t,y)\right)\mathrm{d} y.
		\]
		Equivalently, writing $p^{BM}_{s,t}(x,y)$ for the transition density of the inhomogeneous Brownian motion
		$\mathrm{d} Y_u=\sqrt{\xi''(u)}\,\mathrm{d} W_u$ (so that $\mathrm{Var}(Y_t-Y_s)=\xi'(t)-\xi'(s)$), one has
		\[
		p_{s,t}(x,y)=\frac{e^{\alpha \Phi_\zeta(t,y)}}{e^{\alpha \Phi_\zeta(s,x)}}\,p^{BM}_{s,t}(x,y),
		\qquad
		p^{BM}_{s,t}(x,y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}}
		\exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-x)^2}{2(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}\right).
		\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["a moment bound with a STRICTLY positive exponent to spare (beta > 0)","a complete metric target space","the conclusion is about a modification, not the original process"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:40.782051+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6bc3c6154eb242793c2a5c251a34ca7565adf2b8c40b69ee5551e9af7d6209b4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X_t)_{t in [0,T]} be a stochastic process with values in a complete metric space, and suppose there are constants alpha > 0, beta > 0 and C < infinity with E[ d(X_t, X_s)^alpha ] <= C |t - s|^{1 + beta} for all s, t in [0,T]. Then X admits a MODIFICATION Xtilde - a process with P(X_t = Xtilde_t) = 1 for every fixed t - whose sample paths are almost surely continuous, and indeed almost surely HOLDER continuous of every exponent gamma in (0, beta/alpha). The exponent beta/alpha is the boundary and is generally not attained. Applications: for Brownian motion E|B_t - B_s|^{2m} = c_m |t-s|^m, so taking alpha = 2m and beta = m - 1 gives Holder exponents up to (m-1)/(2m), which approaches 1/2 as m grows - matching the known fact that Brownian paths are Holder of every exponent below 1/2 and of no exponent at or above 1/2. The theorem produces a MODIFICATION, not the original process: the original may have wildly discontinuous paths, and the two agree at each fixed time but not, in general, simultaneously at all times. The strictly positive beta is essential: E|X_t - X_s|^alpha <= C|t-s| with no exponent to spare does not suffice, as the Poisson process shows, where E|N_t - N_s| = |t - s| exactly and the paths are genuinely discontinuous. The d-dimensional time-parameter version holds with 1 + beta replaced by d + beta. [Kolmogorov, published by Slutsky and by Chentsov; see Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Theorem I.2.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.649879+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6bf12581a2707be998f637d3709babc3528d8727bcb291609030049e5a8e5833","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2 of arXiv:2607.24170, '\large\bf ON NON-MONOTONICITY OF LOGARITHMIC ENERGY\\ FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:19:56.654736+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6bffcc9e21183b3bbb9035e35d2beba6468cc674195a4547bb86ffd94e304756","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] A vector field $H : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to have 
\emph{locally bounded directional variation} if, for every 
$(t_0,x_0) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $\delta>0$ and a constant $C>0$
such that
\[
\sum_{i=1}^N 
\bigl| H(t_i,x_i) - H(t_{i-1},x_{i-1}) \bigr|
\;\le\; C
\]
for every finite sequence $(t_i,x_i)$, $i=0,\ldots,N$, satisfying
\[
(t_0,x_0) \prec (t_1,x_1) \prec \cdots \prec (t_N,x_N),
\qquad t_N < t_0 + \delta .
\]
Here $\prec$ denotes the partial order on $\mathbb{R}^2$ induced by the cone
\begin{equation}
    \Gamma_M := \{ (t,x) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| \le M t\}, 
\end{equation}
namely
\begin{align}
(t,x) \prec (t',x')
\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
|x - x'| \le M (t - t') .
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:51:12.745299+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6c1fffda741a77159f27c71f87a70a85479cd1f363dddc958a7d69ddde43e5d5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 (Cylinders and configurations) of arXiv:2605.02499, '2605.02499'] A cylinder $C$ is a set of the form
\[
C = C_I = \underset{i \in I}{\bigtimes} C_i
\]
for some $I \subseteq \Nb$, such that, for all $i \in I$, we have $C_i \in \{R, B, \ast, \varnothing\}$. We imply that $C_I=\varnothing$ if $C_i=\varnothing$ for some $i\in I$. 
If $C_i \in \{R, \ast\}$ for all $i \in I$, we speak of an \emph{$R$-cylinder}. We write $R_I$ for the cylinder $\bigtimes_{i\in I} R\in \varSigma_I^R$, where $\varSigma_I^R$ denotes the set of $R$-cylinders with index set $I$. Similarly, let $\varSigma_I$ be the set of all cylinders with index set $I$, and
\[
\varSigma = \bigcup_{I \subseteq [N]} \varSigma_I
\]
the collection of all cylinders with index set contained in $[N]$; $\varSigma^R$ is defined analogously. For $C \in \varSigma^R$ and $T \in \{R, B, \ast\}$, define $n_T(C) \coloneqq \bigl|\{\, i \in I : C_i = T \,\}\bigr|$, and note that $n_R(C) + n_B(C) + n_\ast(C) = |I|$.

Elements $c_I \in C_I \in \varSigma_I$ are called \emph{configurations}. For $\zeta\in\{\mathrm{r},\mathrm{b}\}$, we define $n_\zeta(c_I) = \lvert \{ i \in I : c_i = \zeta \}\rvert$, and note that $n_\mathrm{r}(c_I) + n_\mathrm{b}(c_I) = |I|$.

When the index set $I$ is clear from the context, we write $C$ and $c$ instead of $C_I$ and $c_I$, respectively. Moreover, in our examples we will usually write $R*BB*$ instead of $R \times * \times B \times B \times *$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.061269+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6c496ee61efec6ccd94989fbfe47f2afc03dc2e64dbebc70d25a4225838caecc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $K$ be symmetric positive definite, let $\sigma>0$, and let
$Q:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and nonconstant.  Define
\[
    A_T=\int_0^T \de s \, Q(X_s)
\]
for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
\[
    \de X_t=-KX_t\,\de t+\sigma\,\de B_t,
    \qquad X_0=x.
\]
Let $\lambda(\beta)$ and $\psi_\beta$ be the lowest eigenvalue and
normalized positive ground state of
\[
    K_\beta=-L_K+\beta Q
    \qquad\text{on }L^2(\mu_K).
\]
For $\theta\in\Theta_Q^{\mathrm{OU}}
       =\lambda'((0,\infty))$ and $\lambda'(\beta_\theta)=\theta$,
put $v_\theta=-\lambda''(\beta_\theta)>0$ as well as 
\[
    I_Q^{\mathrm{OU}}(\theta)
       =\lambda(\beta_\theta)-\beta_\theta\theta.
\]
Then, for every fixed $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
    \bbP_x^{\mathrm{OU}}(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim
    \frac{
      \psi_{\beta_\theta}(x)
      \langle\psi_{\beta_\theta},\mathbf 1\rangle_{L^2(\mu_K)}
    }{
      \beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}
    }
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_Q^{\mathrm{OU}}(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\]
The asymptotic is locally uniform in $(x,z)$.

Moreover, on every fixed time interval, the conditioned process converges
in total variation to the ground-state diffusion
\[
    \de Y_t
      =
      \left[
        -KY_t+\sigma^2\nabla\log
        \psi_{\beta_\theta}(Y_t)
      \right]\de t
      +\sigma\,\de B_t,
    \qquad Y_0=x.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.975304+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_6c50eee3d3aaaa3e7e8670b9ac4a1cadf500f1c68a3c070a57f95e583076bf96","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 42 (Independent failure mechanisms) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Each part of the architecture has an independent role.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item Without filteredness, an algebraic order-one vector may be sent to
      singular values $N^{-1/2}$, so no finite critical upper grade exists.
\item With filteredness but proper kernel support, every nonzero probe in the
      annihilator of that support is invisible at the correct grade.
\item A full-support kernel may carry an oscillatory boundary representative;
      valuation equality then holds without an asymptotic equivalent.
\item If the grade-one boundary class is nilpotent under tensor product, one
      grade-one certificate cannot propagate to every depth.
\item If labels are discarded, equal singular-value profiles can represent
      distinct coefficient directions, so annihilator reconstruction fails.
\item A universal coefficient-pure kernel says nothing about an unrelated raw
      observable until its native readers are shown to push forward that
      kernel with full support.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}
