{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:28:04.863521+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7340ae7e09cc7bc41fbcbaab47349c12002b615c0c6ecec7bf43c185eba6c4ca","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 25 of arXiv:2511.22156, ''] There is a Feller process $((X_t)_{t>0},(P^x)_{x\in \tilde{F}})$ on $\tilde{F}$ such that there exists a transition density $p_t(x,y)$ satisfying the two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimate 
	\begin{equation}
	\begin{split} 
		C_1\frac{1}{\mu(B(x,t^{1/\beta}))}\exp(-C_2(\frac{|x-y|^{\beta}}{t})^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}})&\leq p_t(x,y)\\&\leq C_3\frac{1}{\mu(B(x,t^{1/\beta}))}\exp(-C_4(\frac{|x-y|^{\beta}}{t})^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}})
	\end{split} 
	\end{equation}
	for $x,y\in\tilde{F}$ and $t>0$. Here, $C_1$--$C_4$ are the same constants in \eqref{e:6.6}. 
	\begin{proof}
		The proof is essentially the same as the construction of Barlow and Bass \cite{barlow1989construction,BB19993d}. We briefly review the key steps here.
		
		First, by \eqref{e:6.4} and the same proof of \cite[Proposition 5.5(c)]{BB19993d},  
		\[
		P_n^x(\sup_{0<s<t}|X^{(n)}_t-x|\geq r)\leq C_7\exp(-C_8(\frac{r^{\beta}}{t})^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}})\quad\hbox{ for } x\in\tilde{F}_n\hbox{ and }r\geq3^{-n},
		\]
for some constants $C_7,C_8>0$, and hence the law of $P_n^{x_n},n\geq1$ is tight for a bounded sequence $x_n\in\tilde{F}_n$ by the Aldous criterion for tightness  (see \cite[Theorem 16.10 and 16.11]{Kallenberg} for example). 
		
		Next, by the elliptic Harnack inequality (Theorem \ref{theorem4.1}), the mean exit time estimate \eqref{e:6.7} and the same proof of \cite[Section 3.1]{BBKT}, we have 
		$U_\lambda^{(n)}f\hbox{ is equicontinuous for }f\in C_c(\tilde{F}_n)$,
		where $U_\lambda^{(n)}$ is the resolvent operator associated with $X^{(n)}$, i.e. 
		\[
		U_\lambda^{(n)}f(x)=E_n^x[\int_0^{\infty}e^{-\lambda t}f(X_t^{(n)})dt].
		\]
		Hence, by a diagonal argument, there is a subsequence $n_k$ so that $U_\lambda^{(n_k)}f$ converges uniformly on $\tilde{F}$ for every $f\in C_c(\tilde{F}_0)$. 
		
		Finally, by the same argument of \cite[Section 6]{barlow1989construction}, there is a $\mu$-symmetric Feller process $X$ on $\tilde{F}$ such that $P^{x_k}_{n_k}((X^{(n_k)}_t)_{t\geq 0}\in \bullet)$ weakly converges to $P^x((X_t)_{t\geq 0}\in \bullet)$ for every $x_k\in \tilde{F}_{n_k}$ and $x\in\tilde{F}$ such that $x_k\to x$. The transition density estimate \eqref{e:6.22}  follows from \eqref{e:6.11} by taking the limit. \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:05.000396+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_738cfc8aa6ab5b93d8e8181f8ce619206429acced9282fb715310ad956efd297","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 94 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(\Omega,\AA,\PP)$ be a probability space, $\BB$ be a sub-$\sigma$-field of $\AA$ and $f\in \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP[ f^+]\land \PP [f^-]<\infty$. The conditional expectation enjoys the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
			\item (Stability.) If $f\in \BB/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$, then $\PP[ f\vert \BB]=f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\item (Law of total expectation/tower property.) $\PP[\PP[f\vert \BB]]=\PP[ f]$.
			\item Let $\CC$ be another sub-$\sigma$-field of $\AA$.
			
			\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
				\item  (Repeated conditioning/tower property (bis).) If $\BB$ and $\CC$ are comparable with respect to inclusion, then $ \PP_\BB\PP_\CC f=\PP_{\BB\cap\CC}f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
				\item  (Irrelevance of trivial events.) If $\BB\lor \PP^{-1}(\{0,1\})=\CC\lor \PP^{-1}(\{0,1\})$, then $\PP_\BB f=\PP_\CC f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\end{enumerate}
			\item  (Irrelevance of negligible events.)  If  also $g\in  \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$  with $f=g$ a.s.-$\PP$, then $\PP g^-\land \PP g^+<\infty$ and $\PP_\BB f=\PP_\BB g$ a.s.-$\PP$. 
			\item (Conditioning w.r.t. a trivial $\sigma$-field.) If $\BB\subset \PP^{-1}(\{0,1\})$, then  $\PP$-a.s. $\PP_\BB f=\PP f$. In particular $\PP_{\{\emptyset,\Omega\}} f=\PP f$.
			\item (Additivity.) If also $g\in  \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $\PP f^-\lor \PP g^-<\infty$, then $\PP_\BB(f+g)=\PP_\BB f+\PP_\BB g$ a.s.-$\PP$. 
			\item (Sufficient condition for defining property.) Assume $\PP\vert f\vert<\infty$. Let also $g\in \mathcal{B}/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$, $\PP\vert g\vert< \infty$. In order that $\PP_\BB f=g$ a.s.-$\PP$ it is sufficient that $\PP[f;B]=\PP[g;B]$ for all $B\in \Pi\cup \{\Omega\}$, where $\Pi\subset 2^\Omega$ is some $\pi$-system  with $\sigma_\Omega(\Pi)=\BB$.
			\item (Defining property extended.) For $h\in \BB/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP(hf)^+\land \PP(hf)^-<\infty$ one has $\PP(h\PP_\BB f)^+\land \PP(h\PP_\BB f)^-<\infty$ and $\PP[hf]=\PP[h\PP_\BB f]$. 
			\item (Conditional determinism/``taking out what is known''. Homogeneity.) If $g\in \BB/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP (fg)^+\land \PP (fg)^-<\infty$, then $\PP_\BB(gf)=g\PP_\BB f$ a.s.-$\PP$. In particular if $c\in \mathbb{R}$, then $\PP_\BB(cf)=c\PP_\BB f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\item  (Monotonicity.) If also $g\in \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP g^-\land \PP g^+<\infty$ and if $f\leq g$ a.s.-$\PP$ (remember: the latter is equivalent to $\PP[f;B]\leq \PP[g;B]$ for every $B\in \AA$), then $\PP_\BB f\leq \PP_\BB g$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\item (Triangle inequality.) $\vert \PP_\BB f\vert\leq \PP_\BB\vert f\vert$ a.s.-$\PP$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:33:06.561696+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73b882c425523866250a75884430f40e37c5bd3d993ed81a7966323040759410","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 31 (\cite{RT}) of arXiv:2608.26068, 'All once-extended 3D TQFTs are Reshetikhin--Turaev theories'] Let $M$ be a closed connected 3-manifold and $\Gamma$ a labelled embedded ribbon graph in $M$ with ribbon-colouring $K$ and vertex labels $\set{f_v}$. The invariant $\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) \in k$ is defined as follows: 

    Let $L$ be a framed link in $S^3$ (viewed as an embedded $S^1\times I$) with $\# L$ components, and $(\Gamma,K,\set{f_v})$ a labelled embedded ribbon graph in $S^3$ such that performing surgery on $L$ yields the pair $(M,|\Gamma|)$. Then, we have an embedding of $|\Gamma\cup L|$ in $S^3$; call this a \emph{surgery presentation} of the pair $(M,|\Gamma|)$. $\Gamma\cup L$ is now a labelled ribbon graph with some uncoloured loops. Additionally, let $X_L$ be the trace of the framed link $L$ (the 4-manifold with boundary $M$ given by attaching 2-handles to $D^4$ along the framed link $L$). Define $\sigma(X_L)$ to be the signature of $X_L$.

    The invariant on the labelled embedded ribbon graph $\Gamma$ is a scalar multiple of the operator invariant of $\Gamma\cup L$: $$\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) := p_-^{\sigma(X_L)}\sqrt{D}^{-\sigma(X_L)-\# L-1} F(\Gamma \cup L,K,\set{f_v}).$$

    In general, if $M$ is not connected, say $(M,\Gamma) = \bigsqcup (M_i,\Gamma_i)$ where each $M_i$ is connected, then we define $$\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) := \prod\tau(M_i,\Gamma_i,K|_{\Gamma_i},\set{f_v})$$ to be the product of $\tau$ over all the components.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T05:37:56.959283+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73bc069b75844adba49e89625e6b0eb1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] For any $\\sigma\\geq 0$, and $0<a<b\\leq 1$, let us define the analytic function $\\begin{split}Z(\\cdot,\\sigma:a,b):z\\in D_{\\sigma}(a,b)\\mapsto Z(z,\\sigma:a,b):=\\frac{1}{\\sigma+f(0)+(1-z)f(0)(1/a-1/b)}\\in\\mathbb{C}\\end{split}$ on the open disc $D_{\\sigma}(a,b)$ of radius $R_{\\sigma}(a,b)$, where $\\begin{split}R_{\\sigma}(a,b)=1+\\cfrac{\\sigma+f(0)}{f(0)(1/a-1/b)}>1\\.\\end{split}$ Then for any $z\\in D_{\\sigma}(a,b)$ we have $\\begin{split}\\lim_{\\varepsilon\\to 0}Z^{\\varepsilon}(z,\\sigma:a,b)=Z(z,\\sigma:a,b)\\.\\end{split}$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.009931+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73bcb31239d41e9890cd7900fe624ca644493718e01d1a221369e09347e39dd3","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For every field $\kk$, the class $\RV$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item It is invariant under permutations of variables and nonnegative
rational linear substitutions, including coordinate restriction.
\item It is closed under products.
\item If $f\in\RV$, then every ordinary coordinate derivative
$\partial_x^\gamma f$ lies in $\RV$.
\item It is closed under coordinatewise lower and upper truncations in the
divided-power basis.
\item It is invariant under common divided-power translations:
\[
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha]}\in\RV
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha+\gamma]}\in\RV.
\]
\item If $f\in\RV$, then its factorial normalization $\Nrm(f)$ lies in
$\RV$.
\item If $F_1,F_2$ have realizable factorial normalizations, then
$\Nrm(F_1F_2)$ lies in $\RV$.
\item Full polarization preserves $\RV$.
\item Membership is invariant under arbitrary field extension; for
polynomials with rational coefficients, it depends only on
$\operatorname{char}(\kk)$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:52:08.667563+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73d0c639faad0d6c7c76fd8740caf43e4cd9f3f12e44e8145caac13ef1aab777","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 17 (Fiber-equivalent torus fibrations) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let
\[
        \pi_i:M\to S^1_i,\qquad i=0,1,
\]
be torus fibrations.  The target circles are not part of the fixed data and may
be different.  Choose a basepoint \(x\in M\) and, for each \(i=0,1\), an identification
\(\pi_1(S_i^1,\pi_i(x))\cong\ZZ\), and let
\[
        \alpha_{\pi_i,x}:\pi_1(M,x)\longrightarrow\ZZ,
\]
be the surjective homomorphism induced by \(\pi_i\).  Changing the
identification changes \(\alpha_{\pi_i,x}\) by a sign.  Equivalently, \(\pi_i\)
determines a cohomology class \([\pi_i]\in H^1(M;\ZZ)\), well-defined up to
sign.  We say that \(\pi_0\) and \(\pi_1\) are \emph{fiber-equivalent}
if
\[
        [\pi_0]=\pm[\pi_1]\in H^1(M;\ZZ).
\]
Equivalently, after choosing a common basepoint,
\[
        \ker\alpha_{\pi_0,x}=\ker\alpha_{\pi_1,x}\subset\pi_1(M,x).
\]
For a different basepoint, the two kernels are changed by the same conjugacy
convention.  Thus, in fiber-subgroup language, the definition says that the
images of the two fiber fundamental groups agree, up to this usual conjugacy
ambiguity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:52:32.333525+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73dae7c82e3536519c8a11b3ae2635d83a67548ef32c88f01ca5fad7ab347c06","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:allHspaces of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] Let $\Gamma$ be a relatively open subset of the boundary $\partial \Omega$ of some bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We define the following subspaces of $L^2(\Omega)$.
    \begin{align*}
    H^1_0(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^1_\Gamma(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_0(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}_N(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_\Gamma(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}_N(f) = 0\},\\
        H^\Delta(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\
         H^\Delta_0(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_0(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\
          H^\Delta_\Gamma(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_\Gamma(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\}.
    \end{align*}
    The first two spaces are equipped with the usual $H^1$-norm, the third and fourth with the usual $H^{\operatorname{div}}$-norm,
    and the latter three spaces with the norm $$
        \|f\|_{H^\Delta(\Omega)}^2  \coloneq  \|f\|^2_{H^1(\Omega)}+ \|\Delta f\|^2_{L^2(\Omega)}
    $$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:29:27.974863+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73df224c7228c7f38adaaaa206c96a9e358b193ee131f6e7953c2dd48eb0f4bb","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 14 (Localized complexity of bounded isotonic calibration) of arXiv:2608.24858, 'Bellman Calibration for Marginalized Importance Weighting in Offline Reinforcement Learnin'] Let \(0<\tau\le M\), and let
\[
  \overline{\mathcal W}_N
  =
  \{u=\theta\circ\widehat w_\pi:
    \theta\text{ nondecreasing},\
    \tau\le u\le M\}.
\]
Define
\[
  \mathcal H_N=\{\log u:u\in\overline{\mathcal W}_N\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal H_N^\circ
  =
  \{h-\mathbb E_{\nu}h:h\in\mathcal H_N\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal H_{N,\Delta}
  =
  \{h_1-h_2:h_1,h_2\in\mathcal H_N^\circ\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal W_N^{\rm norm}
  =
  \left\{
    \frac{u}{\mathbb E_{\nu}u}:u\in\overline{\mathcal W}_N
  \right\}.
\]
For \(Q_{\nu,\Delta}\) and \(Q_{\nu,\pi}\) as in
\eqref{eq:calibration-critical-radius}, define
\[
  \mathcal G_{N,\times}
  =
  \{(x,x^+)\mapsto \omega(x)b(x^+):
    \omega\in\mathcal W_N^{\rm norm},\ b\in\mathcal H_{N,\Delta}\}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\tau,M}<\infty\) such that, for every \(r>0\),
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal R_N(\mathcal H_{N,\Delta},r;P)
  &\le
  C_{\tau,M}
  \left\{\sqrt{\frac{r}{N}}+\frac{1}{Nr}\right\},
  \qquad P\in\{\nu,\mu_{0,\pi}\},\\
  \mathcal R_N(\mathcal G_{N,\times},r;Q)
  &\le
  C_{\tau,M}
  \left\{\sqrt{\frac{r}{N}}+\frac{1}{Nr}\right\},
  \qquad Q\in\{Q_{\nu,\Delta},Q_{\nu,\pi}\}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Consequently, the corresponding critical radius satisfies
\[
  \mathfrak r_{N,\rm fit}
  \le
  C_{\tau,M}N^{-1/3}.
\]
Moreover, one may take
\[
  C_{\tau,M}
  \le
  C\{1+M/\tau\}^{4}
\]
for a universal finite \(C\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(X,B,mu) is a probability space and T preserves mu (invertibility is not needed)","P and Q are countable measurable partitions","H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity","entropies are taken with a fixed logarithm base throughout"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090248+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, entropy","id":"claim_73e397e27849e65c29b0ad85dd4fc2d78bd89a46e9ea1748bcc9855a192424af","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let T be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space (X, B, mu) and let P and Q be countable measurable partitions with H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity. Write P_n for the join of T^{-i}P over 0 <= i <= n-1 and h_mu(T,P) = lim_n (1/n) H_mu(P_n) (the limit exists by subadditivity and equals the infimum over n). Then h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P) + H_mu(Q | P). Two standard consequences: if P refines Q then H_mu(Q | P) = 0 and hence h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P), so the partition entropy is monotone under refinement; and |h_mu(T,P) - h_mu(T,Q)| <= H_mu(P | Q) + H_mu(Q | P), i.e. the map P -> h_mu(T,P) is 1-Lipschitz for the Rokhlin metric. WHERE IT FAILS: finiteness of H_mu(P) and H_mu(Q) is used - with infinite-entropy partitions both sides can be infinite and the inequality carries no information. The inequality is one-sided: nothing bounds h_mu(T,P) from below in terms of h_mu(T,Q) unless the conditional entropy in the other direction is also controlled. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:19:42.577408+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7405fcfc60ba2e2b510f49b725ba23ec3d1ae5ec2bd38cd0f3790d4437a8427b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 1 of arXiv:2609.03512, ''] Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$, and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ be a vector of positive integers. The \emph{blow-up} $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by replacing each vertex $v_i$ with an independent set
\[
V_i = \{v_i^1,\ldots,v_i^{m_i}\}
\]
of $m_i$ vertices, and joining $v_i^s$ to $v_j^t$ if and only if $v_iv_j\in E(G)$. We call $V_i$ the \emph{part of $G\bigodot m$ corresponding to $v_i$}, and say that $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplication of vertices} (Golumbic \cite{Graph-multiplication-Golumbic}, p.~53).

If $m_j=1$ for all $j\ne i$, we say $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplying the single vertex $v_i$}; if moreover $m_i=2$, this is called \emph{duplicating} $v_i$ (Henning and Southey \cite{Henning-Michael}). If $G$ has a vertex of degree $2$, \emph{degree-$2$ vertex duplication} denotes the operation of duplicating any such vertex.

For graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_k$, we write $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$ for the family of all graphs obtainable from some $G_\ell$ by multiplication of vertices. Since $G\bigodot(1,\ldots,1)=G$, each $G_\ell$ itself belongs to $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.808109+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_743cf06b65abbce3837731c48aedf308156ff722d986e3dbe43f324ccbc4041f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm FirstPresentation of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathcal{Q} $ be an acyclic quiver with $ N $ vertices such that the vertices $ 1, \ldots, n $ are mutable 
	and $ n+1, \ldots, N $ are frozen.  
	Let $ K $ be a field
	and let $ \boldsymbol{x} = (x_1, \ldots, x_N ) $ be an $ N $-tuple of elements that are algebraically independent over $ K $.
	The cluster algebra $ \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{Q}) \subset K(\boldsymbol{x}) =  K(x_1, \ldots, x_n, \ldots, x_N) $ (defined over $ K $) corresponding to $ \mathcal{Q} $ is isomorphic to
	
	\begin{equation}
		 
		K[x_{n+1}^{\pm 1}, \ldots, x_{N}^{\pm 1}][x_1, \ldots, x_n, x_1', \ldots, x_n']
		/ \langle x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \} \rangle 
	\end{equation}
	where $ (x_1', \ldots, x_n') $ is another tuple of algebraically independent elements over $ K $, 
	the products range over those vertices $ i $ of $ \mathcal{Q} $ for which there is an arrow $ i \rightarrow k $ (resp.~$ i \leftarrow k $),
	and
	$ b_{ik} \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $ is the number of arrows $ i \rightarrow k $ which is negative if there are arrows $ i \leftarrow k $. 
	\\
	Moreover, 
	$ (x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \}) $ 
	is a Gr\"obner basis for the ideal which it generates with respect to any term order
	giving preference to $ x_1', \ldots, x_n' $ over $ \boldsymbol{x} $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:01:01.827867+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_743d5d91ec5fa0d1bc263db5a121c45eb8eb88690abe3f623f6e6499dcabf8b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:CGO-PhS_int-by-parts of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] [zbMATH07801151]\sl 
Consider $F \in L^2(\Sigma)$ such that 
there exists $c > 0$ so that $e^{c|\mathrm{x}|} F \in L^2(\Sigma)$.
Let $u \in C([0,T]; L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ satisfy the conditions

\[
\left\{

		\begin{aligned}
		& (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u = F & & \textnormal{in} \enspace \Sigma, \\
		& u(0, \centerdot) = u(T, \centerdot) = 0 &  & \textnormal{in} \enspace \mathbb{R}^n.
		\end{aligned}

	\right.
\]

For every $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$,
consider a measurable function 
$v^\nu : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ such that

\[ \sup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} \big[ 2^{-|\alpha|/2} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} \big] + \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} 2^{|\alpha| \theta} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} < \infty, \]
for some $\theta \in (0, 1/2)$. Then,

\[\int_\Sigma (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u \overline{v^\nu} = \int_\Sigma u \overline{(i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta)v^\nu} \, \]
for all $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:35:05.847715+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_743d8ab82a44d95452e5859b4d8664f0515c640850c73fc24487dec1d16c4265","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:cheeger-M of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Let $A\subset S$ with $\pi(A)\le 1/2$ be a set achieving the Cheeger
constant~$h_P$, and assume $h_P \le 1 - \pi(A)$ (at equality the bound
below has zero numerator; see Remark~(rmk:cheeger-balanced of the paper)).
Then there exists $x^*\in A$ with $P(x^*,A)\ge 1-h_P$, and
\[
  M
  \;\ge\;
  r(x^*)
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{(1-h_P)\log\dfrac{1-h_P}{\pi(A)}
  +h_P\log\dfrac{h_P}{1-\pi(A)}}{\log\!\bigl(1/\pi(x^*)\bigr)}.
\]
The term involving $h_P$ is interpreted by continuity as $0$ when $h_P=0$.
In particular, for small $h_P$,
$M \gtrsim \log(1/\pi(A))/\log(1/\pi_{\min})$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.339073+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_745e5681f8b0886f342dc96352830c0936cd6c44a07fdad151e955aaaba841b8","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 16 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (Two-blocks estimate,
cf.\ Lemma 5.6 of \cite{BFS})
Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$ 
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists 
a constant $C = C(u_0,\ell_0)$ such that, for $\ell \geq  \ell_0$,  and 
a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x)\\
& \hskip 20mm \times\Big\{
E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm  \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2}\ell^{p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times \Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^p \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1N \sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:30.017980+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7463beeea5e6e439db51790c99eaf33807214ea361def5c7eb7baa2ed41e5398","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Let $\{\mu_n, \mu\} \subset {\cal D}$ and let $\{A^n, A\}$ be the corresponding PCAFs.
Assume that $d_{\cal D}(\mu_n, \mu) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the following assertions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm (1)] For any compact set $K \subset E$, there exists a subsequence $\{n_k\}$ such that the PCAFs $A^{n_k}$ converge to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to $K$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$. That is,
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} \left| \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA^{n_k}_u - \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA_u \right| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E.
$$

\item[\rm (2)] Suppose there exists a compact nest $\{F_\ell\}$ satisfying the following tail estimate:
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \sup_{\nu \in {\cal S}_{c,00}^1} \left\{ \left( \sup_n \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu_n \right) \vee \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu \right\} = 0.
\end{equation}
Then, there exists a further subsequence $\{n'_k\}$ such that $A^{n'_k}$ converges to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$:
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} |A^{n'_k}_s - A_s| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E,
$$
where ${\cal S}_{c,00}^1 := \{ \nu \in {\cal S}_0 : \mathrm{supp}[\nu] \text{ is compact}, \nu(E) \le 1 \text{ and } \|U_1\nu\|_\infty \le 1 \}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.014998+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74658e5ccb345d79abbc16286e160e28ffdd41d4fb19177b3dbfc2534065e983","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 4 (Exact interlacing transition densities) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $(z_{ij})_{i,j\geq1}$ be independent centered circular complex Gaussian variables with $\E\abs{z_{ij}}^2=1$. Let $((m_t,n_t))_{t=0}^H$ be an elementary up-right path of positive integer pairs. Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 X_t&=(z_{ij})_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m_t\\1\leq j\leq n_t}},
 &p_t&=\min(m_t,n_t),\\
 q_t&=\max(m_t,n_t),
 &r_t&=q_t-p_t.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Almost surely, $X_t$ has $p_t$ distinct positive squared singular values
\[
 \lambda_1^{(t)}>\cdots>\lambda_{p_t}^{(t)}>0.
\]
For $x_1>\cdots>x_k>0$, put
\[
 \Delta_k(x)=\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq k}(x_i-x_j).
\]

For $x_1>\cdots>x_p>0$ and $y_1>\cdots>y_p>0$, define
\[
 s_p(x,y)
 =
 \ee^{-\sum_{j=1}^py_j+\sum_{i=1}^px_i}
 \frac{\Delta_p(y)}{\Delta_p(x)}
 \ind_{\{y_1>x_1>y_2>x_2>\cdots>y_p>x_p\}}.
\]
For $r\geq1$, $x_1>\cdots>x_p>0$, and $y_1>\cdots>y_{p+1}>0$, define
\[
 \begin{split}
 b_{p,r}(x,y)
 &=
 \frac1{(r-1)!}
 \ee^{-\sum_{j=1}^{p+1}y_j+\sum_{i=1}^px_i}
 \frac{\Delta_{p+1}(y)}{\Delta_p(x)}\\
 &\quad\times
 \frac{\prod_{j=1}^{p+1}y_j^{r-1}}
      {\prod_{i=1}^px_i^r}
 \ind_{\{y_1>x_1>\cdots>y_p>x_p>y_{p+1}>0\}}.
 \end{split}
\]
Conditionally on $\lambda^{(t)}=x$, the density of $\lambda^{(t+1)}$ is $s_{p_t}(x,y)$ when $p_{t+1}=p_t$, and it is $b_{p_t,r_t}(x,y)$ when $p_{t+1}=p_t+1$. In the second case $r_t\geq1$. Both functions integrate to one over their decreasing chambers. Consequently, conditionally on $\lambda^{(0)}$, the multi-time density of
\[
 (\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(H)})
\]
is the product of these transition densities.

If $(M_N)$ is nondecreasing and
\[
 \sup_N(M_{N+1}-M_N)\leq K,
\]
the path $(M_N,N)$ has the same exact product representation after refining each transition into one column addition followed by $M_{N+1}-M_N$ row additions. At most $K+1$ elementary kernels are used per sample-size transition.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:44:27.938636+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7479adb8ddad3f7e5ff8bebcb3690cc94b7cb7a83bd3e9b54e290e1a692bbdaa","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 11 (Kernel expansion and stretch inputs) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] With high probability, for every fixed $r$,

\[
        f^{\mathsf T}\Delta_{\Kernel}f
        =\sum_{ab\in E(\Kernel)}(f(a)-f(b))^2
        \ge c\sum_{a\in V(\Kernel)}f(a)^2
\]
whenever $\sum_a f(a)=0$. Thus every pair of kernel vertices has
effective resistance $O(1)$.

If $L_e$ denotes the stretch of a kernel edge, then for every fixed $r$,
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{e\in E(\Kernel)}L_e^r=O_r(N\eps^{-r}).
\end{equation}
In addition, for every fixed $r$ and every kernel-measurable choice of edge
weights $q_e$, fixed after conditioning on the kernel and independent of the
stretch lengths, with $0\le q_e\le1$ and $\sum_e q_e=O(N)$,
\[
        \sum_e L_e^r q_e=O_r(N\eps^{-r})
\]
with high probability over the stretches; the same remains true after
multiplying $q_e$ by any fixed-degree polynomial in the endpoint degrees.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:13:21.346535+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74b28a3fda1cb90af3908b6162b3f7048645570fd27077f1b5079f72b9fd28a8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (The Blocking Probability) of arXiv:2609.01559, 'Erlang Loss Model with Energy Constrained Servers'] Let
\[
\rho_Q = \frac{\lambda}{\mu}, \qquad 
\rho_C = \frac{\lambda p}{\gamma}, \qquad 
\rho = \rho_Q + \rho_C,
\]
and define
\[
Z_k = \sum_{n=0}^k \frac{\rho^n}{n!}.
\]
Then, the blocking probability is given by
\[
\mathbb{P}(Q+C = k) = \frac{\rho^k/k!}{Z_k}.
\]
\begin{proof}
We begin by computing the marginal distribution of $N = Q + C$:
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}(N=n) 
&= \sum_{q=0}^n \mathbb{P}(Q=q, C=n-q) \\
&= \frac{1}{Z_k} \sum_{q=0}^n \frac{\rho_Q^q}{q!} \frac{\rho_C^{n-q}}{(n-q)!}.
\end{align}

Using the binomial identity
\[
\sum_{q=0}^n \frac{\rho_Q^q}{q!} \frac{\rho_C^{n-q}}{(n-q)!}
= \frac{(\rho_Q + \rho_C)^n}{n!}
= \frac{\rho^n}{n!},
\]
we obtain
\[
\mathbb{P}(N=n) = \frac{\rho^n/n!}{Z_k}, \quad n=0,\dots,k.
\]
Thus, $N$ is a Poisson$(\rho)$ random variable conditioned on $N \le k$.  Finally, we set the total queue length and number of charging servers equal to $k$ and therefore we obtain 
\[
\mathbb{P}(Q+C = k)
= \mathbb{P}(N=k)
= \frac{\rho^k/k!}{Z_k}.
\]
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:55:18.935574+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74b39e07c13e92a52ff20256d6e61396cd1d51251d718ab4282cdfc1de5f2259","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:Bernoulli-basic of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Let $(B_s)_{s\ge 0}$ be the Bernoulli numbers, defined by

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:55.056193+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74dd1bada3ca3b546ba102ccdb0e550227e7ab7cfe659716f57c191e23d1f1b9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:int-ik-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Diamond$-p model, then
  $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ and $x \in W$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only prove the modal cases.
    We note that $\Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent by the proof of Proposition (prop:hybrid-persistency of the paper).

    ($\Box\Leftrightarrow$)
    Easily proven by the induction hypothesis.

    ($\Diamond\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then $\forall x'\, (x \leq x' \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y'\, (x' \sqsubset y' \mathrel{\text{\&}} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi))$.
    This and $x \leq x$ imply that there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, then $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    Now take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$,
    then by the $\Diamond$-p condition, $x' \geq x \sqsubset y$ implies that there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y' \geq y$.
    Here, $y \leq y' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by persistency,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.432046+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74ecfeb3596696dc875c4e1e12763ce9b3c90cb3eca1bd9b37058b930e3572e9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma Affine invariance of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:affine_invariance}
Let $X \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ be discrete, 
let $f_Y \in \Sym(X)$, 
let $A$ be a linear bijection on $\mathbb{R}^d$
and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^d$. 
Then $f_{AY - b} \in \Sym(AX + b)$. 

Moreover, for any fixed $c>0$, $H(AY-b) \ge cH(AX + b)$ iff $H(Y) \ge cH(X)$, 
and for $d=1$ and nonzero $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Var(aY-b) \ge c\Var(aX+b)$ iff $\Var(Y) \ge c\Var(X)$. 

\begin{proof}
For the first claim it is sufficient to check the symmetry equations, 
and indeed
\[ 
f_{AX+b + AY-b}(z)

= f_{X+Y}(A^{-1} z)
= f_{X+Y}(-A^{-1} z)

= f_{AX+b + AY-b}(-z). 
\]

Also, $H(AY-b) = H(Y)$ and $H(AX+b) = H(X)$. 
Finally, $\Var(aY-b)= a^2\Var(Y)$ and $\Var(aX+b) = a^2\Var(X)$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.288103+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_751d5c4cc86e8f585e3946444e3dfae97468af8a5bae4a4a8460565dfacdb4cc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop best of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $(M^4,g)$ be a smooth compact oriented Riemannian manifold,

$c_1^+= [c_1(L)]^+$ denote the self-dual part of the harmonic $2$-form

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.690241+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7523021ae5c269225f71a59452e2e2641a43bfea5347f65a9b68cf1c434cc5f1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 111 (Finite-dimensional rough/finite-variation stability) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix $p\in(2,3)$ and $1<\nu<p/(p-1)$.  Let $V_0$ be bounded globally
Lipschitz.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item If $V\in\operatorname{Lip}^\rho$ for some $\rho>p$, the solution map of
\[
 \dd Z=V_0(Z)\,\dd t+V(Z)\,\dd\mathbf z
\]
is locally Lipschitz on bounded geometric $p$-rough-path balls for
$d_{p\text{-var}}^{\rm hom}$.
\item If $V\in\operatorname{Lip}^{\rho+1}$ for some $\rho>p$, the solution map
of
\[
 \dd Z=V_0(Z)\,\dd t+V(Z)\,\dd\mathbf z
 -\frac12\langle\mathcal W_V(Z),\dd q\rangle_{\rm tr}
\]
is locally Lipschitz on bounded sets for
\[
 d_{p\text{-var}}^{\rm hom}(\mathbf z,\widetilde{\mathbf z})
 +\|q-\widetilde q\|_{\nu\text{-var};\mathcal S_1}.
\]
Both solution maps are causal under terminal restriction and obey the usual
subinterval-restriction and concatenation laws.  They do not commute with
stopping of $(\mathbf z,q)$ alone when $V_0\ne0$; exact stop preservation is
recovered by adjoining the finite-variation clock channel $\ell_t=t$, with
its canonical Young augmentation, and stopping $(\ell,\mathbf z,q)$
simultaneously.  More precisely,
for every driver radius $R$ and compact initial set $K\subset\R^m$, there is
$C_{R,K}$ such that solutions $Z,\widetilde Z$ starting in $K$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \|Z-\widetilde Z\|_\infty
 \le C_{R,K}\left(
 d_{p\text{-var}}^{\rm hom}(\mathbf z,\widetilde{\mathbf z})
 +\|q-\widetilde q\|_{\nu\text{-var};\mathcal S_1}
 +|Z_0-\widetilde Z_0|\right),
\end{equation}
whenever the two rough drivers and the two finite-variation drivers have
radius at most $R$.  In part~\textup{(i)}, the $q$-term is omitted.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

A second-order operator in divergence form is Lu = -sum_{i,j} D_i(a^{ij}(x) D_j u) + sum_i b^i(x) D_i u + c(x) u, written Lu = -div(A grad u) + b.grad u + c u, where A = (a^{ij}) is a real n x n matrix-valued measurable function on Omega (not necessarily symmetric, not necessarily continuous) and b = (b^i), c are real measurable functions. L is uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda if for a.e. x in Omega and all xi, eta in R^n: A(x)xi.xi >= lambda|xi|^2 and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta|; one normally also assumes b, c in L^infinity(Omega). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:32:58.301200+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_75709dd5f2dc73b63b81f372db4678ef3bbe3e2ee643593b134f378343ad3f51","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm: density R configuration of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] Let \( (v_1, \dots, v_k) \) be an inductive configuration with covariance matrix \( R \), and assume that
\[
\norm{v_k - v_{k-1}}_2 \neq \operatorname{diam}\left(\bigcap_{j < k-1} S_{v_j, r_j}\right).
\]

Then for any measurable set \( A \subseteq \mathbb{S}^{n-1} \) with \( \sigma(A) \geq \omega_R(n^{-\epsilon_R}) \), the probability that a uniformly random tuple \( (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta(n, R) \) lies entirely in \( A \) satisfies
\[
\mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta(n, R)}(x_1 \in A, \dots, x_k \in A) \geq \Omega_R(\sigma(A)^{C_R}),
\]
as \( n \to \infty \). The constant \( C_R \) is given by
\[
C_R = \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \frac{2}{1 - |c_i|} \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} \frac{1 + |c_j|}{1 - |c_j|},
\]
with
\[
c_1 = r_1, \quad c_i = (f_{c_{i-1}} \circ \cdots \circ f_{c_1})(r_i), \quad i = 2, \dots, k-1,
\]
and \( f_c(r) = \frac{r - c^2}{1 - c^2} \). The constant $\epsilon_R$ is given by
$$\epsilon_R=\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{1-|c_i|}{1+|c_i|}.$$","status":"unverified"}

A cross-cut is an antichain C, containing neither 0 nor 1, that meets every maximal chain from 0 to 1. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:48:30.905598+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_75d2df2d614717f3dc0285f5415349470ee1fced15634a5ea84f9d9ca81ea6ef","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 15 (Projective realization and integrability of the Jacobi kernel) of arXiv:2609.00922, 'The Morse Index, Nullity and Jacobi Fields of Constant-Curvature 2-Spheres in Complex Proj'] Let $n\ge1$ and $0\le k\le n$.
Every normal Jacobi field along $\phi_{n-2k,n}$ is the normal component of the
variational field of a family $\Phi_k(A_t)=(G')^k(A_t\circ f_0)$ with
$A_0=\Id$.
Equivalently, the normal differential
\[
 \mathfrak d_k:T_{d_0}\mathscr D_n\longrightarrow\ker J_{n-2k,n}
\]
is an isomorphism.  Hence every normal Jacobi field is integrable
through a family of minimal $2$-spheres.

The map $\mathfrak d_k$ is an isomorphism of real $\SU(2)$-modules.
Equipping the source with its natural complex structure and the target with
$I_{\mathrm{hom}}$, one obtains the following abstract complex
$\SU(2)$-module decompositions:
\[
 T_{d_0}\mathscr D_n
 \simeq
 \mathfrak{sl}(V_n)/\dd\rho_n\bigl(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)\bigr)
 \simeq\bigoplus_{\ell=2}^{n}V_{2\ell},
 \qquad
 (\ker J_{n-2k,n},I_{\mathrm{hom}})
 \simeq\bigoplus_{\ell=2}^{n}V_{2\ell}.
\]
Here $\dd\rho_n:\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)\to\mathfrak{sl}(V_n)$ denotes the
complex-linear extension introduced in Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.822200+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_75dd65ad3c90c552febfc6fcd0b31055cb83fad18c5584be8ed7ac94fb76baa8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:rank-frequency of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$.  For every $n\in\mathcal R(h,k)$, the function
\[
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)=
 \#\left\{A\in\binom{[q]}k:|hA|=n\right\}
\]
is a quasipolynomial in $q-1$ (and hence in $q$).  Its degree is exactly
\[
 \deg F^{(k)}_{h,n}=k-r_{h,k}(n).
\]
In particular, there is an explicitly computable positive rational number
$c_{h,k,n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)
 =c_{h,k,n}q^{k-r_{h,k}(n)}
  +O_{h,k}\!\left(q^{k-r_{h,k}(n)-1}\right).
\end{equation}
The possible frequency exponents therefore belong to
$\{2,3,\ldots,k\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:57:44.942619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_75f3feba910cc773f54b511a7f352aa50e21cd04aa787c111a17615bda234f11","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Perron 1 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] Let $A \in M_n$, $n \geq 2$, be irreducible with nonnegative entries. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item There exists a  number $\mu > 0$, called the Perron--Frobenius eigenvalue of $A$, such that $\mu$ is a simple eigenvalue of $A$ and any other eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ verifies $|\lambda| \leq \mu$. Thus $\rho(A)=\mu$.

\item The Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue of $A$ fulfils the row-sum inequalities
\begin{equation}
\min_{1\leq i \leq n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} \leq \mu \leq  \max_{1\leq i \leq n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}.
\end{equation}

\item The matrix $A$ is similar to $e^{2\pi i /h} A$ and the spectrum of $A$ is invariant under multiplication by $e^{2\pi i /h}$.

\item If $h>1$, there exists a permutation matrix $P$ such that
\begin{equation}
            P^{\intercal}AP =
            \begin{bmatrix}
        0&\!\!\!\smash{A_{{1,2}}}&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0 \\
        0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\smash{A_{{2,3}}}&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0 \\[-4pt]
        \vdots&\!\!\!\vdots&\!\!\!\vdots&\!\!\!\ddots&\!\!\vdots \\
        0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!\smash{A_{{h-1,h}}} \\
        \smash{A_{{h,1}}}&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0
\end{bmatrix},
\end{equation}
where the non-zero blocks are square matrices.

\item If $h=1$, then the limit $$\lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{A^m}{\mu^m}$$ exists. This limit is called the \emph{Perron projection} of $A$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:28:53.672283+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7601754935f4eaee7e7a482971cc4990ee01d4c129669d7c288c74c6a361823d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 12 (leave probability and exit distribution) of arXiv:2605.13648, 'Sticky CIR process with potential: invariant measure and exact sampling'] \label[corollary]{cor:leave-zero}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.486800+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_761b2d8f3655734a94ab4ea519ee44debdd80eba52b88e90ff61f055e52f8b37","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Suppose the coefficient $G:=gg^\top/2$ is non-degenerate in $y$ uniformly with respect to $x$ and the drift $f$ satisfies the weak recurrence condition

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.219408+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7663636cd1e0dfa30578941f7c7e6f97c365af33ac796736a45470b15303a539","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:spectral-structure of arXiv:2607.05693, 'Free multiplicative convolution and Erlang moments in monitored quantum transport'] The limiting law $\mu_\tau$ has an atom at $1$ of mass
\[
  \mu_\tau(\{1\})=(1-\tau)_+.
\]
Consequently, the mass away from the atom at $1$ is $\min\{1,\tau\}$. Moreover,
the Stieltjes-transform equation has a real branch point at
\[
  x_*(\tau)=\tau \mathrm{e}^{1-\tau}.
\]
At $\tau=1$ this branch point reaches $1$, precisely where the atom at $1$
disappears.

\begin{remark}
Beenakker [Beenakker2501] computes the $\tau=1$ moments for the
\emph{orthogonal} version of the model, in which
$Q_N=\prod_{n=1}^N\bigl(I-u^{(n)}(u^{(n)})^\top\bigr)$ is a product of $N$
real rank-$(N-1)$ projectors, and obtains
\[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Tr(Q_NQ_N^\top)^p\bigr]
  =\frac{(p/\mathrm{e})^p}{p!}.
\]
This agrees exactly with the law identified here: setting $\tau=1$ in
(equation eq:moment-formula of the paper) and using $G_p(1)=p^{p-1}$ (a short induction,
or Cayley's formula for the number of labelled rooted trees on $p$
vertices) gives
\[
  m_p(1)=\mathrm{e}^{-p}\frac{p^{p-1}}{(p-1)!}
  =\mathrm{e}^{-p}\frac{p^p}{p!}
  =\frac{(p/\mathrm{e})^p}{p!}.
\]
Our rigorous results are stated for the complex (unitary) ensemble, whereas
Beenakker's computation is for the real (orthogonal) one; the two limiting
moment sequences coincide because the leading-order free limit does not
depend on the symmetry class, the difference appearing only in the $1/N$
corrections. Beenakker further notes, following a question of Bulatov, that
at $\tau=1$ the squared singular values are \emph{approximately} distributed
as $\mathrm{e}^{-\pi X^2}$ with $X$ standard normal, and asks for a direct
explanation. The measure $\mu_1$ identified here is the exact limiting law:
the approximate Gaussian form is its Stirling approximation, with the factor
$\pi$ originating from Stirling's constant in
$(p-1)!\sim\sqrt{2\pi p}\,(p/\mathrm{e})^{p-1}$.
\end{remark} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}  P_{\mu}^k \varphi(\wt b) 
=  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}  \bb E \varphi(g_k \cdots g_1 \wt b)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.161069+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_76804a3a87c48929c68daf05e6e3d2decc6088f5077b4716f90e77a58e30b1b8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 9 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1 > 0$ and $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, we have $S_\star(\lambda,\mu) \subseteq S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_1)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.272893+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7690caf819e9092bf71a4e77b99396e752be9e66dec7c4917ea195a8c319988a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Satz thm:HigherOrder of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Given Assumptions (ass:Set1 of the paper), let $f\colon \mathcal{X} \to {\mathbb R}$ be a suitable function with ${\mathbb E} f = 0$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.776888+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_76a718cca5e1483bec9e0c58b8401d724441e7d9c9fda4cac712e08c0dc60d1f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Assume that $\domO$ is a bounded and sufficiently smooth domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$.

Assume that $\psi: \mathbb{R}    \to \mathbb{R}$ is the Landau potential. Assume that  $(\Omega,\mathscr{F},\mathbb{P})$ is a probability space with a right-continuous filtration $\mathbb{F}=(\mathscr{F}_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ 
 such that on this probability space two i.i.d. copies of  $\ell^2$-cylindrical $\mathbb{F}$-adapted  Wiener processes are defined.
Then, there exist an $\ell^2$-cylindrical $\mathbb{F}$-adapted Wiener process $W=(w_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N} \setminus\{0\}}$, progressively measurable processes $\bu$, $\phi$, $p$, and a sequence $(p_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N} \setminus\{0\}}$, whose trajectories belong to suitable functional spaces, such that the tuple $(\bu,p,\phi,(p_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N} \setminus\{0\}})$ is a weak solution of the following problem:
\begin{equation}
\left\{\begin{aligned}
&\d \bu + [\diver(\bu \otimes \bu) - \nu \Delta \bu + \nabla p + \newK \diver(\nabla \phi \otimes \nabla \phi)]\,\d t \\
&\hspace{0.5 truecm} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}  \left[(\sigma_k(t,x) \cdot \nabla) \bu -\nabla p_k + \bg_k(t,x,u) \right]\d w_k &\mbox{ in } (0,T) \times \domO,
\\
&\diver \bu= 0 &\mbox{ in } (0,T) \times \domO,
  \\
&\d \phi + \diver(\phi \bu) \,\d t= 
\,\Delta \left(-  \Delta \phi(t) + \,\psi^\prime(\phi(t)) \right)\d t &\mbox{ in } (0,T) \times \domO.
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.566999+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_76a808fec1f29b8d01c2055814d3c6693c8a4a8eddd48767148cb64574d200a0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem.conditional-renewal-tau-k of arXiv:2605.26082, 'Quantitative Einstein relation for reversible diffusions in a random environment'] Let $k\ge 1$ and $R=R(\lambda)$. Define
		\[
			\mathsf L_k\coloneqq\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:e_1\cdot y\le e_1\cdot X^\lambda(\tau_k)-4R\}\, ,
			\qquad
			\mathsf R_+\coloneqq\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:e_1\cdot y\ge -2R\}\, .
		\]
		Let $\mathcal G_k$ denote the $\sigma$-algebra generated by:
		\begin{enumerate}
		\item[\rm(a)] the time $\tau_k$, the diffusion path $(X^\lambda(s))_{0\le s\le\tau_k-\lambda^{-2}}$, and the endpoint $X^\lambda(\tau_k)$;
		\item[\rm(b)] the auxiliary Bernoulli variables $(Y_n)_{0\le n<\lambda^2(\tau_k-\lambda^{-2})}$;
		\item[\rm(c)] the environment $(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})|_{\mathsf L_k}$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Let the shifted future data be
		\[
			\mathcal Y_k\coloneqq\bigl(
				(X^\lambda(\tau_k+t)-X^\lambda(\tau_k))_{t\ge0},\
				(Y_{\lambda^2\tau_k+n})_{n\ge 0},\
				T_{X^\lambda(\tau_k)}(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})\bigr|_{\mathsf R_+}
			\bigr)\, ,
		\]
		where $T_x(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})(z)\coloneqq(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})(x+z)$, and let $\mathcal Y_0$ be given by the same formula with $k=0$ and $\tau_0=0$. Then for every bounded measurable function $\Phi$ of such triples and every bounded $\mathcal G_k$-measurable random variable $H$,
		\begin{equation}
			\widehat{\mathbb E}_0^\lambda[\Phi(\mathcal Y_k) H]
			=\widehat{\mathbb E}_0^\lambda[\Phi(\mathcal Y_0)\mid D=\infty]\,\widehat{\mathbb E}_0^\lambda[H]\, .
		\end{equation}
		In particular, $\mathcal Y_k$ is independent of $\mathcal G_k$ under $\widehat{\mathbb P}_0^\lambda$, and the law of $\mathcal Y_k$ equals the law of $\mathcal Y_0$ under $\widehat{\mathbb P}_0^\lambda[\,\cdot\mid D=\infty]$.
		Moreover, writing $M_i\coloneqq(\Delta A_i^\lambda,\Delta\tau_i)$ for the clock-duration block:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[\rm(i)] for every integer $i$ with $1\le i\le k-2$, the block $M_i$ is $\mathcal G_k$-measurable;
			\item[\rm(ii)] there is a measurable map $\Psi$, defined on the common state space of the shifted future data, such that
			\[
				(M_k,M_{k+1},\ldots)=\Psi(\mathcal Y_k)
			\]
			holds $\widehat{\mathbb P}_0^\lambda$-almost surely.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["finite reversible chain","continuous time"],"created_at":"2026-10-05T21:18:10.823960+00:00","domain":"probability/markov-chains/mixing","id":"claim_76b0d870245046ffaed4fd91ce5230e9","kind":"counterexample","schema_version":1,"statement":"Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.48(a) is answered in the negative: tau_1 <= tau_0 fails. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.587616+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_76e5cef7bc6272ef61099dfe54518d4ccf43a3e4fa693b1d8474e369421e509a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn of arXiv:2603.13873, '{Solvability of BSDEs with possibly unbounded stochastic coefficients \\ on a general weig'] A continuous function $u:\bar {G}\rightarrow{\mathbb R}^k$ is a viscosity sub-solution (super-solution) of PDE (equation PDE-1 of the paper) if for any $1\leq i\leq k$ and any function $\phi\in C^2(\bar {G};{\mathbb R})$, it holds that

\begin{array}{c}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:58:24.517485+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7705c43eb63198ec74f754b5e6e5d52f598ef4d5d482adc600311aca8bca9f5c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem t:joint.sum.max.star of arXiv:2601.12677, 'Stable and Fréchet limit theorem for subgraph functionals in the hyperbolic random geometr'] $(i)$ If $\frac{1}{2} (k-1)<\alpha< k-1$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
\begin{align}
&\left( \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n\cdot\,]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) - [N_n\cdot\,]  \mathbb{E} [\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_1)] \bigg), \ \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}\bigvee_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot \,]} \mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i)\right)  \Rightarrow (S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot),\, Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot)),   
\end{align}
in the space $D\big([0,1], {\mathbb R} \times [0,\infty)\big)$ of right-continuous functions from $[0,1]$ to ${\mathbb R}\times [0,\infty)$ with left limits. The weak limit in (equation e:weak.conv.join.sum.max.star of the paper) is defined by the hybrid characteristic–distribution function
\begin{equation}  
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{ivS_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t)} {\mathbf 1} \{ Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t) \le z \} \big] = t\int_0^z e^{ivy} g(v,y)^t e^{-ty^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}} \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif y),  \  \ v\in {\mathbb R},\,  z\ge 0,  
\end{equation}
where
$$
g(v,y) := \exp \Big\{ \int_0^\infty \big( (e^{ivx}-1){\mathbf 1} \{ x<y \} -ivx \big) \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif x)\Big\}, 
$$
and $\mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a Radon measure on $(0,\infty]$ satisfying $\mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}\big((y,\infty]\big)=y^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}$ for $y>0$. \\
Marginally, $S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a zero-mean $2\alpha/(k-1)$-stable L\'evy process whose characteristic function is given by (equation e:chf.first.comp.zero.mean.stable of the paper) below. Furthermore, $Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is an extremal $2\alpha/(k-1)$-Fr\'echet process; that is, for $0\equiv t_0<t_1<\cdots <t_m<\infty$ and $z_i\ge0$, $i=1,\dots,m$, 
$$
\mathbb{P}\big( Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t_i)\le z_i, \, i=1,\dots,m \big)=\exp \Big\{ -\sum_{j=1}^m (t_j-t_{j-1}) (z_j \wedge \cdots \wedge z_m)^{-2\alpha/(k-1)} \Big\}. 
$$
$(ii)$ If $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<\frac{1}{2} (k-1)$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
$$
\left( \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}  \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot\, ]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i), \ \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \bigvee_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot \,]} \mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) \right)  \Rightarrow (\widetilde{S}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot), Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot)), \ \ \text{in } D\big( [0,1], [0,\infty)^2\big), 
$$
where the weak limit is defined by 
\begin{equation}  
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{iv\widetilde{S}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t)} {\mathbf 1} \{ Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t) \le z \} \big] = t\int_0^z e^{ivy} \, \widetilde{g}(v,y)^t e^{-ty^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}} \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif y),  \ \ \ v\in {\mathbb R},\,  z\ge 0,  
\end{equation}
with 
$$
\widetilde{g}(v,y) := \exp \Big\{ \int_0^y (e^{ivx}-1) \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif x)\Big\}. 
$$
Marginally, $\widetilde S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a $2\alpha/(k-1)$-stable subordinator (i.e., a stable L\'evy process with increasing paths) with its characteristic function given by (equation e:chf.first.comp.zero.stable.subordinator of the paper) below. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:27:25.791643+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7754caf2c164aae1fa5a545cc57e36008f3e9a844f3df67d5cc1aa5e1a256641","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem.mathcalY of arXiv:2605.11785, 'Regularization of a mean-field SDE by an additive common noise: the conditional expectatio'] For any $\mu_0\in \mathcal P_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, there exists a unique Borel measurable map $\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}: [0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d\times  {\mathcal C}\to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for any $(t,x,\bm{x})\in [0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d\times {\mathcal C}$, 
$$
\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(t,x, {\bm{x}}) = x-\overline \mu_0+\int_0^t  b(\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(s,x, {\bm{x}})+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)ds - \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} b(\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(s,y, {\bm{x}})+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)\mu_0(dy)ds.

$$

   \forall t\in[0,T],\;y^i_t=x^i_0-\frac 1N\sum_{j=1}^Nx^j_0+\int_0^t  b(y^i_s+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)ds - \int_0^t\frac 1N\sum_{j=1}^Nb(y^j_s+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)ds,\;i\in\{1,\cdots,N\},

then

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:11:09.317987+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7769ad35ea798402e2d9dfb68648b26bba59b5f29562b4786a3e123a8f4beb65","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:vrjp-on-G-r-pos-rec of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let $G=(\Lambda,E)$ be a connected undirected graph without self-loops

    &P_\rho^{W,\Lambda_r}((X^{\Lambda_l\neq},T^{\Lambda_l\neq})\in\cdot)=\int_{{\mathbb R}^{\Lambda_r}}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:49:17.488530+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_776ab115bfe011064b680e79bfed6462b4b0d5b744c88900cf946ddffddaec1a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2605.28473, 'The BKT transition and surface tension differentiability'] Consider the measure $\BM_{\Gamma,\beta}$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:55:37.821677+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_777c1f8dc11f0b211f115acdab510f10051796e40714785ffd737fbc7203d710","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi defCBDI of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] \
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item  We call $\mathrm{CBDI}$ any $[0,\infty]$-valued càdlàg Markov process $\big(X, (\mathbb{P}_x)_{x\in [0,\infty]}\big)$, solution to the following martingale problem $\mathrm{MP}\big(\mathcal{X},\mathrm{C}^2_c((0,\infty))\big)$:
\[\forall x\in (0,\infty), \ f\in \mathrm{C}^2_c((0,\infty)), \quad \left(f(X_t)-\int_0^{t}\mathcal{X}f(X_s)\mathrm{d} s,\ t\geq 0 \right) \text{ is a } \mathbb{P}_x\text{ - martingale}.\]
\item  We call minimal and denote by $X^{\mathrm{m}}$, any $\mathrm{CBDI}$ process  whose boundaries $\{0,\infty\}$ are absorbing, namely: 
\[\forall x\in [0,\infty], \ \mathbb{P}_x-\text{a.s.}\  X^{\mathrm{m}}_t=\begin{cases} 0 &\text{ if } t\geq \sigma_0^{-} \text{ and }  \sigma_0^{-}<\sigma_\infty^{+}, \\
\infty  &\text{ if } t\geq \sigma_\infty^{+} \text{ and }  \sigma_\infty^{+}<\sigma_0^{-}.
\end{cases}
\]
\item  For $\Delta\in \{0,\infty\}$, we say that a process $\big(X^{\mathrm{e}\Delta},(\mathbb{P}_x)_{x\in [0,\infty]}\big)$ is a $\mathrm{CBDI}$ extended at $\Delta$, if it is a $[0,\infty]$-valued  Markov process, which once stopped at the boundary $\Delta$, has the same law as the minimal process: namely, if one sets  $\zeta^{\Delta}:=\inf\big\{t\geq 0: X_{t-} \text{ or } X_t =\Delta\big\}$, then one has
\[\forall x\in [0,\infty]\setminus \{\Delta\}, \ \  (X^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_{t\wedge \zeta^{\Delta}},t\geq 0)\overset{\mathrm{law}}{=}(X^{\mathrm{m}}_t,t\geq 0)\ \text{ under } \mathbb{P}_x.\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[-]The process $X^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}$ is said furthermore to be a continuous extension if its boundary $\Delta$ is continuous in the sense of Definition~(def:boundary of the paper)-(def:continuous of the paper). 
\item[-] It is a Fellerian extension of $X^{\mathrm{m}}$ if  its semigroup $(P^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ satisfies for any $f\in \mathsf{C}([0,\infty])$,
    $P^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_tf(x) \underset{t\rightarrow 0+}{\rightarrow} f(x),\ x\in [0,\infty]$ 	and $P^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_tf \in \mathsf{C}([0,\infty])$.
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["U ⊂ C is open","all members of the family are holomorphic (respectively meromorphic) on the same open set U"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.483658+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_778fb0bb31baea70fbabe9efe4cbc496909f379fa127979c6c8cf41293005128","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let U ⊂ C be open and F a family of holomorphic functions on U. F is normal (in the finite sense) if every sequence in F has a subsequence converging uniformly on every compact subset of U; the limit is then automatically holomorphic, and it need not belong to F. F is normal in the extended sense if every sequence in F has a subsequence which, on each connected component of U, either converges uniformly on compact subsets to a holomorphic function or tends to ∞ uniformly on compact subsets (equivalently, the reciprocals tend to 0 uniformly on compact subsets). For families of meromorphic functions, normality means that every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets with respect to the chordal metric of the Riemann sphere; restricted to holomorphic families this coincides with the extended sense, because a spherical limit of zero-free reciprocals is, by Hurwitz's theorem, either holomorphic or identically ∞ on each component. Normality is a local property: F is normal on U if and only if every point of U has a neighborhood on which F is normal. Normality asserts the existence of convergent subsequences only; it does not assert convergence of the family itself, and the limit function may leave the family (for instance the limit of injective functions may be constant).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.969356+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_779af4b65f168c330570cd29cf153b943f59e61fb27b908aa1167f04f96b0e42","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 14 (Filtered BCH and the initial ancestry symbol) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let \(A:V\to V\) be linear and write \(L(A)\) for its functorial action
on \(L\).  Then
\[
 L(A)\gamma_r(D)\subseteq\gamma_r(D),
 \qquad
 [\gamma_r(D),\gamma_s(D)]\subseteq\gamma_{r+s}(D).
\]
Consequently every truncation in ordinary tensor degree is nilpotent and
filtered for
\(F_0L=L\), \(F_rL=L\cap J^r=\gamma_r(D)\).  It therefore defines BCH
laws on the ordinary-degree completions of \({\operatorname{gr}}_FL\) and of the extended
Rees Lie algebra
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_F(L):=
 \sum_{r\geq0}F_rL\,z^{-r}\mathbf k[z]
 \subseteq L[z,z^{-1}],
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_F(L)/z\mathcal R_F(L)\cong{\operatorname{gr}}_FL,
 
\end{equation}
Reduction modulo \(z\) records the associated-graded deformation.  If
\(x\in F_rL\setminus F_{r+1}L\),
its full initial symbol is the nonzero class
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{in}^{\mathrm{full}}_F(x)
 :=x+F_{r+1}L\in{\mathfrak L}_r(Q).
 
\end{equation}
Thus filtration order cannot decrease under linear transport (with the
value \(+\infty\) if the transported element vanishes), and
\begin{equation}
 \nu_F([x,y])\geq\nu_F(x)+\nu_F(y)
 
\end{equation}
for nonzero \(x,y\), with the convention \(\nu_F(0)=+\infty\).  Exact
valuation is preserved
by transport precisely when the induced associated-graded map does not kill
the initial symbol; injectivity of that map on the containing graded layer
is sufficient.  Likewise,
equality holds in \eqref{cc:eq-valuation-superadditive} precisely when
the associated-graded bracket of the two initial symbols is nonzero.
Otherwise transport,
bracketing, cancellation in a sum, or a BCH component may raise the order
or annihilate the element.  A full Rees lift of a causal logarithm requires
a Rees jet or a splitting and is not supplied canonically by the filtration.

In the ordinary-degree completion, exponentiation identifies the special
fibre with
\begin{equation}
 \exp\!\left(V_{\mathrm{ab}}\ltimes_\rho\widehat{{\mathfrak L}}(Q)\right).
 
\end{equation}
Here
\(\widehat{{\mathfrak L}}(Q)=\prod_{n\geq1}{\mathfrak L}(Q)_n\) denotes completion in
ordinary tensor degree.
Moreover, the associated-graded bracket induces
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak b_{a,b}:G^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,a}(V)\otimes
 G^{\mathrm{full}}_{m,b}(V)
 \longrightarrow G^{\mathrm{full}}_{n+m,a+b}(V),
 \qquad \mathfrak b_{a,b}([x],[y])=[x,y],
 
\end{equation}
and this is the mixed quadratic symbol of BCH:
\begin{equation}
 \left.\partial_s\partial_t\right|_{s=t=0}
 {\operatorname{BCH}}(sx,ty)=\tfrac12[x,y].
 
\end{equation}
If the three layers in \eqref{cc:eq-ancestry-bracket} are finite
dimensional, duality gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak b_{a,b}^{\vee}:E^{\mathrm{full}}_{n+m,a+b}(V)
 \longrightarrow E^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,a}(V)\otimes
 E^{\mathrm{full}}_{m,b}(V).
 
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:16.143738+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_77d13d62a763c601621af711fc29176926cbc7c4c955995446c49e198910fcdc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 3 (Rightmost eigenvalue) of arXiv:2604.13134, '\bf From Gaussian to Gumbel: extreme eigenvalues of complex Ginibre products with exact ra'] Let \(\widetilde X_n\), \(\alpha\), and \(\alpha_n\) be defined as above.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(\alpha=+\infty\), then
\[
\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\big|\mathbb P(\widetilde X_n\le x)-e^{-e^{-x}}\big|
=
\frac{25(\log\log \alpha_n)^2}{16e\log \alpha_n}(1+o(1))
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).

\item If \(\alpha=0\), then
\[
\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\big|\mathbb P(\widetilde X_n\le x)-\Phi(x)\big|
=
(1+o(1))
\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
\phi(x)\big|
\frac{\sqrt{2}+4\ln 2}{2}\sqrt{\alpha_n}
-\frac{x}{4n}
\big|
\]
as \(n\to+\infty\).

\item If \(\alpha\in(0,+\infty)\), then for each fixed \(x\in\mathbb R\), the
infinite-dimensional matrix \(\widetilde M(x,\alpha)\) defines a trace-class operator on
\(\ell^2(\mathbb N)\). Hence
\[
\widetilde\Phi_\alpha(x):=\det({\rm I}-\widetilde M(x,\alpha))
\]
is well defined. Moreover, \(\widetilde\Phi_\alpha\) is a distribution function and
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\mathbb P(\widetilde X_n\le x)=\widetilde\Phi_\alpha(x),
\qquad x\in\mathbb R.
\]
The family \(\{\widetilde\Phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}\) interpolates continuously between the
Gaussian and Gumbel laws, and its boundary asymptotics are given by
\[
\lim_{\alpha\to0^+}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha}}
\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|\widetilde\Phi_\alpha(x)-\Phi(x)\right|
=
\frac{\sqrt{2}+4\ln 2}{2\sqrt{2\pi}},
\]
and
\[
\lim_{\alpha\to+\infty}
\frac{\log\alpha}{(\log\log\alpha)^2}
\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|\widetilde\Phi_\alpha(x)-e^{-e^{-x}}\right|
=
\frac{25}{16e}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:30:50.719620+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_77d22f8e137b4ddfe44d0122fb2f25cae17e1a1654cb9727f0b0d6238380db92","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:knn-gap of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] In the setting of (thm:knn-gaussian-limit of the paper), let $r=d-m\ge2$ and $a=\log(2q)$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:48:43.463233+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_77d47a96f45be9ed781038dd32eb03ccaf72ea883fc8205a829579749f75d2fd","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 1 (Asymptotics of the solutions) of arXiv:2608.06565, 'Smoothness of the survival probability in models with a random environment: the annuity an'] Let $\sigma>0$, $c<0$, $\lambda>0$ and
$\mathcal L^0\psi:=\sigma^2u^2\psi''/2+(au+c)\psi'$. Consider the equation
$\mathcal L^0\psi-\lambda\psi=0$. It has a fundamental system of solutions
$\{\pup,\pdn\}$ with $\pup(0+)=0$ and $\pdn$ bounded at infinity, and as
$u\to0+$
\begin{equation}
    
    \pup(u)=C_\uparrow\,u^{\beta}\exp\left(-\frac{\kappa}{u}\right)
    \bigl(1+O(u)\bigr),\quad \kappa=\frac{2|c|}{\sigma^2},\quad
    \beta=2-\frac{2a}{\sigma^2},
\end{equation}
where $C_\uparrow>0$, while $\pdn(0+)$ is finite and non-zero. As
$v\to\infty$ one has $\pdn(v)\sim C_\downarrow v^{\rho_-}$, where $\rho_-<0$
is the smaller root of
$$
    \tfrac12\sigma^2\rho^2+\bigl(a-\tfrac12\sigma^2\bigr)\rho-\lambda=0 .
$$
The solutions may be chosen positive; then $\pup$ is strictly increasing,
$\pdn$ is strictly decreasing, they are linearly independent, the Wronskian
$\mathcal W=\pup\pdn'-\pup'\pdn$ is strictly negative, and by Liouville's
formula
\begin{equation}
    
    \mathcal W(v)=C_{\mathcal W}\,v^{-2a/\sigma^2}\,e^{2c/(\sigma^2v)},
    \qquad C_{\mathcal W}<0 .
\end{equation}
For $c\ge0$ the behaviour of the solutions is different. Zero is inaccessible,
$\pdn(0+)=+\infty$, and the role of $\pup$ is played by the solution bounded at
zero. For $c>0$ such a solution is unique up to a factor and satisfies
$\pup(0+)>0$, while every solution not proportional to it grows like
$u^{\beta}e^{2c/(\sigma^2u)}$. For $c=0$ the equation is of Euler type and
$\pup(u)=u^{\rho_+}$, $\pdn(u)=u^{\rho_-}$, where $\rho_+>0$ is the larger root
of the same equation. Formula \eqref{eq:liouville} and the negativity of the
Wronskian hold for every sign of $c$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Independent arrays and standard Gaussian channel noise; N,P>=2,M>=1; X=UV^T/sqrt(N)","Fixed centered unit-variance factor laws with finite fourth moments; bounded tau_U,tau_V","E[u h]=E[tau_U h'], E[(u^2-1)h]=E[eta_U h']; corresponding V identities and E[(tau_V-1)h]=E[zeta_V h'] for bounded C1 h with bounded derivative","Square-integrable eta_U,eta_V,zeta_V; precise constants and all rate bounds are in proof Eqs2,13","Positive finite convergent aspects only for limiting coefficient; no information-limit existence assumed"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:16:13.028659+00:00","domain":"probability; Gaussian channels; extensive-rank matrix factorization","id":"claim_77f6ac5e73d28069a2817defb72ab668c6f3bbc97c7a3b33f41566584c157634","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own work, proof (unaudited), novelty unestablished.

U in R^(N by M), V in R^(P by M), N,P>=2,M>=1, have independent
iid real entries within each array; the arrays are independent.
Their fixed scalar laws u,v are centered with variance one and
finite fourth moments u4,v4. Assume measurable scalar functions
tau_U,eta_U,tau_V,eta_V,zeta_V satisfy, for bounded C1 functions h
with bounded derivative, including their bounded smooth compositions
in the proof,

 E[u h(u)]=E[tau_U(u) h'(u)],
 E[(u^2-1)h(u)]=E[eta_U(u) h'(u)],
 E[v h(v)]=E[tau_V(v) h'(v)],
 E[(v^2-1)h(v)]=E[eta_V(v) h'(v)],
 E[(tau_V(v)-1)h(v)]=E[zeta_V(v) h'(v)].             (1)

Assume |tau_U|<=T_U, |tau_V|<=T_V almost surely and
E eta_U^2,E eta_V^2,E zeta_V^2 finite. No differentiability of
these five functions and no posterior independence is assumed.
Bounded truncation of h(x)=x gives E tau_U=E tau_V=1.
Define the finite scalar constants

 t_U=E tau_U^2, t_V=E tau_V^2,
 e_U=E eta_U^2, e_V=E eta_V^2, z_V=E zeta_V^2,
 a_U=E[tau_U u^2], a_V=E[tau_V v^2],
 b_U=E[tau_U u], b_V=E[tau_V v],
 h_U=E eta_U, h_V=E eta_V,
 L_N=N-2+2*a_U^2+2*b_U^4.

Let independent Z have iid standard Gaussian entries, X=UV^T/sqrt(N),
Y=sqrt(s)X+Z, d=NP, alpha=P/N, beta=M/N, v_s=1+beta*s.
Set g=beta/v_s, m_N=E||X-E[X|Y]||^2/d and
B_N=log(v_s)/2-I(X;Y)/d, with natural logs.

## Explicit constants and result

Put A=beta^2*(N-1)*(P-1)/N^2 and

 E3=6*(N-1)*(P-1)*M*(t_U^2*t_V-1)/N^4,
 Ec=6*(N-1)/N^4 *
       [M*T_U^4*T_V^2*(v4+2*(P-1))+M*(M-1)*a_V^2],
 Eeta=2/N^3 * [M*P*e_U*T_V^2+M*(M-1)*h_U^2*b_V^2],
 Ezeta=2*N*M*z_V/N^3,
 E4=24*(N-1)*(P-1)/N^5 *
       [M*T_U^4*T_V^2*e_V*N+2*M*(M-1)*b_U^2*h_V^2],
 W=120*(N-1)*(P-1)*(P-2)/N^6 *
       [M*T_U^4*T_V^6*N*(N-1+u4)+M*(M-1)*L_N],
 F2=2*(Eeta+Ezeta), F3=2*(E3+Ec), F4=E4.            (2)

All constants are nonnegative. For all s>0,delta>0,

 g-m_N <= (1+delta)*s^3/v_s^2*(sqrt(A)+s*sqrt(W))^2
       +3*(1+1/delta)/v_s^2*(s^2*F2+s^3*F3+s^4*F4). (3)

For the exact R_N in038(10), define

 a=(N+u4-3)/N, b=(P+v4-3)/N,
 Q(s)=v_s^3+beta*(a+b)*v_s*s^2+beta*a*b*s^3,
 D(s)=v_s^2*Q(s), delta_N=1/floor(sqrt(N)),
 eps_N=delta_N*A+3*(1+1/delta_N)*(F2+F3+F4),
 K_N=A*(Q(1)-1)+(1+delta_N)*(A+2*W).

For 0<=s<=1 the requested estimate and its integral are

 0<=R_N(s)<=eps_N*s^2+K_N*s^4,                      (4)
 half integral_0^s R_N(t)dt<=eps_N*s^3/6+K_N*s^5/10. (5)

In particular the full finite-N two-sided information bound is

 -A*(D(1)-1)*s^5/10
 <= B_N(s)-A*s^4/8
 <= eps_N*s^3/6+K_N*s^5/10.                         (6)

For fixed priors with positive aspect ratios bounded above,
F2,F3,F4=O(1/N), W,A,Q(1) are uniformly bounded,
eps_N=O(N^(-1/2)), and K_N is uniformly bounded.
If alpha_N->alpha>0,beta_N->beta>0, every limiting information
envelope therefore satisfies

 B(s)=alpha*beta^2*s^4/8+O(s^5), 0<=s<=1,            (7)

with the explicit remainder constants in (6). Existence or uniqueness
of the information limit is not required. The finite-N error in (6)
is additive O(N^(-1/2)*s^3), not a pure uniform Taylor remainder
after dividing by s^4 arbitrarily close to zero.

Equivalently the normalized mutual information has the explicit
finite-N polynomial

 P4_N(s)=beta*s/2-beta^2*s^2/4+beta^3*s^3/6
                              -(beta^4+A)*s^4/8,

and

 -eps_N*s^3/6-K_N*s^5/10
 <= I(X;Y)/d-P4_N(s)
 <= [beta^5+A*(D(1)-1)]*s^5/10.                     (6a)

The elementary identity log(1+x)=x-x^2/2+x^3/3-x^4/4
+integral_0^x t^4/(1+t)dt, valid for all x>=0, pays the log remainder.
Thus the limiting quartic term in I/(NP) is
-(beta^4+alpha*beta^2)*s^4/8, and no prior fourth cumulant enters
at that order within this class. The channel parameter is s=1/Delta;
I(UV^T;Y)=I(X;Y) because deterministic nonzero rescaling of the
input is invertible.

## Non-Gaussian example and whole-family scope

Both priors may independently be uniform on [-sqrt(3),sqrt(3)].
For either law take tau(x)=(3-x^2)/2, eta(x)=x-x^3/3;
for the V law take zeta(x)=-eta(x)/2. Their endpoint values vanish,
and their negative derivatives are x, x^2-1, and tau(x)-1,
respectively. Ordinary one-dimensional integration by parts proves
(1), without a Gaussian prior or a boundary contribution.
Exact constants are T=3/2, fourth moment9/5, t=6/5,
e=8/35, z=2/35, a=3/5, b=h=0.
Gaussian priors also satisfy (1) with tau=1,eta=x,zeta=0.
The result applies to every fixed law satisfying the stated kernel
conditions, not just these examples. Discrete Rademacher priors do
not satisfy (1) for arbitrary smooth tests and are not covered.
Specifically choose a compact smooth cutoff of (3*x-x^3)/2 which
equals that polynomial near {-1,1}. At a Rademacher input, h(u)=u
and h'(u)=0, so E[u*h(u)]=1 while E[tau(u)*h'(u)]=0 for every
finite function tau on its support. This is an obstruction to
applying the present derivative-transfer route to that law, not a
counterexample to quartic universality for discrete priors.

More concretely, each of U and V may have any standardized beta
law, with its own arbitrary fixed positive shape parameters p,q.
Let k=p+q, C=1/k, B=(q-p)*sqrt(k+1)/(k*sqrt(p*q)), and
x=(t-p/k)/sqrt(p*q/[k^2*(k+1)]) for t~Beta(p,q). Then

 tau(x)=1+C+B*x-C*x^2,
 eta(x)=tau(x)*(x+B)/(1+C),
 zeta(x)=B*tau(x)-C*eta(x).

The beta density times tau vanishes at both endpoints, including
when the density itself is unbounded there, because p,q>0.
Direct integration of its derivative proves E[x h]=E[tau h'].
Writing Q=x^2-1, the identity tau-1=B*x-C*Q and applying this
first identity to x*h(x) give
(1+C)E[Q*h]=E[tau*(x+B)*h']; this proves the eta identity.
The zeta identity follows by the same linear relation tau-1.
All kernels are bounded on the compact standardized support, so
every hypothesis of (1) is paid. This covers two asymmetric beta
priors as well as the symmetric subfamily. For an asymmetric exact

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:15:36.157488+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_77fdca3bb28312596952beb32b6bebf13676562a75fe0943c5ce0317951c7fab","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 1 (Methodological scope and structural innovations) of arXiv:2609.01589, 'Uniform stability of expanding simple waves for Euler--Poisson--Boltzmann: a singular comp'] \normalfont
Write $\mathrm{N1}$--$\mathrm{N6}$ for the defining features of \cref{thm:main}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=*]
\item the warm-ion Euler--Poisson system with Maxwell--Boltzmann electrons,
  $p_i'(n)\ge p_*>0$;
\item the boundaryless cylinder $\R\times\T$ and a prescribed smooth
  expanding planar simple wave connecting two distinct neutral end states;
\item fully two-dimensional $H^s$ perturbations, completely removing any 
  irrotationality or zero-vorticity hypothesis;
\item stability under relative perturbations that are strictly independent of 
  $\eps$; $\eps$-preparedness is imposed only to capture the expansion rate;
\item for every finite $M$, the construction of an even Debye composite through 
  order $\eps^{2M}$ yielding a residual of $O(\eps^{2M+2})$;
\item a uniform lifespan on every fixed $[t_0,T]$, $t_0\ge0$, based on a novel 
  compensated topology that directly controls $\norm\psi_{H^s}+\eps\norm{\nabla\psi}_{H^s}$ 
  without $\eps^{-1}$ losses over the distinct end states.
\end{enumerate}
Contextualized against the existing literature, these contributions advance the 
state of the art in the following ways:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Cordier--Grenier \cite{cordier2000quasineutral} laid the rigorous 1D foundation 
  for the ion--Boltzmann quasineutral limit. The present work substantially advances 
  this theory by capturing fully two-dimensional rotational dynamics \textup{(N3)} 
  and simultaneously managing the distinct distinct-end-state geometry \textup{(N2)} 
  over an arbitrary finite-order hierarchy \textup{(N4)}--\textup{(N5)}.

\item Wang \cite{wang2005quasineutral} provided multidimensional uniform-lifespan theories for 
  periodic problems yielding incompressible Euler and Navier--Stokes limits. Our 
  framework successfully addresses the distinct analytical challenges of a 
  compressible flow limit connecting heterogeneous far fields.

\item Peng--Wang--Yong \cite{peng2006quasi} rigorously justified finite-order 
  expansions for periodic non-isentropic flows. We pioneer this hierarchical expansion 
  for the compressible ion--Boltzmann limit \textup{(N1)}, introducing the relative 
  compensated topology \textup{(N6)} strictly required to handle the dispersing background.

\item G\'erard-Varet--Han-Kwan--Rousset \cite{gerard2013quasineutral,gerard2014quasineutral} 
  masterfully resolved the multidimensional half-space problem, where boundary data 
  generate Debye layers. We complement this by solving the Cauchy stability problem 
  for a boundaryless wave \textup{(N2)}, where the analytical stiffness stems entirely 
  from the internal singular electric transition.

\item Slemrod--Sternberg \cite{slemrod2001quasi} provided a comprehensive 
  center-to-wall asymptotic analysis for bounded plasmas. In contrast, our focus is 
  the Cauchy stability of the class \textup{(N2)}--\textup{(N4)} on an unbounded cylinder, 
  avoiding boundary layers to isolate the wave asymptotics.
\end{enumerate}
In summary, the present paper develops a novel compensated energy topology that 
rigorously isolates the stability of the smooth expanding wave from the singular 
Debye scaling. By establishing uniform nonlinear stability over a heterogeneous 
background, this framework provides a critical analytical stepping stone toward 
the full global geometric theory of multidimensional quasineutral rarefactions. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}
