{"assumptions":["f is 1-periodic and Lebesgue integrable over one period"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.262136+00:00","domain":"Fourier series on the circle","id":"claim_82389d4e8f4fb9ac13809cff86a8079ad0ec59befe3fccefb0bd229569f870b4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $\\mathbb{T}=\\mathbb{R}/\\mathbb{Z}$, identified with $[0,1)$ with Lebesgue measure, and $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb{T})$. The Fourier coefficients are $\\hat f(n)=\\int_0^1 f(x)e^{-2\\pi i n x}\\,dx$, $n\\in\\mathbb{Z}$, with $|\\hat f(n)|\\le\\|f\\|_1$; the Fourier series is $\\sum_n\\hat f(n)e^{2\\pi i n x}$. Convolution on $\\mathbb T$ is $(f*g)(x)=\\int_0^1 f(x-y)g(y)\\,dy$ and $\\widehat{f*g}(n)=\\hat f(n)\\hat g(n)$. The symmetric partial sums are $S_Nf(x)=\\sum_{|n|\\le N}\\hat f(n)e^{2\\pi i n x}=(f*D_N)(x)$ with the Dirichlet kernel $D_N(x)=\\sum_{|n|\\le N}e^{2\\pi i n x}=\\sin((2N+1)\\pi x)/\\sin(\\pi x)$; $D_N$ is even, $\\int_0^1 D_N=1$, but it changes sign and its Lebesgue constants $\\|D_N\\|_{L^1(\\mathbb T)}=\\frac{4}{\\pi^2}\\log N+O(1)$ tend to infinity. The Fejer (Cesaro) means are $\\sigma_Nf=\\frac{1}{N+1}\\sum_{k=0}^N S_kf=f*F_N$ with the Fejer kernel $F_N(x)=\\frac{1}{N+1}\\left(\\frac{\\sin((N+1)\\pi x)}{\\sin(\\pi x)}\\right)^2=\\sum_{|n|\\le N}\\left(1-\\frac{|n|}{N+1}\\right)e^{2\\pi i n x}$; $F_N\\ge0$, $\\int_0^1F_N=1$, and $F_N(x)\\le\\min\\{N+1,\\;1/((N+1)\\sin^2(\\pi x))\\}$. Periods other than 1 are handled by rescaling (for period $2\\pi$: $\\hat f(n)=\\frac1{2\\pi}\\int_{-\\pi}^{\\pi}f(t)e^{-int}dt$).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:19:56.667909+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82569eac319851fc9b61918b4456d2ede367ff53dd139ff902162bd4638e0254","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] Given a constant $a>0$, let $v:[0,\tau]\times\R \rightarrow \R$ be a function with properties:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] The function $x\rightarrow v(t,x)$ increases at all times.
    \item[(ii)] For every Lipschitz curve $t\rightarrow\gamma(t)$ with derivative $\dot\gamma(t)\ge a - \varepsilon$, the composite function $t\rightarrow v(t,\gamma(t))$ is decreasing. 
\end{itemize}
Consider any couple of Lipschitz functions $y,z:[0,\tau]\rightarrow \R$ such that 
\[
y(0)=z(0)=0, \quad \dot y(t) \ge a,  \ \dot z(t)\ge a \quad \mbox{for a.e. } t\in[0,\tau],
\]
and define 
\[
v_{max}=\sup_{t,x} v(t,x), \quad v_{min}=\inf_{t,x} v(t,x), \quad \delta(t) = \sup_{0<s<t}|y(s)-z(s)|.
\]
Then, for every $t\in[0,\tau]$ one has
\begin{equation}
    \int_0^t |v(s,y(s))-v(s,z(s)))| ds \leq 2 \delta(t)\,\frac{v_{max}-v_{min}}{\epsilon}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:36:16.006131+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82658a1c1f8b54f1802bd8f224904b9f0569dee37575c18bc3c9b1f6d1879948","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:HI-before-HS of arXiv:2606.27573, 'Conditional Path Decomposition at the Infimum and Maximum Drawdowns for Spectrally Negativ'] Under $\mathbb{P}_{a,b}^{<}$, the pre-$H_I$ process, the intermediate process
$$
\{X_{H_I+u}:0\le u\le H_S-H_I\},
$$
and the post-$H_S$ process are independent.  Their laws are as follows.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The pre-infimum process is the Doob transform of the process killed on leaving $(a,b)$ through the lower boundary, with
\begin{equation}\hspace{-1,4cm}
h_1(x)=
\frac{W^{(\gamma)\prime}(x-a)W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)-W^{(\gamma)\prime}(b-a)W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)}
     {\big(W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)\big)^2},
\qquad a<x<b.
\end{equation}

\item The intermediate process has the law of $a+\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is the Doob transform of a spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process killed at $\tau_{b-a}^+\wedge\tau_0^-$, with
\begin{equation}
h_2(z)=e^{-\Phi(\gamma)(b-a-z)}\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(z)}{W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)},
\qquad 0<z<b-a.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, in the original coordinate $x=a+z$,
\[
h_2^a(x)=e^{-\Phi(\gamma)(b-x)}\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)}.
\]

\item The post-$H_S$ process is the Doob transform of the process killed on leaving $(a,b)$ before $T$, with
\begin{equation}
h_3(x)=1-Z^{(\gamma)}(x-a)+\big(Z^{(\gamma)}(b-a)-1\big)\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)},
\qquad a<x<b.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:09:43.679990+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8279799a429a348dfcdaa6e7c1791029b57a934fd81414128a1cb82a89e070d9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition p:mppmix_double of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Fix $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$ and $r \in (0, \infty)$. Assume that $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ satisfies condition~(ii:mppmix_double of the paper)  of Lemma~(p:mppmixcl_double of the paper). Let $\xi: \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{K}'$ be a marking function such that $\xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mu}) =  \xi^{(r)}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mu}) =\xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mu}\cap B_r(x))$ for all $(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mu}) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}}$. Consider the marked point process $\dbtilde\mathcal{P}=\sum_{x \in \mathcal{P}} \delta_{(x,V(x))}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d\times \mathbb{K}'$ where $V(x) := \xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})$.  

Then, for  all $f \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^p),$   $g \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^q)$, for almost all $\bk x1{p+q}\in\mathbb{R}^{d(p+q)}$ such that $s:=d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q}) >4r$, and with ${w}_0= 4(p+q)\theta_d r^d$
we have
\begin{align} \nonumber
& \Big| \mathbb {E} _{\bk x1{p+q}}[f(\bk V1{p})g(\bk V{p+1}{p+q})]\rho^{(p+q)}(\bk x1{p+q}) -
\mathbb {E} _{\bk x1p}[f(\bk V1p)] \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1{p}) \; \mathbb {E} _{\bk x{p+1}{p+q}}[g(\bk V{p+1}{p+q})]\rho^{(q)}(\bk
x{p+1}{p+q}) \Big|
\\
&\le 
\phi( \frac{s}{2})\sum_{l=1}^\infty \frac{w_0^l}{l!}  C_{l+p+q}
=:\phi( \frac{s}{2})\hat{C}_{p+q}<\infty.
\end{align}

Thus the marked point process
 $\dbtilde\mathcal{P}$ satisfies the inequality~(equation e.Bmppmixing of the paper)  in Definition~(B-omega-mixing of the paper)(Bmixing of the paper) 
for $s>4r$, with  $\omega_{p+q}(s):=\hat C_{p+q}\phi(s/2)$ where  $p,q,\phi$ are as above.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:37:25.868627+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82a1ca92e8af08ba0b1ddcbf5b1ac99c46ba70dc9ae6ad40340f99c8872e8abe","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.29501, 'Disorder Thresholds and Free Energy of Brownian Directed Polymers with\\ Product and Radia'] Set \(m:=q-r\). Let \(0<s_0<\cdots<s_m<T\), and

\[
  d_\ell:=s_\ell-s_{\ell-1}\quad(1\le\ell\le m),
  \qquad s_m-s_0\le qu,
  \qquad
  \lambda(t):=\frac{\Lambda(t)}{1+t}.
\]
Thus \(d_\ell\) is the transition duration between the
\((\ell-1)\)-st and \(\ell\)-th Gaussian vertices in each chain. After
relabeling the paired Gaussian variables as \(x_\ell,x'_\ell\), the
Gaussian vertices are \((s_\ell,x_\ell)\) and \((s_\ell,x'_\ell)\),
arising from the pairing in
\eqref{eq:critical-retained-gaussian-pairing}. Recall the anchor
\(Q(z-B_{\widehat t})\) selected above. Its original index is \(j_*\),
so \(\widehat t=t_{j_*}\); the symbol \(z\) continues to denote its
original spatial coordinate and is distinct from the relabeled
Gaussian variables \(x_\ell,x'_\ell\). When \(j_*=0\), one has
\(z=\bar x_0\), the original left endpoint. Assume
\(0<\widehat t<T\) and

\[
  |\widehat t-s_0|\le qu,
\]
and write \(\rho:=|\widehat t-s_0|\). Since \(j_*\in A\), whereas the
first-chain Gaussian indices lie in \(A^c\), one has
\(\widehat t\ne s_\ell\) for every \(\ell\). Hence exactly one of the
following cases occurs (empty products below are one):

\[
  \begin{array}{lll}
    k=0: & \alpha=s_0-\widehat t>0,\\
    1\le k\le m: & 0<\alpha=\widehat t-s_{k-1}<d_k,\\
    k=m+1: & \alpha=\widehat t-s_m>0.
  \end{array}
\]

Accordingly, define
\begin{align}
  \Gamma^{(1)}_{0,\alpha}(z,\mathbf x)
  &:=\1_{\{z\in\mathcal C_T\}}\,p_\alpha(x_0-z)
    \prod_{\ell=1}^{m}p_{d_\ell}(x_\ell-x_{\ell-1}), \\
  \Gamma^{(1)}_{k,\alpha}(z,\mathbf x)
  &:=\1_{\{x_0\in\mathcal C_T\}}
    \prod_{\ell=1}^{k-1}p_{d_\ell}(x_\ell-x_{\ell-1})
    p_\alpha(z-x_{k-1}) \notag\\[-1mm]
  &\hspace{18mm}\times
    p_{d_k-\alpha}(x_k-z)
    \prod_{\ell=k+1}^{m}p_{d_\ell}(x_\ell-x_{\ell-1}),
    \qquad 1\le k\le m, \\
  \Gamma^{(1)}_{m+1,\alpha}(z,\mathbf x)
  &:=\1_{\{x_0\in\mathcal C_T\}}
    \prod_{\ell=1}^{m}p_{d_\ell}(x_\ell-x_{\ell-1})
    p_\alpha(z-x_m).
  
\end{align}

The second-chain kernels are

\begin{align}
  \Gamma^{(2)}_0(\mathbf x')
  &:=\1_{\{x'_0\in\mathcal C_T\}}
    \prod_{\ell=1}^{m}p_{d_\ell}(x'_\ell-x'_{\ell-1}), \\ 
  \Gamma^{(2)}_1(a',\bar x'_0,\mathbf x')
  &:=\1_{\{\bar x'_0\in\mathcal C_T\}}
    p_{a'}(x'_0-\bar x'_0)
    \prod_{\ell=1}^{m}p_{d_\ell}(x'_\ell-x'_{\ell-1}),
  \qquad 0<a'<qu.
  
\end{align}

For \(\varepsilon'=0\), set

\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak a^{(0)}_{k,\alpha}(B)
  &:={}
  \int Q(z-B_{\widehat t})\Gamma^{(1)}_{k,\alpha}(z,\mathbf x)
  \Gamma^{(2)}_0(\mathbf x')
  \prod_{\ell=0}^{m}Q(x_\ell-x'_\ell)\,
  \dd z\,\dd\mathbf x\,\dd\mathbf x',
\end{aligned}
\]
and, for any interval \(I'\subset(0,qu)\) satisfying
\(0<s_0-a'<T/4\) for every \(a'\in I'\), set

\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak a^{(1)}_{k,\alpha}(B)
  &:={}
  \int_{I'}\int Q(z-B_{\widehat t})
  Q(\bar x'_0-B_{s_0-a'})
  \Gamma^{(1)}_{k,\alpha}(z,\mathbf x)
  \Gamma^{(2)}_1(a',\bar x'_0,\mathbf x')\\[-1mm]
  &\hspace{20mm}\times
  \prod_{\ell=0}^{m}Q(x_\ell-x'_\ell),
  \dd z\,\dd\mathbf x\,\dd\mathbf x'
  \,\dd\bar x'_0\,\dd a'.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then, uniformly in \(B\), \(k\), \(\alpha\), and \(I'\),

\begin{equation}
  \mathfrak a^{(\varepsilon')}_{k,\alpha}(B)
  \le
  C^{m+1}\Lambda(T)^2\Lambda(2qu)^4
  \prod_{\ell=1}^{m}\lambda(d_\ell),
  \qquad \varepsilon'\in\{0,1\}.
  
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T14:01:11.606209+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82b243bfd1bdebcf927fafa46de1d7d9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 2.5 of arXiv:2512.19517v1, 'Spiking and Resetting' (Cédric Bernardin and Vsevolod Vladimirovich Tarsamaev); numbered Proposition 6 in the earlier card; corrected to the increment form]

## Proposition 2.5 (increment form)

Assume the standing hypotheses of Section 1: (f,h\in C^2([0,1])), (f(1)<0<f(0)), (h(1)=0), (h'(1)\ne0), and (h(x)>0) on ([0,1)). Let

\[
e_1^\varepsilon=\inf\{t\ge0:X_t^\varepsilon>y_*^\varepsilon\},\qquad
e_2^\varepsilon=\inf\{t\ge e_1^\varepsilon:X_t^\varepsilon=0\},
\]

and define the post-(e_1^\varepsilon) holding time

\[
d_2^\varepsilon:=e_2^\varepsilon-e_1^\varepsilon.
\]

Then, for every (t\ge0),

\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\mathbb P(d_2^\varepsilon>t)=e^{f(1)t},
\]

so (d_2^\varepsilon\Rightarrow \operatorname{Exp}(-f(1))).

The proof in the paper restarts the deterministic flow at (e_1^\varepsilon) with local time (s=0); its displayed survival integral is therefore for (d_2^\varepsilon), not the absolute epoch (e_2^\varepsilon). The source says that after the stopping time “the process evolves deterministically until the next reset” (v1 HTML lines 252-257), which is precisely an increment statement.

## Later alternating holding-time sentence

For the recursively defined epochs (e_k^\varepsilon), the strong Markov property applies to the increments

\[
e_{2k+1}^\varepsilon-e_{2k}^\varepsilon,
\qquad
e_{2k+2}^\varepsilon-e_{2k+1}^\varepsilon,
\]

not to the increasing absolute epochs themselves. The alternating increments are the quantities that can be independent and have the two respective holding-time laws. Any downstream card should preserve this distinction.

## Why the absolute-time statement cannot hold as written

For every (\varepsilon), (e_2^\varepsilon\ge e_1^\varepsilon), hence

\[
\mathbb P(e_2^\varepsilon>t)\ge\mathbb P(e_1^\varepsilon>t).
\]

This stochastic order must persist at continuity points of any weak limits. Yet the paper permits (f(x)=1-3x) and (h(x)=1-x), for which (f(0)=1) and (f(1)=-2). Its two displayed absolute-time limits would require (e^{-2t}\ge e^{-t}) for (t>0), an immediate contradiction. No additional relation between (f(0)) and (f(1)) is present in the standing hypotheses.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T14:24:13.477078+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82bf60ef29eb019353b57d9cb9b4acf8aa885aaabf0b0cca759d50f62863a1a2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A standard Brownian motion, or Wiener process, is a real-valued stochastic process (W_t)_{t >= 0} on a probability space such that (i) W_0 = 0 almost surely; (ii) for 0 <= s < t the increment W_t - W_s is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance t - s; (iii) increments over disjoint time intervals are independent; (iv) almost every sample path t |-> W_t is continuous. Existence is Wiener's theorem (constructed for instance by the Levy-Ciesielski series or as the Kolmogorov-extension limit with continuity from Kolmogorov's criterion, since E|W_t - W_s|^4 = 3 (t - s)^2). Consequences packaged with the definition: the covariance is E[W_s W_t] = min(s, t); paths are almost surely nowhere differentiable and have unbounded variation on every interval, with quadratic variation t; Brownian scaling c^{-1/2} W_{c t}, time inversion t W_{1/t}, and reflection are again Brownian motions; W is a continuous martingale and a Markov process with transition density the Gaussian kernel. Conditions (i)-(iii) characterise the finite-dimensional laws; (iv) selects the continuous version, which is the object meant in every theorem about paths.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:04:55.803679+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82e1fb73b905c93cef6ba328d232023d2182fb50d755a7adee4701fa8046681d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemm l:mesh-geo-deloc of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] For $u=(0,z;\delta^{3/2},w)$ with $z,w\in J^\delta$, 
    let $\Gamma_u$ be the mesh geodesic (see (def:discrete-LPP of the paper)).
    For $k\in\llbracket1,n-1\rrbracket$, we define the event
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{MeshGeoDeloc}^k_u \coloneqq  
        \left\{
            (\bm{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{near}}, \bm{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{far}}, \bm{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{bdry}}) : 
            \left|
                \Gamma_u(t_k)
            \right|
            \wedge
            \left|

    where the supremum is over all $u=(0,z;\delta^{3/2},w)$ with $z,w\in J^\delta$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:13:22.513685+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8311a7454b8bc517593c2e5d2443f81f8d93fbe7c44dfa12d993ef75ca467d82","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn localization of measure of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] Let $\Omega \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ be a simply connected domain, and let $u$ be a marked boundary point. Let $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ be distinct prime ends of $\partial \Omega$, and let $U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n$ be disjoint closed neighborhoods of $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ in $\Omega$ such that $u \notin U_j$ for all $j$ and $U_i \cap U_j = \emptyset$ for $1 \leq i < j \leq n$. 

We consider probability measures
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}
\]
on $n$-tuples of unparametrized continuous curves, where each curve starts at $z_j$, is contained in $U_j$, and exits $U_j$ almost surely. 

A family of such measures, indexed by different choices of neighborhoods $\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)$, is called \emph{compatible} if for all $U_j \subset U_j'$, the measure $\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}$ is obtained from 
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1', U_2', \ldots, U_n'\right)}
\]
by restricting each curve to the portion before it first exits the smaller domain $U_j$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.344422+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_831e2c88dc1a290dec8fd9a96edd614d49cb237c6387a23f5814892437cd717a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Satz thm:HigherOrderIndep of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $X$ be a random vector with independent components, $f: \mathcal{X} \to {\mathbb R}$ a measurable function satisfying $f = f(X) \in L^\infty(\IP)$, ${\mathbb E} f(X) = 0$ and $d \in {\mathbb N}$.

        \[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:07:56.709839+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_832623f4fb151fca5d4960658b8dfc5c81436aea135e9b4afa95c31912cd2cb3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:vary of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\mathcal W$ be a white noise with respect to some filtration $\mathcal F$. Let $\overline{\delta}$ be a drift function with respect to $\mathcal F$. We call a collection of continuous processes $\mathcal S=(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ a ${\rm BESQ}(\overline{\delta})$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ if 
   
    (1) The restriction of $\mathcal S$ to each $A_i$ is a ${\rm BESQ}^{\delta_i}$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$.

    (2) The regularity conditions of Definition (def:BESQflow of the paper) hold.
 

If $E$ is a (possibly random) Borel set, we call $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow killed on $E$ the flow obtained from the $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow by absorbing the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at $0$ at time $\inf\{x \in E\cap (r,\infty) \,:\, \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$.

 If $E={\mathbb R}$, we will simply say that $\mathcal S$ is a killed  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow. We call general  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow a $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow or a  killed $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:11:44.460227+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8326bce44c888e2b0437f2230fd0425e811f63e685f49590fb6fb1fa97d42591","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $V$ be a $k[H]$-module. Let $R$ be such that it contains $R_s$. Let $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus p\mathbb Z$. Let $o$ be the order of $[t]_{p^s}\in (\mathbb Z/p^s\mathbb Z)^{\times}$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} The following statements are equivalent.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (1.a)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is cyclic.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.b)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is indecomposable.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.c)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is strongly indecomposable.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.d)} We have $\imath_V\in\{0,1\}$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.e)} Each lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ is cyclic.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.f)} Each lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ is cyclic and strongly indecomposable.

\medskip
{\bf (2)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ has a lift $\mathcal H$ to $R$ which is an end-hull of $V$ and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules. Moreover, if $\jmath_V=0$, then we can also assume that $r_{\mathcal H}=0$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} Suppose that $V$ is cyclic. Let $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ be two lifts of $V$. Then the $R[H]$-modules $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ are isomorphic if and only if the $B[H]$-modules $\mathcal V_1\otimes_R B$ and $\mathcal V_2\otimes_R B$ are isomorphic.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} The $k[H]$-modules $V$ and $V^{(t)}$ are isomorphic.

\smallskip
{\bf (5)} The following statements are equivalent.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (5.a)} There exists a lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ which is $t$-invariant and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules (resp.\ which is $t$-invariant and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules with $r_{\mathcal V^H}=0$).

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (5.b)} For each $b\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket\setminus o\llbracket1,\lfloor\frac{p^s}{t}\rfloor\rrbracket$ such that $\mu_V(b)\neq 0$, $\mu_V(b)$ is a sum of cardinals of orbits of the action of $[t]_{p^s}$ on $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$ (resp.\ $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s^{\ast})$), equivalently of subsets $\Phi$ of $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$ (resp.\ $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s^{\ast})$) with $[t]_{p^s}\cdot\Phi=\Phi$.

\medskip
{\bf (6)} Suppose that $p$ is odd, $[t]_{p^s}=[p^s-1]_{p^s}$ (equivalently, $o=2$) and $\dim_k(V)$ is even. Then $V$ has a lift to $R$ which is a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules and is $t$-invariant.

\medskip
{\bf (7)} Suppose that $p$ is odd, $[t]_{p^s}=[p^s-1]_{p^s}$, $\mu_V(d)$ is even for each odd $d\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$, and $\jmath_V=0$. Then $V$ has a lift $\mathcal V$ to $R$ which is a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules and is $t$-invariant with $r_{\mathcal V}=0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:43:45.378682+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_832e0a6a6b6a7e7e307cae8b5f1d37301d5cf39a0e2ed20a8a05b6f5d2991a88","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 (Finite von Neumann algebra and trace) of arXiv:2609.03993, 'The Endpoint Fractional Riesz Estimate on the Hamming Cube'] A concrete von Neumann algebra $\cN$ is a unital $*$-subalgebra of
		bounded operators on a Hilbert space that is closed in the weak operator
		topology.  A finite trace on $\cN$ is a linear functional
		$\tau:\cN\to\mathbb C$ satisfying
		\[
		\tau(x^*x)\ge0,\quad
		\tau(x^*x)=0\Longrightarrow x=0,\quad
		\tau(xy)=\tau(yx),\quad
		\tau(1)<\infty,
		\]
		and normality, meaning preservation of suprema of increasing bounded nets
		of positive elements.  We normalize finite traces by $\tau(1)=1$ unless
		an unnormalized matrix trace is explicitly specified.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T07:39:33.522659+00:00","domain":"inner product spaces, Gram matrices and orthogonal projection","id":"claim_8330c1df610861744d90a78e2b4e245f46b17ad569d1f13a55649116daf74193","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For vectors u and v in an inner product space, the Gram determinant det [[<u,u>, <u,v>], [<v,u>, <v,v>]] equals ||u||^2 ||v||^2 - |<u, v>|^2, which is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when u and v are linearly dependent.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.690500+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8331965cbab96b277d94421b79becb5e084ed4d4bb680b695e7d535f83d2fc9c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 113 (Bracket-corrected finite-dimensional It\^o flow) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix $p\in(1/\alpha,3)$ and choose
\begin{equation}
 1<\nu<\frac p{p-1}.
\end{equation}
Assume $V_0$ is bounded globally Lipschitz and
$V\in\operatorname{Lip}^{\rho+1}(\R^m;\mathcal L(H,\R^m))$ for some
$\rho>p$.  For $x\in G_*^{\boldsymbol\vartheta}$ define $\Psi$ by
\begin{equation}
 \dd Z
 =V_0(Z)\,\dd t+V(Z)\,\dd\mathbf X^S
 -\frac12\langle\mathcal W_V(Z),\dd Q\rangle_{\rm tr}.
\end{equation}

{"assumptions":["the prescribed zeros form a sequence with no finite accumulation point (|a_n| → ∞ if infinite)","the integers p_n satisfy Σ_n (r/|a_n|)^{p_n+1} < ∞ for every r > 0","multiplicities are encoded by repetition in the list"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.483061+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_8351e8110eb79c81b9035b42e43878b64a0b2a5e2f562abb232805d1c7984b15","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Define the elementary factors E_0(w) = 1 - w and, for p ≥ 1, E_p(w) = (1 - w) exp(w + w^2/2 + ... + w^p/p). Choose nonnegative integers p_n such that the series Σ_n (r/|a_n|)^{p_n + 1} converges for every r > 0 (the choice p_n = n - 1 always works). Then the product P(z) = z^m Π_n E_{p_n}(z/a_n) converges absolutely and uniformly on compact subsets of C and defines an entire function whose zero set is exactly {0} (with multiplicity m, omitted if m = 0) together with the points a_n, each with multiplicity equal to the number of times it is listed. Conversely, every entire function f whose zeros are exactly these (with these multiplicities) has the form f(z) = exp(g(z)) P(z) for some entire function g. {"assumptions":["H is a complex Hilbert space","in (a): A is self-adjoint, not merely symmetric","in (b): U(t) unitary for every real t, group law on all of ℝ, and strong (or weak) continuity"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.771144+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, spectral theory, quantum dynamics","id":"claim_83536995a52f9d6f74e19531f52ed168e8c98c144cb0af2e28337b9615d9255d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H be a complex Hilbert space. (a) If A is self-adjoint on H, then U(t) = e^{itA} (Borel functional calculus) defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: U(t + s) = U(t)U(s), U(0) = I, U(t)* = U(−t), and t ↦ U(t)x is continuous on ℝ for each x. Moreover D(A) = {x ∈ H : lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/t exists} and for x ∈ D(A) that limit equals iAx; D(A) is invariant under each U(t). (b) Conversely, let (U(t))_{t ∈ ℝ} be a family of unitary operators with U(t + s) = U(t)U(s), U(0) = I, and t ↦ U(t)x continuous for each x ∈ H. Then there is a unique self-adjoint operator A with U(t) = e^{itA} for all t, namely Ax = lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/(it) on the set where the limit exists. (c) Weak continuity suffices in (b): if t ↦ ⟨U(t)x, y⟩ is continuous for all x, y, the group is strongly continuous, since ‖U(t)x − x‖² = 2‖x‖² − 2Re⟨U(t)x, x⟩. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.904699+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8374c7b57703b981a0eb69503356340ab30b6c11c70146ddff8d3063533aa779","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Conjecture of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] For each $d \ge 2$ and each $1 \le k \le d - 1$, there exists $0 < \lambda_{c,k}<\infty$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.555366+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_83a24b0c264cb398aae42cfe985efd4a6c45611389c6cae027212d499bf65535","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 17 (Epi-convergence) of arXiv:2604.02312, 'A weak transport approach to the Schrödinger--Bass bridge'] Let ${\psi_n,\psi:\Rd \to \mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}}$, and let $E \subset \Rd$. We say that $\psi_n\to \psi$ in \emph{epi-convergence} on $E$ if, for every $x\in E$,
    \begin{align*}
        \psi(x)
        &\le
        \liminf_{n\to\infty} \psi_n(x_n)
        \quad\text{for every sequence }x_n\to x\text{ in }E,\\
        \psi(x)
        &\ge
        \limsup_{n\to\infty} \psi_n(x_n)
        \quad\text{for some sequence }x_n\to x\text{ in }E.
    \end{align*}
    Moreover, for ${\varphi_n,\varphi:\Rd \to \mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}}$ we say that $\varphi_n\to \varphi$ in \emph{hypo-convergence} on $E$ if $-\varphi_n\to -\varphi$ in epi-convergence on $E$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:12:13.585474+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_83be08c5ce16833d709f234da619c98fc2dfe15d587232719c2deb8fd78585ee","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 43 (Finite-dimensional relative entropy chain rule) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Fix \(N\geq1\).  Let \(P_t^N\) and \(Q_t^N\) be the laws of two
diffusions on \((\R^d)^N\) with common diffusion coefficient
\(\sqrt{2\varepsilon}I\) and respective drifts \(b_t^N\) and
\(\bar b_t^N\), that is, with Fokker-Planck equations given by
\begin{equation}
    \partial_tP_t^N
    =
    -\nabla\cdot(b_t^NP_t^N)+\varepsilon\Delta P_t^N,
    \qquad
    \partial_tQ_t^N
    =
    -\nabla\cdot(\bar b_t^NQ_t^N)+\varepsilon\Delta Q_t^N,
\end{equation}
where \(\varepsilon>0\).
Suppose that \(P_0^N,Q_0^N\in\mathcal P_2((\R^d)^N)\)
and that, for every \(T<\infty\), \(b_t^N\) and
\(\bar b_t^N\) are in $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\alpha/2,\,1+\alpha}
    \bigl((0,T]\times\mathbb R^{dN};\mathbb R^{dN}\bigr)$ for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$, and
satisfy
\[
    \|b_t^N(X)\|+\|\bar b_t^N(X)\|
    \leq C_{N,T}(1+\|X\|),
    \qquad 0\leq t\leq T.
\]
If \(\KL(P_0^N\|Q_0^N)<\infty\), then 
\(u\mapsto\KL(P_u^N\|Q_u^N)\) is locally absolutely continuous and,
for \(0\leq s\leq t\),
\begin{align}
    \KL(P_t^N\|Q_t^N)-\KL(P_s^N\|Q_s^N)
    &=
    \int_s^t\int
       \left\langle
          b_u^N-\bar b_u^N,
          \nabla\log\frac{dP_u^N}{dQ_u^N}
       \right\rangle
       dP_u^N\,du
    \notag\\
    &\quad
    -\varepsilon\int_s^t
       I(P_u^N\|Q_u^N)\,du.

\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

Then there exists a natural equivalence ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$G$-gl}^{\circ}[-]\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\Phi_G(-)(\textup{id}_G)$ of functors $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\Spc$, where $\Phi_G\colon{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$G$-gl}\to\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})$ is obtained from the unique equivalence $\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul\Spc_\textup{Glo}$ by evaluating at $\mathbb B{G}$.
    \begin{proof}
        If we continue to view $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ as an \emph{unenriched} category, the cocartesian unstraightening of the 1-functor $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\textbf{\textup{Cat}}\hookrightarrow\Cat_\infty,X\mapsto \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_{/X}$ is given by $\Ar(\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top})$. Postcomposition with $\Phi_G$ and localizing therefore yields a natural transformation ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}[-]\to\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})_{/\Phi_G(-)}$ given pointwise by the composite equivalence
        \[
            {{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}[X]\xrightarrow[\raise3.5pt\hbox{$\smash{\scriptstyle\sim}$}]{\,\textup{Lemma~(lemma:slice-over-fibrant of the paper)}\,}({{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl})_{/X}\xrightarrow[\raise3.5pt\hbox{$\smash{\scriptstyle\sim}$}]{\;\,\Phi_G\,\;}\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})_{/\Phi_G(X)},
        \]
        which clearly restricts to ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}^\circ[X]\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})_{/\Phi_G(X)}^\circ$. We will now construct for every small $\infty$-category $T$ with a terminal object $1$ a natural equivalence $\PSh(T)_{/-}^\circ\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ev_1$ of functors $\PSh(T)\to\Spc$; applying this to $T=\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}}$ (with terminal object $\textup{id}_{\mathbb B{G}}$) will then complete the proof of the theorem.
        
        To prove the claim, note that the cocartesian unstraightening of $\PSh(T)_{/-}$ is given by the target map $\Ar(\PSh(T))\to\PSh(T)$, so that the cocartesian unstraightening of $\PSh(T)_{/-}^\circ$ is given by the forgetful map $\PSh(T)_{1/}\to\PSh(T)$. The latter is also the cocartesian unstraightening of ${\textup{Hom}}(1,-)$, which agrees with $\ev_1\colon\PSh(T)\to\Spc$ by the Yoneda lemma.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:10:43.969987+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_83d77facb4109173b9f5744923f556f1c52b23d613094a79d520b7d2573f36f6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:covering of arXiv:2412.04539, 'Counting minimal cutsets and $p_c<1$'] Let $n \geq 1$. Let $P=(p_{i,j})_{i,j \in [n]}$ be a symmetric matrix of non-negative entries such that\footnote{We can think of $P$ as the transition matrix of a Markov chain which is killed at $i$ with probability $1-\sum_{j} p(i,j)$.} $\sum_{j \in [n]} p(i,j) \leq 1$ for all $i \in [n]$. Let $\Gamma$ be the set of all sequences $\gamma=(\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)$ in $[n]$ (for any $k \geq 1$) with $\gamma_0=1$ such that the unique element $i\in [k]$ satisfying both $\gamma_i=1$ and $\{\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_i\} = [n]$ is $i=k$. \[
          p(\gamma) := \prod_{i=1}^k p\left(\gamma_{i-1},\gamma_i\right).
\]

then $\delta :=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{16e^2}$ satisfies

{"assumptions":["f in L^1(R^d) for the weak (1,1) bound; f in L^p for the strong bound","Lebesgue measure on R^d (the doubling property of the measure is what the proof uses)"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751428+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis","id":"claim_83dc1a42b76b6de69325a6175207b7e1669093bf0f53df5985f5dc3e5cdce959","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For f in L^1_loc(R^d) define the centred maximal function Mf(x) = sup_{r > 0} (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy. Then M is of WEAK type (1,1): for every f in L^1(R^d) and every lambda > 0, |{x : Mf(x) > lambda}| <= 3^d ||f||_1 / lambda. For 1 < p <= infinity, M is bounded on L^p: ||Mf||_p <= C(d,p) ||f||_p, with C(d,p) blowing up like p/(p-1) as p decreases to 1. M is NOT bounded on L^1: if f is not almost everywhere zero then Mf(x) >= c_d ||f||_1 / |x|^d for |x| large, which is not integrable, so Mf is in L^1 only when f = 0 a.e. The uncentred maximal function (supremum over all balls containing x) is comparable to the centred one, with constants depending only on d. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Theorem 1.1 and Chapter 3]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X takes values in a finite set of size m","X_hat is a function of Y alone, so X -> Y -> X_hat is a Markov chain","P_e = Pr(X_hat != X)"],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236127+00:00","domain":"information theory","id":"claim_83dc491008b3e031d0e3a0ac5475fb48986b2f077baf5876dcd333a684d89f6b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a discrete random variable taking values in a finite set of size m, let Y be any random variable jointly distributed with X, and let X_hat = g(Y) be any estimator of X computed from Y alone, so that X -> Y -> X_hat forms a Markov chain. Let P_e = Pr(X_hat != X) be the error probability. Then H(X|Y) <= H_b(P_e) + P_e * log(m-1), where H_b(p) = -p*log p - (1-p)*log(1-p) is the binary entropy function. Consequently, if the conditional entropy H(X|Y) is bounded away from 0, the error probability P_e cannot be made arbitrarily small.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:52:57.675095+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_83ec28042911942c9a5c0fc0e3953f1b20a5202fb1e8b8992e6fd469b78b08b6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 9 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional $(n \geq 2)$  forward complete connected Finsler metric measure manifold with $\Lambda_{F}<\infty$. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$. Let $R_{0}>\Lambda_{F}\pi$ be a constant. Given $p \in (\frac{n}{2}, n]$, $\alpha\in [\frac{1}{2},1)$. Then there exist nonnegative constant $\varepsilon =\varepsilon(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$ and positive constants $C_{3}=C_{3}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$ and $\beta =\beta(n,p,\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$ such that when
$$
\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{\Lambda_{F}^{2}}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}\leq \varepsilon ,
$$
we have
\be
{\rm{diam}}(M) \leq \Lambda_{F}^{-1}\left(\pi+C_{3}\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{\Lambda_{F}^{2}}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\beta}\right) \leq \frac{\Lambda_{F}^{-1}(\Lambda_{F}+1)\pi}{2}, 
\ee
where

{"assumptions":["Real Lebesgue density p supported on a finite interval; p>=m>0 almost everywhere","Mean zero and variance one; no continuity, derivative or upper density bound assumed","For the matrix corollary: fixed independent iid real factor laws, Gaussian observation noise, N,P>=2,M>=1, positive finite aspect limits"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:16:22.797292+00:00","domain":"probability; Stein kernels; Gaussian matrix channels","id":"claim_83f6a1f11daf0b73d42501d7da22edf147524c35169a2125815646401fbaafd6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own work, proof (unaudited); standard-form construction, novelty unestablished.
Let p be a Lebesgue density supported on a finite interval [a,b],
p(x)>=m>0 for almost every x in that interval. Assume E u=0,
E u^2=1. No continuity, differentiability, or upper bound on p is
assumed. Define, almost everywhere on its support,

 tau(x)=[integral_x^b y*p(y)dy]/p(x),
 eta(x)=[integral_x^b (y^2-1)*p(y)dy]/p(x),
 zeta(x)=[integral_x^b (tau(y)-1)*p(y)dy]/p(x).       (1)

Then, for every bounded C1 h with bounded derivative,

 E[u*h(u)]=E[tau(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(u^2-1)*h(u)]=E[eta(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(tau(u)-1)*h(u)]=E[zeta(u)*h'(u)],               (2)

and the explicit bounds are

 0<=tau<=1/m, E tau=1,
 |eta|<=2/m, |zeta|<=2/m.                           (3)


Matrix corollary: let U in R^(N by M), V in R^(P by M) be independent iid factor arrays with fixed real laws having the preceding compact-density, centering and variance hypotheses, each with its own positive density floor. Let Z be independent standard Gaussian noise, X=UV^T/sqrt(N), Y=sqrt(s)X+Z, and I be measured in nats. If P/N->alpha>0 and M/N->beta>0 are finite, every limiting upper or lower per-entry information envelope satisfies I(X;Y)/(NP)=beta*s/2-beta^2*s^2/4+beta^3*s^3/6-(beta^4+alpha*beta^2)*s^4/8+O(s^5) as s decreases to zero. The remainder constant depends on the fixed priors and aspect bounds, not the matrix dimensions. No assertion of information-limit uniqueness or discrete-prior coverage is made.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:50:44.876779+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_840b038413d15d1ea0e64bff4b63a374fe56d72cbac494573cc7c974fb37e80c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 61 (Sharp singular Wick multipliers on the torus) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $m\ge2$ and $(m-1)D/(2m)<\sigma\le D/2$, and set
$\beta_m:=m(D/2-\sigma)$.  On
$\mathbb T^D=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^D$ with normalized Haar measure,
define
\[
 X_N(\theta):=\sum_{|x|\le N}g_x\langle x\rangle^{-\sigma}
 e^{\mathrm i x\cdot\theta},
\]
and define its order-$m$ Wick power by
\[
 V_{m,N}(\theta):=\wick{X_N(\theta)^m}
 =\sum_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}
 \wick{g_{x_1}\cdots g_{x_m}}
  \prod_{j=1}^m\bigl(\langle x_j\rangle^{-\sigma}
  \mathbf1_{\{|x_j|\le N\}}\bigr)
 e^{\mathrm i(x_1+\cdots+x_m)\cdot\theta}.
\]
Here the real isonormal process is extended complex-linearly; thus $X_N$
is generally complex-valued, and no relation between $g_x$ and $g_{-x}$
is imposed.  In particular, this is the complexified real-isonormal model,
not the conjugate-symmetric real Fourier model.
Let $J$ be the Fourier multiplier
$Je^{\mathrm iq\cdot\theta}=\langle q\rangle e^{\mathrm iq\cdot\theta}$.
Write $\norm{f}_{H^t}:=\norm{J^tf}_{L^2}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Fix $1\le r<\infty$ and $a,b\ge0$.  Then
$J^{-a}M_{V_{m,N}}J^{-b}$ is Cauchy in
$L^2(\Omega;\Sch_r(L^2(\mathbb T^D)))$ if and only if
\[
 a>\beta_m,\qquad b>\beta_m,\qquad
 a+b>\beta_m+\frac Dr,
\]
which is precisely \eqref{eq:all-order-singular-lattice-range}.  Under these
conditions
it converges in every finite $L^p$, converges almost surely in $\Sch_r$,
and satisfies all rates in
Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-singular-lattice-transfer}.
In particular, trace-norm convergence holds exactly when
\[
 a>\beta_m,\qquad b>\beta_m,\qquad a+b>\beta_m+D.
\]

\item[(ii)] For every $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}

 V_{m,N}\longrightarrow V_m
 \quad\text{in}\quad
 \begin{cases}
  L^2(\Omega;H^{-\beta_m-\varepsilon}(\mathbb T^D)),&\sigma<D/2,\\
  L^2(\Omega;H^{-\varepsilon}(\mathbb T^D)),&\sigma=D/2.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
These Sobolev indices are mean-square sharp: the cutoffs are not Cauchy in
$L^2(\Omega;H^{-\beta_m})$ below the endpoint or in
$L^2(\Omega;L^2(\mathbb T^D))$ at the endpoint.

\item[(iii)] Fix $a,b\ge0$.  The cutoffs
$J^{-a}M_{V_{m,N}}J^{-b}$ converge in
$L^2(\Omega;\cL(L^2(\mathbb T^D)))$ to a random compact operator if and
only if
\begin{equation}

 a>\beta_m,\qquad b>\beta_m.
\end{equation}

\item[(iv)] Fix $1\le r<\infty$.  For the balanced sandwich
$a=b=s/2$, $s\ge0$, the exact
finite-$r$ Schatten phase diagram is
\begin{equation}

 s>\max\left\{2\beta_m,\ \beta_m+\frac Dr\right\}
 \quad(\sigma<D/2),
 \qquad
 s>\frac Dr
 \quad(\sigma=D/2).
\end{equation}
In this balanced case, the compactness condition in part~(iii) reduces to
$s>2\beta_m$, equivalently to $s>0$ when $\sigma=D/2$.
The exact trace-class threshold is $s>\beta_m+D$.
Indeed, the local hypothesis gives $\beta_m<D/2$, so this condition already
implies $s>2\beta_m$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:54:12.280152+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_842f9181e60cd1102d504a29d4a533927cc07b024858ae5269aa08a231230e9d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem main2 of arXiv:2603.14302, 'On Partition Functions for Time-Inhomogeneous Branching Random Walks'] \textsc{(Phase Transition and Universality for Time-inhomogeneous BRW)}
Let $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ be a continuous, non-increasing function with $f(0)=1$. Define the normalized partition function for time-inhomogeneous weights by
\[
\bar{W}_n^\beta=\frac{1}{d^n}\sum_{|\mathbf{x}|=n} e^{\beta \bar{H}_n(\mathbf{x})-\frac{\beta^2}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n f\!\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)},
\]
where
\[
\bar{H}_n(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{i=1}^n \sqrt{f\!\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)}w(x_i)
\]
is the Hamiltonian for a branch $\mathbf{x}$ with $|\mathbf{x}|=n$. Then $\bar{W}_n^\beta$ exhibits a phase transition for its limit in probability (whose existence is established separately), with critical value
\[
\bar{\beta}_c := \sup\Bigl\{\beta \geq 0 \mid \mathbb{P}\{\bar{W}_\infty^\beta = 0\} > 0\Bigr\},
\]
which is well-defined and equals $\sqrt{2\log d}$ (coincides with that of the homogeneous model $W_n^\beta$, i.e., $\beta_c = \bar{\beta}_c$). Moreover, the following universality in $L^1$ limit holds:
\[
\mathbb{E}\bigl[|W_n^\beta - \bar{W}_n^\beta|\bigr] \to 0
\quad\text{as }n\to\infty,\text{ for all }\beta<\beta_c=\sqrt{2\log d}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.500020+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_844632df9d07d948f2bea97212fa34693150060d65ddc229f8b27e4ffb44fe7d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Two unital \(*\)-subalgebras \(\mathscr{A}_1,\mathscr{A}_2\) of a tracial
\(*\)-probability space \((\mathscr{A},\varphi)\) are freely independent
if
\[
 \varphi(a_1\cdots a_n)=0
\]
for \(n\geq1\) whenever \(\varphi(a_k)=0\), each \(a_k\) belongs to one of
\(\mathscr{A}_1,\mathscr{A}_2\), and consecutive factors belong to
different subalgebras.  Self-adjoint elements are freely independent when
the unital subalgebras that they generate are freely independent.  The law
of a self-adjoint element \(\mathsf{a}\) in a tracial
\(C^*\)-probability space is the unique compactly supported probability
measure \(\rho\) on \(\R\) determined by
\[
 \varphi(\mathsf{a}^k)=\int_{\R}x^k\dd\rho(x)
 \qquad(k=0,1,2,\ldots).
\]
For
compactly supported probability measures \(\rho,\eta\) on \(\R\), their
additive free convolution \(\rho\boxplus\eta\) is the law of
\(\mathsf{a}+\mathsf{b}\), where \(\mathsf{a}\) and \(\mathsf{b}\) are
freely independent self-adjoint elements in a tracial
\(C^*\)-probability space, with respective laws
\(\rho\) and \(\eta\); this law does not depend on the chosen
realisation.  See \cite{BercoviciVoiculescu,MingoSpeicher,NicaSpeicher}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236543+00:00","domain":"numerical analysis","id":"claim_8448b322d9af94267599948f7ac8e35e7642de9c07050163cb44f14c3c789388","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"An explicit s-stage Runge-Kutta method for the initial value problem y' = f(t,y), y(t_0) = y_0, advances y_n to y_{n+1} = y_n + h * sum_{i=1}^{s} b_i * k_i, where k_i = f( t_n + c_i*h, y_n + h*sum_{j<i} a_{ij}*k_j ), and the coefficients a_{ij}, b_i, c_i (the Butcher tableau) typically satisfy c_i = sum_{j<i} a_{ij}. The method has order p if, for sufficiently smooth f, its Taylor expansion in h agrees with the Taylor expansion of the exact solution through the h^p term (equivalently, the local truncation error is O(h^{p+1})). Matching these Taylor expansions imposes polynomial equations on (a_{ij}, b_i, c_i) called order conditions: for example, order 1 requires sum_i b_i = 1, and order 2 additionally requires sum_i b_i*c_i = 1/2. In Butcher's rooted-tree theory there is one order condition per rooted tree up to order p, and the number of independent conditions grows faster than the number of stages s, which is why, for instance, no explicit Runge-Kutta method can reach an order equal to its stage count once the order exceeds 4.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The allocations are defined along sizes with positive conditioning probability.","0 < nu < lambda and the boundary-tilted law pi has generating-function radius one."],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_844ce3c8e953cf9771d011278dae7176f5cf70c2fb67a2cf71d54183386d59e7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked; reduction plus asserted conditional, not a solution] Svante Janson's Problem 18.39 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510, asks whether Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability is possible in the condensation regime 0 < nu < lambda. Janson conjectures that it is not possible for the full sequence and, more strongly, that there are always epsilon > 0 and a subsequence along which Y_(1) >= epsilon n w.h.p. (Example 18.36 gives Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability along a subsequence.) Setting: let w_k >= 0 with w_0 > 0, let Phi(z) = sum_k w_k z^k have radius rho in (0,infinity) with Phi(rho) < infinity, and put pi_k = w_k rho^k/Phi(rho), a law with generating-function radius one and finite mean nu > 0. Let m_n/n -> lambda > nu. (Y_1,...,Y_n) is n i.i.d. pi variables conditioned on sum m_n, Y_(1) = max_i Y_i, and M = (lambda-nu)n. Heuristic rate: carrying M in r = M/a boxes of size a has class weight binomial(n,r) pi_a^r up to the bulk's fluctuation, giving log P = M Lambda(a) + o(M) with Lambda(a) = [log pi_a + log(a/(lambda-nu)) + 1]/a. For pi_k ~ c k^(-beta) and for pi_a = exp(-a^gamma), 0<gamma<1, Lambda increases on large a, so the optimum is a = M (one box), matching the known condensation picture. Since limsup_a Lambda(a) = 0 and Lambda < 0 for large a, Lambda has infinitely many upper records a_1 < a_2 < ... (Lambda(a_j) > Lambda(a) for all a < a_j) exactly when Lambda(a) < 0 for every a; if Lambda(a) >= 0 for some a the maximum is attained and there are finitely many records (Lambda(1) = log pi_1 + log(1/(lambda-nu)) + 1 is positive once lambda - nu < e pi_1). The record asserts, as author-checked and with no proof given beyond reference to an analogous step for Problem 18.40 in a companion memo, the following Proposition: if for some epsilon > 0 and every C, along infinitely many records, Lambda(a_j) - max_{a <= epsilon a_j} Lambda(a) > C a_j^(-1/2), then along n_j = a_j/(lambda-nu), P(Y_(1) >= ((lambda-nu)/2) n_j) -> 1, so the conjecture holds. Caveat: the only derivation offered is the heuristic rate with an o(M) error, which is coarser than the order sqrt(a_j) resolution this hypothesis requires, so the record does not establish the Proposition. The record poses the open Question whether, for every law pi on Z_{>=0} with radius one and finite mean, [log pi_a + log a]/a has infinitely many records with gap exceeding a_j^(-1/2) below max_{a <= epsilon a_j} for some fixed epsilon > 0. This is not a proved equivalence with the conjecture. A negative answer would only give a candidate counterexample, still requiring proof that the allocation spreads. The Question's normalisation and fixed threshold also differ from the Proposition's hypothesis. The problem remains open. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:55:57.005848+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_846df787eb9fd2a2674bded3a1a735297a801e121a3d502c21aee4355036594b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 21 (Wishart distribution) of arXiv:2609.02790, 'Full-Model Optimality for Tunable Linear Generative Priors in Compressed Sensing'] Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$ have i.i.d. rows $x_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)$, where

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:31:57.872890+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_846fa419f6615c6dfe5b737902c8fe123754174ee88aebb0402d399004ce0911","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:quasicont of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] If $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E}_p,\mathcal{F}_p , \Gamma_p)$ is a regular local $p$-Dirichlet space, then the following hold
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item \textbf{Existence:} Every $f\in \mathcal{F}_p$ has a quasicontinuous representative: there exists a function $\tilde{f}:X \to \mathbb{R}$ which is quasicontinuous and $f=\tilde{f}$ a.e. Moreover, $\tilde{f}:X \to \mathbb{R}$ can be chosen such that there exists a sequence $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of functions in $\mathcal{F}_p \cap C_0(X)$ and a decreasing sequence of open sets $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that 
			\[
			\cCap(B_n)^{1/p} \le 2^{-n}, 
			\]
			and
			\[\abs{f_k(x)-\tilde{f}(x)} \le 2^{1-n} \quad \mbox{for all $k \ge n$ and $x \in B_n^c$.} \]
			\item \textbf{Uniqueness:} If $f,g\in \mathcal{F}_p$ are quasicontinuous and $f=g$ a.e., then $\cCap(\{f\neq g\})=0$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.362474+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_849021ad4af2582e969c5f082b6ca4faa362ad0ac6fd9d12fc2840a96a6371dc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 11 of arXiv:2604.21669, 'Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts:\\ II. order-order interface convergence'] Let $\gamma$ be a deterministic set of edges forming a simple path that connects $v_L$ to $v_R$.
	Let ${\gamma_\shortuparrow}$ and ${\gamma_\shortdownarrow}$ be the sets of edges in $\bar{\mathsf{E}}\setminus \gamma$ that are above and below $\gamma$, respectively. For any $a_0,b_0\in\{0,1\}^{\gamma},\;a_{\shortuparrow},b_{\shortuparrow}\in\{0,1\}^{{\gamma_\shortuparrow}}$ with $a_0\cup a_{\shortuparrow}\subseteq b_0\cup b_{\shortuparrow}$,
	\begin{align*}
		&\matrc_{\mathsf{K}}\big( (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma_\shortdownarrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma_\shortdownarrow}) \in\cdot \bgiven (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma})=(a_0,b_0),\, (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma_\shortuparrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma_\shortuparrow}) = (a_{\shortuparrow},b_{\shortuparrow})\big)
		\\
		&\preccurlyeq
		\matrc_{\mathsf{K}}\big( (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma_\shortdownarrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma_\shortdownarrow})\in\cdot \bgiven \omega_\tau|_{\gamma} \equiv 1,\,(\omega_\tau|_{\gamma_\shortuparrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma_\shortuparrow})=(a_{\shortuparrow},b_{\shortuparrow})\big)
		\\
		&=
		\matrc_{\mathsf{K}}\big( (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma_\shortdownarrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma_\shortdownarrow})\in\cdot \bgiven \omega_\tau|_{\gamma}\equiv 1\big).
	\end{align*}
	In the same fashion, for \(\gamma^*\) a path of dual edges connecting \(v_L'\) to \(v_R'\),
	\begin{align*}
		&\matrc_{\mathsf{K}}\big( (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma^*_\shortuparrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma^*_\shortuparrow}) \in\cdot \bgiven (\omega_\tau|_{*\gamma^*},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{*\gamma^*})=(a_0,b_0),\, (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma^*_\shortdownarrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma^*_\shortdownarrow}) = (a_{\shortdownarrow},b_{\shortdownarrow})\big)
		\\
		&\succcurlyeq
		\matrc_{\mathsf{K}}\big( (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma^*_\shortuparrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma^*_\shortuparrow})\in\cdot \bgiven \omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{*\gamma^*} \equiv 0,\,(\omega_\tau|_{\gamma^*_\shortdownarrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma^*_\shortdownarrow})=(a_{\shortdownarrow},b_{\shortdownarrow})\big)
		\\
		&=
		\matrc_{\mathsf{K}}\big( (\omega_\tau|_{\gamma^*_\shortuparrow},\omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{\gamma^*_\shortuparrow})\in\cdot \bgiven \omega_{\tau\tau'}|_{*\gamma^*}\equiv 0\big).

{"assumptions":["the group is the two-element Cayley group; the claim is a counterexample, not a general theorem","relaxation time is 1/(1 - lambda_2), the standard spectral-gap convention","the target is the geometric-time law of the base walk at tilt p"],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869264+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_8494f2b7e60391b8ead2ab87b96e7454cadc38307316484de8264628972059fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: author_checked_limited_argument - a first-pass structural calculation; no independent review, prior art unverified, and the other questions in the source are untouched] For Metropolis chains targeting a geometric-time law on a Cayley group, the source asks whether the relaxation time decreases monotonically in the tilt p. CLAIM: NO, and the counterexample is the smallest possible one - the two-element group - with relaxation defined the standard way as 1/(1 - lambda_2). (i) NONLAZY BASE. The base walk flips the two states; the target is mu_p = (1/(2-p), (1-p)/(2-p)); the Metropolis matrix is [[p, 1-p],[1, 0]], whose second eigenvalue is p - 1, so tau(p) = 1/(2 - p), STRICTLY INCREASING in p. (ii) LAZY BASE, which removes the convention ambiguity because its spectrum is nonnegative. The base matrix has all entries 1/2, mu_p = ((1+p)/2, (1-p)/2), the Metropolis off-diagonal rates are (1-p)/(2(1+p)) and 1/2, and tau(p) = 1 + p, again increasing. (iii) If laziness is imposed AFTER forming the nonlazy Metropolis kernel, tau(p) = 2/(2 - p), still increasing. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it refutes the literal monotonicity direction only. It does not answer the source's other universal-bound questions and does not resolve its undefined tau(infinity). CONVENTION CAVEAT recorded with the result: if 'relaxation' meant the inverse absolute spectral gap of a nonlazy chain, that convention differs - the lazy example exists precisely to remove the ambiguity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Normalized random-walk rho","Infinite connected d-regular Cayley graph","Sufficient criterion, not equivalence"],"created_at":"2026-10-10T09:11:38.048103+00:00","domain":"Bernoulli bond percolation on graphs","id":"claim_84a5edcb56cb3e3ab5affe7a2fef6535bd7b550c252ea1c6a2dfcdf5fcf9bcaf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"DRAFT source-backed correction, pending referee check. {"assumptions":["Omega is a bounded open subset of R^n","A is measurable, bounded and uniformly elliptic: alpha|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)| <= Lambda","f is in L^p(Omega) with p > n/2 (any p > 1 when n = 2)","u is in H^1_0(Omega) and solves the equation in the weak (distributional, H^1_0-tested) sense","n >= 3 for the stated form of the exponents"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:13:10.395913+00:00","domain":"elliptic PDE, regularity of weak solutions","id":"claim_84be9b126c53ea76ef648ad1432c521b08e53b7112e61244437e9ab9a5acaef4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Omega be a bounded open subset of R^n with n >= 3, and let A be a measurable matrix field on Omega with |A(x)| <= Lambda and A(x)xi.xi >= alpha|xi|^2 for all xi in R^n and a.e. x, with alpha > 0 (bounded measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients; no continuity is assumed). Let f be in L^p(Omega) with p > n/2, and let u in H^1_0(Omega) be the weak solution of -div(A grad u) = f, i.e. integral_Omega A grad u . grad v = integral_Omega f v for all v in H^1_0(Omega). Then u is in L^infinity(Omega) and ||u||_{L^infinity} <= C ||f||_{L^p}, where C depends only on n, p, alpha and |Omega| (not on Lambda and not on any regularity of A). For n = 2 the same conclusion holds for every p > 1. WHERE IT FAILS: the exponent threshold is sharp. At p = n/2 the conclusion is false: on the unit ball of R^n, n >= 3, the function u(x) = log log(1 + 1/|x|) lies in H^1, is unbounded near the origin, and its Laplacian lies in L^(n/2); the borderline case only yields exponential integrability (Brezis-Merle type), not boundedness. Boundedness of Omega is used through the measure |Omega| in the constant. The estimate is one-sided in nothing: it bounds |u| because the argument is applied to u and to -u alike. Ellipticity is essential; for a degenerate A the truncation argument loses the Sobolev inequality it needs.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:53:53.170971+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84c4b1d375637b72e8c258b393189ece2d0257899f489403b5bc58577d3d9e3c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2606.11511, 'Convergence of a Critical Multitype Bellman--Harris Process with One Infinite-Mean Lifetim'] Let \(X\) be a nonnegative, non-arithmetic random variable with distribution
\(F\), renewal measure \(U\), and tail
\[
  \overline F(t):=F((t,\infty))=\Pbb(X>t)
  \sim c t^{-\gamma},
  \qquad t\to\infty,
  \qquad 0<\gamma<1.
\]
Assume that, for every fixed \(h>0\), there exists \(C_h>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
  \Pbb(x<X\le x+h)
  \le C_h x^{-1-\gamma},
  \qquad x\ge1.
\end{equation}
Then the strong renewal estimate holds:
\begin{equation}
  m_X(t)\bigl(U(t+h)-U(t)\bigr)
  \longrightarrow
  \bigl[\Gamma(\gamma)\Gamma(2-\gamma)\bigr]^{-1}h,
  \qquad t\to\infty,
  \qquad h>0,
\end{equation}
where
\[
  m_X(t):=\int_0^t \Pbb(X>s)\,ds.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\kappa>\gamma\),
\begin{equation}
  \int_{[0,t]}(1+t-s)^{-\kappa}\,U(ds)
  \longrightarrow0,
  \qquad t\to\infty.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:15:16.648672+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84c5bd4cc4d3495d0aeaec8618a93ff93c6e4701530d955016ce9e3be9725024","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 2 (cf. \cite{AC11}, Proposition 3.14.) of arXiv:2608.30743, 'Perspectives on the Bott spectral sequence for Lie groupoids'] Let $G$ be a Lie groupoid and $\mathcal{D}$ a connection on $G_1$ with respect to $s$. Then the adjoint (split two-term) representation up to homotopy is defined on the complex of vector bundles
    \[
    E^\bullet = A[2] \xrightarrow{\rho} T G_0[1]
    \]
    by the terms
    \[
    R^\bullet_1 \in \Gamma(G_1, \Hom(s^*E, t^*E))
    \]
    and
    \[
    R^{-1}_2 \in \Gamma(G_2, \Hom(s^*TG_0, t^*A)).
    \]
    
    $R_1$ is given by
    \begin{align*}
        G_1 \times TG_0 & \rightarrow TG_0 \\
        (x, Y) & \mapsto R^{-1}_1(x)(Y) := T t(Z)
    \end{align*}
    where $Z \in \mathcal{D}_x$ denotes the unique element satisfying $Ts(Z) = Y$ and
    \begin{align*}
        G_1 \times A & \rightarrow A \\
        (x, Y) & \mapsto R^{-2}_1(x)(Y) := T \mu (Z, Y, 0_x)
    \end{align*}
    where $Z \in \mathcal{D}_x$ denotes the unique element satisfying $Ts(Z) = \rho(Y)$.

    $R_2$ is given by the basic curvature of $\mathcal{D}$, i.e the map
    \begin{align*}
        G_2 \times TG_0 & \rightarrow A \\
        (x,y, Y) & \mapsto R^{-1}_2(x)(Y) := T\mu(T \mu(V,W)-Z, 0_{(\mu(x,y))^{-1}}) \in (\ker(Ts))_{1_{t(x)}},
    \end{align*}
    where $W \in \mathcal{D}_y$ denotes the unique element satisfying $Ts(W)=Y$ and $V \in \mathcal{D}_x$ denotes the unique element satisfying $Ts(V)=Tt(W)$, as well as $Z \in \mathcal{D}_{\mu(x,y)}$ denotes the unique element satisfying $Ts(Z)=Y$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.341853+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84cfc224db6b7fa396ea49448e46983d599563f717df849a5b991424184b2ed1","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (Local split--merge--rewire rule) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(\omega\) be a configuration, let \(\cL(\omega)\) be the associated loop
configuration, let \(e=\{x,y\}\in E\), and let \(s\in S^1\setminus T(\omega)\) be a
regular time. Consider the effect of inserting at \((e,s)\) either a cross or a bar.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item If \(I_{\neq}(\omega;e,s)=1\), then inserting either a cross or a bar
    merges the two loops containing \((x,s)\) and \((y,s)\) into one.

    \item If \(I_+(\omega;e,s)=1\), then inserting a cross splits the loop into two,
    whereas inserting a bar rewires the loop without changing the number of loops.

    \item If \(I_-(\omega;e,s)=1\), then inserting a bar splits the loop into two,
    whereas inserting a cross rewires the loop without changing the number of loops.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:25:41.653524+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84d1c0bff6ee2928c1b5d7c1f22c961f42beb26b566f731a372a479b154b39f9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:Levy-stable-graph-approximation of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r)$ be a regular based loop family. A \emph{stable graph approximation} of $L$ is the data of a sequence of embedded topological maps $({\mathbb{G}}_n)_{n\geq1}$, and a sequence of graph-loop families
\[
 L_n=(\ell_{1,n},\ldots,\ell_{r,n}),
 \qquad
 \ell_{i,n}\in L_o({\mathbb{G}}_n),
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathrm{mesh}}({\mathbb{G}}_n)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0$;
\item for every $i=1,\dots,r$,
\[
 d_1(\ell_{i,n},\ell_i)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0;
\]
\item for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a homeomorphism $h_n$ such that $L_n$ and $L$ have the same marked ambient ribbon type; and if $C_1,\ldots,C_m$ are the connected components of $\Sigma\setminus\Gamma(L)$ and
\[
 C_{j,n}:=h_n(C_j),
\]
then
\[
 |C_{j,n}|\longrightarrow|C_j|,
 \qquad j=1,\ldots,m.
\]
\end{enumerate}
We say that $L$ has a stable graph approximation carried by the sequence $(\mathbb{G}_n)$.
The same notation is used for the corresponding cut-open compact surfaces with boundary.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:44.238388+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84d86185fc57232af9570324294c85ae1abb69d185671f69761b8633a6c2ff9f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 12 (Chaoticity properties on path space) of arXiv:2604.14427, 'A criterion for proving entropy chaos on path space'] Let $\mathbb{P}_N$ be a sequence of (symmetric) probability measures on $\Omega^{N}$ and let $\mathbb{P}$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$. Denote by $\mathbb{P}^{(k)}_N$ the $k-$th marginal measure of $\mathbb{P}_N$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item We say that $\mathbb{P}_N$ is $\mathbb{P}$-Kac chaotic if, for any $k\in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{P}^{(k)}_N$ converges to $\mathbb{P}^{\otimes k}$ in distribution.
        \item We say that $\mathbb{P}_N$ is (weakly) $\mathbb{P}$-entropy chaotic (with respect to the Wiener measure) if  
        \[
        \lim_{N \rightarrow +\infty}\mathcal{H}\left(\mathbb{P}^{(k)}_N|\mathbb{W}^{\otimes k}\right) = \mathcal{H}\left(\mathbb{P}^{(k)}|\mathbb{W}^{\otimes k}\right).\] 
        \item We say that $\mathbb{P}_N$ is strongly $\mathbb{P}$-entropy chaotic if  \[\lim_{N \rightarrow +\infty}\mathcal{H}\left(\mathbb{P}^{(k)}_N|\mathbb{P}^{\otimes k}\right) =0.\]
        \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:51:11.462278+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84df8febc302453700a3fd9a719c80d22356b02eaba6257700137fb2c717841f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 12 ({\cite[Definition~2.26) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {BST}}]
The multiplier module $\J(\omega_X,\Gamma)$ is defined as
\[ \J(\omega_X,\Gamma):=\bigcap_{\pi:Y\rightarrow X} \Image ({\Tr}_{\pi}:\pi_{*}{\omega}_{Y}(-\lfloor \pi^{*}\Gamma \rfloor) \hookrightarrow {\omega}_{X}(- \lfloor\Gamma\rfloor)),\]
where $\pi$ runs through all proper birational morphisms $Y\rightarrow X$ with $Y$ normal.
For a log $\Q$-Gorenstein pair $(X,\Delta)$, the multiplier ideal $\J(X,\Delta)$ is defined by
\[ \J(X,\Delta):=\J(\omega_X, K_X +\Delta), \]
where $K_X$ is a canonical divisor associated with ${\omega}_{X}$. Since the choice of $K_X$ determines the inclusion ${\omega}_{X}\subset K(X)$, the multiplier ideal $\J(X,\Delta)$ can be regarded as an ideal of $\sO_X$. Note that the resulting ideal $\J(X,\Delta)\subset\sO_X$ is independent of the choice of $K_X$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.353526+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_852b0d4dc9f07b4a7615f1f6a29dbffaeb09c786792fcf84fedbb2a651fa5708","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 204 (spatial rerandomization for spherical perceptron) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We use the buckets from Definition~\ref{d:buckets} to
 define a new process $\vY\equiv\vY^{\RomI:\RomIII}$, as follows. First let $a(q_0)$ be sampled uniformly at random from $[M]$. Then, conditional on $a(q_0), \ldots, a(q_d)$, we let $a(q_{d+1})$ be sampled from the measure $\bP$ conditional on the bucket at time $q_d$, that is,
    \[a(q_{d+1})
    \sim \bP
    \bigg( a = \cdot \,\bigg|\, 
    a\in B(q_d,a(q_d)) \bigg)\,.
    \]
We then let $\vY(q_d)$ be the average of $\vX^\trunc$ over all the particles in the bucket containing $a(q_d)$, 
    \beq
    \vY(q_d)
    =
    \sum_{a\in B(q_d,a(q_d))}
    \frac{\vX^\trunc(q_d,a)}{|B(q_d,a(q_d))|}
    \,.
    \eeq
Informally, $\vY$ is the process $\vX^\trunc$ with ``spatial rerandomization at scale $\eta$.'' It is easy to check (by induction) that each $a(q_d)$ is marginally uniform on $[M]$, which implies that $\vX^\trunc(q_d)$ and $\vY(q_d)$ are within $W_{\infty}$ distance $O(\eta/\delta)$ for each fixed $d$.  Likewise, we define $\vY^\frozen\equiv\vY^{\frozen,\RomI:\RomIII}$ to be the spatial rerandomization of $\vX^\frozen$ at scale $\eta$, with random indices $a^\frozen(q_d) \in[M^\frozen]$
and buckets $\mathcal{B}^\frozen(q_d)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. rows with finite eighth moments (mean zero, or centered)","p/n -> gamma in (0, infinity)","loss is the scaled Frobenius norm tr(A A^T)/p"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:37:33.911486+00:00","domain":"multivariate statistics","id":"claim_856459c0e30e1791fc55427a5987d2b06eff22f3cf10fd5350dd6c9ef3854d04","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $x_1, \\dots, x_n \\in \\mathbb{R}^p$ be i.i.d. with mean zero, covariance $\\Sigma$ and finite eighth moments, $S = \\frac{1}{n}\\sum_i x_i x_i^T$, and let $\\mu = \\operatorname{tr}(\\Sigma)/p$, with the scaled Frobenius norm $\\|A\\|^2 = \\operatorname{tr}(A A^T)/p$. Define $\\alpha^2 = \\|\\Sigma - \\mu I\\|^2$, $\\beta^2 = E\\|S - \\Sigma\\|^2$, $\\delta^2 = E\\|S - \\mu I\\|^2 = \\alpha^2 + \\beta^2$. THEOREM (Ledoit and Wolf, 2004). Among all estimators of the form $\\rho_1 I + \\rho_2 S$ with nonrandom $\\rho_1, \\rho_2$, the expected loss $E\\|\\hat\\Sigma - \\Sigma\\|^2$ is minimized by $$\\Sigma^* = \\frac{\\beta^2}{\\delta^2}\\, \\mu I + \\frac{\\alpha^2}{\\delta^2}\\, S,$$ a convex combination of the sample covariance and the scaled identity, with expected loss $\\alpha^2 \\beta^2 / \\delta^2$. The constants have consistent plug-in estimates under general asymptotics $p/n \\to \\gamma \\in (0, \\infty)$: $\\hat\\mu = \\operatorname{tr}(S)/p$, $\\hat\\delta^2 = \\|S - \\hat\\mu I\\|^2$, $\\hat{\\bar b}^2 = \\frac{1}{n^2}\\sum_i \\|x_i x_i^T - S\\|^2$, $\\hat\\beta^2 = \\min(\\hat{\\bar b}^2, \\hat\\delta^2)$, $\\hat\\alpha^2 = \\hat\\delta^2 - \\hat\\beta^2$, and the resulting estimator $\\hat\\Sigma^* = \\frac{\\hat\\beta^2}{\\hat\\delta^2}\\hat\\mu I + \\frac{\\hat\\alpha^2}{\\hat\\delta^2} S$ has the same asymptotic loss as $\\Sigma^*$, is always well conditioned and invertible, and is uniformly no worse than $S$. The shrinkage target is the scaled identity, so the estimator pulls all eigenvalues of $S$ toward their mean $\\hat\\mu$; when one eigenvalue of $\\Sigma$ dominates the trace (a strong spike), $\\hat\\mu$ is dominated by that spike and the target is far from the small eigenvalues.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:20:07.899634+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_85752c1649b8206748d41744da79287d96c8950ab944b65799073fb1b3383b5a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma sylvester_solution_explicit of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] \mbox{}\\
    Let $\mathbf{Z} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ be an arbitrary matrix
    with SVD given by 
    $ \mathbf{Z} = \sum_{i=1}^d \sigma_i (\mathbf{Z}) \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^{\top} $,
    where $\sigma_1(\mathbf{Z}) \ge \sigma_2(\mathbf{Z}) \ge \ldots \ge \sigma_d(\mathbf{Z}) \ge 0$
    are the singular values of $\mathbf{Z}$.
    Here,
    $\{ \mathbf{u}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{u}_{d_1} \} \subset \R^{d_1}$
    and
    $\{ \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{d_2} \} \subset \R^{d_2}$
    are orthonormal bases of 
    $\R^{d_1}$ and $\R^{d_2}$,
    consisting
    of left and right singular vectors of $\mathbf{Z}$, respectively.
    Let $ \widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{\mathbf{U}} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_1}, \widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{\mathbf{V}} \in \R^{d_2 \times d_2}$
    be positive definite matrices
    which are diagonal in the bases $\{ \mathbf{u}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{u}_{d_1} \}$
    and $\{ \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{d_2} \}$, respectively.
    Then, the unique solution $\mathbf{W} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$
    of the Sylvester equation
    \begin{equation*}
        \widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{\mathbf{U}} \mathbf{W} + \mathbf{W} \widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{\mathbf{V}} = 2 \mathbf{Z}
    \end{equation*}
    is given by
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbf{W}
        =
        \sum_{k=1}^d
        \frac{2 \sigma_k (\mathbf{Z})}{
            \innerproduct{ \widetilde{ \mathbf{L}}_{\mathbf{U}}, \mathbf{u}_k \mathbf{u}_k^\top}
            +
            \innerproduct{\widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{\mathbf{V}}, \mathbf{v}_k \mathbf{v}_k^\top}
        }
        \mathbf{u}_k \mathbf{v}_k^{\top}.
    \end{equation*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.714585+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_858fb757b1666fb26e2d0df71b35bebe4def8be329564f7d3dfa42cf98c8c08a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Tauberianthm of arXiv:2603.24499, 'A central limit theorem for connected components of random coverings of manifolds with nil'] Let $b(t)$ be a measurable function $[0,\infty)\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ which is bounded on finite intervals, and such that
\[
G(s):=\int_0^{\infty}b(t)e^{-st}{\rm d}t
\]
converges (in Lebesgue sense, i.e., absolutely) for all $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with ${{\rm Re}(s)}>0$. Suppose also that there exists an integer $m\ge 1$ and there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that
\[
\lim\limits_{t\rightarrow\infty}tb(t)
\int_{0}^{\varepsilon_0}u^{m-1}e^{-tu}{\rm d}u=1\ .
\]
Let $a(t)$ be a nondecreasing function $[0,\infty)\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$. Suppose there is some $\alpha>0$ such that
\[
f(s):=\int_0^{\infty}a(t)e^{-st}{\rm d}t
\]
converges (absolutely) for all $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with ${{\rm Re}(s)}>\alpha$.

Suppose that for some constant $c_0>0$, the function 
\[
F(s):=f(s)-c_0 G(s-\alpha)
\]
can be rewritten as
\[
F(s)=\frac{g(s)}{(s-\alpha)^{m-1}}+h(s)\ ,
\]
where $g(s)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $m-2$ if $m\ge 2$, or identically zero if $m=1$, and where $h(s)$ is a function which is continuous on ${\rm Re}(s)\ge \alpha$
and holomorphic on the domain ${\rm Re}(s)>\alpha$.

Then, the previous hypotheses imply the asymptotics
\[
a(t)=(c_0+o(1))\ e^{\alpha t}\ b(t)\ ,
\]
as $t\rightarrow\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:20:07.939692+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_85b0d20c1a0c09dc4fc0b6689a8b59a7dc563de96a422bb16b54328370686fc3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:mu0 of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] A proof of Conjecture~(conj:CE of the paper) cannot restrict to selections with

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.499113+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_85b4d531e3413cd1ebc43fb25e8b32a2d3a0034016166e4e7dca19789dfc3151","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:IBJ-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})
_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
  \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with
the kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data
and $B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ as the propagator.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f measurable and a.e. finite","|E| < infinity (or E sigma-finite, applied piecewise)","the measure is Borel regular, so that inner regularity by closed sets is available"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T17:07:35.550181+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_85c2d201a83f46e0b6df467d153d01f4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f : R^d -> C be Lebesgue measurable and finite almost everywhere, let E be a measurable set of FINITE measure, and let eps > 0. Then there is a compact (hence closed) set F contained in E with |E \\ F| < eps such that the RESTRICTION of f to F is continuous. Moreover one may take g in C_c(R^d) with g = f on F and sup |g| <= sup |f|. The theorem does not assert that f is continuous AT the points of F as a function on R^d: the indicator of the rationals is nowhere continuous on R, yet it agrees with the zero function off a set of measure zero, and Lusin's F can be taken to be any closed set of irrationals of nearly full measure. Finiteness of |E| may be relaxed to sigma-finiteness by exhausting E, at the price of stating the conclusion with |E \\ F| < eps for each piece. [standard; e.g. Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Theorem 2.24]\n\nConverse (Lusin's criterion): let E be a Lebesgue measurable subset of R^d of finite measure and let f:E->C be a function. If for every eps>0 there is a closed F contained in E with |E\\F|<eps such that f restricted to F is continuous, then f is Lebesgue measurable on E. Thus measurability of an a.e.-finite function on such E is equivalent to continuity of its restriction on closed subsets missing arbitrarily small measure. Applied on every bounded measurable piece, this gives the local criterion on R^d.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.292523+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_85c3ec1682437f996a40b72b4509c18c8cb8b2518f1f2f6be43c2fd963fdb193","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:higher of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $\mu$ be $n$-AD-regular with constant $c_0$ and $\mu(\mathbb{R}^d)=\infty$, let $\phi$ be

\[
\lambda^{-1}\le|F'(s)|\le\lambda
\quad\text{and}\quad
|F^{(m)}(s)|\le\Lambda\ \ (2\le m\le k)
\qquad\text{for all } s\in J_\phi.
\]

The constants depend on $k$, $\lambda$, $\Lambda$, $\phi$, $n$ and $c_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\(g\in C^\gamma([0,T];\mathbb R)\), where

\[

\]
