{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:12:46.901711+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_85e51b84f134cec0370252059adfd4921957bb8e922d3e5b69d191e358281beb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma ballGWmass of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] We keep the above notation. 
Let $\xi$ be proper (i.e.~$\xi (1)\! = \!  0$) and (sub)critical. Let $(S_r)_{r\in \mathbb{R}_+}$, 
$(N_r)_{r\in \mathbb{R}_+}$ and $(Y_k,W_k)_{k\in \mathbb{N}^*}$ be independent processes that are distributed as follows: $S$ is a subordinator with Laplace exponent $\phi$ as in ((Khint of the paper)), $N$ is a homogeneous Poisson process with unit intensity, the $(Y_k,W_k)$ are independent 
$(\{ -1\} \! \cup \! \mathbb{N}) \! \times \! \mathbb{R}_+$-valued r.v.s whose laws are given by 
$$  {\bf E} \big[s^{Y_0} e^{-yW_0}  \big] \! = \!  F^\varnothing_{\!\! \varrho, \Lambda_\varnothing} (s,y) \quad \textrm{and} \quad  {\bf E} \big[s^{Y_k} e^{-yW_k}  \big] \! = \!  (cs)^{-1}F_{\xi, c, \Lambda} (s,y) , \;  k\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}^*.$$
We next define the following processes: 
$$\forall r\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+, \quad (X^+_r,M_r) \! := \! (Y_0, W_0)+ \!\!\!  \sum_{1\leq k \leq N_{cr}} \!\!\! (Y_k,W_k) \; , \quad 
R_0 \! :=\!   \inf \big\{r\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+ \! : \! X^+_r\! = \!  0 \big\}, $$
and  $C_r \! :=\!  R_0 \wedge \inf \{ u\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+ \!  : A_u \! >\! r \}$ where $ A_r \! = \!  
 \int_0^r du/X^+_u$ if $r\! < \! R_0$ and $A_r \! = \!  \infty$ otherwise, and with the convention that $\inf \emptyset\! = \!  \infty$. Then the following holds true. 

\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$]  $\big( Z^+_r\! , {\boldsymbol{\lambda}} ([0,r])\big)_{\! r\in \mathbb{R}_+}$ under $P_{\xi,c, \phi ,\Lambda, \varrho, \Lambda_{ \varnothing}}$ has the same law as $(X^+_{C_r} , S_{C_r}\! +\!  M_{C_r})_{r\in\mathbb{R}_+} $.  In particular 
the total mass $\langle {\boldsymbol{\lambda}} \rangle $ has the same law as $S_{R_0}+ M_{R_0}$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] Let us set 
$g_r( s,y) \! = \!  Q_{\xi, c, \phi, \Lambda} \big[ s^{Z^+_r} e^{-y{\boldsymbol{\lambda}} ([0, r])} \big] $ and $\gamma (y)\! = \!   Q_{\xi, c, \phi, \Lambda} \big[ e^{-y \langle {\boldsymbol{\lambda}} \rangle}\big] $, for all $r,y\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+$ and all $s\! \in \!  [0, 1]$. Then the following holds true for all $s\! \in \!  [0, 1]$ and $y\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+$. 

\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(ii$-$a)$] If $s \! < \! \gamma (y)$ (resp.~if $s \! > \! \gamma (y)$), then $F_{\xi,c, \Lambda} (s,y)  - s(c+\phi(y)) \! >\! 0$ (resp.~$< \! 0$). Otherwise, if $s \! = \! \gamma (y)$, $F_{\xi,c, \Lambda} (\gamma(y),y) \! =\! \gamma (y)(c+\phi(y))$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii$-$b)$] If $s \! \neq \gamma (y)$, then 
\begin{equation}
r= \! \int^{g_r(s,y)}_s \!\!\!\! \frac{du}{F_{\xi,c, \Lambda} (u,y)\! -\! u(c+ \phi(y))}  \; .
\end{equation}
Moreover, $P_{\xi, c, \phi, \Lambda, \varrho, \Lambda_\varnothing} \big[ s^{Z^+_r} e^{-y{\boldsymbol{\lambda}} ([0, r])} \big] \! = \!  F^\varnothing_{\!\! \varrho, \Lambda_\varnothing} \big( g_r (s,y), y \big)$. 
\end{compactenum}
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Canonical reference: Bonami, 1970, Annales de l'Institut Fourier; Beckner, 1975, Annals of Mathematics; O'Donnell, Analysis of Boolean Functions, 2014, Cambridge University Press.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:23:05.300110+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_860687168ce8d3ce7102561892b7fb672e35da044784d3b34cc4c16e8d539e1d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 15 (Matched-spectrum orientation dependence) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Let $X_0\sim\calN(0,\Sigma)$ with eigenvalues
$\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d>0$, let $1\le d_y\le d$, let
$A\in\R^{d_y\times d}$, and let $R_A=AX_0+\varepsilon$ with
$\varepsilon\sim\calN(0,\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y})$.  Assume
$AA^\top=\Id_{d_y}$.  Thus every admissible $A$ has the same nonzero singular
values; isotropic measurement noise leaves orientation relative to \(\Sigma\)
as the only design variable.  Define
\[
C_\gamma=(\Sigma^{-1}+\gamma\Id_d)^{-1},
\qquad
\Sigma_A^{\rm post}
=
(\Sigma^{-1}+\sigma_y^{-2}A^\top A)^{-1},
\qquad
\psi_\gamma(\lambda)
=
\frac12\log
\frac{\sigma_y^2+\lambda}
{\sigma_y^2+\lambda/(1+\gamma\lambda)}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal M_\gamma(A)=\MI(R_A;Y_\gamma)
=
\frac12\log
\frac{\det(\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y}+A\Sigma A^\top)}
{\det(\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y}+AC_\gamma A^\top)}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, among all row-orthonormal rank-$d_y$ measurements,
\begin{align}

\frac12\sum_{i=d-d_y+1}^{d}
\log\!\left(1+\frac{\lambda_i}{\sigma_y^2}\right)
&\le \MI(X_0;R_A)
\le
\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{d_y}
\log\!\left(1+\frac{\lambda_i}{\sigma_y^2}\right),\\

2\MI(X_0;R_A)
&=
\log\frac{\det\Sigma}{\det\Sigma_A^{\rm post}},\\

\sum_{i=d-d_y+1}^{d}\psi_\gamma(\lambda_i)
&\le \mathcal M_\gamma(A)
\le
\sum_{i=1}^{d_y}\psi_\gamma(\lambda_i).
\end{align}
For every $\gamma>0$, $\psi_\gamma$ is strictly increasing.  Equality in the
upper (respectively, lower) bounds is attained by choosing the row space of
$A$ to be the span of the largest (respectively, smallest) $d_y$ prior
eigenvectors.  If the boundary eigenvalue is repeated, the extremizing row
space need not be unique: the required dimensions may be chosen arbitrarily
within that eigenspace.  Hence equal operator
singular values do not determine clean
measurement information, posterior covariance-volume contraction, or
reverse-path assimilation once the prior is anisotropic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Real finite data with 1<=rank(X)=q<n; hidden width h>=min(m,n)","Euclidean continuous gradient flow; unrestricted linear-regression comparator","Effective imbalance delta_eff>0, with the precise zero-padded eigenvalue indices"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:55:59.752362+00:00","domain":"Linear-network gradient flow and LoRA initialization","id":"claim_86480a93c006d4288d3376eeb3e6b4c4235f9c037c4718b56ca06aab516c37c7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a real N-by-n design of rank q>=1 with q<n, Y an N-by-m response matrix, and hidden width h>=min(m,n). Choose an orthonormal basis Phi1 of the data row space, set U1=Phi1^T U, and let a=lambda_q(X^T X)>0 be the smallest positive design-covariance eigenvalue. The latent imbalance D=U1^T U1-V^T V is constant along the flow. Using decreasing eigenvalues with lambda_i=0 when i exceeds the matrix dimension, define delta_eff=max(lambda_q(D),0)+max(lambda_m(-D),0). Positive definiteness of the h-by-h D alone is insufficient when q>h: its q-th eigenvalue is zero by convention, while all eigenvalues of -D are negative (or zero-padded). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.954535+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_865c329f8b3b031e45b94c26b88c6f26dd333c4965cf02ef2133ae7c3ddbbd06","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 20 (Weak-profile transfer by diagonal congruence) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(H\), \(S\), \(D\), and \(\widetilde H\) be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:R3-stochastic-normalization}.  Suppose in addition that
\begin{equation}
 \norm{D-I}_\infty=o(N^{-1/2})
\end{equation}
and that the variables \(\sqrt N H_{ij}\) are uniformly bounded.  Let
\(m^S(z)=(m_i^S(z))\) solve
\begin{equation}
 -\frac1{m_i^S(z)}=z+\sum_jS_{ij}m_j^S(z),
 \qquad
 \overline m^S(z):=\frac1N\sum_i m_i^S(z),
\end{equation}
and let \(m(z)=m_{\rm sc}(z)\).  On every fixed analytic LSS contour
\(\Gamma\) at positive distance from \([-2,2]\), with the standard spectral
confinement cutoff,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{z\in\Gamma}\E\left|
 \left[\Tr(H-zI)^{-1}-N\overline m^S(z)\right]
 -\left[\Tr(\widetilde H-zI)^{-1}-Nm(z)\right]
 \right|^2=o(1).
\end{equation}
Consequently, uniformly for \(z,w\in\Gamma\),
\begin{align}
 &\left[\E\Tr(H-zI)^{-1}-N\overline m^S(z)\right]
 -\left[\E\Tr(\widetilde H-zI)^{-1}-Nm(z)\right]=o(1),
 \\
 &\Cov\!\left(\Tr(H-zI)^{-1},\Tr(H-wI)^{-1}\right)
 \nonumber\\
 &\qquad-
 \Cov\!\left(\Tr(\widetilde H-zI)^{-1},
              \Tr(\widetilde H-wI)^{-1}\right)=o(1).
 
\end{align}
The same comparison holds for joint characteristic functions of finitely many
analytic LSS after subtracting the exact Dyson centering
\(-N(2\pi\ii)^{-1}\oint\varphi\overline m^S\) at the \(H\) endpoint and the
scalar semicircle centering at the \(\widetilde H\) endpoint.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:13:22.518787+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_867478407d7ff42ed8967600dc1639ae6dbae608d2fb4c49c2296cf79eef947a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Deformation of arXiv:2505.16585, 'Expanded regimes of area law for lattice Yang--Mills theories'] Let $\mbf{e}$ be an edge of $\ell_i$ for some loop $\ell_i$ of $s$. Then $\ell_i = a \mbf{e} b$. For any oriented plaquette $p \in \mc{P}_\Lambda$ which contains (the lattice edge corresponding to) $\mbf{e}$, we may consider the loop given by $\ell_p = \mbf{e}' c$ tracing the boundary of $p$. Here, $\mbf{e}'$ is the same lattice edge as $\mbf{e}$. We define $\ell_i \oplus_\mbf{e} p := a \mbf{e}' c \mbf{e} b$, and define the \textit{positive deformation} of $s$ at $\mbf{e}$ to be the string $s' := (\ell_1, \ldots, [\ell_i \oplus_{\mbf{e}} p], \ldots, \ell_n)$.

Similarly, for any oriented plaquette $p \in \mc{P}_\Lambda$ which contains (the lattice edge corresponding to) $\mbf{e}^{-1}$, we may consider the loop given by $\ell_p = \mbf{e}' c$ tracing the boundary of $p$. Here, $\mbf{e}'$ is the same lattice edge as $\mbf{e}^{-1}$. We define $\ell_i \ominus_\mbf{e} p := a c b$, and define the \textit{negative deformation} of $s$ at $\mbf{e}$ to be the string $s' := (\ell_1, \ldots, [\ell_i \oplus_{\mbf{e}'} p], \ldots, \ell_n)$

Given an edge $\mbf{e}$ of $s$, we let $\mbb{D}_{+}(s, \mbf{e})/ \mbb{D}_-(s, \mbf{e})$ to be the set of all positive/negative deformations of $s$ at $\mbf{e}$. We will frequently use the notation $\mbb{D}_{\pm}(s, \mbf{e})$ to denote the set of positive or negative deformations of $s$ at $\mbf{e}$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:42:55.336004+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_869349968fe908617457a152b589c043b2199dfadd126b1ad64f1e5eb9e4f4d4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The comparison and rigidity arguments used below are collected in the following proposition.

\textup{(i)} Assume that for some compact interval $K$, $\delta>0$ and $W\ge1$,
\[
W(x)\to+\infty,\; (\cA_\R+\lambda)W\le-\delta W\;\hbox{in }\R\setminus K.
\]
Let $U$ be one of the two components of $\R\setminus K$. If $u\in C^1(U)$ extends continuously to the interaction collar of $U$, satisfies $u^+=o(W)$ at the infinite end, $(\cA_\R+\lambda)u\ge0$ in $U$, and $u\le0$ on the finite interaction collar of width $R_J$, then $u\le0$ in $U$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$. Assume that there exist a compact interval $K$, $\delta>0$ and $W\in C^1(\R)$ such that $W\ge1$, $W(x)\to+\infty$, and
\[
(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)W\le-\delta W\;\hbox{in }\R\setminus K.
\]
Suppose that every positive eigenfunction associated with $\lambda_p$ is $o(W)$. Then every such eigenfunction has $W$-minimal growth, and $\lambda_p$ is simple in the positive cone: any two positive eigenfunctions associated with $\lambda_p$ are proportional.

\textup{(iii)} Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}. Let $u>0$ satisfy $u=o(W)$ and $(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)u\le0$ in $\R$, where $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$. Then $u$ is a positive multiple of the principal eigenfunction. In particular the inequality is necessarily an equality.

\textup{(iv)} Under the same hypotheses, let $f\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $f\ge0$ and $f\not\equiv0$. There is no positive $u\in C^1(\R)$ with $u=o(W)$ satisfying $(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)u=-f$ in $\R$.

\textup{(v)} Assume the Lyapunov hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}. Let $u,v>0$, $u=o(W)$, $v=o(W)$, satisfy
\[
(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)u\ge0,\qquad (\cA_\R+\lambda_p)v\le0.
\]
If $u\le Cv$ on one compact interaction collar containing the Lyapunov core, then $u\le Cv$ on $\R$. If equality of the optimal constant is attained at one point and both differential inequalities are equalities, then $u$ and $v$ are proportional.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:05:52.423809+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_86b032be2503acb14910aa599130d995a3052f2b43f489c4b584dbc535f8c128","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition proposition4.7 of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] [[WOS:000542157900013], Lemma 6.1]
    Let $B>0$, and $\zeta\in\Gamma_B$ be a random variable having a finite, $n$-independent log-Sobolev constant. Consider $A_n\sim\operatorname{Sym}_n(\zeta)$, and denote by $\sigma_1,\cdots,\sigma_n$ the eigenvalues of $A_n$. Define the empirical measure $\rho_{A_n}^n$ via

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:45:02.063106+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_86b3fa63a0310eb4b2320ffced0a75087f6a0711096dc40d34bee6ba13f5db0d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def:size-biased-tree of arXiv:2601.00119, 'The largest common subtree of two random trees'] Let $\tau_\infty$ be a random infinite plane tree and $U_\infty=(J_i)_{i\geq 1}$ be a sequence of random positive integers. Set $U_0=\varnothing$ and $U_n=(J_1,\ldots,J_n)$ for all $n\geq 1$. We say that $(\tau_\infty,U_\infty)$ is a \emph{size-biased Bienaymé tree with offspring distribution $\mu$} if it satisfies the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] For all $n\geq 0$, $U_n$ is almost surely an element of $\tau_\infty$.
    
    \item[(b)] The random pairs $(\mathrm{k}_{U_n}(\tau_\infty),J_{n+1})$ for $n\geq 0$ are i.i.d.~and distributed as follows:
    \[\forall k,j\in\mathbb{N}^*,\quad \mathbf{P}(\mathrm{k}_{U_n}(\tau_\infty)=k\, ;\, J_{n+1}=j)={\mathbf 1}_{\left\{j\leq k\right\}}\mu(k)/m_\mu.\]
    
    \item[(c)] Conditionally given $(\mathrm{k}_{U_n}(\tau_\infty),J_{n+1})_{n\geq 0}$, the random plane trees $\theta_{U_n*(j)}\tau_\infty$ for $n\geq 0$ and $j\in \{1,\ldots,\mathrm{k}_{U_n}(\tau_\infty)\}\setminus\{J_{n+1}\}$ are independent Bienaymé trees with offspring distribution $\mu$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X_1, ..., X_n independent (not necessarily identically distributed)","f(X) square-integrable","no boundedness or Lipschitz assumption; those are needed only for the exponential tail (McDiarmid), not for the variance bound"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.049339+00:00","domain":"concentration of measure (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_86cf1e9337e554632973d7e667c68acea223b8cc18e958d4dd1752b1136526fa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and f a square-integrable function of them, Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n). Let X_1', ..., X_n' be an independent copy of the X_i and Z_i' = f(X_1, ..., X_i', ..., X_n) the value with the i-th coordinate resampled. Then Var(Z) <= (1/2) sum_{i=1}^n E[(Z - Z_i')^2] = sum_{i=1}^n E[(Z - E_i Z)^2], where E_i denotes expectation over X_i alone (Efron and Stein 1981; Steele 1986 for the constant 1/2). Equivalently Var(Z) <= sum_i E[Var_i(Z)]. The inequality is tight for linear f. It needs independence of the coordinates (it is the sum over coordinates of one-coordinate variances, a tensorization statement) but no boundedness; the bounded-differences (McDiarmid) inequality is the exponential-tail counterpart under the extra assumption that changing one coordinate changes f by at most c_i, in which case Var(Z) <= (1/4) sum c_i^2.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:22:20.961325+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_86f69de57732201a2c189534d165b1ced1df60f730328d3dd41bb0d30d77a327","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 34 (Tikhonov reconstruction from weak data) of arXiv:2604.20634, 'Distributional Statistical Models:\\ \large Weak Moments, Cumulants, and a Central Limit T'] Let $\varphi\in\mathcal{S}(\R)$ satisfy $\varphi(x)>0$ for all $x$, and

\[

:=

\]
Then:

\[

\frac{\lambda}{\varphi^2 + \lambda} f

\]
In particular, if $\lambda=\lambda(\delta)\downarrow 0$ and
$\delta/\sqrt{\lambda(\delta)}\to 0$, then

{"assumptions":["the domain is reflexive for the converse direction","compactness always implies complete continuity, with no reflexivity needed","terminology must be checked in older sources, where 'completely continuous' can mean 'compact'"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:46.573661+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, compact operators, Banach space theory","id":"claim_8709e389c807abb0604721e0033898acf007e6902456fe85b7b0c2585491a096","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Compact operators are completely continuous: they send weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent ones. The converse needs the domain to be reflexive, because the proof runs 'bounded sequence -> weakly convergent subsequence -> norm convergent image', and the first arrow is exactly reflexivity (with the Eberlein-Smulian theorem). The counterexample is the identity of l^1: by Schur's property, every weakly convergent sequence in l^1 converges in norm, so the identity is completely continuous, yet it is not compact because l^1 is infinite-dimensional. A related trap in the other direction is the use of weak sequential compactness of the unit ball: in a nonreflexive space such as c_0 or L^1([0,1]) a bounded sequence need not have any weakly convergent subsequence, so arguments of the form 'the sequence is bounded, so pass to a weakly convergent subsequence, and then apply compactness of T' are invalid there. Also note that the older literature uses 'completely continuous' as a synonym for 'compact'; when reading a classical source, check which meaning is in force before transporting a statement.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.684375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_872275d9465d671e04c6a26b80dfce8663fa08fc9e3ab19fa8af73023d3c07f6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Classification of entire logarithmic signatures) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $\gamma:[0,T]\to V$ be continuous and of bounded variation, and put
\[
\overline\gamma_t=\gamma_t-\gamma_0,
\qquad
 g=S(\gamma),\qquad l=\log g,\qquad v=\gamma_T-\gamma_0.
\]
Assume $R(l)=\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $v=0$, then $g=1$; equivalently, $\gamma$ is tree-like.
\item If $v\neq0$, there is $t_*\in[0,T]$ such that, with
\[
\alpha=\overline\gamma|_{[0,t_*]},
\qquad a=S(\alpha),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
S(\gamma)=a\e^v a^{-1}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Conversely, if $a$ is a bounded-variation signature, then $a\e^v a^{-1}$ has an entire logarithmic signature for every $v\in V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.238624+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8728b00822c0b2b9e9c41ed866ca109ce6620ab1d01750182a26ffe444532798","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:box-counting-dimensions of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] {Falconer2014}}]

For a nonempty bounded set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\delta>0\), let
\(N_\delta(F)\) be the least number of closed balls of radius \(\delta\)
needed to cover \(F\).  The upper box-counting dimension of \(F\) is
\[
\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}(F)
=
\limsup_{\delta\to0}
\frac{\log N_\delta(F)}{-\log\delta}.
\]
The base of the logarithm is immaterial in this ratio.

The upper modified box-counting dimension of a set
\(E\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is defined by
\[
\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{MB}}(\emptyset)=0,
\]
and, for \(E\ne\emptyset\), by
\[
\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{MB}}(E)
=
\inf
\left\{
\sup_j \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}(E_j):
\begin{array}{l}
E\subseteq\bigcup_{j\in\omega} E_j,\\
E_j\ne\emptyset\text{ and }E_j\text{ is bounded for every }j
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:15:15.526637+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8741c83666e0bdf4dbf5f8d92e8064887e53adb4fdf64d68c7420a3aef232d62","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def-srr2 of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] A density $h(u,v)$ on $[0,1]^{2}$ is \textit{strictly
reverse regular of order 2} ($SRR_{2}$) if 
\begin{equation}
h(u_{1},v_{1})\,h(u_{2},v_{2})\;<\;h(u_{1},v_{2})\,h(u_{2},v_{1})

\end{equation}
for all $0\leq u_{1}<u_{2}\leq 1$ and $0\leq v_{1}<v_{2}\leq 1$ such that
all four points lie in a region where $h>0$.

Equivalently (under standard regularity so that conditional expectation and
density exist), for $H$ a bivariate distribution with density $h$, the
conditional mean $x\mapsto m_{2|1}^{H}(x)=E[\,X_{2}^{H}\mid X_{1}^{H}=x\,]$
is strictly decreasing on every compact subinterval of $(0,1)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:38:58.691332+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_876673648c2c4bb84119b0dee853f23f3812876d768892796c7dbd30fb06a01f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition eq:ascention_proto of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$ be a positive integer, and consider two sequences
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \quad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m)
\]
 of positive integers in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$
Assume that $i_1,\dots,i_m$ are distinct
and that none of them equals $n$.
Then the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \left[ r_{i_1 j_1} r_{i_2 j_2} \cdots r_{i_m j_m} \right]
\]
vanishes unless $\bm{j}$ is a permutation of $\bm{i}$.

\begin{equation} 
\sum_{t=0}^f (-1)^{m-t} \binom{f}{t} \frac{1}{n^{\uparrow (m-t)}},

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.163448+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87759836e81f17895efdf77150cc0707d64729d7d8cfffca25cd91b8db896b68","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 26 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall $F^{\riv}$ from \eqref{e:F.iv}, and
$F^{\rv}$ from \eqref{e:F.rv}. 
    For sufficiently large $N$, we have for all $t\in \R$
    \[
    \P(F^{\riv} \ge t)
    \le \P\bigg(
    F^{\rv}+ \frac{\epsilon'}{5}
    \ge t
    \bigg) + e^{-cN} \,.
    \]
That is, $F^{\rv}$
approximately stochastically dominates
$F^{\riv}$.

\begin{proof}
For each $j\in[r]$, let
    \[\bv_1(B_j)\equiv
    \frac{\bz(B_j)}{\|\bz(B_j)\|}\,,\]
and complete this to a (Haar random)
orthonormal basis
$(\bv_a(B_j) : 1\le a \le |B_j|)$
of $\R^{|B_j|}$. Let $\tau_j \equiv \|\bz^{B_j}\|^2 / |B_j|$. Then we can rewrite \eqref{e:F.v} and \eqref{e:bar.F.U} as
    \begin{align*}
    F_v(\bG,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j}{MN}
        \sum_{a=1}^{|B_j|}
        (
         \bv_a(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2
         \,,\\
    \bar{F}_U(\bG,\bz,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\tau_j \hU_j}{MN}
        ( \bv_1(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2\,.
    \end{align*}
If we split off the $a=1$ term of $F_v$ and combine it with $\bar{F}_U$, then we see that $F_v+\bar{F}_U$ is the same as the sum of the two terms
    \begin{align*}
    F_{v\setminus1}(\bG,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j}{MN}
        \sum_{a=2}^{|B_j|}
        (
         \bv_a(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2
         \,,\\
    \bar{F}_{U+}(\bG,\bz,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j+
            \tau_j \hU_j}{MN}
        ( \bv_1(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Fix arbitrary representatives $a_j \in B_j$, and denote
    \begin{align*}
    \acute{F}_{v\setminus}
    (\bG,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j}{MN}
        \sum_{a\in B_j\setminus a_j}
        (\bg^a,\by)^2
    \le F_v(\bG,\by)\,, \\
    \acute{F}_{U+}
        (\tbmeta,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j+
            \tau_j \hU_j}{MN}
    (\tbmeta^{r+j},\by)^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Recalling $F_w$ from \eqref{e:F.w} and
$\bar{F}_B$ from \eqref{e:bar.F.B}, define
    \begin{align*}
    \acute{F}_-(\bG,\tbmeta,\by)
    &\equiv F_w(\by)
    +\acute{F}_{v\setminus}
        (\bG,\by)
    +\bar{F}_B(\tbmeta,\by)
    +\acute{F}_{U+}
        (\tbmeta,\by)
    \\
    &\le F_w(\by)
    +\acute{F}_v(\bG,\by)
        +\bar{F}_B(\tbmeta,\by)
        +\acute{F}_{U+}
        (\tbmeta,\by)
    \equiv\ddot{F}(\bG,\tbmeta,\by)
    \end{align*}
By gaussian rotational invariance,
$\bar{F}$ has the same distribution (as processes indexed by $\by$) as $\acute{F}_-$, which in term is dominated by $\ddot{F}$. Finally, the difference between $\ddot{F}$ and $\acute{F}$
is bounded, for all $\|\by\|^2=N$, by
\[
        \bigg|\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{(\tau_j-1) \hU_j}{MN}
        (\tbmeta^{r+j}, \by)^2\bigg|
        \le \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{|\tau_j-1| |\hU_j|}{M}
        \|\tbmeta^{r+j}\|^2\,.
    \]
It holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$ that
    \[|\tau_j-1| \le \frac{\alpha \iota \epsilon'}{20r},\quad
    \max_{j\in[r]}
    \frac{\|\tbmeta^{r+j}\|}{N^{1/2}}
     \le 2\,.
    \]
On this event, the above quantity is bounded by 
    \[
        r \cdot \frac{\alpha \iota \epsilon'}{20} \cdot \frac{\|\hU\|_\infty}{M} \cdot 4N 
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:fp-normalization-bd}}{\le} \frac{\epsilon'}{5}\,,
    \]
which concludes the proof.\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu_1 and mu_2 strictly positive on a common finite distributive lattice closed under meet and join","the pointwise Holley ratio condition mu_1(x v y) mu_2(x ^ y) >= mu_1(x) mu_2(y) holding for all pairs x, y","events being compared are increasing with respect to the same partial order used to define the lattice"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.972949+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8778e7a65e49c4be1f23175bfeb78103a14f5cdd5ed03f4f8cc84200ea1e4687","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu_1, mu_2 be strictly positive probability measures on a common finite distributive lattice (e.g. {0,1}^E ordered coordinatewise). If the Holley condition holds, mu_1(x v y) mu_2(x ^ y) >= mu_1(x) mu_2(y) for all configurations x, y, then mu_1 stochastically dominates mu_2, meaning mu_1(A) >= mu_2(A) for every increasing (monotone) event A. This is a purely combinatorial, pointwise sufficient condition for stochastic domination between two measures that need not be product measures, and it strictly generalizes the FKG inequality, which is recovered as the special case mu_1 = mu_2. It is the standard tool for comparing Gibbs measures with different boundary conditions or parameters in the Ising model, the random-cluster model, and other lattice systems, and for monotone-coupling arguments more generally. The theorem does not establish the Holley condition itself, which can be as hard to verify as the comparison one is trying to prove; it gives only qualitative stochastic domination, with no quantitative bound on the total-variation distance between mu_1 and mu_2; and it requires strict positivity of both measures on the entire lattice. Typical failure: Assuming the Holley condition holds because mu_1 looks larger than mu_2 in some averaged or marginal sense; the condition is a pointwise, multiplicative statement that must hold for every pair of configurations including their join and meet, and it can fail even when mu_1 does stochastically dominate mu_2 for unrelated reasons, or when only checked on a generating set of configurations rather than genuinely all pairs. Canonical reference: Holley, 1974, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Georgii, Haggstrom and Maes, 2001, in Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena, vol. 18, Academic Press.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:22:46.462522+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8799228f51664a63a96697e1e1b421fa75b84701342c09e29dfb0fd72c5e5f0c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 23 of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] [The geometric wave-transport-divergence-curl formulation of the compressible Euler equations]
	
	Let $\overline{\varrho} > 0$ be any constant background density,\footnote{Recall
	that $\LogDensity$ depends on $\overline{\varrho}$; see Def.~\ref{D:LOGDENS}.}
	and assume that $(\LogDensity,v^1,v^2,v^3,\Ent)$ is
	a solution
	to the compressible Euler equations 
	\eqref{E:BVIEVOLUTION}--\eqref{E:BENTROPYEVOLUTION}
	in three spatial dimensions under an arbitrary equation of state $p = p(\varrho,\Ent)$ with positive sound speed 
	$\Speed$ (see \eqref{E:SOUNDSPEED}).
	Let $\Transport$ be the material derivative vectorfield defined in \eqref{E:MATERIALDERIVATIVEVECOTRFIELD},
	let $\gfour$ be the acoustical metric from Def.~\ref{D:ACOUSTICALMETRICDEF},
	let $\square_{\gfour}$ be the corresponding covariant wave operator from Def.~\ref{D:COVWAVEOP},
	let $\almostRiemannfunction  = \almostRiemannfunction(\LogDensity,\Ent)$ be the function from
	Def.~\ref{D:ALMOSTRIEMANNINVARIANTS},
	and let 
	$\vortrenormalized$,
	$\GradEnt$,
	$\VortVort$,
	and
	$\DivGradEnt$
	be the higher order variables from Def.~\ref{D:HIGHERORDERFLUIDVARIABLES}.
	Then the scalar-valued functions
	$\LogDensity$,
	$v^i$, 
	$\almostRiemann_{(\pm)}$, 
	$\Ent$,
$\vortrenormalized^i$,
$\GradEnt^i$,
$\Flatdiv \vortrenormalized$,
$\VortVort^i$,
$\DivGradEnt$,
and
$(\Flatcurl \GradEnt)^i$,
	($i=1,2,3$),
	also solve the following equations,
	where $\upepsilon_{ijk}$ is the fully antisymmetric symbol normalized by $\upepsilon_{123}=1$, 
	and \textbf{the Cartesian component functions $v^i$ are 
	treated as scalar-valued functions
	under covariant differentiation on LHS~\eqref{E:VELOCITYWAVEEQUATION}}:

\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{\upshape Covariant wave equations}}.
	\begin{subequations} 
	\begin{align}
		\square_{\gfour(\wavearray)} v^i
		& = 
			- 
			\Speed^2 \exp(2 \LogDensity) \VortVort^i
			+ 
			\nullform_{(v)}^i
			+ 
			\mathfrak{L}_{(v)}^i,
				\\

	\square_{\gfour(\wavearray)} \LogDensity
	& = 
		-
		\exp(\LogDensity) \frac{p_{;\Ent}}{\overline{\varrho}} \DivGradEnt
		+
		\nullform_{(\LogDensity)}
		+
		\mathfrak{L}_{(\LogDensity)},
			 
				\\
	\square_{\gfour(\wavearray)} \Ent
	& = 
		\Speed^2 \exp(2 \LogDensity)  \DivGradEnt
		+
		\mathfrak{L}_{(\Ent)}.
	
\end{align}
\end{subequations}\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{\upshape Transport equations}}.
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}	\Transport \vortrenormalized^i
	& = \mathfrak{L}_{(\vortrenormalized)}^i,
		
		\\
	\Transport \Ent
	& = 0,	
		
			\\
	\Transport \GradEnt^i
	& = \mathfrak{L}_{(\GradEnt)}^i.
		
\end{align}
\end{subequations}\medskip	
	
\noindent \underline{\textbf{\upshape Transport-divergence-curl system for the specific vorticity}}.
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align} 
	\Flatdiv \vortrenormalized
	& = 
		\mathfrak{L}_{(\Flatdiv \vortrenormalized)},
		\\
\Transport \VortVort^i
& = 
	\mainnullform_{(\VortVort)}^i 
	+ 
	\nullform_{(\VortVort)}^i
	+	
	\mathfrak{L}_{(\VortVort)}^i. 
	 
\end{align}	
\end{subequations}\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{\upshape Transport-divergence-curl system for the entropy gradient}}.
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align} 	
\Transport \DivGradEnt
	& =  \mainnullform_{(\DivGradEnt)} +
			\nullform_{(\DivGradEnt)},
 
			\\
	(\Flatcurl \GradEnt)^i & = 0.
	
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
	Above, the main terms $\mainnullform_{(\VortVort)}^i$ and $\mainnullform_{(\DivGradEnt)}$ 
	in the transport equations for the modified fluid variables are 
	the \textbf{null forms relative to} $\gfour$ (see Def.~\ref{D:STANDARDNULLFORMS})
	defined by:\footnote{Actually, the last the last term on
 RHS\,\eqref{E:TRANSPORTDIVGRADENTMAINTERMS} is not a null form, but rather 
	a simpler harmless error term.}
	\begin{subequations}
	\begin{align}
	\begin{split} 
		\mainnullform_{(\VortVort)}^i & \eqdef 
		- 
		2 \updelta_{jk} \upepsilon_{iab} \exp(-\LogDensity) (\partial_a v^j) \partial_b \vortrenormalized^k
		+
		\upepsilon_{ajk}
		\exp(-\LogDensity)
		(\partial_a v^i) 
		\part (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.294390+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_879ca6c3e966bedb0f2d0fdbf7379ce0b7538e14538cc96793b30a7b7f18d781","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition $\varepsilon$-nets, covering numbers, and packing numbers of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho)$ be a metric space and let $\varepsilon>0$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.339159+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87a90c70f96c1bc9b97397372cb4133eac320cac7fdcc3a49f87a50c18deee80","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 17 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (cf.\ Lemma 5.7 of \cite{BFS}) 
Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$  
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists a constant 
$C = C(u_0,\ell_0)$ such that, for $\ell \geq  \ell_0$, and a function
$h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}   
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}}h(s,x)\\
& \hskip 10mm \times
\Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}\big[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)\big] 
-\frac{1}{2} \tilde f''(u_0) \Big((\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x) - u_0)^2- \tfrac{{\rm var}(u_0) }{2\ell +1}\Big)\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag \\
& \hskip 5mm\leq \ CT^{p-1} N^p \ell^{-3p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in \T_N}|h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times\Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)] 
-\tilde f'(u_0)
\big(\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)-u_0\big) \Big\} ds\Big|^p\Big] 
\notag  \\
& \hskip 10mm
 \leq \ CT^{p-1} N^p \ell^{-p} \|f\|^{p}_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})} \int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in \T_N}|h(t,x)|^p dt.  \notag
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Omega open in R^n (bounded for the global space)","k >= 0 integer","0 < alpha <= 1"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:46.146895+00:00","domain":"function spaces for PDE","id":"claim_87b428ba115e4106c40672432530cf35b534ad47a8d140e4c6e4bfa9dc7929da","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Omega in R^n be open, k >= 0 an integer and 0 < alpha <= 1. For a function v on a set S, [v]_{alpha;S} = sup over x, y in S with x != y of |v(x) - v(y)| / |x - y|^alpha. For bounded Omega, C^{k,alpha}(closure of Omega) is the space of u in C^k(Omega) such that every derivative D^beta u with |beta| <= k extends continuously to the closure and ||u||_{C^{k,alpha}} = sum_{|beta| <= k} sup_Omega |D^beta u| + sum_{|beta| = k} [D^beta u]_{alpha;Omega} is finite; it is a Banach space. The local space C^{k,alpha}(Omega) consists of u in C^k(Omega) with u in C^{k,alpha}(closure of U) for every open U with compact closure in Omega. C^{0,1} is the Lipschitz class; C^{1,1} (bounded second difference quotients, equivalently W^{2,infinity} locally) is strictly larger than C^2. A bounded open set Omega is a C^{k,alpha} domain if every boundary point has a neighborhood U such that, in suitable rotated coordinates, Omega intersected with U = {x in U : x_n > g(x_1, ..., x_{n-1})} for some g of class C^{k,alpha}. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:48:49.898663+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87c6b58b312714c9f075d9efd8a22d4a6c9bf1de6d27ea97ba26e4513835c354","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:deywu23_SK of arXiv:2510.26960, 'Free energy fluctuations in SK and related spin glass models: \\ A literature survey'] {DeyWu23}}] 
Consider the SK model with Gaussian disorder. Assume that the external field is scaled as $h = \rho N^{-\alpha}$ for some positive constants $\rho$ and $\alpha$. Let
 \begin{equation} 
v_1^2 := -\frac12\log(1-\beta^2) - \frac{\beta^2}{2} \quad \text{and} \quad v_2^2 := \frac{\beta^2}{2(1-\beta^2)}.
 \end{equation} 
We then have the following statements of convergence in distribution. 
\begin{enumerate}
     \item (Sub-critical) For $\alpha>1/4$ and $\beta<1$,
        \[
        N \left(F_N - \left(\log(2\cosh h)+\frac{N-1}{4N}\beta^2\right)\right) \to \mathcal{N}(-\frac12 v_1^2, v_1^2).
        \]
        \item (Critical) For $\alpha=1/4$ and $\beta<1$,
        \[
        N \left(F_N - \left(\log(2\cosh h)+\frac{N-1}{4N}\beta^2\right)\right) \to \mathcal{N}(-\frac12 \left(v_1^2 + \rho^4 v_2^2 \right), v_1^2+\rho^4 v_2^2).
        \]
        \item (Super-critical) There exists $\beta_0\leq 1$ such that, for $\alpha<1/4$ and $\beta<\beta_0$,
        \[
        \frac{\sqrt{N}}{h^2}\left(F_N - \left(\mathbb{E} \log(2\cosh(\beta\sqrt{q}\eta+h))+\frac14\beta^2(1-q)^2\right)\right) \to \mathcal{N}(0,v_2^2),
        \]
        where $\eta$ is a standard Gaussian random variable and $q\in [0,1]$ is the solution to 
        \[
        q = \mathbb{E} \tanh^2(\beta \sqrt{q}\eta +h).
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.910528+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87f3967443c18424bb5600bfd5ad952aca99f1ea7fd50bc731e86d172bc9ad7f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 16 (Randomly initialized neurons specialize) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Under \cref{data:neuron-specialization}, \cref{train:neuron-specialization} and \cref{init:neuron-specialization}
there are universal constants $R_0,C<\infty$ such that the following holds
for every $R\geq R_0$. For almost every draw of
$\omega_1^0,\ldots,\omega_m^0$, there are cluster labels
$J_1,\ldots,J_m\in[K]$ and orientations
$\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_m\in\{\pm1\}$ such that, for every $\delta>0$, there
exist a finite time $T_\delta$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$ for which
\[
    0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \left\|
        \frac{w_j(T_\delta)}{\|w_j(T_\delta)\|_2}

distributed on $[K]$. Consequently,
\[

\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.143238+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88171b3bff4767675288df1575dfdfc282982120431430153abd723045933ee1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:constant-overshoot-families of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] Consider the first passage of an additive mean-zero walk above an integer level.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Bounded integer up-steps (C1).} If the increments take integer values with maximal up-step $+1$, the walk lands exactly one unit above the level, so $\omega=1$. (For any such $X$, $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>0]=1$.)
\item \emph{Geometric positive increments (C(2,$\cdot$)).} If the positive increment has the geometric law on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$ with success probability $q\in(0,1)$, namely $\mathbb{P}(X=k)=q(1-q)^{k-1}$, then by the memorylessness of the geometric the conditional overshoot is again geometric with the same law, and $\omega=1/q$. (Equivalently, the companion's parametrization gives $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>k]=k+p/(1-p)$ in the decay-ratio convention; see (rem:geometric-param of the paper).)
\item \emph{Exponential right tail (C(3,$a$)).} If the positive increment has an exponential right tail, $\mathbb{P}(X>y)=c e^{-ay}$, then by the memorylessness of the exponential the overshoot is exponential with mean $\omega=1/a$, and $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>y]=y+1/a$ (the constant $c$ is irrelevant).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T16:46:51.519522+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_881cc0825a27c3b2e8c5d0212f5b4813ca1a41b021b0e5c2c36188af50956696","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In probability theory, the central limit theorem states that, under certain circumstances, the probability distribution of the scaled mean of a random sample converges to a normal distribution as the sample size increases to infinity. {"assumptions":["(X,d) is a compact metric space","T: X -> X is continuous","for the non-compact extension, T is uniformly continuous and the entropy is taken as a supremum over compact subsets, and then depends on the uniform equivalence class of d"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.814666+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_885e1c5ce5a142a5b0817a051568e1c6290d72f8e2a8225eed7dad76bf607388","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T: X -> X continuous. For n >= 1 define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max_{0 <= i <= n-1} d(T^i x, T^i y). A set E contained in X is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if d_n(x,y) > eps for all distinct x, y in E; let s_n(eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n, eps)-separated set. A set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if for every x in X there is y in F with d_n(x,y) <= eps; let r_n(eps) be the smallest cardinality of an (n, eps)-spanning set. Both are finite by compactness. THEOREM (Bowen, Dinaburg): h_top(T) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log s_n(eps) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log r_n(eps), and this common value coincides with the Adler-Konheim-McAndrew topological entropy defined through open covers. The limits in eps exist in [0, +infinity] because s_n(eps) and r_n(eps) are nonincreasing in eps, so the inner quantities are nonincreasing in eps. The two counts are comparable at shifted scales: r_n(eps) <= s_n(eps) <= r_n(eps/2). SHARP EDGES. (a) The order of the limits is not negotiable: for a FIXED eps the quantity limsup_n (1/n) log s_n(eps) is in general strictly smaller than h_top(T) (it is the 'entropy at scale eps'), and it is only after eps -> 0 that one gets the entropy. The single exception worth remembering is an expansive homeomorphism, where any eps below the expansive constant already gives the answer. (b) Compactness is used to make the counts finite and to make the value a topological invariant. Bowen's extension to a uniformly continuous map of a possibly non-compact metric space, taking the supremum of the above over compact subsets, defines a quantity h_d(T) that depends on the METRIC and not only on the topology: uniformly equivalent metrics give the same value, but merely topologically equivalent ones need not, so on non-compact spaces 'the topological entropy' is not well defined without naming the metric. (c) Separated and spanning counts measure ORBIT distinguishability over a finite time window; they say nothing by themselves about invariant measures. The link to measures is the variational principle, h_top(T) = sup over T-invariant Borel probabilities mu of h_mu(T), which is a separate theorem and is not proved by the counting argument below. (d) The definition uses only forward iterates 0, ..., n-1, and for a homeomorphism this already gives the entropy of T; the two-sided window max over |i| <= n gives the same number, not twice it.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0116-deterministic-1-epsilon-approximation-of-the-cover-time","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.047234+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88689b59ad4cd74fb60fc028182b55645390b06a9646cda648134edb7bc52296","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the Gaussian free field characterisation can be made asymptotically exact. Result: DLP show t_cov ≍ |E| (E max GFF)^2; the later result of Ding (2012, 'Asymptotics of cover times via Gaussian free fields: bounded-degree graphs and general trees') gives asymptotic equality t_cov ~ |E| (E max eta)^2 for bounded-degree graphs when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, and Zhai (2018) proved the asymptotic formula for general graphs under the same condition. Given the asymptotic formula, a (1+eps) approximation of t_cov reduces to a (1+eps) approximation of E max of a Gaussian vector with given covariance (the Green function), which is a deterministic computational problem: computing E max of a Gaussian vector to within 1+eps is not known to be in deterministic polynomial time in general (the majorizing-measure/generic-chaining bounds are only within constants; exact computation of Gaussian maxima expectations is #P-hard in some formulations). So the question reduces, for graphs with t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, to the deterministic approximability of E max of a Gaussian vector with a graph-Laplacian covariance; a positive answer would follow from a deterministic FPTAS for Gaussian expected maxima on such covariances, which is open; graphs with t_cov ≍ t_hit (e.g. cycles, where the cover time is dominated by hitting times) need a separate treatment and are the easier case since hitting times are computable exactly. Reduction recorded. Key identity: t_cov ~ |E| (E max GFF)^2 when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity (Ding; Zhai), so (1+eps)-approximation reduces to approximating a Gaussian expected maximum. Obstruction: No deterministic (1+eps) algorithm for Gaussian expected maxima with general covariance.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.677288+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_888a46adcfccab289a1f78fb9b6dabc6c5d99077795a9c2450bddc2f5dd0ff31","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 15 (Lossless-chart factorization) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $(\mathsf Z,Z)$ be a $\cP$-causal state.  Let
\[
 \mathcal O:\mathsf Z\to\mathsf R,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D:\mathsf R\to\mathsf Z
\]
be stable-causal maps between causal Polish spaces such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D\mathcal O=I_{\mathsf Z}.
\end{equation}
Then $\mathcal O$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed retract
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal O(\mathsf Z)=\operatorname{Fix}(\mathcal O\mathcal D)
 \subseteq\mathsf R.
\end{equation}
This retract is generated by the stable-causal idempotent
$\mathcal O\mathcal D$.
For a $\cP$-causal source state $(\mathsf S,S)$, a joint realization of the
chart is a stable-causal map $\Psi:\mathsf S\to\mathsf R$ satisfying
$\Psi(S)=\mathcal O(Z)$ $P$-almost surely for every $P\in\cP$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item Every joint realization yields the stable-causal factor
$\mathcal D\Psi:S\to Z$, and every stable-causal factor $R:S\to Z$ yields
the joint realization $\mathcal O R$.  Thus
\begin{equation}
 \Psi\longmapsto\mathcal D\Psi,
 \qquad
 R\longmapsto\mathcal O R
\end{equation}
are inverse after maps agreeing on the realized source state under every law
are identified.  In particular, the source realizes the lossless chart if and
only if $Z\preceqsc S$, and the factor is unique on the realized source.

\item Every stable-causal readout
$F:\mathsf Z\to\mathsf T$ factors through the chart on its image:
\begin{equation}
 F=(F\mathcal D)\mathcal O.
\end{equation}
The factor $F\mathcal D$ is unique on $\mathcal O(\mathsf Z)$.  If in addition
$\mathcal O\mathcal D=I_{\mathsf R}$, it is the unique factor on all of
$\mathsf R$.

\item Suppose a stable-causal map
$\pi:\mathsf Z\to\mathsf Y$ preserves the full chart in the sense that
$\mathcal O=\Psi\pi$ for a stable-causal
$\Psi:\mathsf Y\to\mathsf R$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 L:=\mathcal D\Psi
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 L\pi=I_{\mathsf Z}.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\pi$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed retract of $\mathsf Y$
generated by the stable-causal idempotent $P:=\pi L$, and
\[
 \pi(\mathsf Z)=\operatorname{Fix}(P).
\]
If $\pi$ is surjective, then $\pi$ is a stable-causal homeomorphism with
inverse $L$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:32:58.360363+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88c86abe4bf4f86f63a97de0fc403cccebe4bc03c105e579fad19371d28a51da","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2506.19064, 'Variational formula for the logarithmic potential of free additive convolutions'] If $\mu,\nu$ are compactly supported probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$, s.t. $\mu$ is non-degenerate, then the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\alph*)]
        
        
        
        \item 
        If $F_{\mu,\nu}$ has a critical point, then $h_{\mu,\nu}^*$ is the leftmost critical point. 
        
        \item  If $F_{\mu,\nu}$ has no critical points, then $h_{\mu,\nu}^* = \sup\dom( F_{\mu,\nu})$.
        
        \item  If $F_{\mu,\nu}$ has no critical points, then furthermore (i) $h_{\mu,\nu}^* = \supp_- \nu$
        and $g^*_{\mu\boxplus\nu} = G_\nu( \supp_- \nu )$, or (ii) $G_\mu( \supp_- \mu ) = G_\nu(h_{\mu,\nu}^*) = g^*_{\mu\boxplus\nu}$.

        \item  If there are constants $c_1,c_2>0$ s.t. $c_1^{-1}\varepsilon^{3/2}\le(\mu\boxplus\nu)(z_{\mu\boxplus\nu}^*,z_{\mu\boxplus\nu}^*+\varepsilon)\le c_1\varepsilon^{3/2}$ for all $\varepsilon \in (0,c_2)$, then $h_{\mu,\nu}^*$ is a local maximum of $F_{\mu,\nu}$ (see Figure \ref{fig:intro_E_mu_nu_z_F_mu_nu_shapes1} b,c,d).

        \item 
        If $F_{\mu,\nu}$ is strictly concave, then $h_{\mu,\nu}^*$ is the global maximum of $F_{\mu,\nu}$, and \eqref{eq:end_point_etc_special_cases_sc_MP} holds for the given $\mu,\nu$
        (see Figure \ref{fig:intro_E_mu_nu_z_F_mu_nu_shapes1} a,b).

        \item 
        The equation $F_{\mu,\nu}(h) = z$ has a solution in $\dom(F_{\mu,\nu}) \cap (-\infty,h_{\mu,\nu}^*)$ iff $z < z^*_{\mu \boxplus \nu}$. If $z < z^*_{\mu \boxplus \nu}$ then $h_{\mu,\nu}^<(z)$ is the unique solution in that set, and $G_{\mu \boxplus \nu}(z) = G_\nu(h_{\mu,\nu}^<(z))$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:54:10.967772+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88cb7556ccd342faa492330ba0134a35a972cc43c02694773098fd89c0bb1b32","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 11 of arXiv:2606.12820, 'Averaging principles for nonautonomous multiscale McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems'] For a matrix-valued map $h(\cdot,\cdot):\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n)\rightarrow\mR^{n \times d_1}$, we say $h\in C^{k,(2,2)}(\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$, if $h(x,\cdot)\in C^{(2,2)}(\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$ for any $x\in\mR^n$, $h(\cdot,\mu)\in C^k(\mR^n,\mR^{n \times d_1})$ for any $\mu\in\cP_2(\mR^n)$, and the derivatives
$$\p_x^ih(x,\mu),\quad \p_x^i\p_\mu h(x,\mu)(\tx),\quad\p_x^i\p_{\tx}\p_\mu h(x,\mu)(\tx),\quad 1\leq i\leq k,$$
$$\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx),\quad \p_{\tx}\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx),\quad \p_{\cx}\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx),\quad \p_{\cx}\p_{\tx}\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx)$$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.586864+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88ee07aa3c33f65af394a6c4c1552e67ace5d65ee20df2a5de2251b1df1d8a31","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.05679, 'Small ball probabilities and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for Gaussian Volterra p'] \cite[Lemma 1.1, p. 138]{JM1978}
		Let $\{Z(t):\ t\ge0\}$ be a separable, centered, real-valued Gaussian process. Assume that 
		\[
		\mathbb E\left[\left(Z(t+h)-Z(t)\right)^2\right]\le \varphi(h)^2, \ \ \ t>0, \  h>0,
		\]
		for some continuous nondecreasing function $\varphi$ with $\varphi(0)=0$. 
         Then, for every integer $K_3>1$, all $t,x>0$, and every sequence of positive numbers ${\theta(p)}_{p\in\mathbb N}$, we have
\begin{align*}
& \mathbb{P}\left\{ \sup_{0\le s\le t}|Z(s)-Z(0)|>x\varphi(t)+\sum_{p=1}^{\infty} \theta(p)\varphi\left(tK_3^{-2^p} \right)  \right\} \\
&\le K_3^2 e^{-x^2/2}+\sum_{p=1}^{\infty} K_3^{2^{p+1}}e^{-\theta(p)^2/2}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:33:11.957227+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88f589c614dce080d582de2c67c899001235973ddf37062cd739b20c516e639c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary Weak Simplex Conjecture of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[corollary]{cor:wsc}
Let $m=d+1$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let the
message $I$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$.  Under the channel
\[
  Y=\lambda x_I+Z,
  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),\quad \lambda>0,
\]
the average probability of correct maximum-likelihood decoding is no larger
than for a regular simplex.  For every fixed $\lambda>0$, equality holds if
and only if the $x_i$ form a regular simplex.  Thus the regular simplex is the
unique maximizer up to rotation and relabeling. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:27:32.362667+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89195fb4e2b885f516856d26bbebc1ca388452002583f8baa542f970ebabf2f5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:c2-reg of arXiv:2509.23086, 'On Optimal Markovian Couplings of L\'evy Processes'] Let $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\in\mathcal{G}_2^\Lambda(\mathbb R^d)$ be L\'evy generators with mean vectors $m_\mathcal{A},m_\mathcal{B}$ and covariance matrices $Q_\mathcal{A},Q_\mathcal{B}$.  
	Define
	\[
	U(t,x,y) := (x-y+t(m_\mathcal{A}-m_\mathcal{B}))^\top(m_\mathcal{A}-m_\mathcal{B}),
	\]
	and let $\{T_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ be a Markovian coupling semigroup of $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{J}\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$ be a Feller coupling generator.
	
	(i) It holds for all $t,h\ge 0$ and $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{2d}$:
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{h}{2}\,U(t,x,y)
		&\le (T_{t+h}c_2)(x,y)-(T_tc_2)(x,y) \\
		&\le h^2\big(|m_\mathcal{A}|^2+|m_\mathcal{B}|^2\big)
		+ h\big[\mathrm{tr}(Q_\mathcal{A}+Q_\mathcal{B})+U(t,x,y)\big].
	\end{align*}
	In particular, the map $t\mapsto (e^{t\mathcal{J}}c_2)(x,y)$ is locally Lipschitz. 
	
	(ii) One has $c_2\in C(\mathcal{J})$.
		
	(iii) If $\mathcal{J}$ itself is a L\'evy generator, then $c_2\in\bar D(\mathcal{J})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:53:30.625681+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_891cb2703b25c5c3e3bbbb7ad37346e11733aa8d810f7128a381237617dc2e99","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn Inner product on affine standard module of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $x, y \in V_{n,m}$ be two radial $(n,m)$-link states and $a,b \in \mathbb{C}$. Define the inner product $\langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m}$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Reflect $x$ across a vertical axis (mirror image).
    \item Glue $x$ to $y$ vertically, forming a closed link diagram called $\mathcal{G}(\alpha, \beta)$.

    \[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:44:12.639750+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_891e5969b139434a9afdd0868f09ad76f515b1ac378d364e113be1b5055d25f6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Schwartz space \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] The \emph{Schwartz space} \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) is the space of all infinitely differentiable functions 
\[
  \varphi: \mathbb{R}^d \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{C}
\]
such that for every pair of multi-indices \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}_0^d\), the seminorm
\[
  p_{\alpha,\beta}(\varphi)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}
  \bigl\lvert x^\alpha\,D^\beta \varphi(x)\bigr\rvert
\]
is finite. Here \(x^\alpha = x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_d^{\alpha_d}\) and 
\[
  D^\beta = \frac{\partial^{\beta_1}}{\partial x_1^{\beta_1}} \cdots \frac{\partial^{\beta_d}}{\partial x_d^{\beta_d}}.
\]
Equivalently, 
\[
  \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)
  \;=\;
  \Bigl\{
    \varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\;:\;\forall\,\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}_0^d,\;
    \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d} \lvert x^\alpha D^\beta \varphi(x)\rvert < \infty
  \Bigr\}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.039834+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8938038b8632ef098b1318e44fd5ec5d156c50c9f6d4eeac87a58c568d9d5409","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 27 (The two zones, geometrised) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] In the canonical realisation, for every $a$ and drift for which the
vertex condition \textup{(V)} holds --- in particular for $a=3,4$
by Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}, and for $5\le a\le8$ by the
numerical evidence of Remark~\ref{rem:walk-V-numeric} --- the
starting sites split into two consecutive zones about the
midpoint,
\[
\underbrace{+\ \cdots\ +}_{z<a/2}\quad
\underbrace{\bigl[\,0\,\bigr]_{a\ \mathrm{even}}}_{z=a/2}\quad
\underbrace{-\ \cdots\ -}_{z>a/2}\, ,
\]
where $\pm$ denotes the constant sign of
$\partial_\gamma C(e_z,\cdot)$. Two things must be distinguished.
That every orbit $\{z,a-z\}$ straddles the midpoint and contributes
exactly one site to each sign class is forced by the orbit
structure alone, and is independent of the parity of $a$. That the
class below the midpoint is the one labelled $+$, on the other
hand, is not: it depends on the orientation chosen for the
directors and on the global sign $\varepsilon$ of \textup{(V)}, and
is fixed here by the canonical orientation together with the sign
of the constant $-2q^{a}$ computed in
Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}. When $a$ is even the midpoint is
itself a site, the unique fixed point of $\sigma$, and it is
exactly reset-neutral; when $a$ is odd the value $a/2$ is not an integer, so no site is a
fixed point of $\sigma$, none is invariant, and the two index
ranges $z<a/2$ and $z>a/2$ exhaust the sites with no neutral index
between them. \textup{(}The ``zones'' are sets of integer sites
throughout, not regions of a continuum.\textup{)} This is the two-zone theorem
of Paper~I, obtained here as a corollary of the geometry: the two
zones are the two sides of the separatrix, the neutral site --- when
it exists --- is its intersection with the vertex set, and the
midpoint is fixed by the site involution $\sigma$, whose fixed
point it is, while the associated spherical reflection $R_L$ fixes
the separatrix pointwise; the two are distinct structures, kept
apart by Proposition~\ref{prop:three-involutions}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:54.984298+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_893e190fde9b409bd91adb514367f4e2c69762a64c3d8ad615b821f770c0783a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:intrinsic-persistency of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {wijesekera_constructive_1990}}] 
  $\Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent for any f-model $\mathfrak{M}$.
  \begin{proof}
    Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ and take any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only prove the cases with modal operators.

    Suppose that $x \leq x'$ and $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$,
    and take any $x'', y''$ such that $x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$.
    Here, $x \leq x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$ implies $x \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$ by $\leq$ being preorder,
    then $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$ implies $y'' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    Now suppose that $x \leq x'$ and $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$,
    and take any $x''$ such that $x' \leq x''$, then $x \leq x' \leq x''$ implies $x \leq x''$ by $\leq$ being preorder.
    Since $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, there is $y'' \sqsupset x''$ such that $y'' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.258899+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_894d63647a3652d93a61cb3ba7aba6bd142d16cec67bf95caa5a78e59ce5c7f5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 11 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $p \in S^m(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $U, V$ be two open sets of $\Rr^d$, $V$ being convex, and let $\chi : U \to V$ be a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying $\|\Jac \chi^{-1} - I_d\|_{L^{\infty}(V)} <1$. 
Let $\psi \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}_c(V)$ and $\rho \in \mathcal{C}_c^{\infty}(U)$ 
such that~\(\rho\) is equal to~\(1\) on a neighborhood of $\chi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp} \psi)$. If~\(f\) is compactly supported in~\(V\) set~\(C_\chi f\) the function corresponding to~\(f\circ \chi\) on~\(U\) and~\(0\) outside~\(U\). Operator~\(C_\chi\) is a bijection between functions compactly supported in~\(V\) and functions compactly supported in~\(U\).
Set 
\[
Q = \psi C_{\chi}^{-1} \rho \Op(p) \rho C_{\chi}\psi,
\]
and define $J(x,y)=\displaystyle\int_0^1 \Jac \chi^{-1}(tx+(1-t)y)^\top\mathrm{d}t$ for $x, y \in V$.

Then, there exists $q\in S^m(\Rr^d \times \Rr^d)$ such that $Q=\psi\Op(q)\psi$, and 
moreover, $q$ admits the following asymptotic expansion on a neighborhood of $\supp \psi$ included in~\(V\):
\begin{equation}
    
        q(x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{\rho(\chi^{-1}(x))}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !} \partial_y^\alpha \left.\partial_{\xi}^\alpha \left(\rho(\chi^{-1}(y))p\left(\chi^{-1}(x),J(x,y)^{-1}\xi\right)\left\vert\frac{\det \Jac \chi^{-1} (y)}{\det J(x,y)}\right\vert\right)\right\vert_{y=x}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.242501+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_895cfe1f7a99a92e12ef6e3745b0d8f821e23c4dd41df6ec46a73ebf705ad4e4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 (the constant-field Fourier representation) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] With $(\tau,\xi)$ the spacetime Fourier variables, $\lambda$ as in
\eqref{eq:Bmult}, and $\tau_\pm=\tau\pm\lambda$, one has

 \widetilde{\mathcal A^-f}=\mathrm i\tau_-\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\Box f}=-\tau_+\tau_-\widetilde f .
\end{equation}
Consequently $D_\pm=-\mathrm i\mathcal A^\pm$ are commuting self-adjoint
operators on $L^2(dt dy)$ and, for every Borel function $\Phi$,
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(D_+,D_-)f
 :=\big(\Phi(\tau_+,\tau_-)\widetilde f\big)^\vee

on its maximal domain.  Moreover

\]
so these groups are isometries on every $L^p$ and unitary on $L^2$.  In particular,

 [\Lambda^{\sreg},\mathcal B]=0

\end{equation}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:09:59.186137+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_897ee2b6d3af2e157311fa72c5bf16f678c0d118f389c8e6c3f86ca31d4e8f4c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:gaps-short of arXiv:2608.05123, 'A central limit theorem for the random assignment problem'] In the increasing ordering \(U_{(1)}<\cdots<U_{(n)}\),
\begin{equation}
 U_{(k+1)}-U_{(k)}=\frac{nE_k}{k(n-k)},\qquad
 E_k\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}{\rm Exp}(1),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 U_{(j)}=\sum_{k<j}\frac{E_k}{n-k}-\sum_{k\ge j}\frac{E_k}{k},
 \qquad
 \bar u_{j,n}:=\mathbb E U_{(j)}=\mathsf H_{j-1}-\mathsf H_{n-j}.
\end{equation}
Moreover
\[
 Z_n^{\rm gap}=\frac{n^{n-1}}{(n-1)!},\qquad
 \frac1n\sum_i\delta_{U_i}\Longrightarrow
 \ell(u)\,\mathrm d u,\quad
 \ell(u)=\frac{e^{-u}}{(1+e^{-u})^2},
\]
in \(W_2\), in probability.  If \(R=\osc U\), then
\begin{gather}
 R=O_{\mathbb P}(\log n),\qquad
 \mathbb E\sum_j(U_{(j)}-\bar u_{j,n})^2=2\mathsf H_{n-1},\\
 \mathbb E\left(\sum_j(U_{(j)}-\bar u_{j,n})^2\right)^2=O(\log^2n),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\left|\frac1n\sum_iU_i^2-\frac{\pi^2}{3}\right|
 =O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right).
\end{gather}
If \(\varpi_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{U_i}\) and
\(\bar\varpi_n=n^{-1}\sum_j\delta_{\bar u_{j,n}}\), then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E W_1(\varpi_n,\ell)^2=O(\log n/n),\qquad
 W_1(\bar\varpi_n,\ell)=O(\log n/n).
\end{equation}
For every fixed \(a,b,M\), there are \(A,C<\infty\), depending only
on \(a,b,M\), such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\bigl[n^a(1+R)^b\1_{\{R>A\log n\}}\bigr]\le Cn^{-M}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:50:44.865169+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89a2a44f297c0e4ebf99f60d795b7c6acb9c92db006509b1fef683f7c3d315ec","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 28 of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] The conditional covariance matrix

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.340351+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89ac5cad7b954e6da1ebf203c7018e3caa1dbffa166a9f1a94566752511ba361","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(d\ge 3\), let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(p_{d,n}\) denote its law. Assume
    \[
    d>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(\lambda>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
    \[
    \lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
    \]
    If
    \[
    \rho>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),
    \]
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:40:21.275184+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89bf1ca61f46ed2d1b79777bdae677faf97127de5de168917e2cfb75ea437b0b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an amenable group $\Gamma$
    admitting a finite-index left-orderable subgroup $H$, with
    $n=[\Gamma:H]$. Consider Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter $p\in(
    0,1)$, an exhaustive F{\o}lner sequence $(A_{r})$, and let $\mathcal{A}$
    be its orbit under $\Gamma$. Then there exists an $H$-fundamental set of
    edges $\tilde E\subset E$ such that, if the stationary $\mathcal{A}$-functional
    $F$ stabilizes in sequence and satisfies a finite moment condition on $\tilde
    E$, then:
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\displaystyle \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{1}{|A_{r}|}\Var_{p}\!\bigl
        (F(A_{r})\bigr)=\sigma^{2}$;

      \item $\displaystyle |A_{r}|^{-1/2}\bigl(F(A_{r})-\E_{p}[F(A_{r})]\bigr
        )\ \overset{d}{\Longrightarrow}\ \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})$,
    \end{enumerate}
    where
    \[
      \sigma^{2}= \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{e\in\tilde E}\E_{p}\!\left[\E_{p}\!\left
      [D_{e}^{\infty}\,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_{e}\right]^{2}\right].
    \]
    Here $D_{e}^{\infty}$ is the limit in probability of $D_{e}(\omega,xA_{r}
    ):=F(\omega,xA_{r})-F(\omega^{e},xA_{r})$ as $r\to\infty$ (the limit
    does not depend on $x$), and $\mathcal{F}_{e}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra
    generated by the edges preceding or equal to $e$ in an $H$-invariant total order on
    $E$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:58:38.089146+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89df85d62c42e0bbef6bca8b3a235e15e14883008bdae4c34b97f04df4e94abd","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] We define the fibered Wasserstein space of order \(p,q \in [1,\infty)\) as

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:26:20.492151+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89e168f74bd653d83855c27b98aadbf0f050b5d8f604388903e34be3896d57b7","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] Let $s = (\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n) \in \mathcal{S}_o$ be a non-null string, and let $\delta = \delta(s)$. For each positive splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, we have that there is some $1 \leq h_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - h_{s'}, h_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto h_{s'}$ on the domain $\mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$ can be chosen to be injective.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:47:53.347678+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89e63157b9ec44a88d0f0c0f01167883f75bb69e123300f577d0d560f6c5d8bd","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 4 (Convex order and irreducibility) of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\mu,\nu\in\Prob_1(\RR)$. We say that $\mu$ is dominated by $\nu$ in
convex order, and write $\mu\preceq_c \nu$, if
\[
	\int_{\RR}\varphi\,d\mu
	\leq
	\int_{\RR}\varphi\,d\nu
\]
for every convex function $\varphi:\RR\to\RR$ such that both integrals are
well-defined.

For $\rho\in\Prob_1(\RR)$, define its potential function by
\[
	C_\rho(x):=\int_{\RR}(y-x)^+\,\rho(dy),
	\qquad x\in\RR.
\]
We say that the pair $(\mu,\nu)$ is
irreducible if $\mu \preceq_c \nu$ and the set
\[
	I:=\{x\in\RR:C_\mu(x)<C_\nu(x)\}
\]
is an interval and satisfies $\mu(I)=1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:18.033823+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89f32938a2e30815b8e0ec3b38b48bc1bb4eec4cbd3f236097b7106338cf0cd7","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:fromfilling of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] The initial setting is defined as follows:

for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$.
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Fix an initialising high-level state $\Psi_0$  with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, 
 send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and birth rate~$\lambda$  (Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)).
For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Fix $t>\tau_0$, 
 and fix a tuple  
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} = \textup{filling}$, 
$\tau^{\psi_{t-1}} = t-1$, and $z_j^{\psi_{t-1}} = 0$ where $j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Consider the evolution of~$V$, conditioned on
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}$.

Define the following quantities, sets, and stopping times.
\[
\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} = \min\{t'  \geq t \colon \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')} = \textup{failure} \mbox{ or }j^{\Psi(t')} = j+1\}.\]
Let $O_0 = t-1$. For all positive integers $x$, let
\begin{align*}
I_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > O_{x-1} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via (R(item:R2 of the paper))(ii) from $j$-filling to $j$-refilling
} \}).\\
O_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > I_{x} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via  (R(item:R6 of the paper))(i) from $j$-stabilising to $j$-filling
} \}).
\end{align*}
Let 
\begin{align*} 
A &= \lceil 4(4 j)^{\phi} W_j\rceil.\\
\mathrm{Ready} &  
= \{ T'\geq t-1 \colon  
\mbox{ $\Psi(T')$ is a $j$-filling state,  
$T' + j^{24} \leq t+A$, and
$
F_j^{\Psi(T')}(T'+1) \ge \mu_j^{\overline{\gamma}} $ }
\}. 
\\
t_{\mathrm{min}} &= \min(\{t+A\} \cup \mathrm{Ready}).
\end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:32:20.751261+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a1fe2d33d15cb4c7617c937cf315961bd0beee778defe1c2724439c4a615514","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3 (=Theorem \ref{invtpoly}) of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of rank $n$, $S$ a torus subgroup of dimension being $n-1$, $T$ a maximal torus of $G$ containing $S$, $\mu\in \chi(T)$ a primitive character of $T$ such that $S=\text{ker }\mu$, $L$ a primitive weight in the weight lattice $\mathfrak{t}^*_\mathbb{Z}$ corresponding to $\mu$ after exponentiation, and $W$ the Weyl group of $G$. Define
	\[\Phi_L:=\left(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}} wL\right)^{n(L)}\in \text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W,\]
	where $W_{[L]}$ is the stabilizer of $[L]:=\{\pm L\}\in \mathfrak{t}^*/\{\pm 1\}$, $n(L)=1$ or 2 depending on whether $\displaystyle\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL$ is $W$-invariant or $W$-anti-invariant, i.e. 
	\[\displaystyle w'(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL)=\text{sgn}(w')\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL\text{ for all }w'\in W.\] 
	Then $(G, S)$ is isotropy formal if and only if $\Phi_L\notin (f_1, \cdots, f_n)^2$, where $f_1, \cdots, f_n$ are the fundamental $W$-invariant homogeneous polynomials on $\mathfrak{t}$, i.e. $\text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W=\mathbb{R}[f_1, \cdots, f_n]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:24:20.957928+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a200e155b746988852d7a3cdc34ec1f89cfa5cbba2b8068d868f5e293e2c9f0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm2.7 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] {\rm (Cuny and Lin)}.
 
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a real strictly stationary, 
{\bf reversible} Markov chain that satisfies $\alpha$-mixing with 
$\alpha_X(n) \to 0$ at least exponentially fast as $n \to \infty$.  
Suppose
$h: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$  is a Borel function such that
\begin{equation}
\label {eq2.71}
0\ <\ E[\, [h(X_0)]^2]\ <\ \infty \indent  {\rm and} \indent E[h(X_0)]\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}
Then $\sigma^2 := E[\, [h(X_0)]^2] + 2 \cdot \sum_{k=1}^\infty E[h(X_0) \cdot h(X_k)]$
exists in $(0, \infty)$, with the sum converging absolutely (in fact with the summands
decaying at least exponentially fast); and
$n^{-1} \textrm{\rm Var}(\sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)) \to \sigma^2$ as $n \to \infty$.
Further, $(1/(n^{1/2}\sigma)) \sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k) \to N(0,1)$ in distribution as $n \to \infty$.  

   Thus, letting $\sigma_n(h) := \|\sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)\|_2$ for each $n \in \mathbb N$, 
one has that $[\sigma_n(h)]^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)$ converges in distribution
to $N(0,1)$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Prey density N >= 0 and predator density P >= 0","Parameters r, K, s, tau, c, d are strictly positive constants"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T10:45:59.532356+00:00","domain":"dynamical systems","id":"claim_8a203d63401fe04430436767ea217341366ff22c6f1274a378d505cf3a215162","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"The deterministic Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey model is the planar autonomous dynamical system for prey density N >= 0 and predator density P >= 0 given by dN/dt = r*N*(1 - N/K) - (s*N*P)/(1 + s*tau*N) and dP/dt = -c*P + d*(s*N*P)/(1 + s*tau*N), where r > 0 is the intrinsic prey growth rate, K > 0 is the prey carrying capacity, s > 0 is the predator search rate, tau > 0 is the prey handling time, c > 0 is the predator mortality rate, and d > 0 is the conversion efficiency. In nondimensionalized coordinates, the system takes the form dN/dt = N*(1 - N/k) - (m*N*P)/(1 + N) and dP/dt = -c*P + (m*N*P)/(1 + N), where k > 0, m > 0, and c > 0.","status":"unverified"}
