{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.211673+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_96d41c51d74c33eb55f3eba30f7fb65c3d0270d0b9ef2e7eadb4f20d454a78e4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Consider $(A_p)_p$ in  Case \caseS or Case \caseR.
There exist constants $c, C>0$ such that for any finite set of primes $B$, and for any  $\{\phi_p\}_p \subset \C$ in Case \caseS or $\{\phi_p\}_p \subset \R$ in Case \caseR, there exists a coupling of $\langle\phi A\rangle_B$ with a  Gaussian $Z_{B}$ such that 
\[
  \mathrm{Cov}(Z_B) = \mathrm{Cov}\langle\phi A\rangle_B\,,
\]
and, letting $\Delta_{B} \coloneqq |\langle\phi A\rangle_B - Z_{B}|$, we have the first moment bound
\begin{align} 
  \E \Delta_{B} \leq C \min\bigg( V_{B}^{1/2} \,,\, \frac{T_{B}}{V_{B}} \bigg)
\end{align}
and the tail bound
\begin{align}
  \P(\Delta_{B} > u ) \leq Ce^{-c u^2/V_B}
\end{align}
for all $u\geq 0$, where we use the interpretation that $1/V_B \coloneqq 0$ if $V_B = 0$.

\begin{proof}
Since the case $V_B = 0$ is trivial, we assume throughout the proof $V_B>0$. Moreover, it is quick to show $\E\Delta_B \leq C V_B^{1/2}$: we simply take the independent coupling between $\langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B$ and $Z_B$ (they are realized as independent random variables on the same probability space). Then $\E\Delta_B \leq \E|\langle\phi A\rangle_B| + \E|Z_B| \leq C V_B^{1/2}$ by Jensen's inequality.

To prove \eqref{eq:block-coupling-expectation}, it  remains to show $\mathbb{E}\Delta_B \le CT_B/V_B$. 
The proofs are identical in Case \caseS and Case \caseR, so for concreteness we take $A_p = \alpha_p$ iid Steinhaus.
We  apply \cref{lem:berry-esseen} in dimension $k=2$, identifying $\C$ with $\R^2$.  Observe 
$\Cov \langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B = \tfrac12 V_B \id$. 
Letting $X_p \coloneq \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}} \phi_p \alpha_p$, we then have 
\[
\sum_{p \in B} \Cov(X_p) = \id \qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sum_{p\in B} \E |X_p|^3 = \big(\tfrac{2}{V_B}\big)^{3/2} \,T_B\,. 
\]
The third-moment condition of \cref{lem:berry-esseen} then becomes, for some constant $c>0$,
\begin{equation}
T_B/V_B^{3/2}\leq c
\end{equation}

Suppose first that \eqref{eq:third-mom-condition-proof} is satisfied.  Then \cref{lem:berry-esseen} yields a Gaussian vector $Z\sim \cN(0,\id)$ with
\begin{align}
  \Big|\P\Big( \Big|\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}} \langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B\Big|  \leq r \Big) - \P (|Z| \leq r )\Big|\ll \frac{1}{(1+r)^3} \frac{T_B}{V_B^{3/2}}
\end{align}
for all $r\geq 0$.
Observe that the $W_1$ distance between two rotationally-symmetric random variables is bounded by the $W_1$ distance between their norms: the same uniform random variable can be used for both angles, taken independently of the norms. 
We may then use the formula \eqref{eq:vallender}
to compute
\begin{align*}
  W_1\Big(\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}} \langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B, Z\Big) \le W_1\Big(\Big|\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}} \langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B\Big|, |Z| \Big) = \int_0^{\infty} \Big| \P\Big(\Big|\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}} \langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B\Big| \leq r\Big) - \P(|Z| \leq r) \Big| \ll \frac{T_B}{V_B^{3/2}}\,.
\end{align*}
Scaling each random variable by $\sqrt{V_B/2}$ yields $W_1(\langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B, Z_B) \ll T_B/V_B$, where $Z_B = \sqrt{V_B/2} Z$ and therefore $\Cov \langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B = \Cov Z_B$. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:block-coupling-expectation} when \eqref{eq:third-mom-condition-proof} holds.

If \eqref{eq:third-mom-condition-proof} does not hold, i.e.,
$T_B/V_B^{3/2} > c$,
then the independent coupling of $\langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B$ and $Z_B$ yields 
\[
  \E\Big|\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}}(\langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B - Z_B)\Big| \leq  \E\Big|\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{V_B}}\langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B\Big| + \E |Z| \leq C'
\]
for some constant $C'>0$. Choose $C$ such that $C' < cC < T_B/V_B^{3/2}$. It follows that 
\[
  E\Delta_B \leq C V_B^{1/2} \frac{T_B}{V_B^{3/2}} = C \frac{T_B}{V_B}\,.
\]

The tail bound \eqref{eq:block-coupling-tail} follows from the triangle inequality and Hoeffding's inequality. Choose any coupling such that \eqref{eq:block-coupling-expectation} holds, and write
\[
\P(\Delta_B >u) \leq \P(|\langle\phi\alpha\rangle_B| > u/2) + \P(|Z_B|> u/2)\,.
\]
Fix any finite mesh of angles  (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:45:27.985537+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_96f2b3bdc8daa0bfa8767478b4f984f2bb860c9486cc22822685a699c603df5c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:prop_adm_classes of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Fix \(A,\sigma_0>0\), and \(R\in(0,\infty]\). Let \(\omega,\omega'>0\) and \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
  All classes below are taken with respect to the same domain \( \mathcal D_{A, \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},
  \sigma_0}\) or \( \mathcal D_{R,A, \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0}\). The following stability
  properties hold.

  \vspace*{-10pt}
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item 
    The classes \(\mathfrak B_\ell\), \(\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega\), \(\mathfrak P_\ell\) and
    \(\mathfrak G_\ell\) are vector spaces. Moreover, \(\omega\geqslant\omega'\) entails that
    \(\mathfrak E_\ell^{\omega}\subset\mathfrak E_\ell^{\omega'}\subset \mathfrak B_\ell\).

    \item 
    Let \(B\in\mathfrak B_\ell\), \(E\in\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega\), \(P\in\mathfrak P_\ell\) and
    \(G\in\mathfrak G_\ell\). Then the product functions \(BE,BP\) and \(BG\) satisfy
    \begin{equation*}
      BE\in\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega, \qquad BP\in\mathfrak P_\ell, \qquad BG\in\mathfrak G_\ell.
    \end{equation*}
    If, in addition, for \(i=1,2\), \(E_i\in\mathfrak E_\ell^{\omega_i}\), \(P_i\in\mathfrak P_\ell\),
    \(G_i\in\mathfrak G_\ell\), then, with \(\bar\omega=\min\{\omega_1,\omega_2\}\),
    \begin{equation*}
      E_1E_2 \in\mathfrak E_\ell^{\bar\omega}, \quad P_1P_2 \in\mathfrak P_\ell,
      \quad P_1G_2\in\mathfrak G_\ell, \quad G_1G_2\in\mathfrak G_\ell.
    \end{equation*}

    \item 
    If \(B\in\mathfrak B_\ell\) then \(B^{-1}\in\mathfrak B_\ell\) provided that
    \begin{equation*}
      \inf_{\|a\|\leqslant A,\ x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\ 0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0} |B(a,x,\sigma)|>0.
    \end{equation*}
    \item 
    If \(P\in\mathfrak P_\ell\), then, for every \(c_0>0\), \(\Gamma_{c_0}P \in\mathfrak G_\ell\).

    \item 
    If \(R=\infty\), \(G\in\mathfrak G_\ell\) and \(B(a,x,\sigma) = \int_{\mathbb
    H_c^m}G(\zeta;a,x,\sigma)\,\mathrm{d}\zeta\), then \(B\in\mathfrak B_\ell\).

    \item 
    Let \(q\ge1\), let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^q\) be open, and let \(\psi\in C^\infty(\Omega)\).
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item[(a)] If \(B=(B_1,\dots,B_q)\),  with \(B_i\in
      \mathfrak B_\ell\), and the range of \(B\) on \(\mathcal D_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0}\) is
      contained in a compact set \(K_\psi \Subset\Omega\), then \(\psi\circ B\in\mathfrak B_\ell\).

      \item[(b)] If \( P=(P_1,\dots,P_q)\) with \(P_i\in
      \mathfrak P_\ell\), and the range of \(P\) on \(\mathcal D_{R,A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\)
      is contained in a compact set \(K_\psi\Subset\Omega\), then \(\psi\circ P\in\mathfrak
      P_\ell\).
    \end{enumerate}
    The same conclusions hold without the compact-range assumption if \(\psi\) and all of its
    derivatives up to order \(\ell\) are globally bounded on \(\Omega\).

    \item
    
    Let \(B\in\mathfrak B_\ell\), \(E\in\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega\), \(P\in\mathfrak P_\ell\) and
    \(G\in\mathfrak G_\ell\). If \(q\in\mathbb N\), then
    \begin{equation*}
      \sigma^qB\in\mathfrak B_\ell, \qquad \sigma^qE\in\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega,
      \qquad \sigma^qP\in\mathfrak P_\ell, \qquad \sigma^qG\in\mathfrak G_\ell.
    \end{equation*}
    If \(M\in\mathbb N\) and \(E\in\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega\), then \(\sigma^{-M}E \in \mathfrak
    E_\ell^\omega\).
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:54:12.568243+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_96f6dc64e0cac4852b1c2f1ecf070ec9e26d3c06b6377aae7282ad1173d30a33","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem T:barraquand-wang of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] {BW}}]
    
Take any parameters $\alpha, \beta > 0$. Let $U, V:\mathbb{Z}^2\to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be arrays of independent random variables, 
such that for each $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{1\}$,
$$
U(1, j) \sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\alpha), \qquad U(i, j) \sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\beta);
$$
and for each $(i,j)\in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge}$, 
$$
V(i, i) \sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\alpha), \qquad V(i, j) \sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\beta),
$$
and $V(i,j)=0$ for each $(i,j)\in\mathbb{Z}^2\setminus \mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge}$.
Then for each $(1,1)\le (n,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge}$, we have
$$

$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:52:45.032691+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_96f7a2113d1872b664bc0a2b42a24504b6e2bcf46da1277af2997b131695ea89","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] Let $0 \neq K \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R_+)$ is completely monotone. Let $L$ be the corresponding resolvent of the first kind. The following assertions hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] Suppose that $K$ is regularly varying of the form \eqref{eq: regularly varying} with $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $\ell$ slowly varying at zero. Then 
        \[
            L_0(t) \sim \frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)}\frac{t^{-\alpha}}{\ell(t)}, \qquad t \searrow 0.
        \]
        \item[(b)] Suppose that $K(0^+) < \infty$ and $-K'(t) \sim t^{\alpha - 1}\ell(t)$ for $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and a slowly varying function~$\ell$. Then 
        \[
            L_0(t) \sim \frac{|K'(t)|}{K(0^+)^2}, \qquad t \searrow 0.
        \]
        \item[(c)] Suppose that $K(0^+) < \infty$ and $|K'(0^+)| < \infty$. Then 
        \[
            L_0(0^+) = \frac{|K'(0^+)|}{K(0^+)^2}.
        \]
        \item[(d)] One has
        \[
            L_0(\infty) = \left( \int_0^{\infty}K(t)\, \mathrm{d}t \right)^{-1}.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:50:44.874649+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_96fd6b3474330155222dfadcf997e8506eb498849298d0d90a5e4427edf9164d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 44 (Typed Peter--Weyl fusion tree) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] A typed Peter--Weyl fusion tree $\mathscr D$ consists of the following data.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A finite connected acyclic graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union
\[
 V(\mathscr D)=V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathscr D)
 \sqcup\{b_1,\ldots,b_N\},
\]
with a distinguished root in $V_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathscr D)$; every boundary
vertex $b_j$ has degree one.
\item At every local vertex $v$, a block family
$\mathbf v_{\boldsymbol\lambda_v}$ as in
Definition~\ref{def:peter-weyl-block-family}.  Each tensor leg is either
paired with exactly one graph edge or is designated external, and the paired
legs at $v$ are in bijection with the graph half-edges incident to $v$.  Every
external negative leg contributes to the global factor
$\conj{\cC_{\mathscr D}}$, and every external positive leg contributes to
$\cE_{\mathscr D}$, through fixed unitary identifications and a fixed order.
\item At $b_j$, fix an integer $m_j\ge0$ and a coefficient-kernel
configuration
\[
 \cH_{j,1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\cH_{j,m_j}
 \otimes\conj{\cC_j}\otimes\cE_j.
\]
Exactly one of its two deterministic coefficient legs is paired with the
incident edge; the other is external.  Its stochastic legs are all external.
The factor $\conj{\cC_j}$ is a negative deterministic leg and $\cE_j$ is a
positive deterministic leg; the attached one is regarded as a
singleton-labelled boundary leg.  Only the compressed local-vertex legs,
not an arbitrary boundary coefficient space, are required to be
finite-dimensional.
The external deterministic factors over all vertices are identified,
in fixed order, with
$\conj{\cC_{\mathscr D}}\otimes\cE_{\mathscr D}$.  With
$q:=\sum_{j=1}^Nm_j$, the stochastic legs are identified with $[q]$ by
concatenating $b_1,\ldots,b_N$ and retaining their internal slot orders.
Writing $\cE_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathscr D)$ for the ordered tensor product of
all surviving factors, the data include a fixed unitary
\begin{equation}

 J_{\mathrm{ext}}:
 \cE_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathscr D)
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^N\bigotimes_{k=1}^{m_j}\cH_{j,k}\right)
 \otimes\conj{\cC_{\mathscr D}}\otimes\cE_{\mathscr D}
\end{equation}
that implements these identifications and orders.  More precisely,
$J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the tensor product of the specified legwise unitaries,
followed by the specified permutation of tensor factors.  In particular,
for every global cut it induces unitaries separately on the input and output
sides of the associated flattening.
\item Every edge $e$ pairs one positive leg
$Z_{e,+}(\rho)$ with one negative leg
$\conj{Z_{e,-}(\lambda)}$.  As part of the edge data, fix a relation
\[
 \mathscr R_e\subset
 \mathscr L_{e,-}\times\mathscr L_{e,+}
\]
of allowed endpoint-label pairs, where $\mathscr L_{e,\pm}$ are the label
sets of the two endpoint legs.  For every
$(\lambda,\rho)\in\mathscr R_e$ the edge
carries a bounded connector block
\[
 U_{e;\lambda,\rho}:
 Z_{e,+}(\rho)\longrightarrow Z_{e,-}(\lambda)
\]
and the contraction on that edge is the complex-linear functional
\begin{equation}

 \operatorname{ev}_{e;\lambda,\rho}
   (\conj y\otimes x)
 :=\ip{U_{e;\lambda,\rho}x}{y}_{Z_{e,-}(\lambda)}.
\end{equation}
If the two factors occur in the reverse tensor order, the canonical flip is
used first.  When an edge comes from a global bounded map $U_e$ between
spectrally decomposed Hilbert spaces, its connector block is, by definition,
$P_\lambda^-U_eP_\rho^+$ viewed as a map from $Z_{e,+}(\rho)$ to
$Z_{e,-}(\lambda)$; thus cross-scale blocks are not discarded.
\item Labels on external legs and on boundary attachments are fixed.
Labels on the remaining internal half-edges vary over the countable set
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathscr D)$ of assignments satisfying
$(\lambda_{e,-},\lambda_{e,+})\in\mathscr R_e$ on every edge.  Fusion and
other vertex restrictions may be encoded by declaring the corresponding
local tensor to be zero.  For
$\boldsymbol\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathscr D)$,
$\boldsymbol\lambda_v$ denotes the tuple incident to $v$.
\en","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.161845+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97106abd4033274e1b7b80450f58f510f15be0af5ab0bb57db151ea3e1c2915f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 14 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
there exists a closed $\cD_\mu$-polytope $P$ such that
    \beq
       K_1 \equiv S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon']
        \subseteq P
        \subseteq S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
        	\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon2\bigg) 
	\equiv K_2\,,
    \eeq
where $K_1,K_2$ are both
 $\cD_\mu$-convex bodies.

\begin{proof}
Note that $\Cost(\YY;\lambda)$, $(\|\BBb\|_2)^2$, and $-\Budget(\YY;\mu)$ are all convex functions of $\YY\in\cD_\mu$. (This uses the fact that for $\YY \in \cD_\mu$, the input to the $(\cdot)_+$ in $\Cost(\YY;\lambda)$ is always nonnegative.) This immediately implies that $K_2$ is a $\cD_\mu$-convex body. It also implies that $S_\star(\lambda,\mu)$ is a $\cD_\mu$-convex body, and therefore so is its $\epsilon'$-neighborhood $K_1$.

We now turn to the construction of the polytope $P$. Lemma~\ref{l:S.star.nbd.in.S.star.eps} gives
    \beq 
        K_1 \subseteq S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
        		\frac\epsilon5,\frac{\epsilon}{3}
		\bigg)
        \subseteq (K_2)^\circ\,,
    \eeq
    where $(K_2)^\circ$ denotes the interior of $K_2$ relative to the topology of $\cD_\mu$. We let $C$ denote the boundary of $K_2$ relative to the topology of $\cD_\mu$, that is,
	\[
	C\equiv \partial K_2
	\equiv K_2 \setminus (K_2)^\circ\,.
	\]
Note that $C$ is a compact set in the topology of $\cD_\mu$. It follows from \eqref{e:S.star.nbd.in.S.star.eps.consequence} that $K_1$ and $C$ are disjoint.

Recall from \eqref{e:D.mu.affine.closure} that we use $\mathcal{F}_\mu$ to denote the affine closure of $\cD_\mu$.
For each $\YY\in C$, by the (strict) hyperplane separating theorem, there exists an open half-space $U_\YY$ of $\mathcal{F}_\mu$ such that $\YY\in U_\YY$ and $U_\YY\cap K_1=\emptyset$. Then $V_\YY\equiv \cD_\mu \cap U_\YY$ is open in the $\cD_\mu$-topology, and we have an open cover
	\[
	C\subseteq
	\bigcup_{\YY\in C} V_\YY\,.
	\]
Since $C$ is compact, this must admit a finite subcover, so there exists finite $S\subseteq C$ such that
	\[
	C\subseteq
	\bigcup_{\YY\in S} V_\YY\,.
	\]
Let $A_\YY \equiv \mathcal{F}_\mu\setminus U_\YY$, a closed half-space of $\mathcal{F}_\mu$. It follows that we can express $A_\YY = \mathcal{F}_\mu \cap H_\YY$ where $H_\YY$ is a closed half-space of the full space $\R^{3r+s}$. We then define the closed $\cD_\mu$-polytope 
	\[
	P\equiv
	\cD_\mu\cap
	\bigg( \bigcap_{\YY\in S} H_\YY
	\bigg)\,.
	\]
Since each $U_\YY$ is disjoint from $K_1$, each $H_\YY$ must contain $K_1$, so we have $K_1\subseteq P$.
On the other hand, since 
	\[
	\cD_\mu \setminus P
	= \cD_\mu \cap 
	\bigg( \bigcup_{\YY\in S} U_\YY
	\bigg)
	\supseteq C\,,
	\]
we see that $P$ does not intersect $C$. Since $P$ is convex, it must be fully contained in either $(K_2)^\circ$ or
$(\cD_\mu\setminus K_2)^\circ$.
Since we already saw that $K_1\subseteq P$, the former must hold, so $P\subseteq K_2$ as claimed.\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:25:49.836363+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_971a9c04656f6bb66707080432205c1db15300c11e0d612d560bd88adab722c7","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.01965, 'A logarithmic Bogomolov--Sommese vanishing theorem on compact K\"ahler manifolds'] A function $\varphi:X\rightarrow [-\infty,+\infty)$ is
    said to be quasi-plurisubharmonic (quasi-psh for short) if $\varphi$ is locally the sum of a plurisubharmonic function and a smooth function 
    (or equivalently, if $\ddbar\varphi$ is locally bounded from below). 

    If $\varphi$ is a quasi-psh function on $X$, the multiplier ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}(\varphi)$ is the ideal subsheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$ defined by
    $$\mathcal{I}(\varphi)_x=\{f\in\mathcal{O}_{X,x}~|~\exists\ U\ni x\  \text{such that}\ \int_U|f|^2e^{-\varphi}d\lambda<+\infty  \},$$
    where $U$ is an open coordinate neighborhood of $x$ and $d\lambda$ is the standard Lebesgue measure in $\mathbb{C}^n.$
    
    It is easy to see that associated to a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ satisfying
    $\image\Theta_{L,h}\geq\gamma$ 
    for some smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\gamma$ in the sense of currents, 
    there is a well-defined multiplier ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}(h)$ on $X$ and $\mathcal{I}(h)$ is coherent (\cite{Nad90}).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:17:33.988198+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_972c739154c7e2110889a4975117f4b3dd1b77d6106c90295eaf4331c4898e73","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03386, 'Twisted Gradient Flow Approach to Vegetation-Rainfall-Bushfire Interactions Model'] For every $\delta \in (1,\infty)$ and $\bar{z} \in L^2(\Omega)$ the bilinear form  
$(\cdot,\cdot)_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}$}}}:L^2(\Omega) \times L^2(\Omega) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by (\ref{Equation-2-18}) is a quasi-variational inner
product on $L^2(\Omega)$.\\
\indent
Moreover, for each $\delta \in (1,\infty)$ the class of inner products 
$\{(\cdot,\cdot)_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}$}}}\,;\,\bar{z} \in L^2(\Omega)\}$ satisfies the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}\leftskip6pt
\item[(1)] There exist constants $C_1>0$ and $C_2>0$ such that

\begin{equation*}
\delta^{-\frac{1}{2}} C_1 \|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le \|v\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}$}}} \le \delta^{\frac{1}{2}} C_2 \|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}, 
\quad \forall v \in L^2(\Omega),~\forall \bar{z} \in L^2(\Omega).
\end{equation*}

\item[(2)] There exists a constant $C_3>0$ such that 

\begin{equation*}
\left| \|v\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}_1$}}}^2-\|v\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}_2$}}}^2 \right| 
\le \delta^3 C_3 \|\bar{z}_1-\bar{z}_2\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \|v\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}_1$}}}^2, 
\quad \forall \bar{z}_1,\bar{z}_2 \in L^2(\Omega),\,\forall v \in L^2(\Omega).
\end{equation*}

\end{enumerate}
where for every $\delta \in (1,\infty)$ and $\bar{z} \in L^2(\Omega)$ we set 
$\|\,\cdot\,\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}$}}}:=\displaystyle{\sqrt{(\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,)_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}$}}}}}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:49:06.315820+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_9730c88f35c990d60a1cce032c9d37ea265aa18dbccc1cad41a7b0cde873ef89","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem th:kahane of arXiv:2601.07759, 'The value of random zero-sum games'] Let $X = (X_1, \dots, X_N)$ and $Y = (Y_1, \dots, Y_N)$ be Gaussian random variables in $\mathbb{R}^N$.  
Assume that $A$ and $B$ form a partition of $\{1, \dots, N\} \times \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that 
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}[X_i X_j] \le \mathbb{E}[Y_i Y_j] \quad \text{if } (i,j) \in A,\quad \text{and},\quad 
    \mathbb{E}[X_i X_j] \ge \mathbb{E}[Y_i Y_j] \quad \text{if } (i,j) \in B.
\end{align*}

Let $f$ be real a function on $\mathbb{R}^N$ whose second derivatives (in the sense of distributions) satisfy
\[
\partial_{ij} f \ge 0 \quad \text{if } (i,j) \in A, \quad \text{and},\quad  \partial_{ij} f \le 0 \quad \text{if } (i,j) \in B.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb{E}[f(X)] \le \mathbb{E}[f(Y)].
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.397124+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_9739eb0e75593e2c95007cdf00188d8ee52693da3ab680e344f398fd24707878","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 2. dfn eq: restriction of a measure to a closed ball of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The vague metric $d_{V}^{S, \rho_{S}}$}]
  We denote the set of Radon measures on $S$ by $\mathcal{M}(S)$.
  For $\mu \in \mathcal{M}(S)$,
  we write $\mu^{(r)}$ for the restriction of $\mu$ to $S^{(r)} \coloneqq \closure (B_{S}(\rho, r))$, 
  that is,
  $\mu^{(r)}$ is a finite Borel measure given by
  \begin{equation}  
    \mu^{(r)}(\cdot) 
    \coloneqq
    \mu|_{S^{(r)}}(\cdot)
    =
    \mu \left( \cdot \cap S^{(r)} \right).
  \end{equation} 
  We then define, for each $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal{M}(S)$,
  \begin{equation}
    d_{V}^{S, \rho_{S}}(\mu, \nu)
    \coloneqq
    \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-r} \left( 1 \wedge d_{P}^{S}(\mu^{(r)}, \nu^{(r)}) \right) dr.
  \end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:31:57.844119+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_9739ebdbd28f5990f42e3350d7362459d2f6c078f7662c8beafcdff1de373ec8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:standardWignerMatrix of arXiv:2510.01021, '\\Large Random Matrices, Intrinsic Freeness, and Sharp Non-Asymptotic Inequalities\\relatedv'] We will call a $d\\times d$ symmetric random matrix a standard Wigner matrix when the upper triangular entries are i.i.d. standard Gaussian, i.e. for all $1\\leq i\\leq j\\leq d$ we have $W_{ij}\\sim \\mathcal{N}\\big(0,\\frac1d\\big)$, all independent.\\footnote{When the diagonal entries are distributed accordingly to $\\mathcal{N}\\big(0,\\frac2d\\big)$ and the off-diagonal ones as $\\mathcal{N}\\big(0,\\frac1d\\big)$ the matrix is invariant to orthogonal conjugation and this case is refereed to as the \\emph{Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE)}. We note that for a standard Wigner matrix, $\\mathbb{E} W^2 = I$.}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:09.850529+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_974f993ea55dbb51cf199b61cd33a42054dbbddaf02c8c5467ece11aa1fdcab6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 2 of arXiv:2605.18751, '\mytitle'] Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be probability measures on \(E\), with likelihood ratio \(\ell\) as in~\eqref{def.ell}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]

\item \emph{Usual stochastic order} ($\st$): \(P\st Q\) if
\(\bar F_P(x)\le\bar F_Q(x)\) for every \(x\in E\).

\item \emph{Hazard-rate order} ($\hr$): \(P\hr Q\) if \(\bar F_P(x)/\bar F_Q(x)\) is nonincreasing wherever \(\bar F_Q(x)>0\) (equivalently, \(h_P(x)\ge h_Q(x)\) wherever both hazard rates are defined).

\item \emph{Likelihood-ratio order} ($\lr$): \(P\lr Q\) if \(\ell\) is nonincreasing on \(\supp(P)\cup\supp(Q)\).

\item \emph{Relative log-concavity} ($\lc$): when \(\supp(P)\) is an interval contained in \(\supp(Q)\), \(P\lc Q\) if \(\log\ell\) is concave on \(\supp(P)\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:58:40.871121+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_975b2aa6121c92f833257a387e962db5e60a6681405c55a206695e01bf249ccd","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $\mathrm{M}_{0}^{+}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the family of nonnegative Borel measures on $S$ as a whole which are finite on sets bounded away from zero.
We define an equivalence relation $\sim$ as follows: $\forall \mu,\nu\in\mathrm{M}_{0}^{+}(\mathbb{R}^d)$,  $\mu\sim\nu$ iff $\mu\mid\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}=\nu \mid\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}$.
Let $\tilde{\mathrm{M}}_{0}$ denote the quotient set $\mathrm{M}_{0}^{+}(\mathbb{R}^d)\slash\sim$.
We equip this space with the metric $d_0$, making $\tilde{\mathrm{M}}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ have the same topology and Borel sets. It is possible since the definition of $d_0$ only involves the restriction of the measures to sets bounded away from zero and one can notice that for every $\mu,\nu\in\mathrm{M}_{0}^{+}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $\mu\sim\nu$ iff $d_0(\mu,\nu)=0$. It is then clear that $\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $\tilde{\mathrm{M}}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ are isometric.
A measure $\mu\in\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ can be seen as the class $[\mu]$ of Borel measures $m$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with $0$ included) such that $m|_{\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}}=\mu$ and $m(\left\{0\right\})\in\mathbb{R}_+\cup\{\infty\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:13:22.510671+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_976dca4caa37fc35118b524dd02b6f2ffa6365318ee0ca838ba7958431a62b88","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def degrees of freedom of arXiv:2505.15940, 'Degrees of Freedom for Critical Random 2-SAT'] The random $k$-SAT problem with clause density $\alpha > 0$ is said to have $f_\star(n)$ degrees of freedom weakly if, for $\Phi \sim F_k(n, \lfloor \alpha n \rfloor)$, every consistent subset $\mathcal{L} \subseteq \pm [n]$ with $|\mathcal{L}| = f(n)$, and for all $\varepsilon > 0$, the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
        \item Whenever $f= O(f_\star n^{-\varepsilon})$, then $$\liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{P}(\Phi_\mathcal{L}\in\text{\texttt{SAT}})=\liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{P}(\Phi\in\text{\texttt{SAT}})>0.$$
        \item Whenever $f =  \Omega(f_\star n^\varepsilon)$, then $$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{P}(\Phi_\mathcal{L}\in\text{\texttt{SAT}})=0.$$
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(X, Sigma, mu) is a measure space (no finiteness needed for the inequality itself)","f and g are Sigma-measurable","1 <= p, q <= infinity and 1/p + 1/q = 1","convention 0 * infinity = 0","for the equality characterization: 1 < p < infinity and both norms finite","for the duality formula: either f in L^p with p < infinity, or mu semifinite"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.552082+00:00","domain":"real analysis, Lp spaces","id":"claim_9778b4e8b95567f6363b1b59827571824d910363d4c7e847d309c4803c4701a1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, Sigma, mu) be any measure space and 1 <= p, q <= infinity with 1/p + 1/q = 1 (1/infinity = 0). Equality case, 1 < p < infinity and ||f||_p, ||g||_q finite: ||fg||_1 = ||f||_p ||g||_q if and only if there are constants alpha, beta >= 0, not both zero, with alpha |f|^p = beta |g|^q mu-a.e. Generalized form: if 0 < p_1, ..., p_k <= infinity and 0 < r with 1/r = 1/p_1 + ... + 1/p_k, then ||f_1 ... f_k||_r <= ||f_1||_{p_1} ... ||f_k||_{p_k} (valid also for r < 1, by applying the two-factor case to |f_i|^r). Duality formula, with the semifiniteness caveat: for 1 <= p < infinity and f in L^p(mu), ||f||_p = sup{ |int fg dmu| : ||g||_{p'} <= 1 } over an ARBITRARY measure space; for measurable f with ||f||_p = infinity (1 < p < infinity), and for p = infinity, the identity requires mu to be SEMIFINITE. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:55:37.821401+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97798ff01689b9f0cc3fdda1ebd673235d071f0d48b7796caa55a32e37d59e74","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theostar Longterm behaviors of $\mathrm{CBs}$ of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $X$ be a $\mathrm{CB}(\Psi)$ process. Then,

\begin{enumerate}
\item One has $\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty}X_t=0$ a.s. if and only if $\Psi$ is critical or subcritical, i.e. $\Psi=\Sigma$, in the notation of Section (sec:LKfunction of the paper). In this case, $\mathrm{y}_t\to 0$ as $t$ tends to $\infty$.
\item One has $\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty}X_t=\infty$ a.s. if and only if $\Psi$ is immortal, i.e. $\Psi=-\Phi$, in the notation of Section (sec:LKfunction of the paper). In this case, $\mathrm{y}_t\to \infty$ as $t$ tends to $\infty$.
\item The process has positive probability  to converge to $0$ and to diverge to $\infty$ if and only if $\Psi$ is supercritical not immortal, i.e. $\Psi$ changes sign. \item The process is absorbed at $0$ in finite time with positive probability if and only if $\int_{x_1}^{\infty}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\Psi(u)}<\infty$ for some $x_1\in (0,\infty)$ (Grey's condition). The latter can only occur for non-immortal mechanism, and when the integral is finite, one has, 
\[\mathbb{P}_x(X_t=0)=e^{-x\mathrm{y}_t(\infty)}\in (0,1),\ \forall t\in [0,\infty), x\in [0,\infty).\]
\item The process is absorbed at $\infty$ in finite time with positive probability if and only if $\int_0^{x_1}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{-\Psi(u)}<\infty$ for some $x_1\in (0,\infty)$ (Dynkin's condition\footnote{Harris [zbMATH02001586] cites Dynkin for the study of explosion}). The latter can only occur for supercritical mechanism and when the integral is finite, one has
\[\mathbb{P}_x(X_t=\infty)=1-e^{-x\mathrm{y}_t(0)}\in (0,1),\ \forall t\in [0,\infty), x\in (0,\infty].\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["F a class of measurable functions with values in a bounded interval [a, b] (for the two-sided form with the stated constant the class should be closed under negation or one accepts an extra factor; see the references)","the sample is i.i.d. from P; delta in (0, 1)","measurability of the suprema (a countable class, or the usual separability assumptions) is assumed throughout"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:40:13.706434+00:00","domain":"statistical learning theory","id":"claim_97839b3fb5a128a097b064c2e4b18409edd68bbc82e49a4901fe22e9f110c5d0","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"DEFINITIONS. Let F be a class of measurable functions f: X -> [a, b], let S = (X_1, ..., X_n) be an i.i.d. sample from a distribution P on X, and let sigma_1, ..., sigma_n be independent Rademacher signs, independent of S. The empirical Rademacher complexity of F on S is R_hat_S(F) = E_sigma [ sup_{f in F} (1/n) sum_{i=1}^{n} sigma_i f(X_i) ], and the Rademacher complexity is R_n(F) = E_S [ R_hat_S(F) ]. Write P f = E f(X) and P_n f = (1/n) sum_i f(X_i). THEOREM. For every delta in (0, 1), with probability at least 1 - delta over the sample, simultaneously for all f in F: P f - P_n f <= 2 R_n(F) + (b - a) sqrt( log(1/delta) / (2n) ), and also P f - P_n f <= 2 R_hat_S(F) + 3 (b - a) sqrt( log(2/delta) / (2n) ) (a bound computable from the data). If F is closed under negation (f in F implies -f in F), the two-sided version sup_{f in F} |P f - P_n f| <= 2 R_n(F) + (b - a) sqrt(log(2/delta) / (2n)) holds with probability at least 1 - delta (for a general F apply the one-sided bound to F and to -F, each with delta/2, which replaces R_n(F) by R_n(F union -F)). Since E sup_f (P f - P_n f) <= 2 R_n(F), a class is uniformly Glivenko-Cantelli whenever R_n(F) -> 0. Standard values of R_n: a finite class bounded by B has R_n <= B sqrt(2 log |F| / n) (Massart); a class of indicators of VC dimension d has R_n <= sqrt(2 d log(e n / d) / n) and in fact O(sqrt(d / n)) (Dudley); linear predictors x -> <w, x> with ||w||_2 <= Lambda on inputs with ||x||_2 <= r have R_n <= Lambda r / sqrt(n); and for L-Lipschitz phi, R_n(phi o F) <= L R_n(F) (Ledoux-Talagrand contraction), which is how the bound passes from a class of predictors to a class of losses. In learning, with f the loss of a hypothesis, the theorem says the true risk of EVERY hypothesis in the class exceeds its empirical risk by at most 2 R_n plus a term of order sqrt(log(1/delta)/n), the modern replacement for VC bounds when the class is not a class of sets.","status":"unverified"}

A \textit{double monoid} in $\catname{C}$ is an object $A$ equipped with morphisms
\[\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=scriptsize]
	{A \square A} & A && I & A && {A \circ A} & A && {J } & A,
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow[from=1-7, to=1-8]
	\arrow[from=1-10, to=1-11]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    which turn $A$ into a monoid in both $(\catname{C},\square,I)$ and $(\catname{C},\circ,J)$, and make the following diagrams commute.
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{(A \circ A) \square (A \circ A)} && {(A \square A) \circ (A \square A)} \\
	{A \square A} & A & {A \circ A}
	\arrow["{\zeta_{A,A,A,A}}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=2-3, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{J \square J} & {A \square A} && {I \circ I} & {A \circ A} \\
	J & A && I & A
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\mu_J}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow[from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\Delta_I}", from=2-4, to=1-4]
	\arrow[from=2-4, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	& A \\
	I && J
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{{\iota_J = \epsilon_I}}"', from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-3, to=1-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    Dually, one can define \textit{double comonoids}. 

    A morphism between two double (co)monoids is a morphism of the two underlying (co)monoids.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:01:48.617359+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97cfdf3e416a43739095433521fe7ee6020f77b8448968cb0fd114be07910a2e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:beta.mgf of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] Let $x$ is sampled uniformly at random from the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. Then $x$ is zero-mean and subgaussian with variance proxy $1/d$.

\begin{proof}
Fix a vector $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
Let $t=\|v\|$. Then $Z=\langle v,x\rangle/t$ is a symmetric random variable, and
    \[
    B=Z^2\sim\operatorname{Beta}\bigg(\frac{1}{2},
        \frac{d-1}{2}\bigg)\,.
    \]
It follows from the moment-generating function of the beta distribution that
    \[
    \mathbb E_x[\mathop{\rm exp}(\langle v,x\rangle)]
    = \mathbb E [\mathop{\rm exp}(tZ)]
    = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{t^{2k}}{(2k)!}
        \prod_{r=0}^{k-1} \frac{1+2r}{d+2r} 
    \le 1 + \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{t^{2k}}{k! (2d)^k}
    = \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{\|v\|^2}{2d}\bigg)\,,
    \]
which proves the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:57:28.221412+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97d3f5e7a5cc025277dcbc8caa4e368b11f81f24c8a6d8d3614e7c571eac6334","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 of arXiv:2607.17662, 'On the Strong Law of Large Numbers under Sublinear Expectations'] A sublinear expectation $\mathbb{E} : \mathcal{H} \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be \textit{continuous} if it satisfies:
		\begin{enumerate}

			$\mathbb{E}[X_n] \uparrow \mathbb{E}[X]$, where $0 \le X_n$, $X \in \mathcal{H}$.
			
			\item[(2)] \textit{Upper-continuity:} If $X_n \downarrow X$, then
			$\mathbb{E}[X_n] \downarrow \mathbb{E}[X]$, where $0 \le X_n$, $X \in \mathcal{H}$.
		\end{enumerate}
		
		A capacity $V : \mathcal{F} \to [0,1]$ is called a \textit{continuous capacity} if it satisfies:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(1)] \textit{Lower-continuity:} If $A_n \uparrow A$, then
			$V(A_n) \uparrow V(A)$, where $A_n, A \in \mathcal{F}$.
			
			\item[(2)] \textit{Upper-continuity:} If $A_n \downarrow A$, then
			$V(A_n) \downarrow V(A)$, where $A_n, A \in \mathcal{F}$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.431561+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97e3804b3bd38df4c13bb36d47f9c369e4c2f55b1ab653dbdcb41f9e1e5abb51","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 4. dfn: resistance forms of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Resistance form and resistance metric, [Kigami_12_Resistance]}] 
  
  Let $F$ be a non-empty set.
  A pair $(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F})$ is called a \textit{resistance form} on $F$ if it satisfies the following conditions.
  \begin{enumerate} [label=(RF\arabic*), leftmargin = *]
    \item 
          The symbol $\mathcal{F}$ is a linear subspace of the collection of functions $\{ f : F \to \mathbb{R} \}$ 
          containing constants,
          and $\mathcal{E}$ is a non-negative symmetric bilinear form on $\mathcal{F}$
          such that $\mathcal{E}(f,f)=0$ if and only if $f$ is constant on $F$.
    \item 
          Let $\sim$ be the equivalence relation on $\mathcal{F}$ defined by saying $f \sim g$ if and only if $f-g$ is constant on $F$.
          Then $(\mathcal{F}/\sim, \mathcal{E})$ is a Hilbert space.
    \item
          If $x \neq y$, then there exists a function $f \in \mathcal{F}$ such that $f(x) \neq f(y)$.
    \item 
          For any $x, y \in F$,
          \begin{equation} 
            R_{(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F})}(x,y)
            \coloneqq
            \sup
            \left\{
            \frac{|f(x) - f(y)|^{2}}{\mathcal{E}(f,f)}
            :
            f \in \mathcal{F},\
            \mathcal{E}(f,f) > 0
            \right\}
            < \infty.
          \end{equation}     
    \item
          If $\bar{f}\coloneqq  (f \wedge 1) \vee 0$,
          then $\bar{f} \in \mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{E}(\bar{f}, \bar{f}) \leq \mathcal{E}(f,f)$ for any $f \in \mathcal{F}$.
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:05:09.629919+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97e92b713f5fb0ae485923c164806f6eca2dc22232484a3f8e3e4538afc5727a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:tech_extent_lowerbound of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{Y}$ be a nonzero pure-jump L\'evy process on $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\psi_{\bm{Y}}(\bm{u})$ denote its L\'evy-Khintchine exponent and $\nu_{\bm{Y}}$ its L\'evy measure.\\
{\normalfont(a)} If $\bm{Y}$ has finite variation and nonzero drift with direction $\bm{u}_*\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. Then $|\psi_{\bm{Y}}(x\bm{u}_*)|\geqslant cx$ for some $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $x>0$.\\
{\normalfont(b)} Suppose there exist a locally finite measure $\rho$ on $(0,\infty)$ and a probability measure $\sigma$ on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ with
\[
\nu_{\bm{Y}}(A)
\geqslant \int_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}\int_{(0,\infty)}\1_A(x\bm{v})\rho(\mathrm{d} x)\sigma(\mathrm{d}\bm{v}),
\qquad A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d_{\bm{0}}).
\]
Define $\Upsilon(x):=\int_{(0,x)}r^2\rho(\mathrm{d} r)$ for $x>0$, and, given any $c\in (0,1)$, suppose that $C_{c,\bm{u}_*}\coloneqq\{\bm{v}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}:|\langle \bm{u}_*,\bm{v}\rangle|\geqslant c\}$ has positive $\sigma$-measure $m:=\sigma(C_{c,\bm{u}_*})>0$ for some $\bm{u}_*\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. Then we have
\[
|\psi_{\bm{Y}}(x\bm{u}_*)|\geqslant \frac{c^2m}{3}r^2\Upsilon(x^{-1})
\qquad\text{for all }x>0.
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:16.153150+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97eadd3bbdbc643b6ff10222c41881b0ecca7b3efcfbff2369bdef82e1989b9f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] For $t\in \mathbb{R}\setminus \mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, we define the \emph{$t$-deformed cumulants} $\{\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}}$ of $A \in U$ by
$$
C^t[A](z) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^\infty \kappa_i^t(A)z^i \coloneqq -\frac{z}{t} \frac{d}{dz}\log \left(1+ \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{t^{k}}{(t)_{\underline{k}}} a_{k} z^{k} \right).
$$
If $A\in U_d$ for some $d\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$, we define the \emph{$d$-deformed cumulants} $\{\kappa_{i}^{d}(A)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}}$ by
$$
C^d[A](z) \coloneqq \lim_{t\to d} C^t[A](z)\coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^\infty \kappa_i^d(A)z^i  = -\frac{z}{d} \frac{d}{dz}\log\left(1+ \sum_{k=1}^d \frac{d^{k}}{(d)_{\underline{k}}} a_{k} z^{k}\right).
$$
We call $C^t[A](z)$ the \emph{$t$-deformed cumulant transform} of $A$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:18:54.264431+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97ee0fa0797f0d7b9ea513fec468ccd6dfd48482c5086c00a8a54d6f790efe9d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Assume that a random variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ has density $\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, in the sense that its law is given by $d\mu(x)=\varphi(x)dx$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The density must be positive, $\varphi\geq0$, and of mass one, $\int_\mathbb R\varphi(x)dx=1$.

\item $\mu(Z)=\int_Z\varphi(x)dx$, which can stand as an alternative definition for $\varphi$.

\item $E(\phi(f))=\int_\mathbb R\phi(x)\varphi(x)dx$, which can stand as well as a definition for $\varphi$.

\item The CDF is $F(x)=\int_{-\infty}^x\varphi(t)dt$, and conversely, we have $\varphi(x)=F'(x)$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:57:30.994414+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_97efde84c687734e23b1ce3ae8052542c0c176f8db17c62eaa957917a20a6546","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 42 (Physical fourth-moment theorem: exact zero stratum) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let $q\ge2$ and
\[
 X_{n,a}=I_q^{W_n}(f_{n,a}),
 \qquad
 \sup_n\sum_{a=1}^dq!\norm{f_{n,a}}^2<\infty.
\]
Write $\Sigma_n=\Cov(X_n)$, fix a free ultrafilter $\mathcal U$, and put
\[
 \xi_a=[f_{n,a}]_{\mathcal U}\in\cH_q,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\Ulim\Sigma_n,
 \qquad
 \kappa_{n,a}=\E[X_{n,a}^4]-3\E[X_{n,a}^2]^2.
\]
The represented terminal has the intrinsic splitting
\begin{equation}
 T_a=\mathbb U_q^{-1}\xi_a
 =A_a^{\phys}+G_a^{\phys},
 \quad
 A_a^{\phys}=\mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cD_q}\xi_a,
 \quad
 G_a^{\phys}=\mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cK_q}\xi_a.
 
\end{equation}
The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\displaystyle\sum_{a=1}^d\mathfrak Q_q(\xi_a)=0$,
 equivalently $\Ulim\sum_a\kappa_{n,a}=0$;
 \item for every $a$ and $1\le r<q$,
 $
  \Ulim\norm{f_{n,a}\otimes_rf_{n,a}}=0
 $;
 \item $\xi_a\in\cK_q$ for every $a$, equivalently
 $P_{\cD_q}\xi=0$;
 \item $A^{\phys}=0$ (equivalently, the limiting active part of
 the reduced Hilbert--Stein trajectory vanishes) and the represented
 laws converge along $\mathcal U$ to $N_d(0,\Sigma)$;
 \item for every $a$,
 $
  \Ulim\E[X_{n,a}^4]=3\Sigma_{aa}^2
 $.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold, every mixed proper contraction also
vanishes:
\begin{equation}
 \Ulim\norm{f_{n,a}\otimes_rf_{n,b}}=0
 \qquad(1\le r<q,\ 1\le a,b\le d).
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, there is a finite constant $C_{q,d}$, depending only on
$(q,d)$, such that for every $n$ and $t\in\R^d$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|
  \E e^{it\cdot X_n}
  -e^{-\frac12t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_nt}
 \right|
 \le C_{q,d}|t|^2
 \left(\sum_{a=1}^d\kappa_{n,a}\right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}
Componentwise, the exact carré-du-champ comparison is
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{3q}\kappa_{n,a}
 \le
 \Var\bigl(\Gamma(X_{n,a},X_{n,a})\bigr)
 \le
 \frac{q-1}{3q}\kappa_{n,a}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus the fourth cumulants detect exactly, and not merely sufficiently,
the disappearance of the decomposable physical sector.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:30.018391+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_980620c96ab93eac9e1e85545da0740e30be70f545956f34f3f387204b3d2594","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 37 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] \rm

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T07:57:26.304821+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_980a5e387101404d9fe5f46c23712037","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In abstract algebra, an abelian group $(G,+)$ is called finitely generated if there exist finitely many elements $x_{1},\\dots,x_{s}$ in $G$ such that every $x$ in $G$ can be written in the form $x=n_{1}x_{1}+n_{2}x_{2}+\\cdots +n_{s}x_{s}$ for some integers $n_{1},\\dots,n_{s}$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:49:15.469530+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_980d9fc9fbe66c83630221d66c4b1b81e417cd59ec39b0358c8adbade39fe9d3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2608.28278, 'Reduction of symmetric time-dependent Hamiltonian systems I: presymplectic principal $\R$-'] [Echevarria, GUTIERREZSAGREDO]
    A presymplectic structure on an $m$-dimensional manifold $M$ is a closed $2$-form $\omega\in \Omega^2(M)$ with constant rank $2k$. The pair $(M,\omega)$ is called a presymplectic manifold of corank $m-2k$.

\end{compactenum}

\smallskip

{"assumptions":["entries of Z i.i.d., mean 0, variance 1, finite fourth moment (necessary for the edge statements)","||Sigma_n|| bounded; spectral distribution of Sigma_n converges to H; p/n -> c in (0, infinity)","the interval [a, b] is outside the supports of the finite-n laws for all large n (not only outside the limiting support)"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T09:21:49.109871+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_98405d3e08a3062d8207dc22178a18452e909979f29e46ab7d8122c66d7b17e8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $S_n = \\frac{1}{n} X_n^T X_n$ with $X_n = Z_n \\Sigma_n^{1/2}$, where $Z_n$ is $n \\times p$ with i.i.d. entries of mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite fourth moment, $\\Sigma_n$ is positive semidefinite with $\\|\\Sigma_n\\|$ bounded, $p/n \\to c \\in (0, \\infty)$, and the spectral distribution of $\\Sigma_n$ converges weakly to $H$. Let $F^{c,H}$ be the limiting spectral distribution of $S_n$ (the Marchenko-Pastur-Silverstein law) and let $[a, b]$ be a closed interval, $a > 0$, lying outside the support of $F^{c,H}$ and outside the supports of $F^{c_n, H_n}$ for all large $n$ (the finite-$n$ laws built from $c_n = p/n$ and $H_n$). Then almost surely no eigenvalue of $S_n$ lies in $[a, b]$ for all $n$ large enough: $\\mathbb{P}(\\text{no eigenvalue of } S_n \\text{ in } [a, b] \\text{ for all large } n) = 1$. Corollary (Bai-Yin 1993, the case $\\Sigma = I$): $\\lambda_{\\max}(S_n) \\to (1 + \\sqrt c)^2$ and, for $c < 1$, $\\lambda_{\\min}(S_n) \\to (1 - \\sqrt c)^2$ almost surely - the Marchenko-Pastur edges - and the finite fourth moment is necessary for the largest eigenvalue to converge. Consequence used throughout: an eigenvalue of a sample covariance strictly above $\\sigma^2(1 + \\sqrt c)^2$ (by a fixed margin) cannot come from an identity-covariance bulk, which is what licenses the bulk edge as a detection threshold in the spiked model, in Gavish-Donoho denoising, and in the median-based noise estimate.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T07:57:26.312369+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_98433226daf84b1b8cd25cb469eca26d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In mathematics, the ideal class group (or class group) of an algebraic number field $K$ is the quotient group $J_{K}/P_{K}$ where $J_{K}$ is the group of fractional ideals of the ring of integers of $K$, and $P_{K}$ is its subgroup of principal ideals. {"assumptions":["fixed design X of full column rank","independent errors with mean zero and possibly different variances","finite fourth moments of errors and regressors; (1/n) X'X -> positive definite; p fixed as n -> infinity for the consistency statement"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:50:37.943831+00:00","domain":"regression","id":"claim_985b54f9338db3244323dab66f1613e14302710ac7bfd8d3569800bb347b6e0c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $y = X\\beta + \\varepsilon$ with $X$ an $n \\times p$ design of full column rank (treated as fixed), $E[\\varepsilon] = 0$, and $\\operatorname{Var}(\\varepsilon) = \\Omega = \\operatorname{diag}(\\omega_1^2, \\dots, \\omega_n^2)$ - independent errors whose variances may differ across observations. Then the ordinary least-squares estimator $\\hat\\beta = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T y$ is unbiased and its exact covariance is the sandwich $$\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat\\beta) = (X^T X)^{-1}\\, X^T \\Omega X\\, (X^T X)^{-1},$$ which reduces to the textbook $\\sigma^2 (X^T X)^{-1}$ only when all $\\omega_i^2 = \\sigma^2$. THEOREM (White, 1980). With $r = y - X\\hat\\beta$ the residuals, the estimator $\\hat V_{\\mathrm{HC0}} = (X^T X)^{-1}\\big(\\sum_i r_i^2 x_i x_i^T\\big)(X^T X)^{-1}$ is consistent for $\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat\\beta)$ in the sense that $n\\,\\hat V_{\\mathrm{HC0}} - n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat\\beta) \\to 0$ in probability as $n \\to \\infty$ with $p$ fixed, under finite fourth moments of the errors and of the regressors (the rows $x_i$ bounded or with $\\frac{1}{n}\\sum_i \\|x_i\\|^4 = O(1)$) and $\\frac{1}{n}X^T X \\to$ a positive definite limit. No model for the $\\omega_i^2$ is needed. In the ill-conditioned directions of $X^T X$ (nearly collinear regressors) the sandwich can exceed the homoscedastic formula by a large factor when the large residuals fall on the observations that determine those directions; the homoscedastic formula then badly understates the sampling noise of the coefficients.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a set and mu* is defined on the entire power set of X","for the construction: E contains the empty set and some countable subfamily of E covers X, so that every subset has at least one admissible cover","rho maps E into [0, +infinity] with rho(empty set) = 0; no additivity or monotonicity of rho is assumed","countable, not arbitrary, families are used in the subadditivity axiom"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:13:10.402410+00:00","domain":"measure theory, Caratheodory construction","id":"claim_9861570c368e84c1c207e946455b7453e592c4255152ddc4ad3423bc0df71072","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a set. A function mu* from the FULL power set of X to [0, +infinity] is an OUTER MEASURE if (1) mu*(empty set) = 0, (2) it is monotone: A contained in B implies mu*(A) <= mu*(B), and (3) it is countably subadditive: mu*(union over n >= 1 of A_n) <= sum over n >= 1 of mu*(A_n) for every countable family of subsets A_n of X, MEASURABLE OR NOT. Note that subadditivity is part of the definition in the abstract setting; the mathematical content lies in the fact that the standard constructions produce it. CONSTRUCTION FROM A COVERING FAMILY (a gauge): let E be a family of subsets of X containing the empty set and covering X by countably many of its members, and let rho : E -> [0, +infinity] with rho(empty set) = 0. Define mu*(A) = inf { sum over k >= 1 of rho(E_k) : E_k in E for all k and A contained in the union of the E_k }, with the convention that the infimum of the empty set is +infinity. Lebesgue outer measure on R^n is the case where E is the family of boxes (or open boxes, or cubes) and rho is the elementary volume. A set A is CARATHEODORY MEASURABLE for mu* if mu*(T) = mu*(T intersect A) + mu*(T minus A) for every test set T; these sets form a sigma-algebra on which mu* restricts to a complete countably additive measure (Caratheodory's theorem). CAUTIONS: an outer measure is defined on all subsets but is in general NOT additive on disjoint sets; it is not a measure on the power set; and the Caratheodory criterion, not the mere inequality in (3), is what recovers additivity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:00:15.230095+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_987742004d280dbadce4294067329646fa5526339aa8dca0b631b982cf3ada51","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let $\lambda,l,\epsilon>0$, $\alpha,\delta\in (0,1]$ be fixed numbers. Let $a_1$ be a symmetric $d\times d$ matrix, and let $a(x),\widetilde{a}(x)$ be a $d\times d$ matrix-valued functions. Assume that for any $x$, $a(x),\widetilde{a}(x)$ are both symmetric, satisfying
	\ce 
	\lambda^{-1}lI\leq a(x)+a_1,~\widetilde{a}(x)+a_1\leq \lambda lI,
	\de 
	where $I$ is the $d\times d$ unit matrix. Additionally, assume that
	\ce 
	\sup_y\|a(y)-\widetilde{a}(y)\|\leq \epsilon.
	\de 
	Let $h$ be a real function such that 
	\ce 
	|h(x)-h(y)|\leq \lambda|x-y|^\alpha 
	\de 
	for all $x,y\in\mR^d$. Let $\zeta,\xi,\eta$ be independent d-dimensional random vectors. Assume that $\zeta$ has normal distribution $\sN(0,I)$, $\eta$ has normal distribution $\sN(0,\sqrt{a_1})$ and $E[|\xi|^\alpha]< \infty$. Define an operater $T^*$ by the formula for Borel measure function $f$ on $\mR^d$
	\ce 
	T^*f(y)=\mE[f(y+\sqrt{a(y)}\zeta)]
	\de 
	and $T$ be the adjoint of $T^*$ in the $L_2$ sense. Let $1\leq i,j\leq d$ be fixed and define 
	\ce
	H(x)=\mE[h(x)(\partial_{x_i,x_j}^2Tf)(x+\eta+\xi)-(\partial_{x_i,x_j}^2T[hf])(x+\eta+\xi)],
	\de 
	\ce 
	F(x)=H(x)+\mE[\mathscr{L}_{\upsilon,R}^{g}Tf(x+\eta+\xi)].
	\de 
	Define $\widetilde{T}^*$, $\widetilde{T}$ and $\widetilde{F}(x)$ analogously, but with $\widetilde{a}$ replacing $a$. 
	
	(i)  We assume that there exists a constant $\beta\in(0,2]$ such that the function $g$ on $\mR^d$ satisfies 
	\ce 
	\|\varGamma_{0,\beta}^{0,R}g\|_{\infty}<\infty.
	\de 
	Then, for any $p\in (d/\beta\vee 1,\infty]$, $p'\in [p,\infty]$, and bounded Borel $f\in L_p(\mR^d)$,
	\be 
	\|F\|_{p'}\leq N\|f\|_{p}[(1+l^{-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\mE[|\xi|^\alpha])l^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-1 +\frac{d}{2p'}-\frac{d}{2p}}+l^{-\frac{\beta}{2}+\frac{d}{2p'}-\frac{d}{2p}}],
	\ee 
	where the constant $N$ depends only on $\lambda,\alpha,\beta, p, p'$.
	
	(ii)  We assume that there exists a constant $\beta\in(1,2]$ such that functions $g$ and $\widetilde{g}$ on $\mR^d$ satisfy
	\ce 
	\|\varGamma_{0,\beta}^{0,R}g\|_{\infty}<\infty,~	\|\varGamma_{0,\beta}^{0,R}\widetilde{g}\|_{\infty}<\infty.
	\de 
	Then, for any $p\in (2d/\beta,\infty]$, $p'\in [p,\infty]$, and bounded Borel function $f\in L_p(\mR^d)$,
	\be 
	\|F(x)-\widetilde{F}(x)\|_{p'}
	\leq N\epsilon\|f\|_{p}\bigg[(1+l^{-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\mE[|\xi|^\alpha])l^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-2 +\frac{d}{2p}-\frac{d}{2p'}}+ (1+\epsilon)l^{-\frac{1}{2}(\beta-\frac{d}{p'}+\frac{d}{p})}
	+l^{-\frac{1}{2}(1+\beta-\frac{d}{p'}+\frac{d}{p})}\bigg],
	\ee 
	where the constant $N$ depends only on $\lambda,\alpha,\beta, p, p'$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:13:49.971936+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_9877467e026f00b612e50d498a661006fbc979653968f984138cef41b06c4d6f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition eq:deftildeupsilon of arXiv:2411.07157, 'Rough differential equations in the flow approach'] We define the family of elementary differentials $(\Upsilon^{\tau}: \tau\in\mathfrak{T})$, with $\Upsilon^{\tau} \in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\tau]$, by using an induction in $\tau$. 
For the base case, we define  $\Upsilon^{\circ} = \big( \Upsilon^{\circ_{r}}\big)_{r \in \N} \in \prod_{r \in \N} \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\circ_{r}]$ by setting, in analogy with (equation eq:elem_diff1_base of the paper), 
\[
\Upsilon^{\circ_{r}}(x_{r}) = V(x_{r})\;.
\]
It is clear that one indeed has $\Upsilon^{\circ_{r}} \in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\circ]$. 
In other words, we could have just fixed a single $r \in \N$, applied the above formula, and then defined $\Upsilon^{\circ} = \pi_{\circ,\circ_{r}} \Upsilon^{\circ_{r}}$ and our construction would be well-defined in that it didn't depend on our initial choice of $r$. 

We now proceed to the inductive step. 
Suppose we have $\tau=[\tau_1,\dots,\tau_k]$, where $k > 0$, the $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_k$ are unlabelled, and $[\cdot]$ denotes joining the roots of unlabelled trees at a new unlabelled root. 
Our inductive assumption is that we have been given $\Upsilon^{\circ} \in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\raisebox{+0.05ex}{\includegraphics[scale=1.5]{figures/Xi.pdf}}]$, and $\Upsilon^{\tau_{j}} \in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}_j]$ for $1 \leqslant j \leqslant k$.

Next, fix any labelled $\underline{\tau} \in \tau$, and choose any labelled $\underline{\tau}_1,\dots,\underline{\tau}_k$ with $\underline{\tau}_j \in \tau_j$, such that $\underline{\tau} = [\underline{\tau}_1,\dots,\underline{\tau}_k]_{r}$ (here we use the notation of (equation eq:product_of_trees of the paper), and $r = r(\underline{\tau})$).
For every $\underline{\sigma}\in \{\circ_{r}, \underline{\tau}_1,\cdots,\underline{\tau}_k\}$, we first set
\begin{equs}
   \Upsilon^{\underline{\sigma}} \eqdef \iota_{\sigma,\underline{\sigma}} \Upsilon^{\sigma}\in\text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\sigma}]\,.
\end{equs}
We then define $\Upsilon^{\underline{\tau}} \in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}]$ in analogy with (equation eq:elem_diff1 of the paper) by setting
\begin{equ}
\Upsilon^{\underline{\tau}}(x_{N(\underline{\tau})})
=
\big( \mathrm{d}^{k} \Upsilon^{\circ_r}(x_{r(\underline{\tau})}) \big) \big[ \Upsilon^{\underline{\tau}_{1}}(x_{N(\underline{\tau}_1)}),\cdots, \Upsilon^{\underline{\tau}_{k}}(x_{N(\underline{\tau}_k)}) \big]\,,
\end{equ}
and finally we can set
\begin{equ}
\Upsilon^{\tau} \eqdef
\pi_{\tau,\underline{\tau}} \Upsilon^{\underline{\tau}}\;.
\end{equ}
In the next lemma we verify that $\Upsilon^{\tau}$ as defined above is well-defined, in that it does not depend on how we realised $\tau$ as the labelled tree $[\underline{\tau}_1,\dots,\underline{\tau}_k]_{r}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:15:45.375169+00:00","domain":"general topology","id":"claim_987a713ab2d41c965d796f3285a70f19fefacd5934de0e8382701f1d12d8b510","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A collection B of subsets of a set X is a basis (base) for a topology on X if (i) every point of X lies in at least one member of B, and (ii) whenever a point x lies in the intersection of two members B1, B2 of B, there is a member B3 of B with x in B3 and B3 contained in the intersection of B1 and B2. The topology generated by B consists of exactly those subsets U of X such that every point of U lies in some member of B contained in U; equivalently, the open sets are precisely the unions of subfamilies of B. Conversely, given a topological space (X, T), a subcollection B of T is a basis for T exactly when every open set is a union of members of B.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["all F_k lie in the SAME fixed chaos of order n >= 2","E[F_k^2] -> sigma^2 > 0","the equivalence is FALSE for sequences not confined to one chaos"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543836+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_987c81863f8063bc739cd937cd38fc426cd1f16bcd26e3a30b1ba5274965a462","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Fix an integer n >= 2 and let F_k = I_n(f_k) be a sequence living in the SAME n-th Wiener chaos, with E[F_k^2] = n! ||f_k||^2 converging to sigma^2 > 0. Then the following are EQUIVALENT: (i) F_k converges in distribution to N(0, sigma^2); (ii) E[F_k^4] -> 3 sigma^4; (iii) the contractions satisfy || f_k contracted with f_k at r indices || -> 0 for every r = 1, ..., n-1. The theorem replaces the infinitely many moment conditions of the method of moments by a SINGLE fourth-moment condition. The hypothesis that the chaos order n is FIXED and the same for every k is essential and is the standard misquotation: for a general sequence of random variables, or for a sequence whose chaos order drifts, matching the fourth moment says nothing about normality - the fourth moment of a suitable two-point law is also 3 times the square of its variance. Also essential is sigma^2 > 0; degenerating variance is excluded. The quantitative form is due to Nourdin and Peccati via Malliavin-Stein: for F in the n-th chaos with E[F^2] = sigma^2, the total variation distance to N(0, sigma^2) is bounded by a constant depending only on n times the square root of ( E[F^4] - 3 sigma^4 ), so the fourth cumulant controls the rate as well as the limit. [Nualart and Peccati (2005), Ann. Probab. 33; Nourdin and Peccati (2009); see Nourdin and Peccati, Normal Approximations with Malliavin Calculus, Theorem 5.2.7]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:47.655524+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_988f2058fa3f1cdfd076c4f853d49e8d47d2636ce9b7d854fd756981b3713116","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 3 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] {\bf(Moderate deviation principle for stochastic approximation $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$)}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.744319+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_98b69e2fa8508940af6a1fbb1117af0e4f28eb9d10d8d89c31b39210aabbe69a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The language $H$ equals the well-defined concatenation $J.G$.
  \begin{proof}
    To every word $w \in H$ there is a \emph{coupon-counting
    function} $f_w\colon \{ 0, 1, \ldots, \lvert w \rvert \} \to \N$
    that tracks the current number of distinct coupons held.
    This means $f_w(0) = 0$ and $f_w(\lvert w \rvert) = m$.
    Choose the smallest $k$ for which $f(k) = m$ and let
    $j$ be the word formed from the first $k$ letters in $w$.
    Then $w$ has the decomposition $j.g$ for some word $g$
    of length $\lvert w\rvert - k$.
    But since $f(k) = f(\lvert w \rvert) = m$,
    each occurrence of $\D_i$ in $g$ must be eventually followed
    by $\C_i$. Hence $g \in G$. There can be no decomposition $j = u.v$
    with $u \in H$ and $v \neq \varepsilon$ because $k > 0$ was selected minimally.
    This establishes $j \in J$ and $w \in J.G$. Thus $H \subseteq J.G$.

    To show $J.G \subseteq H$, take some $j.g \in J.G$ and
    consider the coupon-counting function $f_{j.g}$.
    Then $f_{j.g}(\lvert j \rvert) = m$ but $g$
    recovers all coupons it drops,
    so $f_{j.g}(\lvert j\rvert + \lvert g \rvert) = 
    f_{j.g}(\lvert j \rvert) = m$. We conclude
    $j.g \in H$ and $H = J.G$.

    We could not have selected a longer word $j' \in J$ in the first
    paragraph because $j' = j.u$ would hold with $u \neq \varepsilon$.
    This gives the contradiction $j' \notin J$.
    So, the factorisation of words $w \mapsto (j, g)$ is unique;
    $J$ and $G$ are well-defined for concatenation.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(F_n) increasing, F_infinity generated by their union","Y integrable"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627314+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_990c757f8a69205734bf9eaa5f8523ff03979cc297993560b1152fd27fd6f9f2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (F_n) be an increasing filtration with F_infinity the sigma-algebra it generates, and let Y be in L^1. Then E[Y | F_n] converges almost surely and in L^1 to E[Y | F_infinity]. Taking Y = 1_A for A in F_infinity gives LEVY'S 0-1 LAW: P(A | F_n) -> 1_A almost surely, so the conditional probability of any event in the limit sigma-algebra converges to 0 or 1. Applied to a tail event of an independent sequence, where F_n is generated by the first n variables and P(A | F_n) = P(A) by independence, this yields Kolmogorov's 0-1 law as a corollary. The theorem is about an INCREASING family; the corresponding statement for a decreasing family is Levy's downward theorem and needs its own proof. The limit is conditional on F_infinity and not on F - the two differ, and writing E[Y | F] would be wrong unless F_infinity = F up to null sets. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Theorem 14.2]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.359169+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_991116ceaaf8e5a639615c82c02677a2452ae511d5d742aeb166ae0c8dbc4fda","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop switching ergodic monomolecular of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] In Example (ex:switching ergodic monomolecular of the paper), $\mathcal R_1$ and $\mathcal R_2$ are evanescent whenever $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. For any $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the mixed process is evanescent as long as $\kappa$ is small enough, but is exponentially ergodic as long as $\kappa$ is large enough.
\begin{proof}
Notice that the respective matrices in different individual environments as well as the stationary environment are given by 
\[
    M_1=\begin{bmatrix}-4&2\varepsilon\\ 2(1-\varepsilon)&0\end{bmatrix},\quad
    M_2=\begin{bmatrix}0&2(1-\varepsilon)\\ 2\varepsilon&-4\end{bmatrix},\quad
    M=\begin{bmatrix}-2&1\\ 1&-2\end{bmatrix}
\]
Note that the eigenvalues of $M_1$ and $M_2$ are $-2\pm2\sqrt{1 + \varepsilon - \varepsilon^2}$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ we have $\varepsilon>\varepsilon^2$, and hence the larger eigenvalue is positive. Since both off-diagonal entries of $M_1$ and $M_2$ are nonzero, it follows from Proposition (prop:dec/inc direction of the paper)(ii) that there exist vectors $v^1,v^2\in\mathbb R^2_{>0}$ such that $v^iM_i\in\mathbb R^2_{>0}$. By Corollary (cor:one-environment-transience of the paper) we conclude that both $\mathcal R_1$ and $\mathcal R_2$ are evanescent for any nonzero state; the existence of inflow reactions means this state is evanescent as well. Similarly, by Theorem (thm:slow-switching-transience of the paper) we conclude that all states are evanescent for the mixed process whenever $\kappa$ is sufficiently small.

However, one sees that if $v=(1,1)$ then $vM=-v$, so by Theorem (thm:fast-switching-ergodicity of the paper) the mixed process converges exponentially fast whenever $\kappa$ is sufficiently large. Since the state space is irreducible, it follows by definition that the mixed process is exponentially ergodic whenever $\kappa$ is sufficiently large.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.527059+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_991e7971736502bc06092723e17af2cf349bf02434680cca634a33b35e30ccf9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 3 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $m \ge 0$ be an integer. A sequence of points 
 $$\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)] \subset \mathbb{Z}^{d}$$ is called a path of length $m$ if $|\lambda(k) - \lambda(k+1)| = 1$ for all $0 \le k \le m-1$. We write $\text{len}\, (\lambda) = m$ for the length of $\lambda$. For $0 \le a \le b \le m$, we set $\lambda[a,b] = [\lambda(a), \lambda(a+1), \cdots, \lambda(b)]$ to denote the portion of the path $\lambda$ between times $a$ and $b$. Furthermore, $\lambda$ is said to be a simple path if $\lambda(j) \neq \lambda(k)$ for all $0 \le j < k \le m$.

     Let $\lambda_{1} = [\lambda_{1}(0), \cdots, \lambda_{1}(m_{1})]$ and $\lambda_{2} = [\lambda_{2}(0), \cdots, \lambda_{2}(m_{2})]$ be two paths in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ of lengths $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$, respectively, and suppose that $\lambda_{1}(m_{1}) = \lambda_{2}(0)$. We define the concatenation of $\lambda_{1}$ and $\lambda_{2}$, denoted by $\lambda_{1} \oplus \lambda_{2}$, by
$$\lambda_{1} \oplus \lambda_{2} = [ \lambda_{1} (0), \cdots , \lambda_{1} (m_{1}) , \lambda_{2} (1), \cdots , \lambda_{2} (m_{2})]. $$
    Then $\lambda_{1} \oplus \lambda_{2}$ is a path of length $m_{1}+m_{2}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:53.178569+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_9924ca6861b829c861a820ad78f8568a2b5c3f90e770f79fded32452d54d9ceb","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 7 (Transfer theorem for leading expectations) of arXiv:2606.29635, 'Extremality and Limit Laws for the Siblings of the Coupon Collector'] Suppose that the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

\[
        \frac{H_{N,j}(x)}{A_{N,j}}\to h_j(x)
\]
uniformly on $K$.

\[
        \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}h_j(x)\e^{-\Lambda(x)}\dd x<\infty.

        \frac{\E U_j^N}{A_{N,j}}\to\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}h_j(x)\e^{-\Lambda(x)}\dd x.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.082211+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_99280207db70966177c3583e39d774cd1c8fe19f6b393039e4becc276d5c92d7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.19832, 'Sharp Convex Concentration for Symmetric Random Tensors with Subgaussian Coordinates'] Let \(A,B\subset\R^n\) be measurable sets with positive \(\Pp\)-probability.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:46.149419+00:00","domain":"elliptic regularity theory","id":"claim_994ea180f3136425e554f422a5cd28077f4672f5e5871e28d1685f524f0bcfca","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Three hypotheses of the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theorem are load-bearing, and each fails concretely. (1) Scalar. The theorem is false for systems: De Giorgi (1968) exhibited, for n >= 3, a linear elliptic system with bounded measurable coefficients satisfying the Legendre-Hadamard and even the strong ellipticity condition whose weak solution is u(x) = x |x|^{-gamma} for an explicit gamma with 1 < gamma < n/2 - a solution in H^1 that is unbounded, hence not even locally bounded, let alone Hoelder. So a referee must check that an application of De Giorgi-Nash-Moser or of Moser's Harnack inequality is to a single equation, not to a system, and that the maximum-principle-based truncations used in the proof are available. (2) The energy class u in H^1_loc. A distributional solution whose gradient is only in L^p for some p < 2 need not be bounded. In the plane take A(x) = I + (mu - 1) x x^T/|x|^2 with mu > 1 (uniformly elliptic, bounded, measurable, discontinuous only at the origin). In polar coordinates div(A grad u) = (1/r) d/dr ( r mu u_r ) + (1/r^2) u_{theta theta}, so u = r^s cos(theta) solves the equation away from 0 exactly when mu s^2 = 1. The choice s = -1/sqrt(mu) in (-1,0) gives u = r^{-1/sqrt(mu)} cos(theta), which is unbounded at 0, lies in W^{1,p}_loc precisely for p < 2/(1 + 1/sqrt(mu)) < 2, and is a distributional solution across the origin (the flux through small circles tends to 0 because s > -1). (3) The Hoelder exponent depends on the ellipticity ratio and cannot be improved to Lipschitz. The same coefficients with s = +alpha, i.e. mu = 1/alpha^2, give the H^1 solution u = r^alpha cos(theta) of a uniformly elliptic equation with ellipticity ratio alpha^{-2}: it is exactly C^{0,alpha} at the origin and no better. Hence the exponent alpha(n, Lambda/lambda) in the theorem must degenerate to 0 as Lambda/lambda tends to infinity, and 'bounded measurable coefficients give Lipschitz solutions' is false. Gradient bounds require continuity (or Dini/Hoelder continuity) of the coefficients.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the walk is on the incipient infinite cluster or a similarly statistically self-similar critical random graph","a known or boundable volume-growth exponent d_f for balls in the cluster","a known or boundable effective-resistance-growth exponent reflecting the bottleneck/dangling-end structure","typically also requires the cluster's law to have appropriate scale-invariance, or at least comparable behavior across scales"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_995bb1851ff2b7c32ba0e7dcdd60e02e63ccc5cf1891c73d2c0eefad0e85bbb6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For simple random walk on the incipient infinite cluster of critical percolation, or more generally on critical random media with anomalous volume growth, Kesten's argument establishes subdiffusive behavior, that the walk's typical displacement after n steps is of order n^{1/d_w} with walk dimension d_w > 2 rather than the diffusive n^{1/2}, by combining a volume-growth estimate showing balls of radius r typically contain of order r^{d_f} points, with d_f the fractal (volume) dimension of the cluster, and an effective-resistance estimate R_eff(0, B(0,r)^c) of order r^{zeta}, reflecting the long dangling ends and low-conductance bottlenecks characteristic of the critical cluster. The expected exit time from a ball of radius r is then of order r^{d_f+zeta} (volume times resistance: the Einstein relation d_w = d_f + zeta), so the displacement is of order n^{1/(d_f+zeta)}, subdiffusive when d_f + zeta > 2; the Nash/heat-kernel machinery or a direct expected-exit-time computation turns the two estimates into bounds. In balls of the intrinsic (graph) metric with unit conductances R_eff(0, B(0,r)^c) <= r, so zeta <= 1 there: for the high-dimensional incipient infinite cluster the intrinsic volume grows as r^2 and the resistance as r, giving d_w = 3. The argument does not give the exact value of the subdiffusivity exponent in most dimensions, only bounds, with the precise exponent known rigorously only in specific settings such as sufficiently high dimension or tree-like/hierarchical models, and it is specific to critical (not subcritical or supercritical) percolation geometry, where the fractal, tree-like structure with many bottlenecks is essential to the argument. Typical failure: Assuming the subdiffusivity exponent established for one setting, such as high-dimensional or tree-based incipient infinite clusters where exact computation is possible, transfers to two-dimensional critical percolation, where the exact random-walk dimension remains a major open problem; volume-growth and resistance-growth exponents are model- and dimension-specific quantities that must be independently estimated rather than imported across models with superficially similar critical geometry. Canonical reference: Kesten, 1986, Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare, Probabilites et Statistiques; Barlow, Jarai, Kumagai and Slade, 2008, Communications in Mathematical Physics.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:46:36.164984+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_997fe855269205198170d0fd2c72b9039f5749738a989f6aa5cdd70e7aa4eae4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Def_ExtendedIsometry of arXiv:2609.02848, 'The universal moduli space of non-degenerate $\Z/2\Z$~harmonic spinors'] The \defined{extended gauge group} of $S$ is the tame Fréchet Lie group $\widehat\mathscr{G}(S)$ constructed as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}  
  \item
    
    An \defined{extended isometry} of $S$ is a diffeomorphism $u \in \Diff(S)$ for which there exists a diffeomorphism $\check u \in \Diff(X)$ such that $u$ defines an isometry $S \cong \check u^*S$.
    These form a subgroup $\widehat\mathscr{G}(S) \leqslant \Diff(S)$.    
  \item
    A moment's thought shows that extended isometries lift to $\mathrm{O}(r)$--equivariant diffeomorphisms of $\Fr(S)$,
    the orthogonal frame bundle of $S$;
    in fact, $\widehat\mathscr{G}(S) = \Diff(\Fr(S))^{\mathrm{O}(r)}$, abusing notation.
    By [Molitor2010:UnimodularAutomorphisms],
    $\widehat\mathscr{G}(S) \leqslant \Diff(\Fr(S))$ is a tame Fréchet Lie subgroup.
  \item
    From the above perspective,
    $\widehat\mathscr{G}(S)$ acts smoothly and tamely on $S = \Fr(S) \times_{\mathrm{O}(r)} \mathbb{R}^r$ and $X = \Fr(S) \times_{\mathrm{O}(r)} \set{*}$ from the left
    by
    \begin{equation*}
      u \cdot [p,\phi] \coloneq [u(p),\phi]
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      u \cdot [p,*] \coloneq [u(p),*],
    \end{equation*}
    respectively.
    As a consequence,
    it acts smoothly and tamely on $\Gamma\paren{X,S}$, $\mathbf{Dir}$, and $\mathbf{Ram}$ from the right by pullback.
    \footnote{
      
      The reader should be warned that $\widehat\mathscr{G}(S)$ does not lift to an action on $\mathbf{Ram}^0$;
      however, the action lifts locally.
      This is sufficient for (Prop_TransformToNormalForm of the paper).
    }
    \qedhere
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}
