{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:55:18.060806+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ae4c6b72ffb363c8d0d45cbc47237d2b68a414c99c5024edd201b16be4dd05b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2606.17381, 'Large deviation principle for friendship-biases\\ in Galton--Watson trees'] {\bf [Properties of the rate function]}

\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (a)}] On $\cD$, $(x,s) \mapsto J(x,s)$ is marginally convex and achieves its unique zero at $(x^*,s^*)$ given by
\[
(x^*,s^*) = \big(\|G(\nu^*)\|_1,G(\nu^*)/\|G(\nu^*)\|_1\big)
\] 
with $\nu^* = (\zeta^{\otimes 2})^{\otimes 3}$, which equals
\[
x^* = \frac{1}{1-p}, \qquad s^* = \big((1-p)-(1-p)^4,\, p^3 + (1-p)^4,\, p-p^3\big).          
\]
\item[{\rm (b)}] 
For every $(x,s) \in \mathrm{int}(\cD)$, the infimum defining $J(x,s)$ is achieved and equals
\[
J(x,s) = -\lambda(x,s) - x \sum_{\chi \in S} s^\chi \lambda^\chi (x,s), 
\]
where $\lambda(x,s)$ and $\lambda^\chi(x,s)$, $\chi \in S$, are Lagrangian multipliers that uniquely solve four equations involving rational functions whose coefficients depend on $(x,s)$ and $p$ (see Section \ref{sec:ProofLDP2}).
\item[{\rm (c)}]
On $\mathrm{int}(\cD)$, $(x,s) \mapsto J(x,s)$ is analytic and marginally strictly convex.
\item[{\rm(d)}] 
$\mathrm{int}(\cD) = \big\{(x,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathcal S_2\colon\, 1 < x < \infty,\,s^- < 1/x < s^-+s^0 < 1 < 3s^-+s^0\big\}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["A is a square real matrix with nonnegative entries"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T02:00:35.438555+00:00","domain":"linear algebra, nonnegative matrices","id":"claim_ae5c6a4cb8084ef24a18e45632bcc8943945094a5e71de887f9245aa6e393816","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A real $n \\times n$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$ is nonnegative ($A \\ge 0$) if all entries are $\\ge 0$, and positive ($A > 0$) if all entries are $> 0$. Associate to $A \\ge 0$ the directed graph $G(A)$ on vertices $1, \\dots, n$ with an edge $i \\to j$ iff $a_{ij} > 0$; then $(A^m)_{ij} > 0$ iff there is a walk of length $m$ from $i$ to $j$. $A$ is irreducible if $G(A)$ is strongly connected (every vertex reaches every other), equivalently if there is no permutation matrix $P$ with $P A P^{\\mathsf T} = \\begin{pmatrix} B & C \\\\ 0 & D\\end{pmatrix}$ with $B, D$ square nonempty blocks, equivalently (for $n \\ge 2$) if $(I + A)^{n-1} > 0$; a $1 \\times 1$ matrix is irreducible by convention (some authors exclude the zero $1\\times1$ matrix). The period (index of imprimitivity) $h$ of an irreducible $A$ is the greatest common divisor of the lengths of all closed walks in $G(A)$; it does not depend on the vertex, and $h = 1$ iff $A$ is aperiodic. $A$ is primitive if $A \\ge 0$ and $A^m > 0$ for some $m \\ge 1$; for nonnegative matrices, primitive $\\iff$ irreducible and aperiodic, and then $A^m > 0$ for all $m \\ge (n-1)^2 + 1$ (Wielandt's bound). Every positive matrix is primitive. Warnings: irreducible does not imply primitive (the cyclic permutation matrix of an $n$-cycle is irreducible with period $n$); a matrix with a positive diagonal entry that is irreducible is automatically primitive; irreducibility is a property of the zero pattern only, not of the magnitudes; a matrix with some negative entries is outside this theory entirely.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.493350+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ae79d6812b4fb7ffa2c3b33c08d4e0e8ba3daead3a304e5986b32ed89a84c3f7","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 11 (Octahedron recurrence) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{def:oct}
We use the max-plus form of the octahedron recurrence, in the sense of
\cite{KTW,Speyer,NarSheffTao}.  One starts with real values assigned to a
stepped surface in the parity sublattice of \(\mathbb Z^3\).  A local move
replaces one face of an elementary octahedron by the opposite face.  If the
six vertices of this octahedron are
\[
(i,j,k\pm 1),\qquad (i\pm 1,j,k),\qquad (i,j\pm 1,k),
\]
and all values except \(F(i,j,k+1)\) are already known, then the missing value
is defined by
\[
F(i,j,k+1)
=
\max\{F(i+1,j,k)+F(i-1,j,k),\,
F(i,j+1,k)+F(i,j-1,k)\}
-F(i,j,k-1).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
F(i,j,k+1)+F(i,j,k-1)
=
\max\{F(i+1,j,k)+F(i-1,j,k),\,
F(i,j+1,k)+F(i,j-1,k)\}.
\]
Iterating these local moves transports the data from one stepped surface to
another.  In the hive setting this transport is the
Knutson--Tao--Woodward/Speyer piecewise-linear, volume-preserving bijection
between the two hive decompositions corresponding to associativity
\cite{KTW,Speyer,NarSheffTao}; we denote it by \(\oct\).

For the applications below, Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv) first lets us regard
Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns as hives with one large-gap side.  With this
identification, \(\oct\) sends a pair of Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns, equivalently
a double hive, to an augmented hive, or to a pair of hives glued along their
common boundary.  Throughout the paper \(h_n\) denotes the hive component of
this image when the input is the deformed GUE double hive.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:05:57.798777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ae7f4f491c57f1500da9e1c3e081a5803ad42a846738f1d551392e0ac265ad19","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 of arXiv:2608.30551, 'Critical Discrete Hardy Inequalities in $L^p$'] Let $\Omega\subseteq X$. A \emph{Hardy weight} for
$\mathcal{E}_p^{X,k}$ on $\Omega$ is a nonnegative function
$w:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ such that
$$
\mathcal{E}_p^{X,k}(u)
\geq
\sum_{x\in\Omega}w(x)|u(x)|^p,
\qquad u\in C_c(\Omega).
$$
A Hardy weight $w$ is called \emph{critical} if every Hardy weight
$\widetilde w$ on $\Omega$ satisfying
$$
\widetilde w(x)\geq w(x),
\qquad x\in\Omega,
$$
coincides with $w$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:33:46.767216+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ae806e2d14ac53d071e815421fa3fd8d8dd630356962ffc4f1102a910336673a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Let $\\Sigma \\subseteq \\mathbb{Z}$ and $\\Lambda \\subseteq \\mathbb{R}$ be an interval. A {\\em $\\Sigma$-indexed line ensemble $\\mathcal{L}$} is a random variable defined on a probability space $(\\Omega, \\mathcal{F}, \\mathbb{P})$ that takes values in $\\left(C (\\Sigma \\times \\Lambda), \\mathcal{C}_{\\Sigma}\\right)$. Intuitively, $\\mathcal{L}$ is a collection of random continuous curves (sometimes referred to as {\\em lines}), indexed by $\\Sigma$, each of which maps $\\Lambda$ into $\\mathbb{R}$. We will often slightly abuse notation and write $\\mathcal{L}: \\Sigma \\times \\Lambda \\rightarrow \\mathbb{R}$, even though it is not $\\mathcal{L}$ which is such a function, but $\\mathcal{L}(\\omega)$ for every $\\omega \\in \\Omega$. For $i \\in \\Sigma$, we write $\\mathcal{L}_i(\\omega) = (\\mathcal{L}(\\omega))(i, \\cdot)$ for the curve of index $i$ and note that the latter is a map $\\mathcal{L}_i: \\Omega \\rightarrow C(\\Lambda)$, which is $\\mathcal{F}/\\mathcal{C}$ measurable. \n\nWe say that a line ensemble $\\mathcal{L}$ is {\\em non-intersecting} if $\\mathbb{P}$-almost surely $\\mathcal{L}_i(t) > \\mathcal{L}_j(t)$ for all $i < j$ and $t \\in \\Lambda$. We say that a line ensemble $\\mathcal{L}$ is {\\em ordered} if $\\mathbb{P}$-almost surely $\\mathcal{L}_i(t) \\geq \\mathcal{L}_j(t)$ for all $i < j$ and $t \\in \\Lambda$. If $[a,b] \\subseteq \\Lambda$, we let $\\mathcal{L}_i[a,b]$ denote the restriction of $\\mathcal{L}_i$ to $[a,b]$, and note that the latter is a measurable map $\\mathcal{L}_i[a,b]: \\Omega \\rightarrow C([a,b])$. If $\\Sigma_1 \\subseteq \\Sigma$ and $[a,b] \\subseteq \\Lambda$, we let $\\mathcal{L}\\vert_{\\Sigma_1 \\times [a,b]}$ denote the restriction of $\\mathcal{L}$ to $\\Sigma_1 \\times [a,b]$, which is a measurable map $\\mathcal{L}\\vert_{\\Sigma_1 \\times [a,b]}: \\Omega \\rightarrow C(\\Sigma_1 \\times [a,b])$.","status":"unverified"}

(Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:22:01.685777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_aea7e6415e1699d9c07021f9c360640cbd5a5b246854760946066eb7e33158b6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def-delta-QLE-finite of arXiv:2605.03385, 'Quantum Loewner evolution in quantum natural time: phases and Markov properties'] Consider either $\gamma \in (\sqrt3 -1,2)$ and $\eta = \frac3{\gamma^2} - \frac12$, or $\gamma \in (0, 4/3) \cup (2\sqrt3 - 2,2)$ and $\eta = \frac{3\gamma^2}{16} - \frac12$. In the former case set $\kappa = \gamma^2$, whereas in the latter case set $\kappa = 16/\gamma^2$.
Let $(\alpha,\beta)$ be defined as follows:
\begin{equation*} (\alpha, \beta) = 
        \begin{cases} 
          (Q-\frac{1}{\gamma},\gamma - \frac2\gamma) & \gamma \in (\sqrt3 - 1,2), \, \, \eta = \frac3{\gamma^2} - \frac12 \\
            (Q-\frac{\gamma}{4},\frac4\gamma - \frac\gamma2) & \gamma \in (2\sqrt3 - 2, 2), \, \, \eta = \frac{3\gamma^2}{16} - \frac12 \\
          (Q-\frac{\gamma}{4},\frac{3\gamma}{2}) & \gamma \in (0, 4/3), \, \,  \eta = \frac{3\gamma^2}{16} - \frac12 
       \end{cases}
    \end{equation*}
Sample $\phi^\delta \sim P_{\alpha, \beta, 1}$. We will define a shrinking process of origin-containing domains $D_s^\delta \subset \mathbb{D}$ beginning with $D_0^\delta = \mathbb{D}$. 
Iteratively for $n \in \mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ we carry out the following:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item (\textbf{Resample the curve tip}): 
        Let $\phi^\delta_{n\delta} = g_{D^\delta_{n\delta}} \bullet_\gamma \phi^\delta$. 
        Sample a point from the probability measure $(\mathcal{L}_{\phi_{n\delta}^\delta}^{\beta})^\#$ on $\partial \mathbb{D}$ and let $p^\delta_n \in \partial D_{n\delta}^\delta$ be its image under $(g_{D_{n\delta}^\delta})^{-1}$. Note that $p^\delta_n$ is understood as a prime end\footnote{If $\kappa \leq 4$, each point on the interior of an SLE$_\kappa$ segment corresponds to two prime ends in $\partial D^\delta_{n\delta}$, namely the boundary points on the left and right of the curve segment.} of $D_{n\delta}^\delta$. 
        
        \item (\textbf{Grow an $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ curve}): Let $\eta^\delta_n$ be radial SLE$_\kappa$ in $D^\delta_{n\delta}$ from $p^\delta_n$ to $0$. 
        Parametrize $\eta_n^\delta$ by quantum natural time as in Definitions~
        (def-quantum-time-simple of the paper)-(def-quantum-time-sf of the paper), and let $\mathcal{S}^\delta_n$ be its duration. 
        For $s \in (n \delta, n\delta + \min(\delta, \mathcal{S}^\delta_n)]$ let $D^\delta_s$ be the connected component of $D^\delta_{n\delta} \backslash \eta^\delta_n([0,s-n\delta])$ which contains 0. If  $\mathcal{S}^\delta_n \leq \delta$, set $\mathcal{S}^\delta = n\delta + \mathcal{S}^\delta_n$ and terminate the process at time  $\mathcal{S}^\delta$. 
    \end{itemize}
    If the process does not terminate, set $\mathcal{S}^\delta = \infty$. Let $K^\delta_s = \overline\mathbb{D} \backslash D^\delta_s$, so $(K^\delta_\cdot)_{[0,\mathcal{S}^\delta]}$ is a growing family of hulls. 
    We call $(\phi^\delta, (K^\delta_\cdot)_{[0,  \mathcal{S}^\delta]})$ a $\delta$-$\mathrm{QLE}(\gamma^2, \eta)$ process.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.069216+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_aec7556d43c449fffb08ec6df68bed9c20534e0822f9c8bdb504100ae3e497ef","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 4 (ULDP) of arXiv:2608.19753, 'Uniform large deviation principles for the stochastic heat equation over unbounded sets of'] Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a Polish space, completely metrized by a metric $d$. 
Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ be a probability space.  Let $ \mathcal{E}_0$ be any set, and let $\{X^\eps_x: \eps>0,x\in \mathcal{E}_0\}$ be a family of $\mathcal{E}$-valued random variables. Let $\{I_x : x \in \mathcal{E}_0\}$ be a collection of lower-semicontinuous maps $I_x : \mathcal{E} \to [0,+\infty]$. 
Let $\mathscr{A}$ be a collection of subsets of $\mathcal{E}_0$.  
Then, the family $\{X^\eps_x: \eps>0,x\in \mathcal{E}_0\}$ is said to satisfy a \emph{Freidlin--Wentzell uniform large deviation principle (ULDP) with respect to the rate functions $I_x$ uniformly over $\mathscr{A}$}, if
\begin{itemize}
\item For any $A \in \mathscr{A}$, $s_0 > 0$, and $\delta > 0$,
\[
\liminf_{\eps \to 0} \inf_{x \in A} \inf_{\varphi \in \Phi_x(s_0)} \big(\eps\log \mathbb{P}(d(X^\eps_x, \varphi) < \delta) + I_x(\varphi)\big) \geq 0.
\]
\item For any $A \in \mathscr{A}$, $s_0 > 0$, and $\delta > 0$,
\[
\limsup_{\eps \to 0} \sup_{x \in A} \sup_{s \in [0,s_0]} \big(\eps \log \mathbb{P}(\mathrm{dist}_d(X^\eps_x, \Phi_x(s)) \geq \delta) + s\big) \leq 0,
\]
\end{itemize}
where $\Phi_x(s) \ceqq \{\varphi \in \mathcal{E} : I_x(\varphi) \leq s\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:59:45.010040+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_aeccbf6ce826c51a465cad74a5ca5f3282abbd81222730df0bb8d668db4d29dc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem ordinary-factorial-bispectrum of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Assume that the reduced second factorial cumulant measure and the reduced third factorial and complete cumulant measures are finite signed measures, so that the Fourier--Stieltjes transforms below are ordinary bounded functions. {"assumptions":["H is a complex Hilbert space","every A_n and A is self-adjoint (so the resolvent set contains C minus R and the resolvent norm bound 1/|Im z| holds)","no relation between the domains of the A_n and of A is assumed","convergence is of the resolvents, applied to a fixed vector (strong) or in operator norm (norm)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090914+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, unbounded self-adjoint operators","id":"claim_aefd17250c9ea1190635da34d922379fe94928d2718e0131592cbabceafdf37c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let A_n (n = 1, 2, ...) and A be self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space H, each on its own dense domain; the domains are not assumed equal or even comparable. One says A_n -> A in the STRONG RESOLVENT SENSE if for every psi in H and every z in C with nonzero imaginary part, (A_n - z)^(-1) psi converges in norm to (A - z)^(-1) psi. Because each operator is self-adjoint, the resolvent (A_n - z)^(-1) is bounded with norm at most 1 / |Im z|, so the family is uniformly bounded and it is enough to verify the convergence for a SINGLE non-real z: one z in the upper half plane suffices, the conjugate point following by taking adjoints and the remaining z by the resolvent identity together with the uniform bound. The NORM RESOLVENT SENSE is the same statement with convergence in operator norm; it implies the strong resolvent sense and is strictly stronger. Practical criterion: if all the A_n and A are essentially self-adjoint on a common core D and A_n psi -> A psi for every psi in D, then A_n -> A in the strong resolvent sense. Without such a hypothesis convergence on a dense subspace says nothing, which is precisely why the resolvent formulation, and not naive pointwise convergence of unbounded operators, is the notion that interacts with the spectral theorem.","status":"unverified"}

\[

\begin{equation}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:33:43.752886+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af148899ad2568e533147c56514327fd2e5213c38adeef15b4543cbbba0efd5a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:prop_of_bessel_space of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Let $p>1$ and $\eta\in\mathbb{R}$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item 
 
The space $C_c^\infty$ is dense in $H_p^\eta$. 
\item 
 
Let $\eta-\frac1p=n+\nu$ for some $n=0,1,\ldots$ and $\nu\in(0,1]$. Then, for every
$i\in\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$,
\begin{equation}
    \|D^i u\|_{C(\mathbb{R})}
    +
    \|D^n u\|_{\mathcal C^\nu(\mathbb{R})}
    \le
    N\|u\|_{H_p^\eta},
\end{equation}
where $N=N(p,\eta)$, and $\mathcal C^\nu$ is the Zygmund space.
\item 

For every integer $i\ge0$, the operator $D^i:H_p^\eta\to H_p^{\eta-i}$ is bounded. Moreover, for every $u\in H_p^{\eta+i}$,
\[
    \|D^i u\|_{H_p^\eta}
    \le
    N\|u\|_{H_p^{\eta+i}},
\]
where $N=N(p,\eta,i)$.

\item 

Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\mu\le\eta$. If $u\in H_p^{\eta}$, then $u\in H_p^{\mu}$ and
\[ \|u\|_{H_p^{\mu}}\le\|u\|_{H_p^{\eta}}. \]
Moreover, if $q\in(1,\infty)$ satisfies $\eta-\frac{1}{p}=\mu-\frac{1}{q}$, then
\[ \|u\|_{H_q^{\mu}}\le N\|u\|_{H_p^{\eta}}, \]
where $N=N(\eta,\mu,p,q)$.

\item 

Let
\[
\varepsilon\in[0,1],
\qquad
p_i\in(1,\infty),
\qquad
\eta_i\in\mathbb{R},
\qquad i=0,1,
\]
and suppose
\[
    \eta=\varepsilon\eta_0+(1-\varepsilon)\eta_1,
    \qquad
    \frac1p=\frac{\varepsilon}{p_0}+\frac{1-\varepsilon}{p_1}.
\]

\[
    \|u\|_{H_p^\eta}
    \le
    \|u\|_{H_{p_0}^{\eta_0}}^\varepsilon
    \|u\|_{H_{p_1}^{\eta_1}}^{1-\varepsilon}.
\]

\[
    \|u\|_{H_p^\eta}
    \le
    \delta\|u\|_{H_{p_0}^{\eta_0}}
    +
    N(\delta)\|u\|_{H_{p_1}^{\eta_1}} .

\item  If $u\in H_p^\eta$, $a\in B^{|\eta|+\alpha}$ and $b\in B^{|\eta|+\alpha}(\ell_2)$, then
\[

\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["real variable on [-1, 1] for the extremal statements; the polynomials themselves are defined on all of R and C"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.479741+00:00","domain":"approximation theory","id":"claim_af2c306d13e82f8e10b1a499cd863744a70e37247652744c79e094c450f9b166","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"The Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind are defined on [-1, 1] by T_n(cos theta) = cos(n theta), n = 0, 1, 2, ...; equivalently T_0 = 1, T_1 = x and T_{n+1}(x) = 2 x T_n(x) - T_{n-1}(x). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:42:16.236249+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af301d480ff0d63b1823f79073205a288d43b79de86ce0d2782100e31d4bfd4e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem kpartW1 of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Let Assumption~(ass:w1-normalized-matern of the paper) hold and suppose the joint initial law of the particles is exchangeable. For fixed \(k\ge1\), define
the random \(k\)-fold empirical occupation measure
\[
        \widehat\mu_T^{N,k}
        :=
        \frac1T\int_0^T (\mu_t^N)^{\odot k}\,dt,
        \qquad
        \overline{\mu^{\otimes k}}_T
        :=
        \frac1T\int_0^T \mu_t^{\otimes k}\,dt,
\]
where
\[
(\mu_t^N)^{\odot k}
:=
\frac{1}{(N)_k}
\sum_{\substack{1\le i_1,\ldots,i_k\le N\\
i_1,\ldots,i_k\ {\rm distinct}}}
\delta_{\bigl(x_{i_1}^N(t),\ldots,x_{i_k}^N(t)\bigr)},
\qquad
(N)_k:=N(N-1)\cdots(N-k+1).
\]
Let \(W_1^{(k)}\) be the Wasserstein distance on \((\mathbb R^d)^k\)
associated with the product cost
\(
        d_k(x,y):=\sum_{\ell=1}^k \|x_\ell-y_\ell\| .
\)
Then, with $\gamma$ as in Theorem~(prop:uniform-time-averaged-w1 of the paper),
\begin{equation}
\lim_{M \to \infty} \, \limsup_{N \to \infty}\,\sup_{T>0}
\mathbb P\left(
W_1^{(k)}
\left(
\widehat\mu_T^{N,k},
\overline{\mu^{\otimes k}}_T
\right)
>
M(\log \log N)^{-\gamma/2}
\right)=0.
\end{equation}
Moreover, suppose the initial distributions satisfy (equation Gaussexp of the paper). 
Define, for $k \ge 1$,
\[
        \bar\mu_T^{N,k}
        :=
        \frac1T\int_0^T
        \mathcal L(x_1^N(t),\ldots,x_k^N(t))\,dt,
        \qquad
        \overline{\mu^{\otimes k}}_T
        :=
        \frac1T\int_0^T \mu_t^{\otimes k}\,dt ,
\]
where $L(x_1^N(t),\ldots,x_k^N(t))$ denotes the joint law of $(x_1^N(t),\ldots,x_k^N(t))$.
Then there is \(C_k<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\begin{equation}
        \sup_{T>0}
        W_1^{(k)}
        \left(
        \bar\mu_T^{N,k},
        \overline{\mu^{\otimes k}}_T
        \right)
        \le
        C_k(\log\log N)^{-\gamma/2}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

For each $i=1, 2, \ldots, \rho$, 
let $(z_{i,1}, z_{i,2}, \ldots)$ be an infinite sequence of parameters 
satisfying $|z_{i,j}|\leq r^j$ for a fixed real $r\geq 1$, and let $Z$ denote 
the collection of all $z_{i,j}$. Then we define the sequence
$C_b^\rho(n;Z)$ by the generating function
\begin{equation}
\sum_{n=0}^\infty C_b^\rho(n;Z)q^n =\prod_{j=0}^\infty\prod_{i=1}^\rho
\left(1+z_{i,1}q^{b^j}+z_{i,2}q^{2\cdot b^j}+z_{i,3}q^{3\cdot b^j}+\dots\right).
\end{equation}
When $z_{i,j}=1$ for all $1\leq i\leq\rho$ and $j\geq 1$, we set
$C_b^\rho(n):=C_b^\rho(n;Z)$, so that
\begin{equation}
\sum_{n=0}^\infty C_b^\rho(n)q^n =\prod_{j=0}^\infty
\left(1+q^{b^j}+q^{2\cdot b^j}+q^{3\cdot b^j}+\dots\right)^\rho
=\prod_{j=0}^\infty\frac{1}{\left(1-q^{b^j}\right)^\rho}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:30:52.739233+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af450bf1c04dd962777a373b3274ebb387b0a16402a997837b1c21544c9d132b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 9 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Alpha Log-Determinant divergences between positive definite trace class operators - \cite{Minh:LogDet2016}}]
			
			Assume that {$\dim(\H) = \infty$}. For {$-1 < \alpha < 1$},
			
			the Alpha Log-Det divergence 
			
			$d^{\alpha}_{\logdet}[(A+\gamma I), (B+ \mu I)]$ between  $(A+\gamma I) > 0, (B+\mu I) > 0$,
			$A, B \in \Tr(\H)$, $\gamma,\mu \in \R$, 
			
			is defined to be
			
			\begin{align}
				&d^{\alpha}_{\logdet}
				[(A+\gamma I), (B+ \mu I)]
				\nonumber
				\\
				& = \frac{4}{1-\alpha^2}  
				\log\left[\frac{\detX\left(\frac{1-\alpha}{2}(A+\gamma I) + \frac{1+\alpha}{2}(B+\mu I)\right)}{\detX(A+\gamma I)^{\beta}\detX(B + \mu I)^{1-\beta}}\left(\frac{\gamma}{\mu}\right)^{\beta - \frac{1-\alpha}{2}}\right],
				
			\end{align}
			where {$\beta = \frac{(1-\alpha)\gamma}{(1-\alpha) \gamma + (1+\alpha)\mu}$}.
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
			
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
			
			The limiting cases $\alpha \approach \pm 1$ are defined by
			\begin{align}
				&
				
				d^{1}_{\logdet}[(A+\gamma I), (B+\mu I)] = \left(\frac{\gamma}{\mu}-1\right)\log\frac{\gamma}{\mu} 
				\nonumber
				\\
				&\;\;\;\;\;+ \trX[(B+\mu I)^{-1}(A+\gamma I) - I] - \frac{\gamma}{\mu}\log\detX[(B+\mu I)^{-1}(A+\gamma I)].
				
				
				
				\\
				&
				
				d^{-1}_{\logdet}[(A+\gamma I), (B+\mu I)] = 
				\left(\frac{\mu}{\gamma}-1\right)\log\frac{\mu}{\gamma} 
				
				\nonumber
				\\
				&+ \trX\left[(A+\gamma I)^{-1}(B+\mu I) - I\right] - \frac{\mu}{\gamma}\log\detX[(A+\gamma I)^{-1}(B+\mu I)].
				
			\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:15:09.103457+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af455860804200f9da1e82a3da978bc5e17d63f809a5d79200dcfcf3d2487a6d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Quotient graph induces by graph of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] Let $G_1,\\dots,G_n$ be unoriented graphs with set of vertices and edges $(V_i,E_i)$ for $1\\leq i\\leq n$. Let $T=(V_T,E_T)$ be an unoriented graph with set of vertices $V_T=\\{G_i:1\\leq i\\leq n\\}$. For each edge $e=\\{G_i,G_j\\}\\in E_T$ we also consider a pair of vertices $\\{v_i,v_j\\}$ where $v_i$ and $v_j$ are vertices of $G_i$ and $G_j$ respectively. We denote the vertices $\\{v_i,v_j\\}$ associated with the edge $e\\in E_T$ by $V(e)$.  \nWe call the triple $T=(V_T,E_T,\\{V(e)\\}_{e\\in E_T})$ a \\textit{graph of the graphs} $G_1,\\dots,G_n$. We let $\\pi_T\\in \\mathcal{P}(\\cup_{i=1}^n V_i)$ be the partition given by $u$ and $v$ being in the same block of $\\pi_T$ whenever there is an edge $e\\in E_T$ such that $V(e)=\\{u,v\\}$. Let $G=\\cup_{i=1}^n G_i$ be the union of the graphs, that is, the graph with set of vertices $\\cup_{i=1}^n V_i$ and set of edges $\\cup_{i=1}^n E_i$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:09:43.682340+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af46b4cf56dd51b7cb69e8bc90c8cf2f734de6ab113c1193e9b207638b55d439","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma NEW-l:pre-Gron of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider Lipschitz diffusion  coefficients $(b,\sigma)$ as defined in Definition~(NEW-d:lip_assum of the paper). Let $\{X[x]\}_{x\in{\cal X }}$ and $\{X'[x]\}_{x\in{\cal X }}$ be two families of  continuous  processes in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$ adapted to the filtration generated by the family of i.i.d. standard Brownian motions $\{Z_x(\cdot)\}_{x \in {\cal X }}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$ on $[0,t_0]$ 
and $\mathbb{E} [\|X[x]\|^2]<\infty$, $\mathbb{E} [\|X'[x]\|^2]<\infty$ for all  $x\in{\cal X }$.
Consider  the family of stochastic processes $\{Y[x]\}_{x\in{\cal X }}$ on $\mathbb {M} $, defined on $[0,t_0]$ by
\begin{equation}
   
Y(x,t):= Y(x,0)+\int_0^t b(t, X[x], X[N_x])\, \mathrm{d} t + \sigma(t, X[x], X[N_x])\, \mathrm{d} Z_x(t),
\end{equation}
along with the family of stochastic processes $Y'(x,t)$ on $\mathbb {M} $ defined as above but with $X'$ instead of $X$.
These processes are indexed by the vertices $x\in{\cal X }$, they utilize the graph neighborhood $N_x=\{y\in{\cal X }:y\sim x\}$ on a given graph $\Psi({\cal X })$
and they share the same initial conditions $Y(x,0)=Y'(x,0)$.
Then for any $x\in{\cal X }$ and $t\in[0,t_0]$, we have
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{E}  [\| Y[x,t] - Y'[x,t] \|^2]
\le 32\max(t,1)K_t^2\int_{0}^t \max_{y\in\mathfrak{B}_1(x)} \mathbb{E}  [\| X[y,s] - X'[y,s] \|^2]\, \mathrm{d} s,
\end{equation}
where $\mathfrak{B}_1(x)$  is graph ball on  $\Psi({\cal X })$ of radius $1$ centered at~$x$
and where $K_t$ is the Lipschitz diffusion constant given in Definition \ref
{NEW-d:lip_assum}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:30:14.145962+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af5746ea66df68d507dfac7b3787faf80c28638878669aedfe08a687ef28898b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem th:split:dynamical of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] Assume that $n\geq2$. Let $v$, $L$, and $L^\perp$ be as in Theorem
  (th:split of the paper). Consider the processes ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and
  ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$ with state space $\mathbb{C}$ and $L^\perp$ defined by
  \[
    S_tv=\operatorname{proj}_L(Z_t^n)=\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n Z_t^{n,j}\Bigr)v
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    W_t=\operatorname{proj}_{L^\perp}(Z_t^n)=Z_t^n-\frac{S_t}{n}(1,\ldots,1)
  \]
  where $(Z_t^n)_{t\geq0}$ is the solution of (equation eq:intro-sde of the paper). Then there
  exist independent Brownian motions $B^S$ on $\mathbb{C}$ and $B^W$ on
  $L^\perp$ such that ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$ solve the
  stochastic differential equations
  \begin{equation}
    \mathrm{d}S_t=\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}}\mathrm{d}B_t^S-\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}S_t\mathrm{d}t
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    \mathrm{d}W_t
    =
    \frac{\sqrt{2\alpha_n}}{n}\,\mathrm{d}B_t^W
    -\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}W_t\,\mathrm{d}t
    +\frac{2\alpha_n}{n^2}b(W_t)\,\mathrm{d}t,
  \end{equation}
  where $b_j(w)=\sum_{k\neq j}\frac{w_j-w_k}{|w_j-w_k|^2}$. In particular
  ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ is a complex Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process and the
  transition semigroup of $Z^n$ is the product of the semigroups of
  ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$. In particular, ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$
  and ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$ are independent whenever $S_0$ and $W_0$ are
  independent. Moreover, if we define
  \begin{equation}
    U_t=|S_t|^2,
    \quad
    R_t=n|W_t|^2
    =\sum_{1\leq j<k\leq n}|Z_t^{n,j}-Z_t^{n,k}|^2,
    \quad
    \kappa=\frac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}.
  \end{equation}
  then there exist independent real Brownian motions $\beta^S$ and $\beta^R$
  such that ${(U_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(R_t)}_{t\geq0}$ solve
  \begin{equation}
    \mathrm{d}U_t
    =
    \frac{4\alpha_n}{n}(1-U_t)\mathrm{d}t +2\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}U_t}\mathrm{d}\beta_t^S
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    \mathrm{d}R_t
    =
    \frac{4\alpha_n}{n}(\kappa-R_t)\mathrm{d}t +2\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}R_t}\mathrm{d}\beta_t^R.
  \end{equation}
  In particular ${(U_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(R_t)}_{t\geq0}$ are
  Cox--Ingersoll--Ross processes with invariant distributions
  $\operatorname{Gamma}(1,1)$ and $\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,1)$,
  respectively. Furthermore, in the stationary case where $Z_0^n\sim\mu_n$,
  the processes $(S_t)_{t\geq0}$ and $(W_t)_{t\geq0}$, and hence
  ${(U_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(R_t)}_{t\geq0}$, are independent and stationary.","status":"unverified"}

\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the Marchenko-Pastur-Silverstein setting (i.i.d. rows with finite twelfth moments in Ledoit-Wolf's statement), p/n -> c in (0, 1)","estimators restricted to the rotation-equivariant class (sample eigenvectors kept)","the identity making the two oracles' limits reciprocal is cited from the paper, not re-derived above"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T09:21:49.110177+00:00","domain":"covariance estimation / portfolio optimization","id":"claim_af6709ee5777434e2a0ecbeedc7d640c4e67e6b22be7b38c5f3187f98400f874","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $S = \\sum_i \\lambda_i u_i u_i^T$ be the sample covariance of $n$ observations in $\\mathbb{R}^p$ with population covariance $\\Sigma$, $p/n \\to c \\in (0, 1)$, in the setting of the Marchenko-Pastur-Silverstein theorem. Consider rotation-equivariant estimators $\\hat\\Sigma = \\sum_i d_i u_i u_i^T$ and the global minimum-variance portfolio $\\hat w = \\hat\\Sigma^{-1}\\mathbf{1}/(\\mathbf{1}^T\\hat\\Sigma^{-1}\\mathbf{1})$ built from them, scored by its true out-of-sample variance $\\hat w^T \\Sigma \\hat w$. Ledoit and Wolf (2017) show: (i) the finite-sample oracle for this loss is $d_i^{\\mathrm{mv}} = 1 / (u_i^T \\Sigma^{-1} u_i)$ (the 'inverse' oracle), whereas the Frobenius-loss oracle is $d_i^{\\mathrm{fro}} = u_i^T \\Sigma u_i$; (ii) in the large-dimensional limit both oracles converge to the SAME nonlinear shrinkage $\\tilde d_i = \\lambda_i / |1 - c - c\\lambda_i \\breve m_F(\\lambda_i)|^2$ (the Ledoit-Peche formula), because the Ledoit-Peche limits of the two quadratic forms $u_i^T\\Sigma u_i$ and $u_i^T\\Sigma^{-1}u_i$ are reciprocal to each other; so the nonlinear shrinkage estimator that is optimal for estimating the covariance in Frobenius loss is also asymptotically optimal for the minimum-variance portfolio - neither too much shrinkage (the linear shrinkage's) nor too little (the sample covariance's). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.811818+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af6852edb99f8c7c12ee528afef108081a36d928e0fee88f67d8253457aca1bd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma Lem:intersec_of_An of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 2} $ be a positive integer with $ n \geq 2 $.

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. nonnegative weights on Z^d, d >= 2","F(0) < p_c(d), so the time constant is a norm and the shape is bounded","E min{t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d} < infinity, equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity for Y the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - and this condition is necessary, not just sufficient","no curvature, strict convexity or differentiability of B_nu is asserted; those are open"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542575+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af7572591de074922b3c8bcd06ef7d3cfa5df7ed73222e70cd4667e68059f97c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d, d >= 2, with edge-weight law nu. Assume the two conditions (i) E min{ t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d } < infinity, where the t_i are 2d independent copies of tau_e - equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity where Y is the MINIMUM of 2d copies, the two being the same because x -> x^d is increasing on [0, infinity) - and (ii) F(0) < p_c(d). Let B(t) = {x : T(0, x) <= t}, the random ball. Then there is a DETERMINISTIC, convex, COMPACT set B_nu in R^d with NON-EMPTY INTERIOR, symmetric about the axes, such that for every eps > 0, P( (1-eps) B_nu is contained in B(t)/t which is contained in (1+eps) B_nu for all large t ) = 1. The set B_nu is the unit ball of the time constant. Condition (i) is NOT merely convenient: if it fails then for every C > 0 the sum over x of P(m(x) > C|x|) diverges, where m(x) is the minimum weight over the edges at x, and Borel-Cantelli forces T(0,x)/|x| > C for infinitely many x almost surely, so the shape statement itself fails. Condition (ii) is what keeps the shape bounded: if F(0) >= p_c then zero-weight edges percolate, the time constant vanishes and B_nu is all of R^d. What is NOT known, and is repeatedly imported elsewhere as an unproven hypothesis: whether the boundary of B_nu is STRICTLY CONVEX, whether it is DIFFERENTIABLE, and whether it has uniformly positive CURVATURE. Those are open for every non-degenerate weight distribution in every dimension, which is why the Newman-Piza exponent bounds and the directed-geodesic results carry non-constructive curvature or differentiability hypotheses. B_nu is not computed explicitly for any non-trivial F. [Cox and Durrett (1981), verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 2.2]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:17.961629+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af89a048691dd8361ce2f92c09050c6510ecf4c310d0e38a2b1cbb233877a577","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:f-track-jammed of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a positive integer~$j$, a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, a $\lambda\in (0,1)$, and a $j$-tuple $\overline{z}\in (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})^j$.

$b_{[j]}^Y(t) \sim \mathsf{Po}(f_{[j]}^{\overline{0},\overline{z}}(\Delta+t-\tau))$.

determined by

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:25:41.650739+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af8fff39e480795e6a31c2248aaf52044bae01a25458d62f5e953a2508810c48","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:edge_removal of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $\mathbb G=(V,E,F)$ be a topological map embedded in $\Sigma_{g,n}$.
Let $e$ be an internal edge incident to two distinct faces $f_1,f_2$, and
let $\mathbb G'$ be obtained by deleting $e$ and merging these faces into
$f_{12}$. Let $\mathcal R$ forget the variable attached to $e$. Then, for
every bounded measurable test function $\Phi$ on
$\Omega^1(\mathbb G',G)$,
\begin{align*}
 &\int \Phi(\mathcal R(U))\,
 d\mu_{\mathbb G,G,Q,\mathrm{vol},\mathfrak t}(U)\\
 &\quad=
 \int \Phi(U')
 (Q_{|f_1|}*Q_{|f_2|})
 \bigl(\Omega^{U'}(f_{12})\bigr)
 \prod_{f\in F'\setminus\{f_{12}\}}
 Q_{|f|}\bigl(\Omega^{U'}(f)\bigr)
 \prod_i\delta_{[t_i]}({\mathrm{Hol}}_{\partial b_i}(U'))\,dU'.
\end{align*}
In particular, if $(Q_t)_{t>0}$ is a convolution semigroup, then
\[
 \mathcal R_*\mu_{\mathbb G,G,Q,\mathrm{vol},\mathfrak t}
 =\mu_{\mathbb G',G,Q,\mathrm{vol},\mathfrak t}.
\]
If, in addition, $Q_{|f_1|+|f_2|}>0$ almost everywhere, the first identity
may equivalently be written as a Radon--Nikodym formula with quotient
$(Q_{|f_1|}*Q_{|f_2|})/Q_{|f_1|+|f_2|}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:12:46.899843+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_af94f44aa11eaa2420809a9804139a28f9da5176e3fb0ced5dfa6aaa2088071c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem cveracomplet of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let  $(h_p)_{p\in \mathbb{N}}$ be $\mathbb{R}^*_+$-valued and strictly decreasing to $0$.  
We recall from ((dderadef of the paper)) the definition of ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}}$. 
Then, the following holds true. 

\smallskip

\begin{compactenum}
\item[$(i)$] $ {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{{\mathtt{era}}}$ metrizes  the convergence in the sense of mass erasure on $\mathbb{T}^*$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] We recall $\jmath_*$ and $\mathbb{T}^*(1)$ from Definition (masserastardef of the paper). Then, $\jmath_*$ is a homeomorphism from $(\mathbb{T}^*\!,  {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ onto $(\mathbb{T}^*(1), {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$.

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] The metric space $(\mathbb{T}^*\! , {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ is Polish and $\mathbb{T}$ is ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}}$-dense in $\mathbb{T}^*$. Namely, $\mathbb{T}^*\! $ is the ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}}$-completion of $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iv)$] Let us recall from ((massheight of the paper)) that $ \langle {\boldsymbol{\mu}} \rangle $ stands for the total mass. Then ${\boldsymbol{\mu}}\! \in \!  \mathbb{T}^*\! \mapsto \! \langle{\boldsymbol{\mu}}\rangle\! \in \! \mathbb{R}_+$ is ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}}$-continuous. 

\item[$(v)$] Let us recall $\mathtt{Ht} ( {\boldsymbol{\mu}} )$ from 
((massheight of the paper)). Let $\emptyset \! \neq \! \mathscr{C}\! \subseteq\!  \mathbb{T}^*$. Then, $\mathscr{C}$ is precompact in $(\mathbb{T}^*, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ iff 
\begin{equation}

\sup \big\{  \langle {\boldsymbol{\mu}} \rangle  \, ; \, {\boldsymbol{\mu}}\! \in \!  \mathscr{C} \big\} <  \infty \quad \;\,\textrm{and} \quad  \; \,   \sup \big\{ \mathtt{Ht} ({\cal E}_{h_p} {\boldsymbol{\mu}}) \, ; \, {\boldsymbol{\mu}}\! \in \!  \mathscr{C} \big\} <  \infty \quad   \forall p\! \in \! \mathbb{N}. 
\end{equation}
\item[$(vi)$]  Let $(T, d , \rho, \mu) \! \equiv \! {\boldsymbol{\mu}} \! \in \!  \mathbb{T}^*$ and 
$(T_n, d_n , \rho_n, \mu_n) \! \equiv \! {\boldsymbol{\mu}}_n\! \in \!  \mathbb{T}$, $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$ such that ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}}({\boldsymbol{\mu}}_n, {\boldsymbol{\mu}}) \!\! \to \! 0$. 
Then ${\boldsymbol{\mu}}\! \in \!  \mathbb{T}$ (without necessarily implying ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}}({\boldsymbol{\mu}}_n, {\boldsymbol{\mu}})\! \to \! 0$)  iff 
\begin{equation}

\lim_{r\to \infty} \, \limsup_{p\to \infty} \, \sup_{n\in \mathbb{N}} {\cal E}_{h_p} \mu_n \big(T_n \backslash B_{T_n, d_n} (\rho_n, r)\big) = 0.  
\end{equation}
\item[$(vii)$] The sequence $({\boldsymbol{\mu}}_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}}$-convergent iff
the set $\{ {\boldsymbol{\mu}}_n ; n\! \in \! \mathbb{N}\}$ is ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}}$-precompact and 
$({\boldsymbol{\mu}}_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ converges in the sense of mass erasure. In that case, the limits are the same. 
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:04:59.434011+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_afa7a9ab0ad47e1dd2adb6cdd3822de9b096a30633e178dcc501fd1e7b1ec702","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:concentration-mf of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Fix \(q>2\), and assume that the objective function \(f\) satisfies
    (assumption:bounded of the paper). Consider \(J\) independent mean-field processes
    \((\overline X_t^j,\overline V_t^j)\), initialized with i.i.d.\ samples from
    \(\overline\rho_0\in\mathcal P_{2q}(\mathbb R^{2d})\).

    Define
    \[
        \overline Y_t^j
        :=
        \overline X_t^j-m_{\overline X}(\overline\rho_t),
        \qquad
        \widehat{\overline Z}_t^j
        :=
        \bigl(\overline V_t^j-m_{\overline V}(\overline\rho_t)\bigr)
        -
        \frac1\gamma\overline Y_t^j,
    \]
    and let
    \[
        \overline L_2^j(t)
        :=
        \psi_2(\overline Y_t^j,\widehat{\overline Z}_t^j),
        \qquad
        \overline L_2^J(t)
        :=
        \frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J \overline L_2^j(t).
    \]
    Assume the parameter conditions needed for
    (prop:ito-mfl-centered-lyapunov-differential of the paper) at \(p=2\) and \(p=2q\).
    Let \(\kappa\) satisfy
    \[
        0<\kappa<\min\left\{\lambda_{2},\frac{\lambda_{2q}}q\right\},
    \]
    and assume the concentration noise absorption condition
    \begin{equation}
        \sigma^2
        \leqslant
        \frac{m^2 c_1^{(2)}(\lambda_{2}-\kappa)}
        {2\tau(S)(1+C_{\mathrm{lem}})}.
    \end{equation}
    Then, for every threshold \(A>0\) and every \(J\in\mathbb N_+\),
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf P\left[
            \sup_{t\geqslant0}
            \e^{\kappa t}\overline L_2^J(t)
            \geqslant
            \mathbf{E}[\overline L_2^J(0)]+A
        \right]
        \leqslant
        \frac{C_{\mathrm{Bad}}^{\mathrm{MF}}}{A^q}
        J^{-\frac q2}\,
        \overline{\mathcal L}_{2q}(0).
    \end{equation}
    Consequently, by the coercivity bound for \(\psi_2\),
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf P\left[
            \sup_{t\geqslant0}
            \e^{\kappa t}
            \mathfrak M_2(\mu_{\overline X_t^J})
            \geqslant
            \frac{\mathbf{E}[\overline L_2^J(0)]+A}{c_1^{(2)}}
        \right]
        \leqslant
        \frac{C_{\mathrm{Bad}}^{\mathrm{MF}}}{A^q}
        J^{-\frac q2}\,
        \overline{\mathcal L}_{2q}(0).
    \end{equation}
    The constant is
    \[
        C_{\mathrm{Bad}}^{\mathrm{MF}}
        :=
        3^q
        \left(
            \overline C_{\mathrm{MZ}}
            +
            C_{Z,q}
            +
            C_{\mathrm{Mart}}
        \right),
    \]
    where
    \[
        \overline C_{\mathrm{MZ}}
        :=
        \frac{C_{{\rm MZ},q} C_\phi^q 2^{q-1}}{c_{1,2q}},
    \]
    \[
        C_{Z,q}
        :=
        \frac{
            2(2K_{\mathrm{tr}})^q C_{{\rm WM},2q}
        }{
            c_{1,2q}\ell^{q-1}(\lambda_{2q}-q\kappa)
        },
        \qquad
        \ell
        :=
        \frac{\lambda_{2q}-q\kappa}{2(q-1)},
    \]
    and
    \[
        C_{\mathrm{Mart}}
        :=
        \frac{
            2^{q+1}C_{\mathrm{BDG},q}C_{\sigma,q}
        }{
            \lambda_{2q}-q\kappa
        }
        \left(
            \frac{q-2}{\lambda_{2q}-q\kappa}
        \right)^{\frac q2-1}.
    \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.493443+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_afd0784f6a4e2a0f6a2e372f70e10a00decceb3dfaee3c146183861321bd38b7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 12 (Maximum entropy triply augmented hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{thm:gaussian1}
Let \(\bar a,\bar b,\bar c\) be parameters in one of the following two regimes:
\[

or

\qquad
-\bar c^2>\bar a^2+\bar b^2.
\]
Let \(\mathbb A^3\) denote the cone of triply augmented hives, where
\[
\mathbb A^3(\lambda,\mu;\nu)
:=
GT(\lambda)\times GT(\mu)\times GT(\nu)\times H_n(\lambda,\mu;\nu),

for

(g_\lambda,g_\mu,g_\nu,h)

and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:28.471618+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_afdd0c2d9e303e403b497db7533ff16a971bf6033a1148d3fc530fa13ef38e9d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 39 (Labelled decoupling and Wick flattening profile) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $m\ge1$, let $F\subset\cH$ be finite-dimensional, and let
\[
  K\in F_\C^{\otimes m}\otimes\conj{\cC}\otimes\cE
\]
have finite-dimensional support in the input and output legs.  Retain the labelled copies, unitary identifications, and deterministic map
$\Dec_m$ from \eqref{eq:early-labelled-map}, restricted to the finite
stochastic support $F_\C^{\otimes m}$.  Thus
\[
  \operatorname{Dec}_mK\in
  \cH_\C^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes\cH_\C^{(m)}
  \otimes\conj{\cC}\otimes\cE.
\]

Let $W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)}$ be independent real isonormal Gaussian
processes over the labelled real Hilbert spaces, extended complex linearly to
their complexifications.  For $h_\nu\in\cH_\C$ and
$\kappa\in\conj{\cC}\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\cE$, the multilinear rule
\begin{equation*}
  \mathfrak D_m^{W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)}}
  \bigl(J_1h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes J_mh_m\otimes\kappa\bigr)
  :=\left(\prod_{\nu=1}^m W^{(\nu)}(J_\nu h_\nu)\right)
    \Theta_{\cC,\cE}(\kappa)
\end{equation*}
takes values in $L^2(\Omega;\Sch_2(\cC,\cE))$, since Gaussian moments
of every order are finite.  By multilinearity, it induces a linear map
\begin{align*}
  \mathfrak D_m^{W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)}}:
  &\cH_\C^{(1)}\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\cdots
   \otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\cH_\C^{(m)}
   \otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\conj{\cC}
   \otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\cE \\
  &\longrightarrow L^2(\Omega;\Sch_2(\cC,\cE)).
\end{align*}
The \emph{labelled decoupling} of the order-$m$ Wick integral is
\begin{equation}

  I_m^{\mathrm{dec}}(K;W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)})
  :=\mathfrak D_m^{W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)}}\!
    \left(\operatorname{Dec}_m(\operatorname{Sym}_mK)\right).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if $(h_i)_{i=1}^N$ is an orthonormal basis of $F$ and
$\widetilde K_{i_1\cdots i_m}$ are the operator coefficients of
$\widetilde K:=\operatorname{Sym}_mK$, then
\begin{equation}

  I_m^{\mathrm{dec}}(K;W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)})
  =\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_m=1}^N
    \left(\prod_{\nu=1}^m
      W^{(\nu)}(J_\nu h_{i_\nu})\right)
    \widetilde K_{i_1\cdots i_m}.
\end{equation}
The intrinsic definition \eqref{eq:decoupled-wick-chaos-intrinsic} shows
that \eqref{eq:decoupled-wick-chaos-definition} is independent of the chosen
orthonormal basis.  When the labelled processes are fixed, they are omitted
from the notation.

For $2\le r\le\infty$, define the \emph{decoupled Wick flattening profile}
by
\begin{equation*}
  \Prof^{\mathrm{dec}}_{m,r}(K)
  :=\Prof_{m,r}\bigl(
       \operatorname{Dec}_m(\operatorname{Sym}_mK)
     \bigr).
\end{equation*}
Here $\operatorname{Sym}_m$ acts only on the stochastic tensor positions;
the definition first symmetrizes the same-field kernel and then applies the
labelled decoupling map.  Unitary invariance of the oriented flattenings
implies that the profile is independent of the labelled copies and the maps
$J_\nu$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:47:07.710066+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b010088109cfd11cd9a0be5e85d7659171731bef9aa6731da0955e8f46b4cea6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 17 (Positive-jump clock and tail) of arXiv:2608.06299, '2608.06299'] Define $I_n=0$ on $\{J_n^{(r)}=0\}$.  On the event
$\{J_n^{(r)}=1\}$, there is a unique random index
$I_n\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ such that
\[
        \Delta_n^{(r)}=\tau_{n,I_n}.
\]
For $1\le j\le r$, the following global conditional
identity holds almost surely:
\begin{equation}
 \Prob(I_n=j\mid\mathcal F_{T_n+1})
 =
 \one_{\{J_n^{(r)}=1\}}\,
 q^{j-r}\prod_{a=1}^{j-1}(1-q^{a-r}),
 \qquad 1\le j\le r,
 
\end{equation}
where an empty product equals one.  Equivalently, after
restricting to $\{J_n^{(r)}=1\}$, these are the conditional
probabilities of the $r$ possible kernel-growth epochs.  Also,
\[
 \Prob(I_n=0\mid\mathcal F_{T_n+1})
 =
 \one_{\{J_n^{(r)}=0\}}.
\]
 Moreover,
\begin{equation}
        \Delta_n^{(r)}\le \mathcal S_n^{(r)}+r
        \qquad\text{on }\{J_n^{(r)}=1\},
 
\end{equation}
and for every integer $h\ge r+1$,
\begin{equation}
 \Prob\bigl(\Delta_n^{(r)}\ge h\mid J_n^{(r)}=1\bigr)
 \le
 \frac{q^{r+1-h}}{q-1}.
 
\end{equation}
The estimate is uniform in $n$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:33:17.750344+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b02c235c0d4f92ee4ca8f7ad8730f3023e1905dc78abdaf30cdce3a5217eba74","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 122 (Third-chaos kernel reduction) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $q_{a,\Lambda}^{(3)}$ be the covariance spectral density of

  \int_{\R^3}
  |\chi^{\mathrm{res}}(m,\xi-m)|^2
  q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}^{[\epsilon_{\mathrm P}]}(t,m)
  p_{a,\Lambda}(t,\xi-m)\dd m.
\end{equation}

\eqref{eq:cubic-flagged-first-picard-density}; by uniform boundedness of the

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:53:53.199577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b02fd5d34763cd070fdcc8423370ba67d5c5e32dc81514e3e73bc040065eb529","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 12 of arXiv:2606.11774, 'Martingale Solutions to a Stochastic Keller-Segel System with nonlocal Source and Super-li'] [Compactness criterion] 
    Let $\mathbb{H}$ be a real separable Hilbert space, $\mathbb{U}$ be a real reflexive Banach space such that the embedding  $\mathbb{U}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{H}$ is continuous and dense. Let  $\mathbb{U}'$ be the  dual space of $\mathbb{U}$   such that  the embedding $\mathbb{U}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{H}\cong \mathbb{H}'\hookrightarrow\mathbb{U}'$  are continuous.
         Let $E,\mathbb{V}$ be real reflexive  Banach spaces  such that the embedding $\mathbb{V}\hookrightarrow  E\hookrightarrow\mathbb{U}'$ are continuous and the embedding $\mathbb{V}\hookrightarrow E$ is compact.
          Let \begin{align}
    \mathcal{Z}
:= C([0,T];\mathbb U') \cap L^{q}_{w}(0,T;\mathbb{V}) \cap L^{p}(0,T;E) \cap C([0,T];\mathbb{H}_{w}),\,1<q\leq p<\infty,
\end{align} with the topology $\mathcal{T}$ induced by the supremum of  corresponding topologies. The definition of these functional spaces and the corresponding topologies can be found in \cite[Section 2.1]{law2014existence}. Then a set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathcal{Z}$ is $\mathcal{T}$-relatively compact if the following
four conditions hold
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(a)] 
$\sup_{v\in \mathcal{K}}\sup_{s\in[0,T]}\|v(s)\|_{\mathbb{H}}<\infty,$
\item[(b)]
$\sup_{v\in \mathcal{K}}\int_{0}^{T}\|v(s)\|_{\mathbb{V}}^{q}ds<\infty,
\quad \text{i.e. } \mathcal{K} \text{ is bounded in } L^{q}(0,T;\mathbb{V}),$
\item[(c)]
$\sup_{v\in \mathcal{K}}\int_{0}^{T}\|v(s)\|_{E}^{r}ds<\infty,
\quad \text{i.e. } \mathcal{K} \text{ is bounded in } L^{r}(0,T;E)$, where $r>p$,
\item[(d)]
$\lim_{\delta\to 0}\sup_{v\in \mathcal{K}}\sup_{\substack{s,t\in[0,T]\\ |t-s|\le \delta}}
\|v(t)-v(s)\|_{\mathbb U'}=0$.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

Then for every $n\ge0$ the atomic part of $\mu^{*n}$ equals the $n$-fold convolution of the atomic part of $\mu$, i.e.
\[
\bigl(\mu^{*n}\bigr)_{\mathrm{at}} = \mu_{\mathrm{at}}^{*n}.
\]

\[

\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:28:08.692330+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b0372ac4044c028a15ca05fb230e393671d8d87517dc7fcff69b8b33c5cb9bb5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] Let $Y=(A,X)\in C^{1-var}([s,t],\mathbb{R}^d)$ as above. For any
$w\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$ with
\[
    \decomp{\mathcal{A}^{\prime}}(w)
    =
    \left(
        (w_0,\ldots,w_k),
        \blue{i_1}\cdots\blue{i_k}
    \right),
    \qquad
    \alpha_j:=[w_j],
    \quad
    j=0,\ldots,k,
\]
it holds that
\begin{equation}
    \big\langle [w],\Sigsym{Y}\big\rangle_\Psi
    =
    \frac{1}{\alpha_k!}X_{s,t}^{\alpha_k}
    \int_{\Delta^{k}_{s,t}}
    \prod_{j=1}^{k}
    \frac{1}{\alpha_{j-1}!}X_{s,t_j}^{\alpha_{j-1}}
    \dd A^{\blue{i_j}}_{t_j}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, for all $w,v\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$,
\begin{equation}
    \big\langle [w],\Sigsym{Y}\big\rangle_\Psi
    \big\langle [v],\Sigsym{Y}\big\rangle_\Psi
    =
    \big\langle
        [w]\gammashufflesym[v],
        \Sigsym{Y}
    \big\rangle_\Psi,
\end{equation}
where $\gammashufflesym$ is the bilinear product recursively determined, for
$w,v\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$, terminal block classes
$\alpha=[r]$ and $\beta=[q]$ with
$r,q\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}$, and
$\blue{i},\blue{j}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime}$, by
\begin{equation}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
\alpha\gammashufflesym\beta
&:=
\frac{(\alpha+\beta)!}{\alpha!\beta!}
(\alpha+\beta)\Big.,
\\
\bigl([w]\blue{i}\alpha\bigr)\gammashufflesym\beta
&:=
[w]\blue{i}
\bigl(
    \alpha\gammashufflesym\beta
\bigr)\Big.,
\\
\alpha\gammashufflesym\bigl([v]\blue{j}\beta\bigr)
&:=
[v]\blue{j}
\bigl(
    \alpha\gammashufflesym\beta
\bigr)\Big.,
\\
\bigl([w]\blue{i}\alpha\bigr)
\gammashufflesym
\bigl([v]\blue{j}\beta\bigr)
&:=
\bigl(
    [w\blue{i}]\gammashufflesym[v]
\bigr)
\blue{j}
\bigl(
    \alpha\gammashufflesym\beta
\bigr)
+
\bigl(
    [w]\gammashufflesym[v\blue{j}]
\bigr)
\blue{i}
\bigl(
    \alpha\gammashufflesym\beta
\bigr)\Big..
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
Suppose now $\widetilde{A} \in C^{1-var}([s,t],\R^m)$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:mambo} with respect to some fixed sequence $\mathbf{w}=(w_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$, and recall its fibre $[\widetilde{A}]_\mathbf{w}$ introduced in \eqref{eq:fibre}. Then the map
\begin{equation*}
    \Psi \circ \wh{\mathrm{Sig}}:
    \left\{
        Y=(A,X)\in C^{1-var}([s,t],\mathbb{R}^d)
        \;\vert\; Y_s = Y_0,\, A \in [\widetilde{A}]_\mathbf{w}
    \right\}
    \,\to\,
    T_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}((\mathbb{R}^d))
\end{equation*}
is injective for some fixed initial condition $X_0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is 1-periodic and integrable over a period","(a): f continuous on the circle","(b): f in L^p(T), 1 <= p < infinity","(c): the one-sided limits of f at x exist"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.262893+00:00","domain":"Fourier series on the circle","id":"claim_b05e3ebe3555a6664d585a7a2ff4aefc00760033fa1c48d72006a9a275f40562","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$ and $\\sigma_Nf=\\frac1{N+1}\\sum_{k=0}^NS_kf=f*F_N$ its Fejer (Cesaro) means. (a) If $f$ is continuous on $\\mathbb T$, then $\\sigma_Nf\\to f$ uniformly on $\\mathbb T$. (b) If $f\\in L^p(\\mathbb T)$, $1\\le p<\\infty$, then $\\|\\sigma_Nf-f\\|_p\\to0$; always $\\|\\sigma_Nf\\|_p\\le\\|f\\|_p$ for $1\\le p\\le\\infty$. (c) If the one-sided limits $f(x^\\pm)$ exist at $x$, then $\\sigma_Nf(x)\\to\\frac12(f(x^+)+f(x^-))$. (d) (Fejer-Lebesgue) $\\sigma_Nf(x)\\to f(x)$ at every Lebesgue point of $f$, hence almost everywhere. Consequences: trigonometric polynomials are dense in $C(\\mathbb T)$ (Weierstrass) and in $L^p(\\mathbb T)$ for $1\\le p<\\infty$; and if the Fourier series of $f$ converges at $x$ (in the symmetric sense) then its sum is the Fejer limit, e.g. it equals $f(x)$ at a continuity point. The contrast with the partial sums $S_Nf$, which can diverge for continuous $f$, is entirely due to $F_N\\ge0$ versus $\\|D_N\\|_1\\to\\infty$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.224926+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b06524cd24f0d85a65d8e6938d6ac789ab39d779547b9874a54a4f8f8ad7dfb8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Period realisation of the finite Gaussian certificate) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(P=P_m+\cdots+P_0\in\cP_{d,m}\), \(m\geq3\), satisfy
\eqref{eq:intro-principal-isolation}, and put
\(\mu=(m-1)^d\).  Fix \(r\geq1\) and
\(\Sigma\in\Sym_r^{++}(\R)\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(I\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}\) is the set of nonzero replica couplings,
then the corresponding twisted polynomial de Rham complex has cohomology
only in top degree, of rank \(\mu^{|I|}\).  Integrating the inactive Gaussian
variables gives compatible finite reduction maps for all inclusions of
supports.  Thus the zero-coupling boundary is a rank-changing family over
the coupling faces, not a vector bundle of constant rank.

\item The balance between the quadratic Gaussian term and \(P_m\) forces,
up to a common reparametrisation,
\[
  \tau_a=\rho^{m-2}\lambda_a,\qquad x_a=\rho^{-1}u_a.
\]
On every fixed support this scaling produces a free radial Rees--Jacobi
lattice of rank \(\mu^{|I|}\).  Writing \(G\) for the leading rescaled
phase, if \(G\) is Morse and
\[
  \operatorname{Crit}(G)\cap G^{-1}(0)=\{0\},
\]
then the critical point \(u=0\) determines a canonical rank-one formal
branch.  Coincidences among nonzero critical values are allowed.  Its
normalised horizontal period is
\(\widehat\Phi^{\mathrm G}_{P,r,\Sigma}\) from
\eqref{eq:intro-central-Wick-section}.

\item On a simply connected tame Morse chamber with pairwise distinct
critical values, choose a Jacobi basis, a
basis of descending thimbles, and any finite family of continued
rapid-decay contours.  Their period matrix factors as
\begin{equation}
  \Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}
  =
  C_{\mathrm{Betti}}\,
  \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}\,
  B_{\mathrm{Jac}}.
  
\end{equation}
Here \(B_{\mathrm{Jac}}\) is a rational-algebraic change from Jacobi normal
forms to de Rham classes, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}\) is the
holomorphic-sectorial thimble-period matrix, and \(C_{\mathrm{Betti}}\) is
the integral, locally constant matrix expressing the chosen contours in the
thimble basis.  The first two square factors are invertible, so every loss
of rank comes from the chosen contour family.

\item If the chamber is obtained from the positive real Gaussian contour
while the local class of the saddle at \(u=0\) is kept fixed, first form the
complete product in \eqref{eq:intro-period-factorisation} and then project it
to the formal branch from part~\textup{(ii)}.  The result is
\(\widehat\Phi^{\mathrm G}_{P,r,\Sigma}\).  Consequently
\eqref{eq:intro-normal-symbol-identity} extracts from that branch exactly the
coordinate \(M_{P,r}(\Sigma)\) of \(\mathbf J_{d,m}(P)\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["N>=5,d=2,K=3,r=2,ell=0,n=6; two A/S pairs and remaining known S contexts","Actual iid factual samples without tags; p uniform on contexts then true candidates; all A truth supports allowed","Each data-dependent generator robustly exact-level source-calibrated at zero in every compatible world","Conditional V(D) maximizes after data; global Gamma_N maximizes over a fixed world before data"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T21:04:18.141881+00:00","domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; global minimax and actual iid data","id":"claim_b06700a866ade064c72020029c1c0095e0197f769e2a689f4972776a20807bd5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. # A genuine zero-budget global averaging obstruction from repeated facts

T379-C020 v2, proof (unaudited), exact all-world checks PASS; audit pending.
Target 1, secondary target 2: auxiliary-route obstruction, not an exact
global frontier. This concerns actual iid training, not only an
artificial conditional posterior or a handpicked world.

## Experiment and objectives

Fix any N>=5. Set d=2,K=3,r=2,ell=0,n=6. There are two A/S pairs,
one A and one S each, and N-4 fixed S contexts. A has an arbitrary
uniform two-element truth support; S has all three truths. Source p
chooses contexts uniformly and then truths uniformly. Observe six
iid factual samples WITHOUT orientation labels or verifier information.
Require every data-dependent generator to have source Mis_infinity=0
in EVERY world compatible with its observed facts, at exact score bins.

For data D let V(D) be the conditional minimum over robustly calibrated
generators of their maximum compatible-world false mass. Let

 B_N=E_w[V(D)],
 Gamma_N=inf_policy max_fixed_world w E_w[H(policy(D))].

B_N is independent of the fixed actual world w: sibling permutations
and within-context candidate permutations map any world to any other,
preserve the model and compatibility, and carry source calibration,
false mass and V(D) with them. The data laws are carried along by the
same bijections. Thus V(D)'s distribution is identical in all worlds.

The candidate strict inequality is

 Gamma_N <= B_N-5/(1008*N^7) < B_N.                      (1)

No numerical value of B_N or Gamma_N is claimed. The point is that
expected conditional worst-world risk overstates global expected
minimax risk even at ZERO source calibration budget.

## Finite conditional selectors exist

There are finitely many actual worlds and finitely many score
partitions of the NK atoms. For a zero-calibrated g its score partition
Pi satisfies g=p_w,Pi for every compatible w, so a fixed Pi admits at
most one such g. Merging equal-score cells preserves this property.
The one-cell uniform generator is always feasible, so each V(D) is
attained among finitely many candidates. Choose any deterministic
conditional minimizer g*_D by a fixed tie rule. This selector is an
existence construction, not a claim of computational efficiency.
For every actual w it satisfies H_w(g*_D)<=V(D) pointwise.
Datasets incompatible with every source world may use the uniform
fallback; they have probability zero under every actual world.

## Observable rare event and its conditional value

Let E be the event that all six samples have this pattern:

* Four copies of ONE candidate in ONE context of one pair;
* one fact in each of the two contexts of the other pair;
* no other observations.

The pair roles, repeated context, candidate identities and sample
order are unrestricted. E is recognizable from the data alone.
Its known-truth counts are (1,0) in the repeated pair and (1,1) in
the other pair, all strictly below r=2. Thus C017's exact zero-budget
frontier, with pairwise minima 0 and 1, gives

 V(D)=1/(3N)+7/(24N)=5/(8N) on E.                        (2)

For clarity, the (1,0) pair's zero-calibrated bins must contain whole
contexts: support swaps make each uncertified set constant-score and
orientation invariance with the zero-known sibling leaves no known
truths available to peel from that context. Forgetting the repeated
fact therefore preserves all source-bin and false-count information.
The resulting balanced (0,0)/(1,1) game has artificial mean densities
1/(3N),7/(24N) on its residual groups, with false risks 1/6,1/4;
safe densities are higher. The per-bin low-density tail argument
gives the lower value (2), and the invariant-group mean attains it
worldwise. This is a conditional worst-world assertion, not an
actual-orientation posterior calculation.

## A causal calibrated generator on E

Let x be the observed four-repeat context. Let a,b be the two contexts
of the other pair and let their single observed candidates be c_a,c_b.
Form B from ALL THREE atoms of x plus the four atoms of a,b other
than c_a,c_b. Its source mass is 1/N+7/(6N)=13/(6N) in every
compatible world; its seven atoms get score q=13/(42N).
Give the two observed atoms in a,b score 5/(12N). Give every other
atom score lambda=1/(3N), including the untouched sibling of x and
all fixed S contexts. The group masses sum to one. All source group
masses are invariant across orientations and supports, so exact-score
mergers preserve source Mis_infinity=0. The rule uses observed context
counts and observed truths only; it never reads the hidden orientation.

If x is actually A, false mass is H_A=2q=13/(21N).
If x is actually S, false mass is H_S=q+lambda=9/(14N).
These identities hold for every compatible truth-support choice.

## Fixed-world event probabilities, not a posterior shortcut

In ANY fixed actual world, summing over the repeated candidate
identity gives repeated-four-fact weights proportional to

 r*(1/(Nr))^4=1/(N^4*r^3) for the A context,
 K*(1/(NK))^4=1/(N^4*K^3) for the S context.

Consequently, conditional on E, the repeated context is actually A
with probability K^3/(K^3+r^3)=27/35, uniformly in every fixed world.
The exponent is THREE, not four: the number of available true
candidate identities must be included. The other pair's one sample
per context contributes 1/N^2 after its identities are summed out.

There are two choices of repeated pair and 6!/(4!1!1!)=30 orders.
Thus in every fixed world

 P_w(E)=60/N^6*(1/8+1/27)=175/(18N^6),                  (3)
 E_w[H_pool|E]=(27/35)*13/(21N)+(8/35)*9/(14N)
             =153/(245N),
 V(E)-E_w[H_pool|E]=1/(1960N).                           (4)

These are ordinary disjoint-event sums under the fixed sampling law;
no independence of learned events or hidden labels is assumed.

## Global policy and strict separation

Use the explicit pooling generator on E and g*_D otherwise. Every
outcome is robustly zero-calibrated. For every fixed actual world,

 E_w H <= E_w[1_{not E}V(D)]+P_w(E)*153/(245N)
       =B_N-P_w(E)/(1960N)
       =B_N-5/(1008N^7).

Taking the maximum over w proves (1). At N=5 the exact strict gap
certified by this construction is 1/15750000. This is an upper bound
on Gamma_N relative to B_N, not an exact value for either objective.

The result complements C014's positive-budget example and C015's
single-outcome pointwise control. Here the improvement is realized
under actual iid data, uniformly for EVERY fixed world, at zero
budget. A global expected lower bound must therefore use a valid
fixed-prior/per-world argument rather than average conditional maxima.
Primary statistic: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3 Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9.
Independent mathematical, priority and target-scope audit pending.

Exact verification: logs/zero_budget_global_separation_check.json
checks all 36 fixed worlds and all 108 rare-event histograms for
N=5,6,9, totaling 6480 positive-probability source-calibration checks
and 108 exact event expectation checks. Another 108 checks verify
whole-source-family transitive relabeling. In every fixed world some
event outcomes worsen risk, so the improvement is genuinely in
expectation. A three-repeat fault produces the wrong sign in all
108 world/parameter cases. The general finite-selector and symmetry
proof supplies the global conclusion; neither B_N nor Gamma_N is
estimated numerically.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Finite nonempty data set with labels +/-1","For fixed inputs, predictor locally Lipschitz and admits the stated Clarke chain rule","Positive homogeneity of a common degree L>0","Summed exponential loss and a globally defined locally absolutely continuous Clarke gradient-flow trajectory","Some finite t0 satisfies summed exponential loss <1"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:34:31.697619+00:00","domain":"Lyu Li; homogeneous neural networks; Clarke subdifferential; exponential loss; gradient flow; margin; KKT","id":"claim_b08bdeae2d05aa04e46fe0188ba2587586feb63e778488bd100ee83f9aef6583","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let a finite nonempty binary-labeled data set (x_i,y_i), y_i in {-1,+1}, and a real-valued predictor Phi(theta;x) with theta in R^d be given. For each fixed x, theta -> Phi(theta;x) is locally Lipschitz and admits the chain rule: for every locally absolutely continuous arc z, (Phi(z(t);x))'=<h,z'(t)> for every h in its Clarke subdifferential at z(t), for almost every t. Assume common positive homogeneity degree L>0: Phi(a theta;x)=a^L Phi(theta;x) for every a>0. Put q_i(theta)=y_i Phi(theta;x_i), q_min(theta)=min_i q_i(theta), and E(theta)=sum_i exp(-q_i(theta)), without averaging by sample size. Let theta:[0,infinity)->R^d be a locally absolutely continuous Clarke gradient-flow trajectory satisfying theta'(t) in -partial^C E(theta(t)) almost everywhere. Assume there is a finite t0 with E(theta(t0))<1. For t>=t0 put r(t)=||theta(t)||_2, gamma_bar(theta)=q_min(theta)/||theta||_2^L, and gamma_tilde(theta)=-log E(theta)/||theta||_2^L. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:59:53.361405+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b0a2d98bce1f63e7d800279235190f5a0a228fa89de95d2ed01f22d5153b060c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:onepoint of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $m(q) := \mathbb{E}[W^{q}]$ and $\lambda(q) := \log m(q)$, for
		the canonical step law $W = 2\sin^{2}(\pi U)$. Then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
			\item for $q > -\tfrac12$,
			\begin{equation}
				m(q) = \frac{2^{q}\,\Gamma(q+\tfrac12)}{\sqrt{\pi}\,\Gamma(q+1)},
				\qquad
				\lambda(q) = q\log 2 + \log\Gamma(q+\tfrac12)
				- \log\Gamma(q+1) - \tfrac12\log\pi,
				
			\end{equation}
			and $\mathbb{E}[(S_{n}'(z))^{q}] = m(q)^{n}$ exactly, for every
			fixed $z$;
			\item $\tfrac1n\log S_{n}'(z) \to -\log 2$ almost surely, and
			\begin{equation}
				\frac{\log S_{n}'(z) + n\log 2}{\sqrt{n}}
				\;\xrightarrow{\ d\ }\;
				\mathcal{N}\Big(0,\ \frac{\pi^{2}}{3}\Big),
				\qquad
				\frac{\pi^{2}}{3} = \lambda''(0)
				= \psi_{0}'(\tfrac12) - \psi_{0}'(1),
				
			\end{equation}
			with $\psi_{0}$ the digamma function, and
			$\tfrac1n\log S_{n}'$ satisfies a large deviation principle with
			rate the Legendre transform of $\lambda$;
			\item the tangents of the free energy are the information constants
			of the deterministic theory,
			\begin{equation}
				\lambda'(0) = \mathbb{E}\log W = -\log 2,
				\qquad
				\lambda'(1) = \mathbb{E}[W\log W] = 1 - \log 2,
				
			\end{equation}
			the relative entropies of the identities~(equation eq:kl-identities of the paper),
			while the deterministic sharp Lipschitz constant $2^{n}$ of
			Proposition~(prop:intertwine of the paper) is the almost sure envelope
			$S_{n}' \le 2^{n}$ and the limiting slope
			$\lambda(q) = q\log2 - \tfrac12\log q + O(1)$ as $q \to \infty$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.552249+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b0be67e39a0d300955fb603890c21971ebe679661fbaf4e11e148a94b91923d6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] Let $f:(\S^{d-1})^n\to \reals$ be $C^2$, and let $\tilde f$ be a $C^2$ extension of $f$ to a
neighborhood of $(\S^{d-1})^n$ in $\reals^{d\times n}$.
Then the Riemannian gradient of $f$ on $(\S^{d-1})^n$ is
\begin{equation*}
\grad f(X)=\proj_X \nabla \tilde f(X),
\end{equation*}
where $\nabla \tilde{f}$ denotes the Euclidean gradient in $\reals^{d\times n}$ of $\tilde f$.

For any tangent vector $V\in \mathsf{T}_X(\S^{d-1})^n$, the Riemannian Hessian satisfies
\begin{equation*}
\Hess f(X)[V]
=\proj_X\left(\nabla^2 \tilde f(X)[V] - V\,\Diag\left(\diag(X^{\sT}\nabla \tilde f(X))\right)\right).
\end{equation*}
Equivalently, component-wise,
\[
\left(\Hess f(X)[V]\right)_i
=\proj_{x_i}\left(\nabla^2_{x_i}\tilde f(X)[V]_i - \langle x_i,\nabla_{x_i}\tilde f(X)\rangle\,v_i\right).
\]
If $V$ is a $C^1$ vector field on $(\S^{d-1})^n$ and $f$ is smooth, then the second-order operator
$V^2$ is
\[
(V^2 f)(X)= V(V f)(X)
= \Hess f(X)[V(X),V(X)] + \langle \grad f(X),(\nabla_V V)(X)\rangle,
\]
where $\nabla_V$ is the Levi--Civita connection on $(\S^{d-1})^n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.564753+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b0d820025a435344d72400d36205ec9151e210ba91ef80b393b7f1e31d889b57","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\\CLE_4$ III:\\\\ uniqueness'] This paper is the third and final article in a series of papers constructing the canonical conformally invariant metric on the set of loops of the conformal loop ensemble ($\\CLE$) with critical parameter $\\kappa=4$. The previous two articles construct, as a subsequential limit of the renormalized graph metric on the loops of $\\CLE_\\kappa$ as $\\kappa \\downarrow 4$, a conformally invariant, local metric on the loops of a $\\CLE_4$ whose metric ball growth from the domain boundary coincides with the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. In this paper, we establish that this metric is uniquely characterized by its properties, as are its geodesics, and that it is a measurable function of the $\\CLE_4$. In particular, we show that the renormalized $\\CLE_\\kappa$ graph metric converges as $\\kappa \\downarrow 4$ without passing to a subsequence. A key step in the proof is to show that the metric is determined by the geodesics from each loop to the domain boundary, which are in turn determined by the uniform exploration; this representation will have important applications in future work.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.359320+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b0edc888f35ce6fb70bfecb178fd1d57453850729a8273fd398ddda2678b3e18","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] In Example (ex:basic switching transient of the paper), $\mathcal R_1$ and $\mathcal R_2$ are exponentially ergodic as long as $\varepsilon$ is small enough. For all small enough $\varepsilon$ and small enough $\kappa$ (possibly depending on $\varepsilon$) the mixed process is exponentially ergodic, but for any $\varepsilon$ the mixed process is evanescent for large enough $\kappa$ (again, possibly depending on $\varepsilon$).
\begin{proof}
The respective matrices in individual environments as well as the average environment are given by 
\[
    M_1=\begin{bmatrix}-1&4\varepsilon\\ 4(1-\varepsilon)&-1\end{bmatrix},\quad
    M_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1&4(1-\varepsilon)\\ 4\varepsilon&-1\end{bmatrix},\quad
    M=\begin{bmatrix}-1&2\\ 2&-1\end{bmatrix}
\]
Note that any $2\times 2$ matrix with negative trace and positive determinant must have two eigenvalues with negative real part. In this case $M_1$ and $M_2$ have trace $-2$ and determinant $1-16\varepsilon+16\varepsilon^2$. This determinant is continuous in $\varepsilon$ and is positive at zero, so it is positive for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Thus both eigenvalues of $M_1$, and both of $M_2$, have negative real part for $\varepsilon$ small. It follows from Proposition (prop:dec/inc direction of the paper)(i) that for $\varepsilon$ small there exist vectors $v^1,v^2\in\mathbb R^2_{>0}$ such that $v^iM_i\in\mathbb R^2_{<0}$.

For such $\varepsilon$, then, applying Corollary (cor:one-environment-ergodicity of the paper) tells us that $\mathcal R_1$ and $\mathcal R_2$ converge exponentially fast, and hence by irreducibility are exponentially ergodic. Similarly, applying Theorem (thm:slow-switching-ergodicity of the paper) tells us that the process that switches between $\mathcal R_1$ and $\mathcal R_2$ is exponentially ergodic for any $\varepsilon$ which is small enough in the sense of the previous paragraph, provided $\kappa$ is small enough.

However, the matrix $M$ has an eigenvalue of $1$ with corresponding eigenvector $v=(1,1)$ so Theorem (thm:fast-switching-transience of the paper) tells us that any state $x\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0}$ with $\operatorname{supp}(v)\cap\operatorname{supp}(x)\ne\varnothing$ is evanescent for the switching process. But $v$ is strictly positive so that includes every state except for $x=(0,0)$; the existence of at least one inflow reaction tells us that $(0,0)$ is a evanescent state as well. Thus every state is evanescent for the switching process, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H must be convex and superlinear for the Hopf-Lax (Lax-Oleinik) representation with L = H*","The Hopf formula requires convex initial datum g instead, with H merely continuous","Counterexample: H(p) = (p^2-1)^2, g(x) = x/2, where Hopf-Lax returns the solution for H** and misses the flux by H(1/2) - H**(1/2) = 9/16"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.418414+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: Hamilton-Jacobi equations","id":"claim_b153eb3a5fb04c6f5b11975f8d220003ec053be109078039e18bb58d9896bdc1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: in u(x,t) = min_y ( t L((x-y)/t) + g(y) ) with L = H*, the Hamiltonian H must be CONVEX (and superlinear). For a nonconvex H the formula does not solve u_t + H(Du) = 0: since H* = (H**)*, the formula reproduces the equation with H replaced by its convex envelope H**. Counterexample (n = 1): H(p) = (p^2 - 1)^2 is continuous and superlinear but not convex, and H**(p) = 0 for |p| ≤ 1, H**(p) = H(p) for |p| ≥ 1. Take the Lipschitz datum g(x) = x/2. The true solution is the classical (hence viscosity) solution u(x,t) = x/2 - t H(1/2) = x/2 - (9/16) t. The Hopf-Lax expression gives min_y ( tL((x-y)/t) + y/2 ) = x/2 - t L*(1/2) = x/2 - t H**(1/2) = x/2, which satisfies u_t + H(u_x) = 0 + (1/4 - 1)^2 = 9/16 ≠ 0 at EVERY point — it is not even an almost-everywhere solution. The correct nonconvex counterpart is the Hopf formula u(x,t) = sup_p ( x·p - t H(p) - g*(p) ), valid for continuous H when the DATUM g is convex; for nonconvex H and general Lipschitz g there is no closed formula and one works with viscosity solutions directly. Auditor's check: whenever a proof writes a value function / Hopf-Lax representation, confirm convexity (of H for Hopf-Lax, of g for Hopf) before trusting it; the corresponding control interpretation (L as a running cost) also fails without convexity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:42.303248+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b162c9199bd7f4aff140db2ccfaf697b85dbc8d4301da1e2c5cd8d3f236c2d8d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 37 (SRI chain) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Fix some integers $k,d\ge 1$, and let $I$ as always be an additive locally compact subgroup of $\mathbb R^d$. Consider a Markov kernel $\br(\x,\mathrm d \mathbf y)$ on $I^k$. We say that the $q^{th}$ moments of $\br$ are bounded by $M$ if\begin{align}\sup_{\mathbf x \in I^k} \int_{I^k}|   y_i-   x_i|^q \br(\x,\mathrm d \mathbf y)&\leq M,\text{ for all } 1\le i \le k,

\end{align} Let $F: [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ be a decreasing function. Let $\nu$ be some probability measure on $I$, and let $M>0$.  
A $k\times d$ \textbf{SRI chain with base measure $\nu$ and decay function $F$} is defined as a Markov kernel $\br$ on $I^k$, satisfying 
\begin{align}\| \br(\x,\bullet) - \nu^{\otimes k} (\mathbf x-\bullet)\|_{TV} &\leq F\big(\min_{1\le i<j\le k} |    x_i-   x_j|\big)\;\;\text{ for all } \x\in I^k .
\end{align} Here $\mathbf x = (   x_1,...,   x_k) \in I^k \subset \mathbb R^{kd}$. 
We denote by $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{SRI}}_{k\times d}(q,M,F)$ the set of all SRI chains on $I^k$ whose $q^{th}$ moments are bounded by $M$, and such that \eqref{tvb2} holds with $F$ on the right side, though we allow the base measure $\nu$ to vary between different elements of $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{SRI}}_{k\times d}(q,M,F)$. 

We furthermore say that the SRI chain is \textbf{centered} if $$\int_{I^k} (y_j-x_j) \br (\x,\dr\y) = \int_I    u \;\nu(\dr    u),\;\; \x\in I^k, 1\le j \le k.$$

We will say that an SRI chain is $\delta$-\textbf{repulsive} 
$$\int_{I^k} |   y_i-   y_j-(   x_i-   x_j)| \br(\x ,\dr \y) 
> \delta
\text{ for all $\x\in I^k$ and all $1\le i <j \le k$.}$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.161181+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b16dada1d2b6d35b3428c8fda0e031d4e220ce870a3028c903adf0c090078896","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 10 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\mu,\mu'$ satisfying condition~\eqref{e:def-Lambda},
if we have $\vwww'\ge0$ with $(\mu',\vwww')=1$,
