{"assumptions":["X_1, ..., X_n independent (arbitrary measurable state spaces, not necessarily identically distributed)","E[Z^2] < infinity","X_i' an independent copy of X_i"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627864+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b4f8bc22f460f25f8d49dffc484368ee58c01fdabcf876f2f9b6345b6ceebd5f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_n be INDEPENDENT random variables taking values in arbitrary measurable spaces - they need NOT be identically distributed and need not be real-valued - and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) with E[Z^2] < infinity. Let X_i' be an independent copy of X_i, independent of everything else, and put Z^{(i)} = f(X_1, ..., X_{i-1}, X_i', X_{i+1}, ..., X_n). Then Var(Z) <= (1/2) sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z^{(i)})^2 ] = sum_{i=1}^n E[ ((Z - Z^{(i)})_+)^2 ]. Equivalently, and often more convenient, Var(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z_i)^2 ] for ANY random variables Z_i that are measurable functions of the n-1 variables other than X_i; taking Z_i = inf over the i-th coordinate of f gives the version used for suprema and for first-passage times. Equality holds if and only if f is a sum of functions of the individual coordinates. Independence is the only structural hypothesis and it is essential; the inequality is FALSE for dependent coordinates. Applied with a bounded-difference function it recovers the variance half of McDiarmid's inequality; applied to first-passage percolation with the geodesic length as the influence bound it produces the linear variance upper bound. [Efron and Stein (1981), Steele (1986); see Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 3.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:25:12.192792+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b505e5456e8a7393f18042acbb06bd12c1b43e2a4972d1cda711c73d94333805","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 4 (Characterization of limits of global empirical measures) of arXiv:2510.22533, 'Marginal dynamics of probabilistic cellular automata on trees'] Let any of the following three cases hold for $\{G_n\}_{n \in \N}$:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item Let $\kappa \ge 2$ be an integer. For each $n \ge \kappa+1$ with $n\kappa$ even, there exists at least one $\kappa$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, and we let $G_n$ be chosen uniformly at random.
    \item Let $\lambda > 0$, and let $G_n$ be the \Erdos graph $G(n,\lambda/n)$, on the vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
    \item Let $G_n$ be drawn from the configuration model with vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and with degree distribution converging weakly to $\rho_{\myroot}$.
    Assume $\rho_{\myroot}$ has finite first and second moments, that is, $\sum_{k=0}^\infty k^2 \rho_{\myroot}(k) < \infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Suppose the initial states $\{X^{G_n}_v(0) : v \in G_n, n \in \N\}$ are i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
Let $\Xbar$ and $G$ be given as follows, for each case above:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item Let $\Xbar$ be as in Construction \ref{constr:regulartree_local}, with $(\Xbar_v(0))_{v=0}^{\kappa}$ i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
    \item Let $\Xbar$ be as in Construction \ref{constr:UGWlocal}, with $\rho_{\myroot}=\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$ and with $(\Xbar_v(0))_{v\in\V_1}$ i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
    \item Let $\Xbar$ be as in Construction \ref{constr:UGWlocal}, with $(\Xbar_v(0))_{v\in\V_1}$ i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the $\PolishX^\infty$-valued random trajectory 
$X^{G_n}_{\myroot_n}$ converges in law  to $\Xbar_{\myroot}$ (or $\Xbar_0$ in case (i)). Moreover, 
the $\P(\PolishX^\infty)$-valued random measure  
$\mu^{G_n}$ converges in law  to $\Lmc(\Xbar_{\myroot})$ (or  $\Lmc(\Xbar_0)$ in case (i)).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:41:03.279998+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5270d97f5f0c45c05f3b6c6478d2e8fe9b1213de39a862a1355f6efe06e5b70","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop integrable-mtg of arXiv:2411.08725, 'Berry-Esseen bounds for large-time asymptotics of one-dimensional diffusion processes via '] Let $a>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm (i)}] 
Let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative Borel function on ${\mathbb R}$ such that 
$\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx<\infty$, and let $M=\sup_{x\in {\mathbb R}}f(x)$. 
Then for any $c<\frac{\sigma_1^2 a^2}{2M}$,
\[
E\left[\exp\left(c\int_0^{\infty}f(x+M_t^x+a\langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right)\right]<\infty, 
\quad x\in {\mathbb R}.
\]
Moreover, if $f$ is nonincreasing, then for any $x_0\in {\mathbb R}$,
\[
\sup_{x\in [x_0,\infty)}E\left[\exp\left(c\int_0^{\infty}f(x+M_t^x+a \langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right)\right]<\infty.
\]
\item[{\rm (ii)}] 
Let $f$ be a bounded Borel function on ${\mathbb R}$ such that $\int_0^{\infty}|f(x)|dx<\infty$. 
Then for any $p\in [0,\infty)$, 
\[
\sup_{t\ge 0}E\left[\left|\int_0^t f(x+M_t^x+a \langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right|^p\right]<\infty, \quad x\in {\mathbb R}.
\]
Moreover, if $f$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing, then for any $x_0\in {\mathbb R}$,
\[
\sup_{x\in [x_0,\infty)}E\left[\left(\int_0^{\infty} f(x+M_t^x+a \langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right)^p\right]<\infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.752117+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b52723f762b29cc48575874d83993ce20106d15295acf242a741b9cadc88d558","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 31 ({\cite[Lemma A.1) of arXiv:2607.08696, 'Spectrum of Directed Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {Coste}}] 
Let $\xx$ and $\yy$ be two vectors of $\R^n$ and $\deterministic =\xx\yy^t$. Let $H_n$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The eigenvalues of the matrix $\deterministic + H_n$ are contained in  
$\mathcal{B}(0, \eps_n) \cup \mathcal{B}(\yy^t\xx, \eps_n)$, where
$$\eps_n = 2\|\xx\|^2\|\yy\|^2(\yy^t\xx)^{-2}\|H_n \|;$$
\item[(ii)] If 
$\mathcal{B}(0, \eps_n) \cap \mathcal{B}(\yy^t\xx, \eps_n) = \emptyset$, then there is exactly one eigenvalue of $\deterministic + H_n$ inside 
$\mathcal{B}(\yy^t\xx, \eps_n)$ and all the other eigenvalues of $\deterministic + H_n$ are contained in $\mathcal{B}(0, \eps_n)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

  \mathbb P\bigl(r_h(A)=1\mid A\text{ is not }B_h\bigr)
   &=1-O_{h,k}(q^{-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
By contrast, if $k\geq4$ is fixed and $N_{h,k}$ is uniform in the finite set
$\mathcal R(h,k)$, then, as $h\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\bigl(r_{h,k}(N_{h,k})\leq1\bigr)
 =\frac{h}{|\mathcal R(h,k)|}
 =h^{-(k-2)+o_k(1)}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Thus principal labels are asymptotically negligible among attainable
cardinalities, although their realizations account for asymptotically almost
every fixed-order configuration in a growing interval.
Here $h$ is fixed before $q\to\infty$;
no joint $(h,q)$ assertion is made.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:18:54.368344+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b55041acf7ac818829dcc62a0c2d128b6a81bc82746cba91e931f44eceb6f4e4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The chi laws in small dimensions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item At $n=1$ the chi law and its moments are as follows:
$$\chi_{1t}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{t\pi}}\,e^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
M_k=\sqrt{\frac{(2t)^k}{\pi}}\,\Gamma\left(\frac{k+1}{2}\right)$$

\item At $n=2$ the chi law and its moments are as follows:
$$\chi_{2t}=\frac{1}{t}\,xe^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
M_k=\sqrt{(2t)^k}\,\Gamma\left(\frac{k}{2}+1\right)$$

\item At $n=3$ the chi law and its moments are as follows:
$$\chi_{3t}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{t^3\pi}}\,x^2e^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
M_k=2\sqrt{\frac{(2t)^k}{\pi}}\,\Gamma\left(\frac{k+3}{2}\right)$$
\end{enumerate}
The law $\chi_{2t}$ is called Rayleigh law, and the law $\chi_{3t}$ is called Maxwell-Boltzmann law.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.168232+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b560f24f9efbd19fbd80834b8329708d1146fc4b0f30eabb95a253d6b655ce86","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:finite-information of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] Let $A$ take values in a finite set $\mathcal A$, let $B,D$ be
countable-valued, and let $C$ take values in a standard Borel space.  Fix
one regular conditional law $p_{A,B,D\mid c}$ of the joint triple
$(A,B,D)$ given $C=c$.  Every conditional marginal and every further
conditional law below is understood to be derived from this joint kernel.
Then
\begin{align}
 0\leq I(A;B\mid C)
 &=H(A\mid C)-H(A\mid B,C)\notag\\
 &\leq H(A\mid C)\leq H(A)\leq\log|\mathcal A|,
 \\
 I(A;B,D\mid C)
 &=I(A;B\mid C)+I(A;D\mid B,C).
 
\end{align}
In particular, $I(A;B)\leq I(A;B,D)$.  Conditional mutual information is
symmetric in its first two arguments.  Consequently, if $B$ is also finite,
then $I(A;B\mid C)\leq H(B\mid C)$.  If $X$ is countable-valued with
$H(X)<\infty$, then $H(A,X)<\infty$ and
\begin{align}
 H(A,X)&=H(X)+H(A\mid X)\leq H(X)+H(A),
 \\
 I(A;X)&=H(A)+H(X)-H(A,X).
 
\end{align}
In particular, independence gives $H(A,X)=H(A)+H(X)$.  If $Y$ is a
deterministic function of a discrete $X$ with $H(X)<\infty$, then
$H(Y)\leq H(X)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:17.749655+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5678995b526e5e8c56487adbda83db4af5b6a5762db06296388e33dbc69c8c4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2511.01456, 'Zero distribution of multiplicative Hermite and Laguerre polynomials'] Let $(b_n)_{n\in \N} \subseteq \C$ and $(c_n)_{n\in \N} \subseteq \N_0$ be sequences such that
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{b_n}{n} = \beta\in\C, \qquad \beta \neq -1,
\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{c_n}{n} = \gamma \geq 0.
$$
The dependence on the parameters $b_n$ and $\beta$ will be suppressed in the notation.  Recall that $\sigma_{k;n}(c_n)$ is the $k$-th moment of the zero distribution of $L_n^*(x; b_n, c_n)$. Then, for all $k\in \N_0$,
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} \sigma_{k;n}(c_n) = f_k(\gamma) := \eee^{- \frac{\gamma k}{1+\beta}} g_k(\gamma),
$$
where the functions $g_k(\gamma)$, $k\in \N_0$, are the same as in Proposition~\ref{prop:conv_to_ODE_laguerre}, and the functions $f_k(\gamma)$, $k\in \N_0$, satisfy the following  system of ODE's:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&f_k'(\gamma)
=
-\frac 1 {1+\beta}  \sum_{j=1}^{k} j  f_j(\gamma)
\widehat{B}_{ k-j} \left(f_1(\gamma),\ldots, f_{k-j}(\gamma); - \frac 1 {1+\beta}\right),
\quad k\in \N,\ \gamma\geq 0,
\\
&f_{0}(\gamma) =  1 \quad (\text{for all } \gamma\geq 0), \qquad f_{k}(0) = 1 \quad (\text{for all } k\in  \mathbb N).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:04:59.428658+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b56fdc10aa73df40b6aa6c0ad331dc029ab643f3264dc005cb857f6a717f5f6f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem pre:gamblersRuin of arXiv:2605.19835, 'Reemergence of the Epidemic Threshold in SIRS Infections on Connected Stars'] {feller1957introduction}}]
    In the gambler's ruin game, a player starts with some amount of money $P_0 \in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}_{\geq 1}$ and then repeatedly throws a coin that shows head with probability $p \in (0,1)$, independent of all other outcomes. If it shows heads, the player's money increases by~$1$, otherwise, it decreases by~$1$. The game ends at time~$T$ when the player either reaches the lower bound $\ell \in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}_{< P_0}$ or the upper bound $u \in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}_{> P_0}$ of money.
    Let $(P_t)_{t \in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}}$ be the amount of money that a player has in a gambler's ruin game that has a probability of $p \in (0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}$ for them to win in each step. Let $q=1-p$.  Then
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\Pr{P_T = \ell} = \frac{1-(p/q)^{u-P_0}}{1-(p/q)^{u-\ell}}$ and
        \item $\Pr{P_T = u} = \frac{1-(q/p)^{P_0-l}}{1-(q/p)^{u-\ell}}$.\qedhere
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:55:56.998830+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b573d67f48c3cebd9a9cb6e93671f410feec30901cc4d96af35bc048ed841506","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Every $\varphi\in\Aut(X_\Delta)$ permutes the irreducible components

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:30:07.958621+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b57c5dd393822be9e606e959b6e1c923cb5df57ca8970b5cb05bc69431331e47","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Recursive Terminal Attachment of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let \(s\) be a square vertex. A recursive terminal attachment at \(s\) is
generated by the following rules.

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Base case: \(h_2\)-attachment.}
    The attachment may be a single \(h_2\)-edge from \(s\) to a circle vertex
    \(a\):
    \[
        s \xleftrightarrow{h_2} a .
    \]

    \item \textbf{Concatenated-path attachment.}
    For any \(t > 1\), let \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_t\) be backbone-dangling
    shapes with compatible circle boundaries, and let    \[
        \tau =\tau_t \circ \tau_{t-1}\circ \cdots \circ \tau_1
    \]
    denote their proper concatenation. $\tau$ is then attached by adding two $h_1$ edges connecting $s$ to $U_\tau$ and $V_\tau$ (assuming $U_\tau\neq V_\tau$).

\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:48:24.616337+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b57ca29244e2560fc9a24ce40b6dd52eb874de9beffd737c1767397a77494009","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:Ttransform-2coord of arXiv:2601.04079, 'TV homogenization inequalities'] Fix $a,b\in[0,1]$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$, and define
\[
a' := \lambda a + (1-\lambda)b,
\qquad
b' := \lambda b + (1-\lambda)a.
\]
Let
\[
\eta := 
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{\lambda(1-\lambda)(a-b)^2}{2(1-ab)}, & ab<1,\\
[1ex]
0, & ab=1,
\end{cases}
\]
and consider the row--stochastic $4\times4$ matrix (indexed by $00,01,10,11$)
\begin{equation}

M_{\lambda}(a,b):=
\left(\begin{array}{cccc}
1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
\eta & \lambda-\eta & (1-\lambda)-\eta & \eta \\
\eta & (1-\lambda)-\eta & \lambda-\eta & \eta \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 1 
\end{array}\right).
\end{equation}
Then all entries of $M_{\lambda}(a,b)$ are nonnegative, and for both $s\in\{+,-\}$,
\[
\Bigl(\Ber\!\left(\tfrac12+s\,\tfrac a2\right)\otimes \Ber\!\left(\tfrac12+s\,\tfrac b2\right)\Bigr)\,M_{\lambda}(a,b)
=
\Ber\!\left(\tfrac12+s\,\tfrac {a'}2\right)\otimes \Ber\!\left(\tfrac12+s\,\tfrac {b'}2\right).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:26:52.673800+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b586c936717730e5a59ad7f47cb6c8974d61395c55c5c31d515e7bc5df892843","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] For every $v, \widetilde{v}, \widehat{v}\in V$, the trilinear form $b$ is continuous on $V\times V\times V$, and there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
 \begin{align}
&|b(v,\widetilde{v}, \widehat{v})|\leq C\left(|v|^{\frac{1}{2}}\|v\|^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\widetilde{v}\||\widehat{v}|^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\widehat{v}\|^{\frac{1}{2}}+|\partial_xv||\partial_z \widetilde{v}||\widehat{v}|^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\widehat{v}\|^{\frac{1}{2}}\right),\\
&\left| \langle B(\widetilde{v}, \widetilde{v}) - B(\widehat{v}, \widehat{v}), \widetilde{v} - \widehat{v} \rangle \right|
\leq C \|\widetilde{v}\| |\widetilde{v} - \widehat{v}| \|\widetilde{v} - \widehat{v}\|
+ C |\partial_z \widetilde{v}|  |\widetilde{v} - \widehat{v}|^{1/2} \|\widetilde{v} - \widehat{v}\|^{3/2}.
\end{align}
 Moreover, for all $v,\widetilde v,\widehat v\in V$,
 \[
 b(v,\widetilde v,\widetilde v)=0,
 \qquad b(v,\widetilde v,\widehat v)=-b(v,\widehat v,\widetilde v).
 \]
 If, in addition, $v\in D(A)$, then
\begin{align}
	\langle v\partial_xv+\mathcal W(v)\partial_zv,\partial_{zz}v\rangle=0.
\end{align}
The last identity is used at the Galerkin level before passage to the limit.
If \( v, \widetilde{v} \in V \) and \( \partial_z \widetilde{v} \in V \), then
\begin{equation}
	\|B(v, \widetilde{v})\|_{V'} \leq C\bigl( (|v| + |\partial_z v|)|\partial_{x} \widetilde{v}| + |v| \cdot \|\partial_z \widetilde{v}\| + |v| \cdot |\partial_z \widetilde{v}|^{1/2}\|\partial_z \widetilde{v}\|^{1/2} \bigr).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:29:14.964225+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b591a180a72440074ccd504ba02b52eac6399ba32ae2a3e1b977df30bb84ec0f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:vonLuxburg of arXiv:2606.14895, 'Effective Resistances and Commute Times in Sparse Random Geometric Graphs'] Let $G_n = (V_n, E_n)$ be an RGG with radius of connection $r_n$ from $n$ uniformly distributed points on $\mathbb{T}^2$ with vertex degrees $D_u$ and graph volume $\mathrm{Vol}(G_n) = \sum_{u\in V_n} D_u$. Suppose that the fixed pair of vertices $u$ and $v$ at positions $X_u$ and $X_v$ are separated by Euclidean distance $d(X_u,X_v) > 8r_n$. Assuming that $n r_n^2 / \ln n \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$, there exists a constant $c$ such that the commute distance satisfies, with probability converging to $1$, 
\[
nr_n^2\left\vert\frac{1}{\mathrm{Vol}(G_n)}C_{uv} -
\left(\frac{1}{D_u}+\frac{1}{D_v}\right)\right| \leq c/nr_n^3\,.
\]
Therefore, further requiring that $r_n\to 0$ and $nr_n^3\to\infty$ yields
\[
C_{uv} \;\to\; \mathrm{Vol}(G_n)\left(\frac{1}{D_u} + \frac{1}{D_v}\right)\qquad almost\;surely\,.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:11:44.461095+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5aca9b87a0a53a376c1614a4e342956b8df7107e354946f0c5c2d4ce94de36a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] We consider a cyclic $C_{p^s}$-extension of $k((t))$, its lower jumps $l_1<\cdots <l_s$, and its upper jumps $u_1<\cdots<u_s$. Then the following properties hold. 

\medskip
{\bf (1)} The lower and upper jumps determine uniquely each other by the recursive identities $l_1:=u_1$ and $l_i:=l_{i-1}+p^{i-1}(u_i-u_{i-1})$ for each $i\in\llbracket2,s\rrbracket$. 

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} For each $j\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket $ we have $l_j=u_1+\sum_{i=1}^{j-1} p^i(u_{i+1}-u_i)$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} For each $j\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ we have identities 
$$\sum_{i=1}^j \frac{l_i}{p^i}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^j p^{i-1}u_i}{p^j}$$
and
$$p^{j-1}u_j:=l_j+(p-1)\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}l_ip^{j-i-1}.$$

{\bf (4)} For $b\in\llbracket0,p^s-1\rrbracket$, write
\[
b=\delta_{1,b}+\delta_{2,b}p+\cdots+\delta_{s,b}p^{s-1}
\]
with $\delta_{i,b}\in\llbracket0,p-1\rrbracket$ for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ and define
\[
N_{s,b}:=\sum_{i=1}^s p^{s-i}\bigl[p-1+(p-1-\delta_{i,b})l_i\bigr].
\] Then for each $b\in \llbracket1,p^s-1\rrbracket$, if $j\in\llbracket0,s-1\rrbracket$ is the largest such that $p^j\mid b$, then we have identities 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
N_{s,b-1}-N_{s,b}&=p^{s-j-1}\Big[l_{j+1}-(p-1)\sum_{i=1}^j p^{j+1-i}l_i\Big]\\
&=p^{s-j-1}[l_1+\sum_{i=1}^j p^i(u_{i+1}-pu_i)].
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
In particular, $N_{s,b-1}-N_{s,b}\ge p^{s-j-1}l_1\ge l_1>0$ and therefore we have $\frac{l_{j+1}}{p^{j+1}}-(p-1)\sum_{i=1}^j\frac{l_i}{p^i}\ge\frac{l_1}{p^{j+1}}>0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:49:17.489093+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5e0d3c2ca35038ddf852624bd30c7447cd64325120f7a3e2897c9a5be188e7e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 13 (Planar duality; Figure~\ref{fig:dual_graph}, \textsc{Right}) of arXiv:2605.28473, 'The BKT transition and surface tension differentiability'] Let $G$ be a leafless connected finite planar graph embedded in the plane; we call it
    the \emph{primal graph}.
    Write $\partial G\subset V(G)$ for the set of vertices incident to the outer face.
    The corresponding \emph{dual graph} $G^*$ is defined as follows.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Its vertex set $V(G^*)$ is the disjoint union of:
            \begin{itemize}
                \item The set of \emph{inner} faces of $G$,
                \item The set of edges of $G$ incident to the outer face.
            \end{itemize}
        \item The edge set $E(G^*)$ is in natural bijection with $E(G)$.
        \item The graph boundary $\partial G^*\subset V(G^*)$ is defined as the set of
            dual vertices corresponding to the edges incident to the outer face of $G$.
    \end{itemize}

    This gives an efficient set-theoretic definition of the dual graph.
    We typically use it through its natural planar embedding,
    see Figure~\ref{fig:dual_graph}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the walk is on the incipient infinite cluster or a similarly statistically self-similar critical random graph","a known or boundable volume-growth exponent d_f for balls in the cluster","a known or boundable effective-resistance-growth exponent reflecting the bottleneck/dangling-end structure","typically also requires the cluster's law to have appropriate scale-invariance, or at least comparable behavior across scales"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.993751+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5e3fa35e1a6d931ebdc3e155642b0dc3bd61f17553d02dc415ed8ee523ff71e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For simple random walk on the incipient infinite cluster of critical percolation, or more generally on critical random media with anomalous volume growth, Kesten's argument establishes subdiffusive behavior, that the walk's typical displacement after n steps scales as n^{1/(2+theta)} for some theta>0 rather than the diffusive n^{1/2}, by combining a volume-growth estimate showing balls of radius r typically contain of order r^{d_f} points, with d_f the fractal (volume) dimension of the cluster, and an effective-resistance estimate showing R_eff(0, B(0,r)^c) grows faster than linearly, of order r^{1+theta}, reflecting the long dangling ends and low-conductance bottlenecks characteristic of the critical cluster. Combining volume growth and resistance growth via the Nash/heat-kernel machinery, or a direct expected-exit-time computation, gives the subdiffusive exponent. The argument does not give the exact value of the subdiffusivity exponent in most dimensions, only bounds, with the precise exponent known rigorously only in specific settings such as sufficiently high dimension or tree-like/hierarchical models, and it is specific to critical (not subcritical or supercritical) percolation geometry, where the fractal, tree-like structure with many bottlenecks is essential to the argument. Typical failure: Assuming the subdiffusivity exponent established for one setting, such as high-dimensional or tree-based incipient infinite clusters where exact computation is possible, transfers to two-dimensional critical percolation, where the exact random-walk dimension remains a major open problem; volume-growth and resistance-growth exponents are model- and dimension-specific quantities that must be independently estimated rather than imported across models with superficially similar critical geometry. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T05:37:56.275926+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2509.26030, 2025): mathematics","id":"claim_b5e9402766bd4ba38427f09638ab674f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 5.3 of arXiv:2509.26030, 'Muon Outperforms Adam in Tail-End Associative Memory Learning'] If Assumptions 5.1 and 5.2 hold, with fixed $\\alpha,\\beta$ such that $\\alpha\\neq\\beta$, and $K$ goes to infinity, we obtain the following results for one-step gd, Muon, and Adam. • For gd, for any $\\widetilde{E}$ and $E$ satistifying Assumption 5.1, we have $\\displaystyle\\varrho_{\\text{GD}}^{\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon^{-r(\\alpha,\\beta)}K^{r(\\alpha,\\beta)-1}),\\text{ where }r(\\alpha,\\beta)=\\min\\bigg\\{\\frac{\\alpha(1-\\beta)}{\\beta(1-\\alpha)},\\frac{\\beta(1-\\alpha)}{\\alpha(1-\\beta)}\\bigg\\}<1.$ • For Muon, for any $\\widetilde{E}$ and $E$ satistifying Assumption 5.1, we have $\\displaystyle\\varrho_{\\text{Muon}}^{\\epsilon}\\geq 1-\\epsilon\\bigg(1+O\\bigg(\\frac{\\log K}{K}\\bigg)\\bigg),\\text{ and }G_{\\text{Muon}}(W_{0})=-\\widetilde{E}E^{\\top}+O\\bigg(\\frac{1}{K}\\widetilde{E}J_{K,K}E^{\\top}\\bigg),$ where $J_{K,K}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{K\\times K}$ is the matrix with all elements equal to $1$. The big- $O$ notation for matrices means that for $A=O(B)$, each entry satisfies $A_{ij}=O(B_{ij})$ for all $i,j$. • For Adam, there exist $\\widetilde{E}$ and $E$ satisfying Assumption 5.1 such that $\\varrho_{\\text{SignGD}}^{\\epsilon}\\geq 1-\\epsilon.$ There also exist $\\widetilde{E}^{\\prime}$ and $E^{\\prime}$ satisfying Assumption 5.1 such that $\\displaystyle\\varrho_{\\text{SignGD}}^{\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon^{-0.7}K^{-0.3}),\\text{ and }\\frac{\\sigma_{\\min}\\big(G_{\\text{SignGD}}(W_{0})\\big)}{\\sigma_{\\max}\\big(G_{\\text{SignGD}}(W_{0})\\big)}\\leq 25\\%,$ where $\\sigma_{\\max}$ and $\\sigma_{\\min}$ are the largest and smallest singular values, respectively.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:25:55.403379+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5eaa74e6e1ee099015d33ae293f118aad892623a0682b4c56cc8f394f3daeae","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[De 1 of arXiv:2607.28078, '2607.28078'] (1) Fix a filtered probability space carrying an $\mathbb{R}^m$-valued Brownian motion $B$ and an $\mathcal{F}_0$-measurable random variable $X_0$. An adapted continuous $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued process $X$ is called a \emph{strong solution} of (\ref{2.1}) if
\[
\mathbb{E} \int_{0}^{t}\bigg\{\big\|b(s,X(s),\mathcal{L}_{X(s)})\big\|_{\mathbb{R}^d}+\big\|\sigma(s,X(s),\mathcal{L}_{X(s)})\big\|^2_{\mathbb{R}^{d\times m}}\bigg\}ds<\infty,\,\, t\geq0,
\]
and if, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely,
\[
X(t)=X_0+\int_{0}^{t}b(s,X(s),\mathcal{L}_{X(s)})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(s,X(s),\mathcal{L}_{X(s)})dB(s),\,\, t\geq0,
\]
where $\mathcal L_{X(t)}\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ for every $t\geq0$. \emph{Pathwise uniqueness} holds if any two such strong solutions defined with respect to the same $B$ and the same $X_0$ coincide almost surely.
		
(2) A pair $(\tilde{X}(t),\tilde{B}(t))_{t\geq0}$ is called a \emph{weak solution} of $(\ref{2.1})$ if it solves the equation on some stochastic basis $(\tilde{\Omega},\tilde{\mathcal{F}},\{\tilde{\mathcal{F}}_t\}_{t\geq0},\tilde{\mathbb{P}})$ and $\tilde B$ is an $\mathbb R^m$-valued Brownian motion on that basis.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:04:07.030867+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5f7b31b3eb5e4eb8f36aaec33631fb202c78baa9143519a46382173c2d87edb","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:reduced-same-shell-increment of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Fix a regular \(f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)\), write
		\(\theta=\theta_f\) and \(\zeta=\zeta_f\), and let \(q\) be the first
		positive contact point of \(\zeta\). Let \(X\) be the
		Auffinger--Chen process associated with \(\zeta\). For
		\(\varepsilon>0\), fix \(\mathbf{m}\in(-1,1)^N\), and define \(b_i\) by
		\[
		m_i=\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i).
		\]
		Write \(\mathbf{b}=(b_i)_{i\le N}\).
		Assume that
		\[
		|q_\mathbf{m}-q|\le\varepsilon,
		\qquad
		W_2\left(
		\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{b_i},
		\mathrm{Law}(X_q)
		\right)\le\varepsilon.
		\]
		For \(f'\in[f-\varepsilon,f+\varepsilon]\), condition on
		\[
		F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=Nf',
		\qquad
		\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0.
		\]
		Assume also that
		\[
		\left|
		f'
		+\frac1N\left(
		F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(\mathbf{m})-F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})
		\right)
		-f
		\right|
		\le\varepsilon.
		\]
		Denote the corresponding conditional expectation by
		\(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{m},f'}\).
		There is a centered Gaussian field \(G_\mathbf{m}\), independent of the
		conditioned value and gradient, such that, for every fixed
		\(r\in(-q,q)\),
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}')-F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})
				&=G_\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{m}')
				+\sum_{i=1}^N\left[
				\frac{\xi'(r)}{\xi'(q)}m'_i b_i
				+\Phi_\zeta^*(q,m'_i)-\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i)
				\right]\\
				&\quad+N\theta\bigl[\xi(r)-r\xi'(r)-\xi(q)+q\xi'(q)\bigr]
				+N o_\varepsilon(1)+N o_\delta(1)+o_N(N),
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}
		uniformly when \(\lvert q_{\mathbf{m}'}-q\rvert\le\delta\) and
		\(\lvert R(\mathbf{m},\mathbf{m}')-r\rvert\le\delta\). Here
		\(o_N(N)/N\to0\) for fixed \(\varepsilon,\delta\), while
		\(o_\varepsilon(1)\to0\) and \(o_\delta(1)\to0\) as their respective
		parameters tend to zero. All errors are uniform over the displayed
		\(\varepsilon\)-window conditions. For two points
		\(\mathbf{m}'^1,\mathbf{m}'^2\) in this slice,
		\[
		\frac1N\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{m},f'}\left[
		G_\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{m}'^1)G_\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{m}'^2)
		\right]
		=
		\xi(R_{12})-
		\frac{\xi'(r)^2}{\xi'(q)}R_{12}+C_r
		+o_\varepsilon(1)+o_\delta(1)+o_N(1),
		\]
		where \(R_{12}=N^{-1}\langle\mathbf{m}'^1,\mathbf{m}'^2\rangle\) and \(C_r\) depends
		only on \(q\) and \(r\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:49.842588+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b5fc02baf6d1bb7cf3ba2526a16bbfb200bd121668bc0313032a700ba3529abe","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 10 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Multi-dimensional Itô Integral}{}
 let $(W_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion. Furthermore, let $f(t, \omega): [0, T] \times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ be a matrix of $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted processes such that each entry $f_{ij}(t, \omega)$ belongs to the space $L^2([0, T] \times \Omega)$, i.e.,
 \[
\mathbb{E}\left[ \int_0^T \| f(t) \|_F^2 \, \mathrm{d}t \right] < \infty,
\]
where $\| f(t) \|_F$ denotes the Frobenius norm of the matrix $f(t)$. Then the \textbf{multi-dimensional Itô integral} is defined as:
\[
\int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t = 
\begin{pmatrix}
\sum\limits_{j=1}^d \int\limits_0^T f_{1j}(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t^j, \dots, 
\sum\limits_{j=1}^d \int\limits_0^T f_{nj}(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t^j
\end{pmatrix}^\top,
\]
where each term is a sum of scalar Itô integrals.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.360475+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6037c8c8459122d7c3759452aab6b463cb95829c2fce94e8bb116ffceef2ba7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 255 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\chi'(1) \le L^2$.

\begin{proof}
Throughout this proof we abbreviate $\bg\equiv(\bG,\bg^\aux)$.  Consider small positive $\delta$, and define
    \[\begin{aligned}
    \bx&=\cA( (1-\delta)^{1/2}\bg+\delta^{1/2}\bg')\,,\\
    \by &= \E(\bx\,|\, \bg)\,,\\
    \bz &= \bx-\by\,.
    \end{aligned}\]
By iterated expectations, we have
    \[
    \frac{\E(\by,\by)}{N}
    =\frac{\E(\bx,\by)}{N}
    =\chi(1-\delta)\,, 
    \]
as well as $\E(\by,\bz)=0$. It follows that
    \beq
    \chi(1)
    =\frac{\E(\bx,\bx)}{N}
    =\frac{\E(\by,\by)}{N}+\frac{\E(\bz,\bz)}{N}
    =\chi(1-\delta) + \frac{\E(\bz,\bz)}{N}\,.\eeq
Let us treat $\bz$ as a function of $\bg'$ for fixed $\bg$. Note that $\E(\bz\,|\,\bg)=0$. Since $\cA$ is $L$-Lipschitz, we see that $\bz$ is $(L\delta^{1/2})$-Lipschitz as a function of $\bg'$. It follows (using e.g.\ Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}) that
    \[
    \frac{\E(\bz,\bz)}{N} \le O(L^2\delta)\,.
    \]
Recalling \eqref{eq:bz}, we see that $\chi(1-\delta) \ge \chi(1)-O(L^2\delta)$, which implies $\chi'(1) \le L^2$ as claimed. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:19:46.228500+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b611e1c92b803b450068416aa660dcb674500a40f671d6832b57bd068ca4c54b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 13 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] If $S$ is any set (not necessarily finite), $Q$ is a positive semidefinite $S$-by-$S$ matrix, and $E,F$ are disjoint finite subsets of $S$, then we write

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:49.842828+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b61605865fc4fb12f849c3892139984bb0137acc0b2f2670fd98e6c359d68d58","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Itô's Integration by Parts}{}
Let \(\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) and \(\{Y_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be two Itô processes defined by
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = \mu_X(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}t + \sigma_X(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t, \quad
\mathrm{d}Y_t = \mu_Y(t, Y_t) \, \mathrm{d}t + \sigma_Y(t, Y_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t,
\]
where \(W_t\) is a Brownian motion. Then, the product \(Z_t = X_t Y_t\) satisfies
\[
\mathrm{d}(X_t Y_t) = X_t \, \mathrm{d}Y_t + Y_t \, \mathrm{d}X_t + \mathrm{d}\langle X, Y \rangle_t,
\]
where \(\mathrm{d}\langle X, Y \rangle_t\) is the differential of the quadratic covariation process of \(X_t\) and \(Y_t\), given by
\[
\mathrm{d}\langle X, Y \rangle_t = \sigma_X(t, X_t) \sigma_Y(t, Y_t)^\top \, \mathrm{d}t.
\]
Therefore, expanding the terms explicitly gives
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{d}(X_t Y_t) 
&= \big( X_t \mu_Y(t, Y_t) + Y_t \mu_X(t, X_t) 
+ \sigma_X(t, X_t) \sigma_Y(t, Y_t)^\top \big) \, \mathrm{d}t \\
&\quad + X_t \sigma_Y(t, Y_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t 
+ Y_t \sigma_X(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:02.096304+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b619662167f1d705824aec518ea871ba76c4eb8c3ab8057e009a8540a570f01f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 33 of arXiv:2604.26026, 'Stochastic Ordering of Dependent Systems under Transformation Models and Archimedean Copul'] Let $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n),\,\boldsymbol{\beta}=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$.
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item (\cite{marshall2011}, Definition~1.A.1)
     The vector $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ is said to be majorized by another vector $\boldsymbol{\beta}$, denoted by $\boldsymbol{\alpha} \overset{m}{\preceq}\boldsymbol{\beta}$, if for each $\ell=1, \ldots, n-1$, we have $\sum_{i=1}^{\ell} \alpha_{i:n} \geq \sum_{i=1}^{\ell} \beta_{i:n}$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_{i:n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n} \beta_{i:n}$, where $\alpha_{i:n}$ and $\beta_{i:n}$ represent the coordinates of $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ and $\boldsymbol{\beta}$, respectively, ordered increasingly.
    \item (\cite{marshall2011}, Definition~3.A.1)
	A function $h:A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is said to be Schur-convex (Schur-concave) on $A$ if
	$$
	\boldsymbol{\alpha} \overset{m}\succeq \boldsymbol{\beta} \Rightarrow h(\boldsymbol{\alpha}) \geq(\leq)\; h(\boldsymbol{\beta}),
    \quad \text { for all } \boldsymbol{\alpha},\, \boldsymbol{\beta} \in A.
	$$
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:01:15.329883+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b61e048f046c0793ed53f034843febd8b7079965d002730ea65fcb0af41cf4ab","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 4 (Second-order origin of the empirical ranking) of arXiv:2608.30374, 'Compact and Infinite-Order Error Analysis\\ for Null-Space SVD Estimation'] Let
\(\lambda_{(0)}(\sigma)\leq\cdots\leq
  \lambda_{(m-1)}(\sigma)\)
be the increasingly ordered eigenvalues of \(A(\sigma)\), and let
\(P_{(i)}(\sigma)\) be rank-one eigenprojectors from an ordered
orthonormal eigenbasis.  When an eigenvalue is simple its projector is unique;
the associated unit eigenvector is unique up to sign.  For \(0\leq i<q_0\),
define
\begin{equation}
 R_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma;\mathcal T)
   =\frac1\tau\operatorname{tr}\!\left(
      A(\sigma)P_{(i)}(\sigma)\right),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma)
   =\mathbb E_{\mathrm{tr}}
      [R_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma;\mathcal T)].
 
\end{equation}
Then, exactly for every realization,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{R_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma;\mathcal T)
       =\frac{\lambda_{(i)}(\sigma)}{\tau}},
 \qquad
 R_{\mathrm{emp},0}^{\mathrm{ord}}\leq\cdots\leq
 R_{\mathrm{emp},q_0-1}^{\mathrm{ord}}.
 
\end{equation}
For every \(1\leq q\leq q_0\), these branch risks decompose the aggregate
risk, both before and after expectation:
\begin{equation}
 R_{\mathrm{emp},q}(\sigma;\mathcal T)
   =\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}R_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma;\mathcal T),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{emp},q}(\sigma)
   =\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma).
 
\end{equation}
If \(\mu_0\leq\cdots\leq\mu_{q_0-1}\) are the ordered eigenvalues of
the effective matrix \(W\) in \eqref{eq:effective-splitting}, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 R_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma;\mathcal T)
   =\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau}\mu_i+O_{\mathcal T}(\sigma^3),
   \qquad \sigma\downarrow0.}
 
\end{equation}
Thus \(W\), rather than an arbitrary clean null-space basis, governs the
first nonzero small-noise separations.  If \(W\) is simple, its locally
analytic labelled sheets coincide with \(\lambda_{(i)}\) for all sufficiently
small \(\sigma>0\).  At larger noise, an eigenvalue crossing may exchange
sheet labels; the parenthesized index always denotes instantaneous SVD order.

Under the Gaussian assumptions of \Cref{sec:equal-ranked-equal}, suppose
also that \(\tau\geq m\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 W\sim\operatorname{Wishart}_{q_0}(\tau-n,I_{q_0}),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma)
   =\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau}\,\overline\mu_i+o(\sigma^2),
 \quad \overline\mu_i=\mathbb E[\mu_i],
 
\end{equation}
and
\(\overline\mu_0<\cdots<\overline\mu_{q_0-1}\).
Let \(\overline{\V{\mu}}=(\overline\mu_0,\ldots,
\overline\mu_{q_0-1})^T\).  Consequently, if
\(\V{e}_{\mathrm{emp}}\) collects the expected ordered empirical risks, then
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emp},i}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\sigma)}
      {\|\V{e}_{\mathrm{emp}}(\sigma)\|_2}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\overline\mu_i}{\|\overline{\V{\mu}}\|_2}
 \quad(\sigma\downarrow0),
 
\end{equation}
which, when \(q_0>1\), is strictly ranked rather than uniform.  Moreover, for every
\(\sigma>0\) the Gaussian sample covariance has simple spectrum almost
surely, so the expected inequalities in \eqref{eq:exact-empirical-order}
are strict.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:21:56.740528+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6228d2a805c6c154d1255a5409ec31daa09a016b65c3048af96e212db9d85e3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition definition-RWREdiscrete of arXiv:2507.19222, 'Convergence of the KMP model to the KPZ equation'] On a probability space $(\Omega^{(\epsilon)}, \mathcal{F}^{(\epsilon)}, \mathbb{P}^{(\epsilon)})$, we define the following random variables: for each bond $(x,x+1)$, let  $\left(\mathcal{I}_{x,x+1}^{(n)}\right)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0}}$ be a Bernoulli process with parameter $\epsilon\in [0,1]$,  independent for each bond. 
	
	
	For each bond $(x,x+1)$ and each $n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0}$,  let  $B_{x,x+1}^{(n)}$ be an independent random variable distributed as  Beta$(\alpha,\alpha)$. 
	We denote a realization of the  environment by $(\text{Bin}, \omega)\in \Omega^{(\epsilon)}$, where  $\text{Bin}$ is a realization of the Bernoulli processes and $\omega$ is a realization of the Beta variables.
	
	
	Given $(\text{Bin}, \omega)\in \Omega^{(\epsilon)}$, we define a random walk $(X^{\epsilon}(n))_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0}}$ as follows. If at discrete-time $n$, $X^{\epsilon}(n)=x$,  the update rule is as follows:
	\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=12pt]
		\item If $\mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x-1,x} = \mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x,x+1} = 1$ or if $\mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x-1,x} = \mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x,x+1} = 0$ the particle does not move. These events happen with probability $\epsilon^{2}$ and $1-2\epsilon(1-\epsilon)$ respectively. 
		\item If $\mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x-1,x} = 1$ and $\mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x,x+1} = 0$: the walker moves to $x+1$ with probability $1 - B^{(n)}_{x,x+1}$, or remains at $x$ with probability $B^{(n)}_{x,x+1}$. This event happens with probability $\epsilon(1-\epsilon)$.
		\item If $\mathcal{I}^{(n)}_{x-1,x} = 0$ and $\mathcal{I}^{n}_{x,x+1} = 1$: the walker moves to $x-1$ with probability $B^{(n)}_{x-1,x}$, or remains at  $x$ with probability $1 - B^{(n)}_{x-1,x}$. This event happens with probability $\epsilon(1-\epsilon)$.
	\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.978406+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6453825bdb329962d437868946559ad77bceec92b078ef5d259a0d71bccf938","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 59 (Intrinsic degree-two endpoint) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Consider symmetric-ideal completions of the finite-rank split state with
the following four properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item finite-rank states are dense and every bounded pushforward
      \(L_\#\) is continuous;
\item the universal positive collision functional
      \(Q\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}Q\) is continuous;
\item the full exterior response is a faithful continuous area reader,
      and the scalar profile \(\mathfrak P_A\) is a continuous spectral
      reader for the singular-value topology;
\item the completion contains every continuous Hilbert-martingale state
      with uniformly bounded terminal trace energy.
\end{enumerate}
Then the collision coordinate must have trace-class strength.  Within the
weak and Lorentz scales, the universal area coordinate reaches exactly
the weak-trace frontier.  It cannot be replaced by any
\(\mathcal S_{p,\infty}\) with \(p<1\), by any finite
\(\mathcal S_{1,\rho}\), or by a little weak space with a prescribed
dimension-free decay modulus.  Requiring a separable finite-rank
completion therefore selects
\[
 H\times\mathcal S^0_{1,\infty}(H)_{\mathrm{skew}}
   \times\mathcal S_1(H)_{\mathrm{sa}}
\]
as the intrinsic degree-two split endpoint in this scale.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:17:33.997008+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6453c40d44a0d196e4c9c4897c99e9dcee39c5230d07e285e06304c3f27a5da","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2609.03403, 'Hyperpositive functions, sector bounded functions and a trace formula'] Let $(H_+ , H_-)$ be a pair of of selfadjoint operators defined on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and with the following two properties:\\

     \]

{"assumptions":["the pool protocol: members fitted on training data, the test rows split 40/60 into calibration and evaluation with a fixed permutation, metric = mean per-sample relative L2","the small-calibration arms subsample the calibration rows only; evaluation rows are never touched"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T07:18:07.915757+00:00","domain":"ensemble learning / covariance estimation","id":"claim_b65e4f03214b2aa782f369b54d75f83a80e5af182457d205fd6bc537075ff3c0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (23 and 18 members; 285 and 40 outputs; 932 and 800 calibration rows; the per-sample relative metric; 70 cells, paired). The error covariance of the members is rank-deficient in practice: $\\lambda_{\\max}/\\lambda_{\\min}$ of $10^{6}$ to $10^{17}$, three to five eigenvalues below $0.05\\,\\sigma^2$ (members that are near-linear combinations of one another). Inside the long-only minimum-variance stack, eight cleaners of that covariance were compared on the same cells, the same split and the same small-calibration draws: the raw sample covariance, the $\\eta$-regularised rotationally invariant estimator with floors $0, 0.05, 0.2, 1.0\\,\\sigma^2$, Ledoit-Wolf 2004 linear shrinkage, Ledoit-Wolf 2020 analytical nonlinear shrinkage and Lam's NERCOME. Result, paired gains against the $0.05$-floor RIE: the raw covariance, the eta-RIE without floor, LW2020 and NERCOME tie at full calibration (median paired gain 0.00 on both corpora; means +0.05, +0.04, +0.09, -0.86 on 40 EMIT cells, the last from one cell at -16; +0.16, +0.01, +0.15, +0.09 on 30 OCO-2 cells), while at $n = 60$ the eta-RIE itself is the worst of them: on OCO-2 raw +6.4, LW2020 +6.0, NERCOME +4.9 percent over it on 30 of 30 cells (on EMIT +0.6, +1.3, +1.0 with 20-28 of 40 wins), and at $n = 240$ on OCO-2 +1.1, +1.0, +0.8 on 30 of 30 at full calibration and in the $n = 60/120/240$ arms; the floors $0.2$ and $1.0$ lose 1.2 and 6.5 percent on EMIT at full calibration (0.2 and 1.1 on OCO-2), 4.5 percent for the heavy floor at $n = 60$ on EMIT; linear shrinkage loses 6.3 percent on EMIT at full calibration and 15 percent at $n = 60$ (a wash on OCO-2, where the members are fewer and the shrinkage target closer); and the sum-to-one (unconstrained-sign) forms of the same cleaners lose 2 to 7 percent at full calibration on EMIT and 13 to 105 percent at $n = 60$; on OCO-2 the raw sum-to-one form is off by factors of 30 to 3,000 (an 18-member rank-deficient covariance inverted). Mechanism (seed 101, medians over outputs): the constraint keeps 7-11 of 23 members; the condition number falls from $10^{6}$-$10^{17}$ on the full covariance to $4\\times10^{2}$-$3\\times10^{4}$ on the active principal submatrix; eigenvalues under the floor fall from 3-5 to 0-1; the active sets of raw, RIE and LW2020 overlap at Jaccard 0.86-0.90 (0.80-0.83 at $n = 60$); the floors and the linear shrinkage keep MORE members active (EMIT: raw 7.2, RIE 7.6, RIE with the 0.05 floor 8.3, floor 0.2 9.4, floor 1.0 12.2, linear shrinkage 13.9, LW2020 7.3, NERCOME 9.6 of 23; OCO-2: 6.9, 7.5, 8.0, 9.1, 11.3, 8.9, 7.1, 7.2 of 18), which is how they lose - a lifted small eigenvalue makes a duplicate look independent. By the active-set lemma the weights depend on the covariance only through $S_{AA}$, which is well conditioned, and there every consistent cleaner is close to the identity; by the entrywise risk bound all of them obey the same $O(\\sqrt{\\log M/n})$ excess-risk guarantee while a floor is a bias that does not vanish with $n$. The reading of the whole program: random-matrix theory identifies what to clean (the error covariance, in the reported metric, with an intercept) and why the plug-in fails (the near-null directions of a collinear ensemble); the fix that survives the population is the long-only constraint, itself a data-determined covariance shrinkage, and the spectral cleaners are interchangeable inside it. The pre-registered contrary hypothesis - that the floor was a kernel-bandwidth artefact which LW2020's theory-fixed bandwidth would remove - was refuted on its first cell: consistent estimators correctly keep the tiny eigenvalues, because in the population they are tiny.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.340592+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6703bad009d889652cc64f04abead235202be056bb91938fe6e010ea70e1bed","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Pointwise macroscopic-loop bounds for integer loop weights) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta\in\mathbb N\) with \(\theta>1\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(d\ge 3\), let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(p_{d,n}\) denote its law. Assume
    \[
    d>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
    \[
    t\ge T_{\theta,u}(d)+\delta,
    \]
    one has
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(\lambda>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
    \[
    \lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
    \[
    t\ge T_{\theta,u}(\lambda)+\delta,
    \]
    one has
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
    \]
    If
    \[
    \rho>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),
    \]
    then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
    \[
    t\ge T_{\theta,u}(\rho)+\delta,
    \]
    one has
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The symmetric part of the operator must dominate: for genuinely non-self-adjoint problems backward uniqueness can fail.","The estimate is an interpolation between the endpoints and is NOT a bound of the solution at time 0 by the solution at time T alone - the backward problem remains ill posed, only uniqueness is recovered, and quantitative continuous dependence requires a prior bound."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:06:45.870954+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations, parabolic equations","id":"claim_b67257027da5be281d79a2ea52bbc955fdea182929264200a1d02ca9174d08e3","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H be a Hilbert space, A a self-adjoint (or more generally accretive with a symmetric part dominating the antisymmetric one) operator, and let u solve the differential inequality || u'(t) + A u(t) || <= C ( ||u(t)|| + ||A u(t)||^{1/2} ||u(t)||^{1/2} ) on [0,T]. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:21:28.763059+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6a71a162c105d8a6febcacfb7ce2231a6554619f66b3d159e5747dd1d2c52f1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:chaining-square-no-sqrtlog of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Fix $0<\beta<\tfrac12$ and $\gamma>0$.
Let $A$ be a normalized GOE matrix.
Choose an operator--norm cutoff $C_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

\beta C_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 1-\gamma.
\end{equation}

Let $\Pi_{C_{\mathrm{op}}}:\mathrm{Sym}_n(\mathbb R)\to\mathrm{Sym}_n(\mathbb R)$ be the metric projection
(with respect to $\schnorm{\cdot}$) onto the closed convex set $\{M:\ensuremath{\left\lVert M \right\rVert_\mathsf{op}}\leqslant C_{\mathrm{op}}\}$.
Set
\[
\overline A:=\Pi_{C_{\mathrm{op}}}(A).
\]

For $a\in[0,1]$ and $W\in\mathcal D_n((0,1])$ let $D:=W^{-1}$ and define
\[
X(a,W):=aI_n-\beta\overline A + D.
\]
For $T\in\mathcal D_n$ with $\schnorm{T}=1$, define the scalar functional
\[
\Phi_{a,W,T}(\overline A):=\operatorname{tr}_n\!\Big(T\,D\,X(a,W)^{-2}D\Big),
\qquad
Z_{a,W,T}:=\Phi_{a,W,T}(\overline A)-\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}_A\big[\Phi_{a,W,T}(\overline A)\big].
\]
Let the index set be
\[
\mathcal{J} \;:=\; [0,1] \;\times\; \mathcal D_n((0,1]) \;\times\; \{T\in\mathcal D_n:\schnorm{T}=1\}.
\]

Then there exist universal constants $C_{\mathrm{ch}},C_{\mathrm{tail}}>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}_A\left[\sup_{(a,W,T)\in \mathcal{J}}|Z_{a,W,T}|\right]
\ \leqslant\
C_{\mathrm{ch}}\,
\frac{\beta}{\sqrt n}\,
\frac{1}{\gamma^4},
\end{equation}
and, for every $p\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\Bigg\{
\sup_{(a,W,T)\in \mathcal{J}}|Z_{a,W,T}|
\ \leqslant\
C_{\mathrm{ch}}\,
\frac{\beta}{\sqrt n}\,
\frac{1}{\gamma^4}
\;+\;
C_{\mathrm{tail}}\,
\frac{\beta}{n}\,
\frac{1}{\gamma^3}\,
\sqrt{\log\frac{2}{p}}
\Bigg\}
\ \geqslant\ 1-p.
\end{equation}

By diagonal norm duality,
\[
\sup_{a\in[0,1]}\sup_{W\in\mathcal D_n((0,1])}\schnorm{E_{\mathcal D_n}\!\Big[D\,X(a,W)^{-2}D\Big] - \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\left[E_{\mathcal D_n}\!\Big[D\,X(a,W)^{-2}D\Big]\right]}
\;=\;
\sup_{(a,W,T)\in \mathcal{J}}|Z_{a,W,T}|,
\]
so (equation eq:chaining-expectation of the paper)--(equation eq:chaining-highprob of the paper) also bound the left-hand side.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["1 ≤ p < ∞","Ω = R^n, or Ω bounded open with Lipschitz boundary (an extension domain); for W^{1,p}_0 any open Ω","compactness statements require Ω bounded"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492521+00:00","domain":"Sobolev spaces, embedding theorems, compactness","id":"claim_b6b2ca78bf6d58de47692329336d31951c68502f00143a7631b268179675e75b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let n ≥ 1, 1 ≤ p < ∞, and let Ω ⊂ R^n be either all of R^n or a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary (more generally a bounded W^{1,p}-extension domain). For p < n write p* = np/(n − p) (Sobolev conjugate, 1/p* = 1/p − 1/n).

(i) Subcritical case p < n (Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev). W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ L^{p*}(Ω) continuously. On R^n one has the scale-invariant form ||u||_{L^{p*}(R^n)} ≤ C(n,p) ||∇u||_{L^p(R^n)} for every u ∈ W^{1,p}(R^n). For bounded Ω, W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ L^q(Ω) for every 1 ≤ q ≤ p*, and the embedding is COMPACT for every q < p* (Rellich–Kondrachov), but not for q = p*.

(ii) Critical case p = n ≥ 2. W^{1,n}(Ω) ↪ L^q(Ω) for every q ∈ [1, ∞), compactly when Ω is bounded, but W^{1,n}(Ω) is NOT contained in L^∞(Ω): in the unit disc of R^2, u(x) = log log(1 + 1/|x|) belongs to W^{1,2} and is unbounded. (For n = 1, W^{1,1} on an interval consists of absolutely continuous functions and does embed into the continuous functions.)

(iii) Supercritical case p > n (Morrey). W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ C^{0,γ}(Ω̄) with γ = 1 − n/p: every u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) has a representative that is Hölder continuous with exponent γ, and ||u||_{C^{0,γ}(Ω̄)} ≤ C ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Ω)}. For bounded Ω the embedding into C^{0,β}(Ω̄) is compact for every β < γ, in particular into C(Ω̄).

(iv) Higher order, Ω bounded Lipschitz, k ≥ 1. If kp < n then W^{k,p}(Ω) ↪ L^q(Ω) with 1/q = 1/p − k/n, compactly into L^r for r < q. If kp > n then W^{k,p}(Ω) ↪ C^{k − ⌊n/p⌋ − 1, γ}(Ω̄), where γ = ⌊n/p⌋ + 1 − n/p when n/p is not an integer, and γ is any number in (0,1) when n/p is an integer.

(v) Zero boundary values. Every statement holds for W^{1,p}_0(Ω) (resp. W^{k,p}_0) on an ARBITRARY open set Ω, bounded for the compactness claims, with no regularity of ∂Ω, because such functions extend by zero to W^{1,p}(R^n).

Where it fails. Without an extension property (Lipschitz or comparable boundary) the embedding W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ L^{p*}(Ω) can fail for bounded Ω: there are bounded domains with a sufficiently sharp outward cusp on which it is false. Compactness fails at the critical exponent q = p* (the rescaled bubbles u_λ(x) = λ^{(n−p)/p} u(λx) keep constant L^{p*} norm and W^{1,p} seminorm but converge weakly to 0) and fails on unbounded domains such as R^n (translates of one bump). The inequality ||u||_{L^q(R^n)} ≤ C||∇u||_{L^p(R^n)} is FALSE for every q ≠ p*: dilation invariance forces q = p*. W^{1,n} ↪ L^∞ fails for n ≥ 2 as shown. The Hölder exponent in (iii) cannot be improved beyond 1 − n/p in general.","status":"unverified"}

Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a nested \clekp{} in a simply connected domain $D$. For each $a\in(0,1)$, $b>0$ there exist $p > 0$ and $c>0$ such that the following holds.

Let $z\in D$ and $j_0\in\Z$ be such that $B(z,2^{-j_0})\subseteq D$. There exists a resampling $\Gamma^\resampled_{z,j}$ of $\Gamma$ within $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$ for each $j>j_0$ with the following property. Let $F_{z,j}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item no loop in $\Gamma^\resampled_{z,j}$ crosses the annulus $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$,
 \item denoting $\CC$ the loops in $\Gamma$ that cross $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$, the collection of loops of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^\resampled_{z,j}$ remain the same in each connected component of $\C \setminus \bigcup\CC$ that is not surrounded by a loop in $\CC$ and intersects $B(z,2^{-j})$, and the gasket of $\Gamma$ in these components is contained in the gasket of $\Gamma^\resampled_{z,j}$.

\[ \p[ F_{z,j} \mid \Gamma ] \geq p\]
is at least $(1-a)k$.  Then
\[ \p[(\wt G_{z,j_0,k})^c] \le c e^{-b k} . \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:35:04.202067+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b6fb3780a597ac88fdb2d567e655163bfc44db277c717ca5da83d3ba219559b6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Geometric characteristic number of a THP) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let $P$ be a trivalent hyperbolic polyhedron in $\mathbb{H}^{3}$ and let $v$ be one of its vertices. Denote the three faces incident to $v$ by $f_{1}, f_{2}, f_{3}$, and write
\[
e_{ij}=f_{i}\cap f_{j}, \quad 1\le i<j\le 3.
\]
Let $\Theta_{ij}$ be the dihedral angle of $P$ along $e_{ij}$. For $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$, define
\[
\theta_{v}^{f_{i}}=\arccos\left(\frac{1+\cos\Theta_{ij}+\cos\Theta_{ik}-\cos\Theta_{jk}}{2\sqrt{1+\cos\Theta_{ij}}\sqrt{1+\cos\Theta_{ik}}}\right)
\]
Equivalently, $\theta_{v}^{f_{i}}$ is the angle at the vertex corresponding to $f_{i}$ in the auxiliary Euclidean triangle whose side lengths are $\ell_{ij}=\sqrt{2+2\cos\Theta_{ij}}$ for $1\le i<j\le 3$.

For a face $f$ of $P$, its geometric characteristic number is defined by
\[
L_{f}(P)=2\pi-\sum_{v\in f}\theta_{v}^{f}.
\]
The geometric characteristic number of $P$ is the collection $L(P)=(L_{f}(P): f\in F(P))$, where $F(P)$ denotes the set of faces of $P$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["independent (product) probability measure on the input coordinates","f is a bounded, typically boolean, function of finitely many coordinates","existence of a randomized decision tree computing f exactly, with well-defined per-coordinate revealments","revealments computed under the same measure used for Var(f) and Inf_i(f)"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.972746+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b71abce6cf84475d6e6984b0c6a4d7ee2a29f331d669301354889ab502d006c7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be evaluated exactly by a randomized decision-tree algorithm T that, over its internal randomness, queries coordinate i with probability delta_i(T) (its revealment), and let Var(f) denote the variance of f under a product probability measure on the input. The OSSS inequality states Var(f) <= sum_{i=1}^n delta_i(T) Inf_i(f), where Inf_i(f) is the influence of coordinate i under the same measure. Consequently, exhibiting an algorithm with small maximal revealment forces the sum of influences to be large, giving lower bounds on total influence and noise sensitivity via algorithmic constructions; for critical planar percolation, an exploration-path algorithm gives revealments comparable to arm-event probabilities, and combined with quasi-multiplicativity this yields sharp bounds on noise sensitivity and, via the Duminil-Copin-Raoufi-Tassion route, on sharpness of the phase transition in all dimensions without reflection positivity or duality. The inequality does not directly compute Inf_i itself, does not apply to non-product (dependent-coordinate) measures without a separate generalization, and it is an inequality rather than an identity, so it can be loose or even vacuous if the algorithm chosen is not well matched to f's structure. Typical failure: Plugging in a naive, non-adaptive algorithm (e.g. querying coordinates in a fixed deterministic order) and expecting a sharp bound; the inequality is only informative when the algorithm is cleverly matched to the function's geometric structure, such as an exploration process for a crossing event, and a poorly chosen algorithm produces a valid but essentially vacuous bound that is easy to mistake for a genuine obstruction to sharper influence or sensitivity estimates. Canonical reference: O'Donnell, Saks, Schramm and Servedio, 2005, Proceedings of the 46th Annual IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science; Duminil-Copin, Raoufi and Tassion, 2019, Annals of Mathematics.","status":"unverified"}

Then $\alpha$ is unique, and the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:56:21.584221+00:00","domain":"combinatorics","id":"claim_b77b87e08d73f761ed5ff25ec04b1c15efb7d1bd8d686854a4b8fb7376cb33b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider finite rooted trees with vertices labeled from a fixed well-quasi-ordered set. One tree topologically embeds in another if there is an injective, ancestor-order-preserving map of vertices to vertices sending labels to weakly larger labels and sending each edge to a path, these paths being internally vertex-disjoint. Kruskal's tree theorem states that finite labeled trees, ordered by topological embeddability, form a well-quasi-order: in any infinite sequence of such trees, some tree embeds into a later one. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:16.152996+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b77f7def15b8beed58d0a2a6f104076a097150a5d2a84ba2160773e9755c1f2f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Arizmendi and Perales {\cite[Proposition 3.3) of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] {arizmendi2018cumulants-joctsa}}]
Given $d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$, the finite free cumulants $\kappa_{1}^{(d)}, \dots, \kappa_{d}^{(d)}$ are unique maps satisfying the following conditions. 
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item $\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f)$ is a polynomial in $p_{1}(f), \dots, p_{i}(f)$ with leading term $\frac{d^{i-1}}{(d)_{\underline{i}}} p_{i}(f)$. 
That is, there exists a polynomial $F_{i}$ in $i-1$ variables such that 
$$
\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f) = \frac{d^{i-1}}{(d)_{\underline{i}}}p_{i}(f) + F_{i}(p_{1}(f), \dots, p_{i-1}(f)).
$$ 
\item Homogeneity: $\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(D_{r}f) = r^{i}\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f)$ for any $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$.
\item Additivity: $\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f \boxplus_{d} g) = \kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f) + \kappa_{i}^{(d)}(g)$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:22:46.463555+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b78e8a7e6ec3aca84432af2daf603cbcd6fa8788ae86890f9006ceca98c49048","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 32 (Metric duality and musical notation) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] If $V$ is a spacetime vectorfield, then $V_{\flat}$ denotes the one-form that is

	If $Y = Y^B \geop{x^B}$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent vectorfield,

	Since $Y$ is $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent, $Y_{\flat}$ can also be viewed as the dual of

	Similarly, if $\upxi$ is a symmetric type $\binom{0}{2}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield, 
	then $\upxi^{\sharp}$ denotes the type $\binom{1}{1}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield

{"assumptions":["X_1, ..., X_n independent (arbitrary measurable state spaces, not necessarily identically distributed)","E[Z^2] < infinity","X_i' an independent copy of X_i"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T04:29:00.269210+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b7911cc88f0c4e9cbcd38f7c8f3a5c04","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_n be INDEPENDENT random variables taking values in arbitrary measurable spaces - they need NOT be identically distributed and need not be real-valued - and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) with E[Z^2] < infinity. Let X_i' be an independent copy of X_i, independent of everything else, and put Z^{(i)} = f(X_1, ..., X_{i-1}, X_i', X_{i+1}, ..., X_n). Then Var(Z) <= (1/2) sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z^{(i)})^2 ] = sum_{i=1}^n E[ ((Z - Z^{(i)})_+)^2 ]. Equivalently, and often more convenient, Var(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z_i)^2 ] for ANY random variables Z_i that are measurable functions of the n-1 variables other than X_i; taking Z_i = inf over the i-th coordinate of f gives the version used for suprema and for first-passage times. Equality in the replace-one bound (in either form) holds if and only if f is a sum of functions of the individual coordinates; equality in the bound with arbitrary Z_i holds if and only if, in addition, Z_i = E[Z | X_j, j != i] almost surely for every i. Independence is the only structural hypothesis and it is essential; the inequality is FALSE for dependent coordinates. Applied with a bounded-difference function it recovers the variance half of McDiarmid's inequality; applied to first-passage percolation with the geodesic length as the influence bound it produces the linear variance upper bound. [Efron and Stein (1981), Steele (1986); see Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 3.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Nonzero feasible rank-at-most-r target; full-row-rank design and noiseless labels","B0=0; nondegenerate Gaussian A0","Step schedule fixed conditional on design independently of A0","Isotropic population prediction risk"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:54:30.733548+00:00","domain":"LoRA gradient dynamics and excess risk","id":"claim_b794a3607b41a0b1d035b802d142402b820e6cfccddde42c0fd0b798721070a7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; T419-C006 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let Delta be any nonzero m-by-p matrix of rank at most r and X a fixed full-row-rank p-by-n design. For noiseless Y=Delta X, the global rank-r empirical least-squares estimate equals Delta, so its isotropic population parameter risk is zero. Simultaneous factor GD from B0=0 and nondegenerate Gaussian A0, with any step schedule fixed conditional on X independently of A0, almost surely has B_t A_t != Delta at every finite t. Each finite-iterate entry is a polynomial in A0; at A0=0 both factors remain zero, so a residual entry corresponding to nonzero Delta_ij has a nonzero constant term. Its zero set is Lebesgue-null, and a countable union over t remains null. This also excludes exact recovery at an almost-surely finite integer stopping time selecting these iterates. Consequently a finite-time constant-factor comparison to the noiseless zero-risk benchmark needs a limit, an additive optimization tolerance or other qualification. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:41:54.341806+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b7e9ae5d7f8dc9a0e31d70cdf304972c9704a43153c4e3ed8f7ba3e1bbbc9b99","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:KPS of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] We say that $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge0}$ is \emph{weak$^\ast$-mean
ergodic} if there exists a Borel probability measure $\mu_\ast$ on ${\mathcal B}(H)$, such that
\begin{equation}\text{w-}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T P_t^\ast\mu\,\mathrm{d} t=\mu_\ast\quad\text{for every }\quad
\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H,{\mathcal B}(H)),
\end{equation}
where the limit is in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.

We say that the \emph{weak law of large numbers} holds for $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge0}$, for a function $F\in\operatorname{Lip}_{b}(H)$ and for a probability measure $\mu$ on ${\mathcal B}(H)$ if
\[\mathbb{P}_\mu\text{-}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T F(X_t^\mu)\,\mathrm{d} t=\int_H F\,\mathrm{d}\mu_\ast,\]
where $\mu_\ast$ denotes the invariant probability measure of $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge 0}$ and $\{X_t^\mu\}_{t\ge 0}$ denotes the Markov process related to $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge 0}$ whose initial distribution is $\mu$ and whose path measure is $\mathbb{P}_\mu$, and where the convergence takes place in $\mathbb{P}_\mu$-probability.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:46:12.272400+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b7ec9f9ffccd92b6255f892ce1950141f14b6f78846d543a082de7d29a8aedeb","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 ($S$-transform under free compression) of arXiv:2604.22114, 'Free compressions of R-diagonal random variables and the semigroup of Brown measures'] Let $a\neq 0$ be a self-adjoint element in $\widetilde\AA$, and assume that either $a\ge 0$ or $a$ is even.

$[P_s (s a) P_s]\in\widetilde\AA_{P_s}$.

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.069456+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b805f2600fb9e4f5742c830760588a0ccaf9945288bad60da37c147e1f16f3b4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.19753, 'Uniform large deviation principles for the stochastic heat equation over unbounded sets of'] Let $T,N\in(0,\infty)$  and suppose that  
$p_1\in(2,\infty]$, $p_2\in[p_1,\infty]$, or  $p_1=2$,  $p_2 \in [2,\infty)$.   
Let $u\in L^2(0,T;L^2(D))$ be such that $\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;L^2(D))}\leq N$. Let 
\begin{equation}
    \tilde p\in\Big(\frac{4}{1-\frac{2}{p_1}+\frac{2}{p_2}},\infty\Big)
\end{equation}
and let $\varphi\in L^{\tilde p}(0,T;L^{p_1}(D))$. 
Define 
\[
Y(t,\xi)\ceqq \big[S*[\varphi(\cdot)u(\cdot)]\big](t)(\xi)=\int_0^t \int_{D} G(t-s,\xi-\eta)\varphi(s,\eta)u(s,\eta)d\eta \dd s.\]

\[
\|Y(t,\cdot)\|_{L^{p_2}(D)}^{\tilde p}  \lesssim_{{\tilde p}} N^{{\tilde p}}(1+T^{\frac{\tilde p}{2}-1})\int_0^t\|\varphi(s,\cdot)\|_{L^{p_1}(D)}^{{\tilde p}}\dd s.
\]
Moreover, if $p_2=\infty$, then $Y\in C([0,T];C(D))$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. nonnegative edge weights on Z^2 with F(0) = 0","mu is the axial time constant; the comparison is with the expectation of the minimum of four independent weights","the refutation is Ahlberg's (2019/2020); this is a rederivation with an explicit instance"],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869107+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_b80639d38026a14989da0a86aa6755d6ea3593aa2551d349ffb00e6d55126985","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: literature_counterexample_rederived - the primary two-page proof was read and the arithmetic author-checked; the result is Ahlberg's, not ours, and novelty is not claimed] For i.i.d. nonnegative edge weights on Z^2 with F(0) = 0, Auffinger, Damron and Hanson (50 years of first-passage percolation, Question 12) ask whether the axial time constant mu is at least the expected minimum of four independent edge weights. CLAIM: NO, and the question was already settled in the literature by Ahlberg (2019/2020), whose bound mu <= 2 t_{2/3} - twice the 2/3-quantile - refutes it. EXPLICIT INSTANCE: take tau = eta + epsilon U with P(eta = 0) = 3/4 and U uniform on [0,1]. For epsilon > 0 this law is atomless and bounded with F(0) = 0. Solving (3/4) t / epsilon = 2/3 gives t_{2/3} = 8 epsilon / 9, hence mu <= 16 epsilon / 9. The expected four-edge minimum is at least 1/256, the probability of the event that all four edges are expensive. At epsilon = 1/1024, mu <= 16/(9 x 1024) = 1/576 < 1/256, so the proposed inequality is reversed. All sufficiently small epsilon do the same. THIS IS NOT AN OPEN PROBLEM and the store's earlier node for P0096 records only a bounded-search exclusion; this node records what the counterexample actually is.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:52:17.579759+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b80a10c3b56c8cb2551d53a2e1cd1fb73910ee05bdecfec729d485fd19663807","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma l:CoincidenceDomains of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] Assume~$\big({\mssE,\msD(\mssE)}\big)$ satisfies~(equation eq:QPP of the paper), and let~$\big({\mcE_\pi,\msD(\mcE_\pi)}\big)$ be the Dir\-ichlet form defined in Proposition~(p:StandardCyl of the paper). Then,~$\hCylP{}{0}\subset\msD(\mcE_\pi)$.

\begin{proof}
In light of the diffusion property~(equation eq:l:DiffusionP:0.1 of the paper), it suffices to show that~$\hat f^\star\in\msD(\mcE_\pi)$ for every~$\hat f=\varphi\otimes f$ with~$\varphi\in\msR_0$ and~$f\in\msA$.

Let~$\left(g_\epsilon\right)_{\epsilon}$ be the family of functions constructed in Lemma~(l:DiagonalEqPot of the paper), and choose representatives~$\tilde{g_\epsilon}$ with~$\tilde{g_\epsilon}^\diag= 1$ everywhere on~$M$ and~$\tilde{g_\epsilon}\geq 0$ everywhere on~$M^{\scriptscriptstyle\times 2}$.

Now, consider the family of functions~$\seq{u_{f,\tilde{g_\epsilon},\varphi}}_\epsilon$  in~(equation eq:l:CapacityConnector:0 of the paper).
It suffices to show that~$\epsilon\mapsto \mcE_\pi(u_{f,\tilde{g_\epsilon},\varphi})$ is uniformly bounded and that~$u_{f,\tilde{g_\epsilon},\varphi}$ converges to~$\hat f^\star$ in~$L^2(\mcQ_\pi)$, in which case the conclusion follows from~[MaRoe92].

The first bound follows from~(equation eq:l:CapacityConnector:1 of the paper) and Lemma~(l:DiagonalEqPot of the paper)(i:l:DiagonalEqPot:3 of the paper).

As for the $L^2(\mcQ_\pi)$ convergence, respectively by: Jensen's inequality and boundedness of~$f\in\msA\subset\mcC_0(\tau)$, by smoothness of~$\varphi$, and again by Jensen's inequality,
\begin{align*}
\int& \abs{\int\braket{\varphi(\mu_x) - \varphi\paren{\int \tilde{g}_\epsilon(x,y) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(y)}f(x)}\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(x)}^2\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mcQ_\pi(\mu)
\\
&\leq \left\lVertf\right\rVert_0^2\int \abs{\varphi(\mu_x)-\varphi\paren{\int \int \tilde{g_\epsilon}(x,y)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(y)}}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(x) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mcQ_\pi(\mu)
\\
&\leq \left\lVertf\right\rVert_0^2 \left\lVert\varphi'\right\rVert_0^2 \int \int\abs{\mu_x-\int \tilde{g_\epsilon}(x,y)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(y)}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(x) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mcQ_\pi(\mu)
 \\
&=\left\lVertf\right\rVert_0^2 \left\lVert\varphi'\right\rVert_0^2 \int\!\!\!\!\!\int \sum_i^N s_i \abs{s_i-\sum_j^N s_j\, \tilde{g_\epsilon}(x_i,x_j)}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol\nu(\mbfx)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\pi(\mbfs)
\\
&=\left\lVertf\right\rVert_0^2 \left\lVert\varphi'\right\rVert_0^2 \int\!\!\!\!\!\int \sum_i^N s_i \abs{\sum_{j:j\neq i}^N s_j\, \tilde{g_\epsilon}(x_i,x_j)}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol\nu(\mbfx)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\pi(\mbfs)
\\
&\leq \left\lVertf\right\rVert_0^2 \left\lVert\varphi'\right\rVert_0^2 \int \sum_i^N s_i(1-s_i) \sum_{j:j\neq i}^N s_j\, \int\abs{\tilde{g_\epsilon}(x_i,x_j)}^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol\nu(\mbfx)
\\
&\leq \left\lVertf\right\rVert_0^2 \left\lVert\varphi'\right\rVert_0^2 \norm{\tilde{g_\epsilon}}_{L^2(\nu^{\scriptscriptstyle\otimes 2})}^2 \,\mathrm{.}
\end{align*}
Since the latter term vanishes as~$\epsilon\to 0$ by Lemma~(l:DiagonalEqPot of the paper)(i:l:DiagonalEqPot:3 of the paper), we have~$L^2(\mcQ_\pi)$-$\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow 0} u_{f,\tilde{g_\epsilon},\varphi}=\hat f^\star$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:30:52.735503+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b80ea27e23a611f0a4114404b317d491952ee4d6242e4c6648d917fa0934209f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theo 13 of arXiv:2506.10213, 'Coupling of forward-backward stochastic differential equations on the Wiener space, and ap'] Let Assumption~\ref{coefficient:assume:general}, Assumption~\ref{fbsde:basic:assume:p:general},
    Assumption~\ref{ass:linear:diffusion} and \eqref{p-condition} hold for some $p\in [2,\fz)$. 
    Then there is $\dz > 0$ such that \eqref{fbsde:equ:re} admits a unique solution
    $\Tz := (X,Y,Z)$ on $[t,T]$ if $T - t \leq \dz$.
    Moreover, if $T - t \leq \dz$,
    considering the coupling operator $\cC_{\vz}$ with respect to the measurable function $\vz: [0,T] \to [0,1]$,
    the following estimation holds
    \begin{align}
        CV_p([t,T])
        &\leq c_{\eqref{equ:small:decoupling}} \left\{\E\left[|\xi - \xi^{\vz}|^p + \left|g(X_T) - g^{\vz}(X_T)\right|^p\right] \right.\notag\\
        &\quad \qquad \left. + \E\left[U_p([t,T])\right] + S_p([t,T])\right\},
    \end{align}
    where the constant $c_{\eqref{equ:small:decoupling}} \in (1,\fz)$ only relies on $p$, $T - t$
    and all the Lipschitz constants in Assumption \ref{coefficient:assume:general}.
    Here the $U_p([t,T])$ is the potential of the coefficients and $S_p([t,T])$ is the term related to the function $\vz$, i.e.
    \begin{align*}
        U_p([t,T]) 
        &:= \left(\int^T_t |\Dz b(u,X_u,Y_u,Z_u)|\,\od u\right)^p\\
        &\quad\quad + \left(\int^T_t |\Dz \sz(u,X_u,Y_u) + \Dz A(u,Z_u)|^2\,\od u\right)^{p/2}\\
        &\quad\quad + \left(\int^T_t |\Dz f(u,X_u,Y_u,Z_u)|\,\od u\right)^p,
    \end{align*}
    with
    \begin{equation*}
        \Dz h := h - h^{\vz}\quad h\in\{b,\sz,A,f\};
    \end{equation*}
    and
    \begin{align*}
        S_p([t,T])
        &:= \left(\int^T_t (\vz(u))^2\,\od u\right)^{p/2}\\
        &\qquad \times \E\left[(L_{\mu,1})^p\sup_{u\in [t,T]}|X_u|^p + (L_{\mu,2})^p\sup_{u\in [t,T]}|Y_u|^p\right]\\
        &\qquad + \E\left[\left(\int^T_t (\vz(u))^2(\sz^0(u))^2\,\od u\right)^{p/2}\right].
    \end{align*}","status":"unverified"}
