{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.367957+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b83995558f11a0cf86aa4ede2b48fa7923510b738bae15c52401b224e24fc69b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 117 (Predictable differentiation of causal trace-class paths) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $q:\Omega_H\to C([0,T];\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sa})$ be total Borel and raw
causal, and let $G$ be a Borel stopping-stable set on which every $q(x)$ takes
values in $\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}$ and is Bochner absolutely continuous in
trace norm.  Put $\Delta_n=T2^{-n}$ and $t_k^n=k\Delta_n$, and define lagged
dyadic averages
\[
 (\mathscr D_nq)_t
 :=\begin{cases}
 0,&0\le t\le\Delta_n,\\[1mm]
 \Delta_n^{-1}\bigl(q_{t_k^n}-q_{t_{k-1}^n}\bigr),
 &t_k^n<t\le t_{k+1}^n,
 \end{cases}
\]
as an $\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sa}$-valued process.  Let
$\iota_1:\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}\hookrightarrow
\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sa}$ denote the continuous inclusion and set
\[
 L_1(q):=\bigl\{(t,x):(\mathscr D_nq)_t(x)\in
 \iota_1(\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa})\ \text{for every }n\bigr\}.
\]
Define the totalized trace-class derivative by
\begin{equation}
 (\mathscr Dq)_t(x):=
 \begin{cases}
 \operatorname{Lim}_{\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}}
 \bigl((\iota_1^{-1}(\mathscr D_nq)_t(x))_{n\ge1}\bigr),
 &(t,x)\in L_1(q),\\
 0,&(t,x)\notin L_1(q),
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
where the Borel selector of \Cref{lem:causal-Borel-limit} returns zero when
the displayed sequence does not converge.  Then $\mathscr Dq$ is a total
Borel predictable
$\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}$-valued process and, for every $x\in G$,
\begin{equation}
 q_t(x)=\int_0^t(\mathscr Dq)_r(x)\,\dd r,
 \qquad
 \mathscr Dq(x)=\dot q(x)\quad\text{a.e.}
\end{equation}
If the path field $q$ obeys exact stopping, shift, or concatenation identities,
then, on the corresponding loci where the transformed paths also belong to
$G$, the derivative classes obey the restriction, time-shift, and
concatenation identities almost everywhere.  The same conclusion holds for
substitution of a bounded raw stopping time whenever the stopped path remains
in $G$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:22:21.902848+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b83b198ef9953ff7287ae50f4bdff9d98eb19ead2dd6ae8a0010e2fbe2991af1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:improved_asymptotic_poincaré_under_PL of arXiv:2411.11415, 'The ballistic limit of the log-Sobolev constant equals the Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz constant'] Suppose that $f \in C^2(\R^d)$, has a unique minimizer $x_\star$,

and that $\Delta f \leqslant L_0 + L_1\,\|\nabla f\|^2$ for some constants $L_0, L_1 > 0$.
Let $\alpha, r_0 > 0$ be such that $\nabla^2 f(x) \succeq \alpha I$ for all $x \in B(x_\star, r_0)$.
Define $\delta  \deq  r_0^2/(2C_{\msf{PL}})$,
take any
$k \geqslant 1$, and put
$$
t_0  \deq  \frac{2\delta}{C_{\msf{PL}} L_0 + 2\delta L_1 + 2k-2}\,.

        e^{-u^2(x^2+y^2+x^ay^a)-u(c_1x+c_2y)}\dd x\dd y .

Then, as \(u\to\infty\),
\begin{align}
        I_{\boldsymbol c}(u)

        &&a=1, \\
        I_{\boldsymbol c}(u)
        &\sim
        L(c_1)L(c_2)u^{-2},
        &&a>1. 
\end{align}
Also,
\begin{equation}
        \int_0^\delta e^{-u^2x^2-ucx}\dd x
        \sim u^{-1}L(c),

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236593+00:00","domain":"numerical analysis","id":"claim_b8a68d2eccee5860bfb70fd0f24e13b2b7626e3471541b131b79447a4472e0ff","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"In a floating-point number system, the machine epsilon eps is the smallest positive representable number such that 1 + eps, computed with that system's rounding rule, is strictly greater than 1; equivalently, eps is the gap between 1 and the next larger representable floating-point number. For IEEE 754 binary double precision (53-bit significand, including one implicit leading bit), eps = 2^(-52). The associated unit roundoff u = eps/2 = 2^(-53) bounds the relative error of rounding a real number x, within the representable range, to the nearest floating-point number fl(x): |fl(x) - x| / |x| <= u. More generally, each basic arithmetic operation (+, -, *, /) computed in IEEE arithmetic satisfies fl(a op b) = (a op b) * (1 + delta) for some |delta| <= u.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.296081+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b8ab82999fefb43edeb515d77eaed8b7f3878d6c086bd96a599f64c1e7989fea","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem random_apprx_noisless of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho)$ be a compact metric space, let $\mu\in\mathcal{P}(X)$, and let
$X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be i.i.d.\ with law $\mu$.  Fix $\varepsilon>0$, set
$M_\varepsilon\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} N_{\varepsilon/4}(X,\rho)$, and let
$x_1^\star,\ldots,x_{M_\varepsilon}^\star\in X$ be such that
$X=\bigcup_{m=1}^{M_\varepsilon}B_\rho(x_m^\star,\varepsilon/4)$.
Assume that
$
    p_\varepsilon
    \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}
    \min_{m\in[M_\varepsilon]_+}
    \mu\big(B_\rho(x_m^\star,\varepsilon/4)\big)
    >
    0.
$
Then, for every $f\in \operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho);1)$ and every $\delta\in(0,1)$, if
\begin{equation}

    N
    \ge
    \frac{1}{p_\varepsilon}
    \log\left(\frac{M_\varepsilon}{\delta}\right)
,
\end{equation}
then the noiseless estimator
$\mathcal{E}(f|((X_n,0))_{n=1}^N)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \sup_{x\in X}\,
        \big|
            f(x)
            -
            \mathcal{E}(f|((X_n,0))_{n=1}^N)(x)
        \big|
        <
        \varepsilon
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\delta
.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:09:23.967682+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b8af826c0cd9366894fae1ba5a6454ce9f31cafe8f46b48911fc599e3dcb8bba","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 11 of arXiv:2607.22416, 'A multi-player optimal stopping game based on a spider Brownian bridge'] Fix $d>0$.
    Recall the definition of $\Gamma_d$ in \eqref{ExpressionGammap0.5} and define $\Upsilon = \Upsilon_d = \Upsilon_{\alpha,\theta,d}:[0,\infty) \mapsto \mathbb{R}$ by $\Upsilon(z) = \Gamma_d(z) - h_\alpha(z)$.
 Then $\tilde{z}$ is a turning point of $\Gamma_d$ if and only if $\tilde{z}$ is a root of $\Upsilon$.
  
The function $\Gamma_{d}$ admits a maximizer, denoted $z^{*}=z^{*}(\alpha,\theta,d)$. 
Furthermore, there exists $\hat{\Theta}:(0,\infty) \times (0,\infty)$ with $\Theta_*(\alpha,d) \leq \hat{\Theta}(\alpha,d)\leq \Theta^*(\alpha,d)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\theta < \Theta_*(\alpha,d)$ then
$\Upsilon$ has a unique root $z_1 \in (\frac{\alpha}{2}, \bar{z}(\alpha))$, and that root is the maximiser of $\Gamma_d$.

\item If $\theta = \Theta_*(\alpha,d)$ then 
$\Upsilon$ has two roots $z_1=0$ and $z_2 \in (\frac{\alpha}{2}, \bar{z}(\alpha))$, and $z_2$ is the maximiser of $\Gamma_d$.

\item If $\Theta_*(\alpha,d) < \theta < \hat{\Theta}(\alpha,d)$ then $\Upsilon$ has two roots $z_1 \in (0, \frac{\alpha}{2})$ and $z_2 \in (\frac{\alpha}{2}, \bar{z}(\alpha))$ and  $z_2$ is the maximiser of $\Gamma_d$.

\item If $\theta= \hat{\Theta}(\alpha,d)$ then $\Upsilon$ has two roots $z_{1}\in (0,\frac{\alpha}{2})$ and $z_2 \in (\frac{\alpha}{2}, \bar{z}(\alpha))$. Both $0$ and $z_{2}$ are maximisers of $\Gamma_d$.

\item If $\hat{\Theta}(\alpha,d) < \theta < \Theta^*(\alpha,d)$ then $\Upsilon$ has two roots $z_{1}\in (0,\frac{\alpha}{2})$ and $z_2 \in (\frac{\alpha}{2}, \bar{z}(\alpha))$. 0 is the maximiser of $\Gamma_d$.

\item If $\theta = \Theta^*(\alpha,d)$ then $\frac{\alpha}{2}$ is the unique root of $\Upsilon$ and $0$ is the maximiser of $\Gamma_d$. 

    
\item If $\theta > \Theta^*(\alpha,d)$ then $\Upsilon$  has no roots and $0$ is the maximiser of $\Gamma_d$. 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:44:12.645435+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b8cb276b9f61563954f345c8ccc5baad97296424c146601a48fc833ea8ad8d65","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Multipliers \(\mathcal O_M(\R^d)\) and slow growth of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] A function \(a\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\) is called \emph{slowly increasing at infinity} if for every multi–index
\(\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^n\) there exists \(N_\alpha\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(C_\alpha>0\) such that
\[
  \left|\partial^\alpha a(x)\right| \le C_\alpha\,(1+\left|x\right|)^{\,N_\alpha}\qquad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb{R}^d .
\]
We write
\[
  \mathcal O_M(\mathbb{R}^d)
  := \bigl\{ a\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d): \text{each } \partial^\alpha a \text{ has at most polynomial growth}\bigr\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal O_M(\mathbb{R}^d)\) is the space of \emph{multipliers} of \(\mathcal S(\mathbb{R}^d)\): those
\(a\) for which \(a\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb{R}^d)\) for all \(\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb{R}^d)\), and the map
\(\varphi\mapsto a\varphi\) is continuous \(\mathcal S\to\mathcal S\).","status":"unverified"}

\[
Y_{n,c_\xi}(t):=\frac{S_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}}{(n c_\xi)^{1/\alpha}},

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:21:28.750964+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b8ddcfebe7b6b76baaf17d5f38740303af576b97f5b1dea16705e2d5a3786c75","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:trace-to-replica of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Let $G$ be the Gibbs measure, $P=\mathrm{Cov}(G)$ and $T=\diag(P)$.
For replicas $\sigma^1,\sigma^2,\sigma^3,\sigma^4\sim G^{\otimes 4}$, define
\[
a_i:=(\sigma_i^1-\sigma_i^2)(\sigma_i^3-\sigma_i^4),
\qquad
f:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n a_i,
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_i^\ell:=\frac{\sigma_i^\ell-m_i}{\sqrt{1-m_i^2}},
\qquad
\widehat f:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (\widehat\sigma_i^1-\widehat\sigma_i^2)(\widehat\sigma_i^3-\widehat\sigma_i^4).
\]
Also, define the ``diagonally weighted'' rectangular sum
\[
f^{\mathrm{diag}}:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n P_{ii}\,a_i.
\]
Then, the following tracial equalities hold conditioned on any choice of $\{A_{ij}\}_{i,j}$,
\begin{align}
\mathsf{Tr}[P^2] &= \frac{n^2}{4}\,\langle f^2\rangle,\\
\mathsf{Tr}[PDP] &= \frac{n^2}{4}\,\langle f\widehat f\rangle, \\
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \langle a_i^2\rangle &= \frac{4}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n P_{ii}^2.  \\

\mathsf{Tr}[TP^2] &= \frac{n^2}{4}\,\langle f\,f^{\mathrm{diag}}\rangle, \\
\mathsf{Tr}[TPDP] &= \frac{n^2}{4}\,\langle f^{\mathrm{diag}}\,\widehat f\rangle. 
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:43:55.606493+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b8fc29b45b4cf64e1c9dd4f913d484dd326274f7e6d846c31ecff0df186a3f1b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Contour of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] If $\mathcal Z=(V_\mathcal Z,E_\mathcal Z)$ is a sub-graph of the $\mathbb{Z}^2$ lattice and
    $\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$, its contour at distance $\varepsilon$ is defined as the graph
    $\mathrm{Cont}[\mathcal Z,\varepsilon]$ with vertex set
    $V_\mathcal Z+\varepsilon\Delta$, where $\Delta\coloneqq\{-1,1\}^2$, and whose edges consist of 
        \begin{itemize}
            \item pairs $(v+\varepsilon\delta,v+\varepsilon\delta')$ with $v\in V_\mathcal Z$

            $\bigl(v,\,v+\tfrac{\delta+\delta'}2\bigr)\notin E_\mathcal Z$,
            and
            \item pairs $(v+\varepsilon\delta,v'+\varepsilon\delta')$ with $(v,v')\in E_\mathcal Z$
            and $\delta,\delta'\in\Delta$ satisfying
            $\tfrac{\delta-\delta'}2=v'-v$.
        \end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T16:46:51.523624+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_b903e3cee17593fc48f4bd33bca8ffaec7da904c9cb287cd97d6c703cf6ff573","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In mathematical analysis, the Kakutani fixed-point theorem is a fixed-point theorem for set-valued functions. It provides sufficient conditions for a set-valued function defined on a convex, compact subset of a Euclidean space to have a fixed point, i.e. a point which is mapped to a set containing it. The Kakutani fixed point theorem is a generalization of the Brouwer fixed point theorem. The Brouwer fixed point theorem is a fundamental result in topology which proves the existence of fixed points for continuous functions defined on compact, convex subsets of Euclidean spaces. Kakutani's theorem extends this to set-valued functions.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:25:40.340891+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b923822b98d964be3b7391212a01bef9edb0c144459e1cb0267c65e2e348fa7b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:layeredmax of arXiv:2609.03081, 'Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids'] For a positive integer $n$, consider the collection of integers

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.475586+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b927d4bfca0e0ed183d4a2cbb709c014fb7b926ca197c2f13b9ef4edad23f4c2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] Let $G$ be compact with left Haar measure $\mu$ and let $G^{\op}$ denote the opposite group of $G$. 
Take the right Haar measure on $G^{\op}$ to be $\mu$. 
Then, 
\[ \Sym_L^G(f) = \Sym_R^{G^{\op}}(f) , \]
where $f$ is any probability density on $G$. 

\begin{proof}
Denote the group operation on $G$ by $\cdot$ and on $G^{\op}$ by $\cdot^{\op}$. 
Note that for any $\mu$-measurable $A \subseteq G^{op}$ and $x \in G^{op}$, 
\[ \mu(A\cdot^{\op} x) 
= \mu(\{ a \cdot^{\op} x \mid a \in A \})
= \mu(\{ xa \mid a \in A \})
= \mu(x\cdot A) 
= \mu(A)
\]
So indeed $\mu$ is a right Haar measure on $G^{\op}$. 

Now take $f,g$ to be probability densities with respect to $\mu$ in $G$. 
Since $G$ and $G^{\op}$ have the same topology, $f,g$ are also probability densities on $G^{\op}$. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
\Sym_R^{G^{\op}}(f)
&= \{ g \mid \forall y \quad (f *^{\op} g)(y) 
                           = (f *^{\op} g)(y^{-1})  \} \\
&= \left\{ g \mid \forall y \quad \int_{G^{\op}} f(w) g(w^{-1}y) \,d\mu(w) 
                           = \int_{G^{\op}} f(w) g(w^{-1}y^{-1}) \,d\mu(w) \right\} \\

&= \left\{ g \mid \forall y \quad \int_{G} g(s) f(ys^{-1}) \,d\mu(s) 
                           = \int_{G} g(s) f(y^{-1}s^{-1}) \,d\mu(s) \right\} \\
&= \{ g \mid \forall y \quad (g * f)(y) 
                           = (g * f)(y^{-1})  \} \\
&= \Sym_L^{G}(f) .\qedhere
\end{align*}
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.496908+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b931729135640d03b6c4fe1eb338bc5aaefb0c83d4cce9e6a788cde552029029","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm commutation_relation_u0 of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, consider $n$ radial SLEs starting at $e^{i\theta_1}, e^{i\theta_2}, \ldots, e^{i\theta_n} \in \partial \mathbb{D}$, with a marked interior point \( u=0 \).
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] Let the infinitesimal diffusion generators be
    \begin{equation}
     
    \mathcal{M}_i = \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} + b_i(\theta_1, \theta_2, \ldots, \theta_n) \partial_i + \sum_{j \neq i} \cot\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_j,
     \end{equation}
    where \( \partial_i = \partial_{\theta_i} \). If the $n$ SLEs locally commute, the associated infinitesimal generators satisfy:
    \[
    [\mathcal{M}_i, \mathcal{M}_j] = \frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right)} (\mathcal{M}_j - \mathcal{M}_i).
    \]

    There exists a positive function $\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta})$, defined on $\mathfrak{X}^n(\boldsymbol{\theta})$, such that the drift term satisfies
    \[
    b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \kappa \partial_i \log \psi,
    \]
    and $\psi$ satisfies the null vector equations:
    \begin{equation}
    \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} \psi + \sum_{j \neq i} \cot\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_i \psi + \left(1 - \frac{6}{\kappa}\right) \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{1}{4 \sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right)} \psi - h_j(\theta_j) \psi = 0,
    \end{equation}
    for \( i = 1, 2, \ldots, n \), with undetermined functions $h_j(\theta_j)$.

    \item[(ii)] By analyzing the asymptotic behavior of two adjacent growth points \( \theta_i \) and \( \theta_{i+1} \) (with no marked points between them), we further deduce that \( h_i(\theta) = h_{i+1}(\theta) \). Consequently, if all growth points are consecutive with no marked points between them, there exists a common function $h(\theta)$ such that
    \[
    h(\theta) = h_1(\theta) = \cdots = h_n(\theta).
    \]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["a well-defined electrical network with nonnegative conductances, on a finite graph or an infinite graph with appropriate limiting or boundary conditions","the comparison is between two networks differing only in conductance values on a common edge set, or related by a clean edge addition, deletion, or vertex identification","finite total energy for the relevant flows or potentials, so the variational characterization is well posed","for random-walk conclusions, the standard correspondence between the electrical network and a reversible Markov chain"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.993128+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b9387245512e1cdb33d492e04652cfd536ce550cebd97a2fc52f4dd9dc6c0a91","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For an electrical network on a graph with nonnegative edge conductances c_e, the effective resistance R_eff(a,b) between vertices a, b is defined variationally, via Thomson's principle, as the minimum of sum_e (1/c_e) i_e^2 over unit flows i from a to b obeying Kirchhoff's node law, or equivalently via Dirichlet's principle over voltage functions. Rayleigh's monotonicity law states that R_eff(a,b) is monotone nonincreasing as a function of each conductance: increasing any conductance, adding an edge, or short-circuiting (identifying) any pair of vertices can only decrease or preserve R_eff(a,b), while decreasing a conductance, or deleting an edge, can only increase or preserve it. This purely variational fact underlies comparisons between random walks on different graphs via the resistance-recurrence correspondence, that a network is recurrent for its associated random walk if and only if R_eff(a,infinity)=infinity, comparisons of hitting and commute times, and resistance-based bounds on percolation-type crossing quantities. It gives only monotone comparisons, no quantitative rates, and using it for random-walk conclusions requires the standard electrical network-reversible Markov chain correspondence, with conductances proportional to transition rates, to be correctly set up first. Typical failure: Applying Rayleigh monotonicity to compare effective resistances between two networks that differ in more than conductance values on a shared edge set, such as networks on genuinely different vertex sets or after a modification that is not literally a conductance increase/decrease, edge addition/deletion, or vertex identification; the monotonicity is a coupling statement about the same underlying network with modified weights, and applying it across structurally different networks without an explicit embedding produces an unjustified comparison. Canonical reference: Rayleigh, 1871, Philosophical Magazine; Doyle and Snell, Random Walks and Electric Networks, 1984, Mathematical Association of America; Lyons and Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks, 2016, Cambridge University Press.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a Banach space","each T(t) is bounded and linear","T(0) = I and the semigroup law holds","strong continuity: T(t)x → x as t ↓ 0 for each x"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.769697+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator semigroups, evolution equations","id":"claim_b969493e2925b353157e0667d9f9106cbc5c6f915440e6e0dd0474b82506b5d4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a Banach space. A strongly continuous semigroup (C_0-semigroup) on X is a family (T(t))_{t ≥ 0} of bounded linear operators on X with T(0) = I, T(t + s) = T(t)T(s) for all t, s ≥ 0, and t ↦ T(t)x continuous from [0, ∞) to X for every x ∈ X (for a semigroup this is equivalent to T(t)x → x as t ↓ 0 for every x, and also equivalent to weak continuity, i.e. continuity of t ↦ ⟨T(t)x, x*⟩ on [0, ∞) for every x ∈ X and every x* ∈ X*). Every C_0-semigroup is exponentially bounded: there are M ≥ 1 and ω ∈ ℝ with ‖T(t)‖ ≤ M e^{ωt} for all t ≥ 0; the growth bound is ω_0 = inf of such ω. It is a contraction semigroup if ‖T(t)‖ ≤ 1 for all t, and quasi-contractive if ‖T(t)‖ ≤ e^{ωt}. Its (infinitesimal) generator is the operator A with D(A) = {x ∈ X : lim_{t↓0} (T(t)x − x)/t exists} and Ax equal to that limit. One says A generates T and writes T(t) = e^{tA}. Norm continuity of t ↦ T(t) at 0 (a uniformly continuous semigroup) holds if and only if the generator is bounded, in which case T(t) = Σ t^n A^n / n!; the typical generators of PDE semigroups are unbounded and the semigroup is only strongly continuous.","status":"unverified"}

endpoint sections \(A_t\in G_t\), \(A_0={\mathbf 1}\), equivalently paths
\(A:[0,T]\to G\) in the fixed trivialization.  The correspondence is

 =\bigl(\alpha_{t,s}(A_s)\bigr)^{-1}\star A_t.

In the stochastic category the correspondence is between deterministic-time
characters modulo almost-sure equality and adapted anchors modulo
modification; the identities are initially asserted for each fixed time
tuple.  It becomes a simultaneous pathwise correspondence after the
optional perfection below.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.439961+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b9843edd181c82e5a6b7dd57e5f80e12f4aac4c7a723a284d776abad80edca2a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 144 (Even--odd exterior spectral decoding) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $A\in\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sk}$ have positive skew singular values
$a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots$, and let
$\mathscr E(x,A)=\sum_{k\ge0}\Xi_k(x,A)$.  Define
\[
 \mathscr D_A(z):=\prod_{j\ge1}(1+za_j^2),
 \qquad z\in\mathbb C.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 
 \mathscr D_A(z)
 =\sum_{N\ge0}\frac{z^N}{4^N}\|\Xi_{2N}(x,A)\|^2,
 \qquad
 \det(\operatorname{Id}+zA^*A)=\mathscr D_A(z)^2.
\end{equation}
In particular, the even energy sequence determines the complete multiset of
nonzero positive skew singular values.

For $z>0$,
\begin{equation}
 
 \sum_{N\ge0}\frac{z^N}{4^N}\|\Xi_{2N+1}(x,A)\|^2
 =\mathscr D_A(z)
 \left\langle(\operatorname{Id}+zA^*A)^{-1}x,x\right\rangle.
\end{equation}
In particular, evaluating the even and odd series at $z=4$ gives the exact
Fock norm
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathscr E(x,A)\|_{\mathscr F^\wedge}^2
 =\mathscr D_A(4)
 \left(1+\left\langle
   (\operatorname{Id}+4A^*A)^{-1}x,x
 \right\rangle\right).}
\end{equation}
Thus \eqref{eq:exterior-Fock-bound} is a direct consequence of
$\mathscr D_A(4)\le\exp(4\|\alpha_A\|^2)$ and
$(\operatorname{Id}+4A^*A)^{-1}\preceq I$.
Consequently, after the even sequence has determined $\mathscr D_A$, the odd
sequence determines the cyclic spectral measure
\[
 \nu_{x,A}(B):=
 \left\langle E_{A^*A}(B)x,x\right\rangle,
 \qquad B\subset[0,\infty)\text{ Borel},
\]
through
\begin{equation}
 
 \frac{\sum_{N\ge0}4^{-N}z^N\|\Xi_{2N+1}(x,A)\|^2}
      {\mathscr D_A(z)}
 =\int_{[0,\infty)}\frac{1}{1+z\lambda}\,
   \dd\nu_{x,A}(\lambda).
\end{equation}
Thus the scalar even--odd exterior response recovers the singular spectrum of
$A$ and the energy of $x$ in every $A^*A$-spectral subspace.  Directions inside a degenerate spectral subspace remain unresolved by these scalar spectral data.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.391534+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b9dc1bca41b2a392927360eca57927efffdc3c40b6ca86258570c4dd7831a905","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Def-BRW of arXiv:2507.19554, 'Full extremal process in four-dimensional membrane model'] Denote $N = 2^n$. For $k = 0, 1, \cdots, n$, let $\mcB_k$ denote the collection of subsets of $\mbZ^4$ consisting of 4-cubes of side-length $2^k$ with corners in $\mbZ^4$, and let $\mathcal{BD}_k$ denote the collection of subsets of $\mbZ^4$ consisting of 4-cubes of the form $\lp \lb 0, 2^k - 1 \rb \cap \mbZ \rp^4 + \lp i2^k, j2^k, m2^k, n2^k \rp$. For $v \in V_N$, let $\mcB_k\lp v \rp(\mathcal{BD}_k\lp v \rp)$ denote the elements in $\mathcal{B}_k (\mathcal{BD}_k)$ that contain $v$. 			\theta_{v}^N = \sum_{i = 0}^n \sum_{B \in \mathcal{BD}_k\lp v \rp} a_{k, B}.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:13:21.347153+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_b9e0b4274124b41385f78ad391ae25b11f3fa50aa6a991f1193ffe25a0426288","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 5 (PGF via Incomplete Gamma Function) of arXiv:2609.01559, 'Erlang Loss Model with Energy Constrained Servers'] Let $(Q,C)$ have the truncated bivariate Poisson distribution with parameters
\[
\rho_Q = \frac{\lambda}{\mu}, \quad
\rho_C = \frac{\lambda p}{\gamma}, \quad
\rho = \rho_Q + \rho_C, \quad
Z_k = \sum_{n=0}^k \frac{\rho^n}{n!}.
\]
and truncation at $k$. Then the bivariate PGF is given by
\[
G(s,t) = \mathbb{E}[ s^Q t^C ] =  \frac{\Gamma(k+1, \rho - (\rho_Q s + \rho_C t))}{\Gamma(k+1, \rho)}.
\]
\begin{proof} 

We have the following expression
\begin{align}
G(s,t) &= \frac{1}{Z_k} \sum_{n=0}^{k} \frac{\rho^n}{n!} \sum_{q=0}^{n} \binom{n}{q} \alpha^q (1-\alpha)^{n-q} s^q t^{\,n-q} \nonumber \\
&= \frac{1}{Z_k} \sum_{n=0}^{k} \frac{\rho^n}{n!} (\alpha s + (1-\alpha) t)^n \nonumber \\
&= \frac{1}{Z_k} \sum_{n=0}^{k} \frac{\big(\rho_Q s + \rho_C t \big)^n}{n!} \nonumber\\
&= \frac{1}{Z_k} \sum_{n=0}^{k} \frac{(\rho_Q s + \rho_C t)^n}{n!} \nonumber\\
&= \frac{\Gamma(k+1)}{\Gamma(k+1,\rho)} e^{-(\rho - \rho_Q s - \rho_C t)} 
\sum_{n=0}^{k} \frac{(\rho_Q s + \rho_C t)^n}{n!} e^{-(\rho_Q s + \rho_C t)} \nonumber\\
&= \frac{\Gamma(k+1)}{\Gamma(k+1,\rho)} \, e^{-(\rho - \rho_Q s - \rho_C t)} \, \frac{\Gamma(k+1, \rho - (\rho_Q s + \rho_C t))}{\Gamma(k+1)} \nonumber\\
&= \frac{\Gamma(k+1, \rho - (\rho_Q s + \rho_C t))}{\Gamma(k+1, \rho)}.
\end{align}
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

        g_s(z):=\sum_{j=1}^m(s_j-1)\mathbf 1_{A_j}(z),

Then \(M_{g_s}K_A\) is trace class and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.679026+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ba23d4db90bab00faa658b1093fc649af70d62ce7fe6b58158854db74f207af6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 28 (Intrinsic principal quadratic response syntax) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] A \emph{principal quadratic response package} on a stopping-stable response
domain is a total causal joint profile
\[
 \mathbf R^{(2)}=(X,\mathcal R_A,\mathcal R_Q)
 \in\widetilde{\mathsf R}_{\mathfrak Q_2}^{\eta}
\]
such that, for every $(s,t)$, the maps in the coefficient variable are the
restrictions to $\mathbb K_A$ and $\mathbb K_Q$ of weakly, respectively
weak-star, continuous linear functionals on
$\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sk}$ and $\mathcal L(H)_{\rm sa}$.  Its restarted
responses satisfy, for $s\le u\le t$,
\begin{align}
 \mathcal R_{A;s,t}(K)
 &=\mathcal R_{A;s,u}(K)+\mathcal R_{A;u,t}(K)
   +\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[K^*\Anti
      (X_{s,u}\otimes X_{u,t})\right],
 \qquad K\in\mathbb K_A,
 \\
 \mathcal R_{Q;s,t}(S)
 &=\mathcal R_{Q;s,u}(S)+\mathcal R_{Q;u,t}(S),
 \qquad S\in\mathbb K_Q.
 
\end{align}
The \emph{intrinsic principal quadratic response syntax}, denoted
$\mathfrak Q_2^{\circ}(H)$, is generated under finite products and
stable-causal postcomposition by the restriction of this package to the
smooth finite-rank coherent source class in
\eqref{eq:coherent-core-response-profile}.  Its canonical stable response
completion $\mathfrak Q_2(H)$ is defined in
\Cref{def:coherent-principal-response-target}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:25:12.191649+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ba2c8b0358e7948fb04d3f38ccc9b080e66fab12b80d483af1b17d61c33b5e22","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Pro 6 of arXiv:2510.21446, '{Uniqueness of adapted solutions to scalar BSDEs\\ with Peano-type generators}\tnoteref{fo'] Suppose that $\xi\in L^p(\R_+)$ for $p>1$, $(L_t)_{t\in\T}$ is an $(\F_t)$-progressively measurable nondecreasing process with $L_0=0$, and the function $g(\omega,t,y,z):\Omega\times\T\times\R_+\times \R^{1\times d}$ is $(\F_t)$-progressively measurable for each $(y,z)\in \R_+\times \R^{1\times d}$ such that $\as$,
$$
g(\omega,t,y,z)\leq f_t(\omega)+\mu |y|+\lambda |z|, \quad (y,z)\in \R_+\times \R^{1\times d},
$$
with $f_\cdot\in \lcal^p(\R_+)$, and $\mu,\lambda\geq 0$ are two nonnegative constants. Let $(Y_t,Z_t)_{t\in\T}$ be an adapted solution of the following BSDE
$$
Y_t=\xi+\int_t^T g(s,Y_s,Z_s){\rm d}s-\int_t^T{\rm d}L_s -\int_t^T Z_s {\rm d}B_s, \ \ t\in\T.
$$
If $Y_\cdot\in\scal^p(\R_{+})$, then $Z_\cdot\in\mcal^p(\R^{1\times d})$ and there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that for each $a\geq \mu+\lambda^2$ and $t\in\T$, we have
$$
\E\left[\left.\left(\int_0^T {\rm e}^{2as}|Z_s|^2 {\rm d}s\right)^{\frac{p}{2}}\right|\F_t\right]
\leq C_p \E\left[\left.\sup\limits_{t\in\T} \left({\rm e}^{apt}|Y_t|^p\right)+\left(\int_0^T {\rm e}^{as}f_s {\rm d}s\right)^p\right|\F_t\right].
$$
Moreover, there exists a constant $\bar C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that for each $a\geq \mu+\lambda^2/[1\wedge (p-1)]$ and $t\in\T$, we have
$$
\E\left[\left.\sup\limits_{t\in\T} \left({\rm e}^{apt}|Y_t|^p\right)+\left(\int_0^T {\rm e}^{2as}|Z_s|^2 {\rm d}s\right)^{\frac{p}{2}}\right|\F_t\right]
\leq \bar C_p \E\left[\left. {\rm e}^{apT}|\xi|^p +\left(\int_0^T {\rm e}^{as}f_s {\rm d}s\right)^p\right|\F_t\right].
$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.644900+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ba82d5c3ae169f44f642125574eddc29a0eec3d9ef0b0eec62da8b3fa48128ad","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def:TSAW of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a vertex $v$, the \emph{tree of self avoiding walks} is the tree $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}$ obtained from $(G,v)$ as follows.
    Fix a total ordering of the vertices of $G$.
    We define the tree $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}$ recursively. 
    If the component of $G$ containing $v$ consists of a single vertex $v$, then $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}=\{v\}$.
    In case the component of $G$ containing $v$ consists of more than $1$ vertex, let $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ denote the neighbours of $v$ in $G$.
    Let for $i=1\ldots d$, $G_i$ be the graph obtained from $G$ by removing $v,v_1,\ldots,v_{i-1}$ from $G$.
    Denote for $i=1,\ldots, d$, $T_i=T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G_{i},v_{i})}$.
    Then $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}$ is defined as the tree obtained from the disjoint union of the $T_i$ adding a vertex $v$ connecting it to each of the $v_1,\ldots,v_d$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:43:00.034567+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ba998fc75283271018c7bee73db81395ab2f4431f1d29af5e05564ad4e7fb397","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 5 (Bethuel's interior theorem) of arXiv:2609.00739, '2609.00739'] Let $D\subset\subset\R^2$ be a bounded smooth domain, and let $v_j$ solve
\begin{equation}

\end{equation}
where $\eps_j\to0$ and
\[
 \cE_{\eps_j}(v_j;D)\leq M.
\]
After passing to a subsequence, there exist a closed countably
$1$-rectifiable set $S_D\subset D$ and Radon measures
$\upnu_D$, $\upzeta_D$, and $\upmu_{D,i\ell}$,
$i,\ell\in\{1,2\}$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \left[\frac{\eps_j}{2}\abs{\nabla v_j}^2
       +\frac{1}{\eps_j}V(v_j)\right]\dd x
 &\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\upnu_D,\\
 \frac{1}{\eps_j}V(v_j)\dd x
 &\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\upzeta_D,\\
 \eps_j\,\partial_i v_j\cdot\partial_\ell v_j\dd x
 &\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\upmu_{D,i\ell}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
as Radon measures locally in $D$, and the following properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\theenumi)$]
\item There exists a locally constant map
\[
 v_\star:D\backslash S_D\to\Sigma
\]
such that
\[
 v_j\to v_\star

\item The limiting measures are concentrated on $S_D$ and admit the

\begin{equation}
 \upnu_D=e_D\,\cH^1\llcorner S_D,

 \upmu_{D,i\ell}
 =m_{D,i\ell}\,\cH^1\llcorner S_D.
\end{equation}
For every $K\subset\subset D$, there exist constants

\begin{equation}
 e_D=m_{D,nn},

Equivalently, the limiting stress--energy tensor
\begin{equation}

has the representation

\begin{equation}

\end{equation}

\item There exists a set $N_D\subset S_D$ with
$\cH^1(N_D)=0$ such that, for every $x\in S_D\backslash N_D$, there are

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:44:39.744180+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_baa0c5750edf13d2bf2a79502e882f1c7a537514c09efc8bb48bf15384df680f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 4 (Stochastic domination) of arXiv:2608.29872, 'Local Laws and Outlier Eigenvalues for Spiked Separable Covariance Matrices'] (i) Let
\[\xi=\left(\xi^{(n)}(u):n\in\bb N, u\in U^{(n)}\right),\quad \zeta=\left(\zeta^{(n)}(u):n\in\bb N, u\in U^{(n)}\right)\]
be two families of non-negative random variables, where $U^{(n)}$ is a parameter set depending on $n$. We say that $\xi$ is stochastically dominated by $\zeta$, uniformly in $u$, if for any fixed (small) $\epsilon>0$ and (large) $D>0$, 
\[\sup_{u\in U^{(n)}}\bb P\left[\xi^{(n)}(u)>n^\epsilon\zeta^{(n)}(u)\right]\le n^{-D}\]
holds for large enough $n\ge n_0(\epsilon, D)$, denoted by $\xi\prec\zeta$. Throughout this paper, the stochastic domination will always be uniform in all parameters that are not explicitly fixed (such as matrix indices, and $z$ that takes values in some compact set). Note that $n_0(\epsilon, D)$ may depend on quantities that are explicitly constant, such as $\tau$ in Assumption \ref{assm_big1} and \eqref{assm_gap}. If for some complex family $\xi$ we have $|\xi|\prec\zeta$, then we will also write $\xi \prec \zeta$ or $\xi=\OO_\prec(\zeta)$.
\medskip

\noindent (ii) We extend the definition of $\OO_\prec(\cdot)$ to matrices in the weak operator sense as follows. Let $A$ be a family of random matrices and $\zeta$ be a family of nonnegative random variables. Then $A=\OO_\prec(\zeta)$ means that $\left|\left\langle\mathbf v, A\mathbf w\right\rangle\right|\prec\zeta \| \mathbf v\|_2 \|\mathbf w\|_2 $ uniformly in any deterministic vectors $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$. Here and throughout the following, whenever we say ``uniformly in any deterministic vectors", we mean that ``uniformly in any deterministic vectors belonging to certain fixed set of cardinality $n^{\OO(1)}$".

\medskip

\noindent (iii) We say that an event $\Xi$ holds with high probability if $\mathbbm{1}_{\Xi^c}\prec0$, or equivalently, for any constant $D>0$, $\mathbb P(\Xi)\ge 1- n^{-D}$ for large enough $n$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu is a probability measure","T is measure-preserving, not necessarily invertible","mu(A) > 0","the value 1/mu(A) for the mean return time requires ergodicity; the general identity does not"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T12:13:53+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, recurrence, induced maps","id":"claim_baade9096b6824c73152f5700a64977d653156c661b715154a8e597b0e136142","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space, $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving (not necessarily invertible), $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, and $n_A(x) = \min\{n \ge 1 : T^n x \in A\}$ the first return time (finite for a.e. $x \in A$ by Poincare recurrence; set $n_A = \infty$ where no return occurs). Then, in general,
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = \mu\Big(\bigcup_{j \ge 0} T^{-j} A\Big),$$
the measure of the set of points whose forward orbit ever meets $A$. In particular $\int_A n_A\,d\mu \le 1$ always, so $n_A$ is integrable over $A$ for EVERY positive-measure set in a probability-preserving system, ergodic or not. If $T$ is ERGODIC, the union has full measure and
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = 1, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \frac{1}{\mu(A)} \int_A n_A\,d\mu = \frac{1}{\mu(A)}:$$
the mean return time to $A$, with respect to the normalised measure $\mu_A = \mu(\cdot \cap A)/\mu(A)$, is exactly $1/\mu(A)$. The induced (first-return) map $T_A = T^{n_A}$ on $A$ preserves $\mu_A$. When $T$ is invertible and ergodic, $(X, \mu, T)$ is isomorphic mod 0 to the tower (Kakutani skyscraper) over $(A, \mu_A, T_A)$ with height $n_A$, of total mass $\int_A n_A\,d\mu / \mu(A)$ in units of $\mu_A$; for non-invertible $T$ the tower map $(x, j) \mapsto T^j x$ is in general only a factor map (for the doubling map with $A = [0, 1/2)$ it is many-to-one).

WHERE IT FAILS. (1) Without ergodicity the mean return time can be strictly less than $1/\mu(A)$: if $A$ is itself invariant then $n_A = 1$ on $A$ and $\int_A n_A = \mu(A) < 1$. (2) In an infinite measure space $\int_A n_A\,d\mu$ can be infinite even for a conservative ergodic $T$ (in fact for an ergodic conservative infinite-measure system it is always infinite for sets of finite positive measure), so 'mean return time $= 1/\mu(A)$' is a finite-measure statement. (3) The lemma controls only the MEAN of $n_A$: no bound on its variance or tail follows; $n_A$ need not be in $L^2$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.822289+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_baf5e47187f91040484bfb7aaa40f81cd892329cac0240baf3e68d8d844bbe86","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:addition-type-frequency of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$.  For a strictly increasing
$a=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$, let $\mathsf T_h(a)$ be the equivalence relation on
$\mathcal U_{h,k}$ defined by
\[
 u\sim_{\mathsf T_h(a)}v
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\cdot a=v\cdot a.
\]
Equivalently, after quotienting the forced permutation symmetries, this is
O'Bryant's weak type of the $h$-fold addition table
[OBryant2025].
Let $\mathfrak T_{h,k}$ be the finite set of types realized by strictly
increasing integer $k$-tuples.  For $\mathsf T\in\mathfrak T_{h,k}$, put
\[
 r(\mathsf T)=\dim_{\mathbb R}
 \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
 \{u-v:u\sim_{\mathsf T}v\}
\]
and
\[
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q)=
 \#\left\{A\in\binom{[q]}k:\mathsf T_h(A)=\mathsf T\right\}.
\]
Then $F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q)$ is a quasipolynomial in $q-1$, valid for
every positive integer $q$, of degree exactly $k-r(\mathsf T)$.  In
particular, there is an effectively computable
$c_{h,k,\mathsf T}\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q)
 =c_{h,k,\mathsf T}q^{k-r(\mathsf T)}
  +O_{h,k,\mathsf T}\!\left(q^{k-r(\mathsf T)-1}\right).
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathsf T\in\mathfrak T_{h,k}\\
 |\mathcal U_{h,k}/\mathsf T|=n}}
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q).
\end{equation}
Hence summing over weak types with $n$ equivalence classes recovers
Theorem~(thm:rank-frequency of the paper).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.540266+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bb24e81ec438e42a0c90a144e24a2769f3d899f78c54b6945278ad382471f715","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 (XY model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{XY model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-\beta H_{\XYM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \[
        H_{\XYM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\sigma) := \sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}} |\sigma_x-\sigma_y|^2/2 + \sum_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}} |\sigma_x-\zeta_y|^2/2.
    \]
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c=\beta_c(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\XY,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c)$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\XY, \beta}$.
    The label $\XYM$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:20:30.648187+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bb31ef58169bfbb0cc10bab607741f05c8e26d489b9fa4c5de1b4e33e033efcc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 39 of arXiv:2609.01932, 'Essential dimension and faithful rank of finite $p$-gerbes'] Choose a $P$-representation $W$ with a nonempty $P$-stable open subset

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:12:19.524803+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bb33752dc9d8c5978f4d5afa7cca6a07fa9ea2c8a4c3176d0928cfe11ed612e5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] There exists a universal constant \(C>0\) such that the following

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:17.753019+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bb6a4eeb23cb1c17de894a67784a89caf55ae97ac0b0aad0f458bdaba9ff2623","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 6 of arXiv:2511.02763, 'The Cayley-Moser problem with Poissonian arrival of offers'] The cumulative density of the sale price $S_t$ is given by

{"assumptions":["U is a linear subspace of R^M","dim U <= d for the inequality","for equality: dim U = d, and every d or fewer of the coordinate functionals restricted to U are linearly independent"],"created_at":"2026-08-20T03:43:30.215160+00:00","domain":"discrete geometry","id":"claim_bb6c5c4ccc460699ad754fdb8735e36361abd65388bbb9e05772a7ab373d6240","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $U$ be a linear subspace of $\\mathbb{R}^M$ with $\\dim U \\le d$, and let $r(U)$ be the number of open coordinate orthants of $\\mathbb{R}^M$ that $U$ meets. Then $r(U) \\le 2\\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\\binom{M-1}{j}$. If $U$ lies inside a coordinate hyperplane then $r(U)=0$. If $\\dim U = d$ and the $M$ coordinate functionals restricted to $U$ are in general position, meaning every $d$ or fewer of them are linearly independent, then equality holds. Equivalently, $M$ points in general position in $\\mathbb{R}^d$ admit exactly $2\\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\\binom{M-1}{j}$ homogeneously linearly separable dichotomies.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:07:15.758120+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bb6caa765d58c50452b53ff75977f76309e7250fe893f236f044eed7620147f3","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:finite-energy-potential of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $\nu,\eta\in\mathcal M_{\rm fe}(D)$.  Then $I_D(|\nu|,|\eta|)<\infty$, so the mutual Green
energy $I_D(\nu,\eta)$ is well defined.  For each
$\sigma\in\{\nu,\eta\}$ there is a unique $U_D\sigma\inH$ characterized by
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E(U_D\sigma,v)=\int_D\widetilde v\,d\sigma,
 \qquad v\inH.
 
\end{equation}
Its quasi-continuous representative is
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{U_D\sigma}(z)
 =\int_DG_D(z,w)\,\sigma(dw)
 \qquad\text{for $\mathcal E$-q.e. }z\in D,
 
\end{equation}
where the signed integral is taken through the Jordan decomposition.  In
addition,
\begin{align}
 I_D(\nu,\eta)
 &=\mathcal E(U_D\nu,U_D\eta),
 \\
 |I_D(\nu,\eta)|
 &\le I_D(\nu)^{1/2}I_D(\eta)^{1/2},
 \\
 \|U_D\nu\|_{H}^2
 &=I_D(\nu),
 \qquad
 \langleU_D\nu,f\rangle_{H}=\int_D\widetilde f\,d\nu,
 \quad f\inH.
 
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu is a probability measure","T is measure-preserving, not necessarily invertible","mu(A) > 0","the value 1/mu(A) for the mean return time requires ergodicity; the general identity does not"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T02:00:35.438087+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, recurrence, induced maps","id":"claim_bb6dcbe5ce02085d2e2e48afcaee2028d3f09a38e89e185dcbbbb02136dd47f5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space, $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving (not necessarily invertible), $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, and $n_A(x) = \min\{n \ge 1 : T^n x \in A\}$ the first return time (finite for a.e. $x \in A$ by Poincare recurrence; set $n_A = \infty$ where no return occurs). Then, in general,
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = \mu\Big(\bigcup_{j \ge 0} T^{-j} A\Big),$$
the measure of the set of points whose forward orbit ever meets $A$. In particular $\int_A n_A\,d\mu \le 1$ always, so $n_A$ is integrable over $A$ for EVERY positive-measure set in a probability-preserving system, ergodic or not. If $T$ is ERGODIC, the union has full measure and
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = 1, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \frac{1}{\mu(A)} \int_A n_A\,d\mu = \frac{1}{\mu(A)}:$$
the mean return time to $A$, with respect to the normalised measure $\mu_A = \mu(\cdot \cap A)/\mu(A)$, is exactly $1/\mu(A)$. Equivalently, the induced (first-return) map $T_A = T^{n_A}$ on $A$ preserves $\mu_A$ and $(X, \mu, T)$ is recovered from $(A, \mu_A, T_A, n_A)$ as a tower of total mass $\int_A n_A\,d\mu / \mu(A)$.

WHERE IT FAILS. (1) Without ergodicity the mean return time can be strictly less than $1/\mu(A)$: if $A$ is itself invariant then $n_A = 1$ on $A$ and $\int_A n_A = \mu(A) < 1$. (2) In an infinite measure space $\int_A n_A\,d\mu$ can be infinite even for a conservative ergodic $T$ (in fact for an ergodic conservative infinite-measure system it is always infinite for sets of finite positive measure), so 'mean return time $= 1/\mu(A)$' is a finite-measure statement. (3) The lemma controls only the MEAN of $n_A$: no bound on its variance or tail follows; $n_A$ need not be in $L^2$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.566543+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bb9f91c11bbcbb3d5b818ceff586b0b5299738dc5e4dae9ad98838b592cd12dc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 16 (Tripartite orientation class) of arXiv:2608.26516, '2608.26516'] For every integer $m\ge2$, set $N_m:=2^{m-1}$ and let $G_m=K_{N_m,N_m,N_m}$ be the complete tripartite graph whose three vertex parts each have cardinality $N_m$. Write $E_m$ for its edge set, so $|E_m|=3N_m^2$ and every vertex has degree $2N_m$.

Let $X_m:=\{0,1\}^{E_m}$ denote the set of all orientations of $G_m$, where the bit indexed by an edge determines which endpoint is its head. For $z\in X_m$ and $e=\{u,v\}\in E_m$, write $\operatorname{head}_z(e)\in\{u,v\}$ for the head of $e$ in the orientation $z$. The vertex sets of the graphs $G_m$ are pairwise disjoint and serve as labels, and the full domain is $\CX^{\mathrm{or}}:=\bigsqcup_{m\ge2}X_m$.

For every edge $e=\{u,v\}\in E_m$, fix one distinguished endpoint $\ell(e)\in\{u,v\}$ and define
\[
    h_e(x)
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \operatorname{head}_x(e),
            & x\in X_m,\\
        \ell(e),
            & x\notin X_m.
    \end{cases}
\]
The \edefn{tripartite orientation class} is $\Hor:=\{h_e:e\in E_m,\ m\ge2\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:44:27.903838+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bbb809515616a783f0c0917647a9502220a6adee29ae22b1068da7aa5c3bc432","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2607.12666, 'Sample-path Large deviations for \\Scheduled Arrival Processes with Unpunctuality'] The sequence $\{\bar A^{(n)}\}_{n\ge1}$ satisfies a large deviations principle on $D([0,T])$, equipped with the Skorokhod $J_1$ topology, with speed $n$ and good rate function
\[
I_T(\phi)
=
\sup_{m\ge1}\sup_{0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T}
I_{t_1,\dots,t_m}\bigl(\phi(t_1),\dots,\phi(t_m)\bigr),
\]
where, for each $0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T$,
\[
I_{t_1,\dots,t_m}(x)
=
\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^m}
\left\{
\sum_{\ell=1}^m \alpha_\ell x_\ell-\Lambda_{t_1,\dots,t_m}(\alpha)
\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the rate function admits the variational representation
\begin{equation}
    I_T(\phi) = \sup_{\theta\in C([0,T]),\gamma\in\R} \left\{ \int_0^T \theta(t) \phi(t)\, dt + \gamma\phi(T) - \Lambda_T(\theta,\gamma)\right\},
\end{equation}
with $\Lambda_T(\theta,\gamma)$ given by
\begin{equation}
    \Lambda_T(\theta,\gamma):=\log \E \exp \left(\int_0^T \theta(t)A(t)\, dt + \gamma A(T)\right).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:04:55.819192+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bbba18cefc3407dbe8b20271a318a6d89b2487c3657b49b56950369ba33a5046","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def_elementaty_curve of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow\Sigma$ be a $\mathcal{C}^1$ curve. We say that $\gamma$ is of elementary type if $\gamma([0,1])$ is transverse\footnote{It precisely means that, for every $t\in[0,1]$, $\text{Span}\{\gamma'(t),V(\gamma(t))\}=T_{\gamma(t)}\Sigma$.} to the flow lines of $\varphi_f^t$, $\gamma((0,1))\subset W^u(a_1)$ and if
$$
N(\gamma):=\sharp \gamma(\{0,1\})\cap (\Sigma\setminus W^u(a_1))\leq 1.
$$
Equivalently, $\gamma$ cuts at most once the union $\cup_{ \mathrm{ind} (a)=1}W^u(a)$ of unstable curves and only at endpoints.

An elementary curve is said to be \textbf{positively (resp. negatively) $V$-oriented} if, for every $t\in[0,1]$, $\gamma'(t)\wedge V(\gamma(t))$ has the same (resp. opposite) orientation compared to $\Sigma$. A $V$-oriented elementary curve is said to be \textbf{primitive} if the map
$$
(s,t)\in(0,1)\times\mathbb{R}_+\mapsto\varphi_f^{-t}(\gamma(s))
$$
is injective.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:14:46.483218+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bbbc3409ced9f2db2bcc2f28d51145dab1af76efc93108911caeb15723bb79ac","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The axioms for probability theory are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item A probability space is a measured space $(X,M,\nu)$ of mass one, $\nu(X)=1$.

\item A random variable on $X$ is a real measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb R$.

\item The expectation of $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is its integral, $E(f)=\int_Xf(x)d\nu(x)$.

\item The law of $f$ is the real probability measure $\mu=f_*\nu$, push-forward of $\nu$ by $f$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.346762+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bbc2bafb891aee173d5635f3b393a3305101bdc2922d2e3a43e5ecdb751f17b9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 147 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $Z$ be a standard gaussian random variable, and suppose $Y(q_0)\sim\zeta^\Ising$ satisfies assumption~\eqref{i:IAMP-main-init} of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}. Then for any $\eta>0$ there exists an odd function $\prxpsi:\bbR\to\bbR$ with bounded Lipschitz norm $\|\prxpsi\|_{\textup{Lip}}\leq \overline{L}(\eta,\zeta^{\Ising})$ such that $\bbW_2\big(\prxpsi(Z),\zeta^{\Ising}\big)\leq \eta$. Additionally, we have $|\bbE[\prxpsi(Z)^2] - q_0| \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}$.

\begin{proof}
    Using a standard quantile coupling, there exists an odd measurable function $\hat\psi\in L^2(\bbR)$ such that the law of $\hat\psi(Z)$ is precisely $\zeta^{\Ising}$. Since bounded Lipschitz functions are dense in $L^2$, there exists a bounded Lipschitz function $\tilde\psi:\bbR\to\bbR$ with $\bbW_2\big(\tilde\psi(Z),\zeta^{\Ising}\big)\leq \min\{\eta, \epsilon^{1/2}\}$.
The first assertion of the lemma immediately follows by taking $\prxpsi=\tilde\psi$.  For the second assertion, recall that under assumption~\eqref{i:IAMP-main-init} of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}, the random variable $Y(q_0)\sim\zeta^\Ising$ satisfies
	\[\Big|\E[Y(q_0)^2-q_0]
	\Big|\le\epsilon\,.\]
Under the $\bbW_2$-optimal coupling of $\prxpsi(Z)$ with $Y(q_0)$, we have
	\begin{align*}
	&\bigg|\E[\prxpsi(Z)^2]
	-\E[Y(q_0)^2] \bigg|
	=\bigg|\E\Big[
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0))
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0)
		+2Y(q_0))
	\Big]\bigg|\\
	&\qquad=\bigg| \E\Big[
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0))^2
	\Big]
	+ 2\E\Big[
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0)) Y(q_0)\Big]
	\bigg|
	\le \epsilon + 2 \epsilon^{1/2}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:16:35.596991+00:00","domain":"statistical learning theory","id":"claim_bbd3a83729c8d9e501cff01bc27d1df869d97b124fee1913e254632b046cae12","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For kernel ridge regression with power-law spectrum $\\eta_k = k^{-\\alpha}$ ($\\alpha>1$, the capacity) and teacher coefficients $\\theta_k = k^{-(1+\\alpha(2r-1))/2}$ ($r \\ge 0$, the source), with label noise of variance $\\sigma^2$ and ridge $\\lambda = n^{-\\ell}$, the excess risk of the ridgeless estimator ($\\ell \\ge \\alpha$, including interpolation) is of order $\\max(\\sigma^2, n^{-2\\alpha\\min(r,1)})$, while the optimally regularised excess risk is of order $n^{-2\\alpha\\min(r,1)}$ for $n$ below a crossover $n_* \\asymp \\sigma^{-1/(\\alpha\\min(r,1))}$ and of order $n^{1/(1+2\\alpha\\min(r,1)) - 1}$ above it (Cui, Loureiro, Krzakala, Zdeborova, NeurIPS 2021). Two consequences that a learning-curve experiment can test directly: (i) with no label noise the interpolant is the optimum of the whole path, so the ratio of the interpolant's risk to the best risk on the path is $1$; (ii) with noise, once $n$ is past the crossover, that ratio grows like $n^{2\\alpha\\min(r,1)/(1+2\\alpha\\min(r,1))}$, and a tenfold increase in the noise level moves the crossover by a factor $10^{1/(\\alpha\\min(r,1))}$ in $n$. Both exponents are read off the Gram spectrum and the labels of the same fit, so the prediction and the measurement come from one object. (For a Burgers-equation emulation corpus at $n=4000$ the estimates are $\\hat\\alpha = 2.02$, $\\hat r = 0.63$, giving a growth exponent $0.72$ and a crossover exponent $0.78$; the noiseless ratio measured $1.00$.)","status":"unverified"}

$$
where $\mathcal{U}^{[m]}_{\lambda,\eps}v_0$ denotes the trace at $s=m$ of the solution to \eqref{eq:abstract elliptic equation} with boundary conditions $v(x,y,0)=v_0$, and $v(x,y,T)=C_{u,T,\lambda}^{-1}(x,y) B(F_{u,T}(\kappa_u(x,y)),T)$, where $B(x,y,z)$ is the solution to \eqref{eq:elliptic evolution} with $B(x,y,0)=B_{\mathrm{in}}$, satisfying the growth condition of Lemma \ref{lemma:notion of solution}, and $T>m$. $$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.451903+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bbdad552f095eb5ad2bdb21fe9f9b9c2ab986e2d763b3f00c67ccc04b85557ff","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Consider the following maps:
    
    \begin{enumerate}[font=\normalfont,label=(\roman*)]
    
        \item $T_{\sigma,\nu}:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell,m}$ for $\sigma,\nu$ permutations, such that 
        $$ T_{\sigma,\nu}(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_1\otimes \cdots \otimes a_m) = h_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\sigma(l)}\otimes a_{\nu(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{\nu(m)}, $$
        
        \item $\langle f|:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell-1,m}$ such that 
        $$\langle f|(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m) = \langle f| h_1\rangle h_2\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l \otimes a_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{m}, $$
        
        \item given $\cU$ a subset of $\cB$ and $p_{\cU}$ the orthogonal projection on $\spn(\cU)$, $\eta_{\cU}: \cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell-2,m}$ such that 
        $$\eta_{\cU}(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m) = \langle p_{\cU}(h_1)| p_{\cU}(h_2)\rangle h_3\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{m},$$

        \item $m:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell,m-1}$ such that 
        $$ m(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_1\otimes \cdots \otimes a_m) = h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_1a_2\otimes a_3\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m, $$

        \item $\tr:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell,m-1}$ such that 
        $$ \tr(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_1\otimes \cdots \otimes a_m) = \tau(a_1) h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_2\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m. $$

    \end{enumerate}

    \noindent If $\mathbf{f} \in \cC^k(\cB)$, and $\cJ \colon \cA^{j,j+1} \mapsto \cA$ is a linear map built out of the maps above, then given $j_0,\dots,j_n$ such that $j_0+\dots+j_n = j$, we have that $\cJ\circ \widetilde{\partial}^{(j_n)}\circ\cdots\circ \widetilde{\partial}^{(j_1)}\circ \partial^{(j_0)} \mathbf{f} \in \cC^{k-j}(\cB)$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.360381+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bbfda4e6f0c5e19e51593f8e671456cc0b18e76af6dcad38839849dfac646379","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 254 ($\bbW_2$-stability of $\mu_\bG(\bx)$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $\bx,\bx' \in \bbR^N$, we have
    \[
        \bbW_2(\mu_\bG(\bx),\mu_\bG(\bx'))
        \le \frac{\|\bG\|_\op \|\bx-\bx'\|}{(MN)^{1/2}}\,.
    \]
\begin{proof}
The $\bbW_2$ distance can be bounded by
    \[
        \bbW_2(\mu_\bG(\bx),\mu_\bG(\bx'))^2
        \le \frac{1}{M} \sum_{a=1}^M \frac{(\bg^a,\bx-\bx')^2}{N}
        = \frac{\|\bG (\bx-\bx')\|^2}{MN}
        \le \frac{(\|\bG\|_\op \|\bx-\bx'\|)^2}{MN}\,.

{"assumptions":["v_1, ..., v_n linearly independent in a real or complex inner product space","for a dependent family the process produces a zero u_k, which is skipped and yields an orthonormal basis of the span"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T14:24:13.476812+00:00","domain":"linear algebra","id":"claim_bc01791ccad0fb7bcf635158f0db13bcca11c5b76eca0ae6dceb03aec1fed455","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let v_1, ..., v_n be linearly independent vectors in an inner product space. Define recursively u_1 = v_1 and u_k = v_k - sum_{j < k} <v_k, e_j> e_j with e_j = u_j / |u_j|. Then every u_k is nonzero, the vectors e_1, ..., e_n are orthonormal, and span(e_1, ..., e_k) = span(v_1, ..., v_k) for every k; the e_k are unique up to the sign (or unit scalar) of each vector given this nested-span condition. Applied to a countable linearly independent sequence the process yields an orthonormal sequence with the same nested spans, which is why every separable Hilbert space has an orthonormal basis. In matrix language, applying it to the columns of an m x n matrix A of full column rank gives the QR factorisation A = Q R with Q having orthonormal columns and R upper triangular with positive diagonal. (Numerically the modified Gram-Schmidt variant, which subtracts each projection as soon as it is formed, loses orthogonality far more slowly in floating point.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:06:21.712845+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bc4c6d339716deba8578fb81c0c8d06aa9f50f49ae5da7f92c53fd366c551960","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 6 ({\cite[Theorem~4.3 and Lemma~4.4) of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] {moench2026horizonProblem}}]

Let \(F\subset\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\) be finite and nonempty.  Then
\(B_F\) is nondegenerate and its precision matrix is Stieltjes: it is
symmetric positive definite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries.  Let
\(a\in\mathbb R^F\).  Here a coordinate conditioning means a normalised
density section obtained by fixing any subset of the current coordinates,
and a coordinate rectangle is a product of intervals in the current
coordinate space.  Any law obtained from \(a+B_F\) or \(a-B_F\) by finitely
many such conditionings, coordinate-rectangle restrictions, and coordinate
marginalisations is MTP\(_2\), provided every required section or restriction
normaliser is finite and strictly positive.  Every such law is therefore
associated, i.e., if \(X\) has one of these laws and \(f,g\) are bounded
coordinatewise nondecreasing functions, then
\begin{equation}
  \EE[f(X)g(X)]\geq \EE f(X)\,\EE g(X).
  
\end{equation}
Whenever the procedure uses only coordinate conditionings and
marginalisations and at least one coordinate remains, its result is a
nondegenerate Gaussian law with Stieltjes precision.  For a split into
retained and exposed blocks, write this precision as
\[
  P=\begin{pmatrix}P_{RR}&P_{RE}\\P_{ER}&P_{EE}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the regression matrix of the retained block on the exposed block is
\(-P_{RR}^{-1}P_{RE}\), which is entrywise nonnegative because
\(P_{RR}^{-1}\geq0\) and \(P_{RE}\leq0\) entrywise. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.095230+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bc87a1f0306ab7cd8def4aa65b1d5f54c084425b6c26fd3d7c040dc6dce3d315","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:bridge of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For every physical $K_5$ core, every declared circuit state $\tau$, and
every compatible ordered root or joint one-token attachment, there is an
exact raw circuit-anchored expansion.  Here $B_u$ and $P_u$ are the two
open daughters of the Bianchi split
$C_{ij,ag}=C_{ia,jg}-C_{ja,ig}$, cut on the internal rail
$u\in\{h,i,j\}$, and $\operatorname{Cl}_u$ closes that cut in its
inherited variance; \crefrange{eq:2.3.7}{eq:2.3.9} give their coordinate
construction.  The six root children are indexed
by $\nu=(u,\epsilon)$ with $u\in\{h,i,j\}$ and
$\epsilon\in\{B,P\}$.  In the canonical state,
$\mathcal W^{\rm root}_{(u,B)}$ (respectively
$\mathcal W^{\rm root}_{(u,P)}$) is the raw one-base presentation which
pairs $\mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}P_{\rm cyc}^*$ with
$\operatorname{Cl}_u(B_u)$ (respectively
$\operatorname{Cl}_u(P_u)$), retaining all ten gap words.  Transport the
whole presentation to $\sigma$ by
\crefrange{eq:2.2.6a}{eq:2.2.6e}, and put
\[
 a^{\rm root}_{\sigma,(u,B)}=-\frac23,\qquad
 a^{\rm root}_{\sigma,(u,P)}= \frac23.
\]
The transport sign $\chi(\sigma)$ is already part of the signed
transported presentation $\mathcal W^{\rm root}_{\sigma,\nu}$ and is
therefore not repeated in the scalar coefficient.
Here $P_{\rm cyc}$ is the fixed leg permutation which realizes the
oriented root hit in (eq:2.3.11 of the paper).  In root mode the expansion is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R^{\rm raw}_{C,\sigma}
 =\sum_{\nu=1}^{6}a^{\rm root}_{\sigma,\nu}
   \mathcal W^{\rm root}_{\sigma,\nu},
 \qquad
 \sum_{\nu=1}^{6}|a^{\rm root}_{\sigma,\nu}|\le4.}
\tag{2.3.1}
\]
For pass mode let
$\underline{\widetilde Q}^{rs}$ and
$\underline{\widetilde H}^{rs}$ be the fully gap-open two- and three-gate
factors at an ordered split $R=\{r,s\}$.  Let $\mathscr S_{rs}$ be the
fixed signed boundary reshuffle which carries the canonical $(0,1)$
residual word, including its variances and formal adjoints, to the
transported ordered pair $(r,s)$.  For every joint attachment of token
degree one,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P^{\rm raw}_{C,rs,\mathcal A}[\Xi]
 =\frac13\sum_{u\in\{h,i,j\}}
 \mathcal A_{rs}[\Xi]\!\left(
  \underline{\widetilde Q}^{rs}\otimes
  \underline{\mathscr S_{rs}\operatorname{Cl}_u(B_u-P_u)}
 \right).}
\tag{2.3.2}
\]
Thus
if $M_{\rm mode}$ is the number of scalar summands and
$A_{\rm mode}$ the sum of the absolute values of their coefficients,
\[
 M_{\rm root}=M_{\rm pass}=6,
 \qquad A_{\rm root}=4,
 \qquad A_{\rm pass}=2.
\tag{2.3.3}
\]
Every term contains each of the ten named gaps exactly once.  A root term
contains the selected two fronts and the other three coefficient gates;
a pass term contains the unchanged incoming token and all five coefficient
gates.  Every term has token degree one.  The identities commute with
ancillary tensoring, arbitrary joint typed attachment, signed transport
of the complete state, and final one-base-per-original-circuit gluing.
The distinguished cap remains
\[
 F_C^*F_C=Q_2=-\sum_a\lambda_a^2A_a^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.3.4}
\]
These proved identities are denoted $\mathsf{PK5}_{\mathrm{root/pass}}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:52:32.341724+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bc87f443935d5eb7f7ebf75b315520e1859ea742d22bc485650d9ee10fe27782","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop contraction to a point case of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $f : X \to Z$ is a projective contraction morphism between two smooth connected separated schemes of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ of dimension $n$ where the exceptional divisor $E$ is smooth and irreducible, and $f$ contracts $E$ to a point $p \in Z.$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:24:20.972501+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bc89b71980d3e3541a221d2bc4de7dc7eec945ab4da102a3ca1fb6cdbd1767f1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] Suppose $\varepsilon$ and $\theta$ satisfy ((eq6.311 of the paper)). 
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a (strictly stationary) Markov chain 
that satisfies Condition $\mathcal H (\varepsilon, \theta)$.
Then the state space of this Markov chain $X$ is
$\{-1,0,1\}$; and the following statements hold: \hfil\break
\noindent (1) The (joint) probability function of the random 
vector $(X_0, X_1)$ is the matrix $\Lambda^{(\varepsilon, \theta)}$ 
from ((eq6.321 of the paper)).
\hfil\break
\noindent (2) This Markov chain $X$ is reversible. \hfil\break
\noindent (3a) One has that $P(X_0 = 0) = 1 - \varepsilon$ and
$P(X_0 = -1) = P(X_0 = 1) = \varepsilon/2$. \hfil\break
\noindent (3b) For each $s \in \{-1,0,1\}$, 
$P(\{X_0 = 0\} \cap \{X_1 = s\}) > 0$; in fact
$P(\{X_0 = 0\} \cap \{X_1 = 0\}) \geq 1 - 2\varepsilon$. \hfil\break 
\noindent (4) One has that $E(X_0) = 0$ and 
$E|X_0| =  E(X_0^2) = \textrm{\rm Var}(X_0) = \varepsilon > 0$. \hfil\break
\noindent (5) The sequence $Y := (-X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$
is a strictly stationary Markov chain that satisfies 
Condition ${\cal H}(\varepsilon, \theta)$. \hfil\break 
\noindent (6) For each $n \in \mathbb N$, 
$\beta_X(n) \leq 6 \varepsilon (1 - \theta)^n 
\leq 6 \varepsilon \exp(-\theta n)$. \hfil\break 
\noindent (7) For each $n \in \mathbb N$,
$P(X_0 = X_n = 1) = 
(\varepsilon/2)(1 - \theta)^n + P(\{X_0 = 1\} \cap \{X_n = -1\})$.
\hfil\break
\noindent (8a) For each $n \in \mathbb N$,
$E(X_0X_n) = \textrm{\rm Cov}(X_0, X_n) = \varepsilon (1 - \theta)^n > 0$. \hfil\break
\noindent (8b) One has that 
$E(X_0^2) + 2 \sum_{n=1}^\infty E(X_0X_n) 
= \varepsilon [ (2/\theta) -1]$.
\hfil\break 
\noindent (9) Letting 
$u_n := (1/n) E[(X_1 + X_2 + \dots + X_n)^2]$ for
each $n \in \mathbb N$, one has that
\begin{equation}

u_1 \leq u_2 \leq u_3 \leq \dots \quad {\rm and} \quad
\lim_{n \to \infty} u_n = \varepsilon [(2 / \theta) - 1].  
\end{equation}
\noindent (10) As $n \to \infty$, the normalized partial sum
$n^{-1/2} (X_1 + X_2 + \dots + X_n)$
converges in distribution to the normal law with 
mean 0 and variance $\varepsilon [(2 / \theta) - 1]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:24:20.971961+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bc8afb947dd6e5752ebec23e5d88c5f2dbdb113fda3670e589297140ac073a2a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] {\rm (Merlev\`ede and Peligrad)}.    
\label {thm5.3}
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a 
(not necessarily Markovian)
strictly stationary sequence of random variables such that
the following three conditions (a), (b), (c) hold: \hfil\break
(a) $E[X_0^2] < \infty$ and $E[X_0] = 0$; \hfil\break
(b) $\liminf_{n \to \infty} n^{-1} 
\textrm{\rm Var}(\, \sum_{k=1}^n X_k) > 0$; and \hfil\break
(c) $\int_0^{\alpha(n)} Q_{|X(0)|}^2(u)\, du 
= o(n^{-1})$ as $n \to \infty$. \hfil\break
Then letting $b_n := (\pi/2)^{1/2} E|\sum_{k=1}^nX_k|$
for each $n \in \mathbb N$, one has that
$b_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, and 
$(1/b_n) \sum_{k=1}^n X_k$ converges in distribution to
$N(0,1)$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:54:28.101435+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bcb8e98672f154de02660cf49d860b751a7d70208ceec900b9fa2aa7f14b0d83","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition G_causal_definition of arXiv:2608.13716, 'Graph Causal Optimal Transport \\ and Wasserstein Distances'] Suppose $G$ is a DAG, $\mu \in \Gprobabilities{\mathcal{X}}$ and $\nu \in \Gprobabilities{\mathcal{Y}}$, the set of their \emph{$G$-causal} couplings is given as
$$
\Gcouplings{\mu}{\nu} := \couplings{\mu}{\nu}\cap \cGprobabilities{\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}},
$$
where $G^c = (V^c, E^c)$ is the graph made of $G$ and its copy $G'$ with additional edges linking $i\in V$ (associated to $\mathcal{X}_i$) and its parents to its copy $i'$ in $V'$ (associated to $\mathcal{Y}_i$): 
    $$
    V^c = \{i,i': i\in V\},\quad E^c = \{(i,j), (i,j'), (i', j'): (i,j)\in E\} \cup \{(i,i'): i\in V\}.
    $$
Moreover, we define the set of \emph{$G$-anticausal} couplings $\Ganticouplings{\mu}{\nu}$ to be the set of measures in $\couplings{\mu}{\nu}$ whose pushforward under the map $(x,y) \mapsto (y,x)$ is in $\Gcouplings{\nu}{\mu}$, and the set of \emph{$G$-bicausal couplings} $\Gbicouplings{\mu}{\nu} \coloneqq \Gcouplings{\mu}{\nu} \cap \Ganticouplings{\mu}{\nu}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:02.090970+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bcb95a9ef48f1735f6c18846973f8970a26e4354af7334bca403ab8cd48c0ff5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 37 (Critical barrier second moment) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Under the assumptions \ref{hyp_A1}, \ref{hyp_A2} and \ref{hyp_A3}, we choose
$0<\alpha<\rho$, and we 
define the barrier event
\[
\mathcal B_h(u)
:=
\left\{\mathcal G_{n,\alpha}(u),\
ah-\omega_n-1\le S_h(u)\le ah-\omega_n, \text{ and }
S_j(u) \leq aj \text{ for all }j\leq h
\right\},
\]
and the truncated count
\[
\widetilde N_h(a)
:=
\sum_{|u|=h}\ind_{\mathcal B_h(u)}.
\]
Then, for $\alpha>0$ small enough, there exist constants $c,C>0$ such that for all large $n$,
\begin{align*}
\mathbb E[\widetilde N_h(a)]
&\ge
c\,\mathrm{e}^{h(\kappa(t)+ta)-t\omega_n}(1+\omega_n)\,h^{-\frac{3}{2}};\\
\mathbb E[(\widetilde N_h(a))^2]
&\le
C\,\mathrm{e}^{2h(\kappa(t)+ta)-2t\omega_n}(1+\omega_n)^2\,h^{-3}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:17.908967+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bcc4ad1900d15fc924562eb44adf8a684a6e0f58d7d9fcba5269589e1b5c8b7a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Skorohod integral of arXiv:2602.14617, 'Stochastic Burgers equation driven by multiplicative Rosenblatt noise: local existence, un'] For a stochastic process $\Phi = (\Phi_s)_{s \in [0,T]}$ such that $\Phi_s \in \mathbb{D}^{2,2}$ for a.e. $s$, the Skorohod integral with respect to the Rosenblatt process is defined by
\[
\int_0^T \Phi_s \, \delta \mathcal{R}_s = \delta(\Phi),
\]

\[
\mathbb{E}\left[ \int_0^T |\Phi_s|^2 ds + \int_0^T \int_0^T |\mathrm{D}_u \Phi_s|^2 du ds + \int_0^T \int_0^T \int_0^T |\mathrm{D}^2_{u,v} \Phi_s|^2 du dv ds \right] < \infty.\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.288019+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bcdcd19af2b491e233e8c31ec4413366ffc96a78db59b520e518793bcecec88b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop subtlety of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $(M,J)$ be a compact complex surface that  satisfies the strict Hitchin-Thorpe inequality
$(2\chi + 3\tau)(M) > 0$, but has  $b_+(M) =1$. Then either $\kod (M, J) = -\infty$ or $\kod (M, J) = 2$.
Moreover,   $(M,J)$ is of K\"ahler type, so we may therefore   define 
a time orientation on $(H^2_{dR}(M, {\mathbb R}),Q)$ 
  by declaring any K\"ahler class $[\omega]\in H^2_{dR}(M, {\mathbb R})$ to be future-pointing. 
 
  
  \bigskip
  
   \noindent 
 If $\kod (M, J) = 2$, so that $(M,J)$ is of general type, then $c_1^+$ is past-pointing for any metric $g$ on $M$ and the spin$^c$ structure determined 
 by $J$. This implies that 
 $\eta =0$ belongs to the chamber $\sphericalangle^+$ containing all future-pointing perturbations, and $n_{\mathfrak{c}}(M, \sphericalangle^+)\neq 0$
 for this chamber.  For any smooth  metric $g$ on $M$ and the spin$^c$ structure determined by $J$, there is consequently a solution of the unperturbed Seiberg-Witten equations.

  \bigskip
  
  \noindent 
  By contrast, if $\kod (M, J) = -\infty$, then $(M,J)$ is obtained from $\mathbb{CP}_2$ by a sequence of blow-ups and blow-downs, and $M$ therefore admits Riemannian metrics
  of positive scalar curvature. In this case,  $\eta =0$ always belongs to the chamber $\sphericalangle^-$ containing the  past-pointing perturbations, 
  and $n_{\mathfrak{c}}(M, \sphericalangle^-)= 0$ for this chamber. Nonetheless,   $n_{\mathfrak{c}}(M, \sphericalangle^+)\neq 0$ for the remaining chamber. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:55:18.059726+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bce04e98f027f497450ce13161a7d475c48ab45fc166d30c658b2e138400299a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 7 (Local normalization and decoupled normal form) of arXiv:2606.16662, '2606.16662'] Fix a cutoff and a dyadic block \((N,Q,M)\).  Consider either one value of the
centered kernel, one increment between two Volterra pairs, or one member of
the finite cutoff family used in the tail argument.  In an increment
estimate, collect jointly all first-Wiener kernels at the two endpoints and
in the finite telescope connecting them.  There exists an integer \(d_0\),
depending only on the finite color family and on the number of telescope
terms, with the following properties.

For every \(\underline m\in\Z^d_+\), there is a standard real Gaussian vector
\[
        G_{\underline m}
        =(G_{\underline m,\mu})_{1\le\mu\le d_0},
\]
and these vectors are independent for distinct representatives.  With
\[
        a=(\underline\ell,\mu),\qquad
        b=(\underline r,\lambda),\qquad c=q,\qquad e=n,
\]
the centered kernel has a finite expansion
\begin{equation}
        B_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}^{i;j,k}(e,c;t,s)
        =\sum_{\nu}\sum_{a,b}
        H_{\nu;a,b,c,e}(t,s)
        \wick{G_{\underline\ell,\mu}G_{\underline r,\lambda}} .
\end{equation}
The pattern index \(\nu\) contains the two Fourier signs, together with the
finite sine--cosine, color and cutoff choices.  For fixed \(\nu\), there are
signs \(\epsilon_{\nu,1},\epsilon_{\nu,2}\in\{+1,-1\}\) such that the
coefficient tensor is supported by
\begin{equation}
        n=q+\epsilon_{\nu,1}\underline\ell
              +\epsilon_{\nu,2}\underline r,
        \qquad |\underline\ell|\sim|\underline r|\sim N,
        \qquad |q|\sim Q,
        \qquad |n|\sim M,
        \qquad Q\le c_{\rm ap}N,
\end{equation}
up to the fixed Littlewood--Paley overlap, and
\begin{equation}
        |H_{\nu;a,b,c,e}(t,s)|
        \lesssim N^{-\Gamma_{i;j,k}}.
\end{equation}
For an increment tensor, the right-hand side carries the additional
increment factor from Assumption~\ref{ass:coeff}.  The number of patterns
and the auxiliary dimension \(d_0\) are uniform in the dyadic scales,
cutoff and time points.

For every finite-dimensional Banach space \(X\), every finite coefficient
family \((C_{a,b})\subset X\), and every \(p\ge2\), write
\(G_a=G_{\underline\ell,\mu}\) for \(a=(\underline\ell,\mu)\),
and similarly for \(G_b\).  Then
\begin{equation}
        \left\|\sum_{a,b}C_{a,b}\wick{G_aG_b}
        \right\|_{L^p(\Omega;X)}
        \le C_{\rm dec}
        \left\|\sum_{a,b}C_{a,b}G_a\widetilde G_b
        \right\|_{L^p(\Omega\times\widetilde\Omega;X)},
\end{equation}
where \((\widetilde G_b)\) is an independent copy.  The constant
\(C_{\rm dec}\) depends only on the chaos order.","status":"unverified"}
